# SIGN
### Of the stone they call ahofar:

<image-desc>A circular miniature within a decorative border. It depicts two men in a small wooden boat on a blue sea. One man is rowing while the other looks into the water, appearing to gather the 'ahofar' (pearls) mentioned in the text.</image-desc>

**O**f the eleventh degree of the sign of Aries: it is the stone they call **ahofar** <term>ahofar: from the Arabic "al-jawhar," a term used here specifically for pearls</term>. This is by its nature hot and dry. It is found in many places, which are: in the Great Sea that surrounds the entire world, inside very large shells where they grow in this manner: when the northern winds blow, the shells open and catch that moisture that comes with the drops of dew that fall into them. They hold it and go swimming to the bottom of the water; and when day comes, they emerge and strive toward the sun, rising up to catch a great deal of its heat, and afterwards, they descend to the bottom. They do this same thing in the evening when the sun sets. And once they understand that the water has curdled <note>meaning the dew has solidified into a pearl</note>, they gather together so that the waves of the sea push them so strongly that they are cast onto the shore. When the tide recedes, some are taken back, and those that remain are sent further out. Being formed in this way, they become round and beautiful and bright. And the larger, whiter, and clearer they are, the more they are worth. Even though this stone is very white, the sight does not pass through it because its whiteness is dense, yet it is very bright from within, just as if it were a pearl. And those that come out with a bad color, or murky, or with a bad shape—those that are not perfectly round or are stunted—this happens only because of a defect in the "slowness" <note>original: "mança," perhaps referring to the lack of movement or "laziness" of the shell</note> of the shells, which did not receive as much air or heat from the sun as they should, nor did they receive it at the proper time, nor were they held long enough by the waves of the sea to be made round. This stone is very noble and highly prized by men. There is great virtue in it, for all who see it love it for its form and for the beauty of its simplicity, which has no need for the help of a workshop <note>meaning it is naturally perfect and requires no cutting or polishing by a jeweler</note>. And great lords prize it highly.

### Of the stone that they call Anetatz: ::::::::::—

<image-desc>A rectangular miniature depicting two men in medieval tunics (one red, one blue) standing outdoors next to a slender column, seemingly engaged in a discussion or a demonstration involving a stone or object.</image-desc>

Of the thirteenth degree of the sign of Aries: is the stone which they call Anetatiz, which means "blood stone" <note>likely Hematite, which produces a blood-red streak when ground</note>. By its nature, it is hot and dry. It is a dark red color that even borders on the color of blood. It is thick so that sight cannot pass through it; it is strong and very hard. And when they polish it, that which comes off it resembles blood in color and in all its qualities. And its virtue is such: that if they hang it over abscesses <term>postema: a painful, inflammatory swelling or abscess</term> that break out, it dissolves them in one day; and even more so if they are anointed with the liquid <note>original: "ponçura," here referring to the residue or "juice" of the stone</note> that comes from it. And if they put this substance that resembles blood into eyes that are weeping, it will heal them. It is helpful for all diseases of the eyes that are caused by humidity: this is because of the great heat and dryness that is within it. It does even more: for he who looks at it every day in the morning when he rises is certain not to have abscesses in the eyes. And the two stars—the one toward the north and the other toward the south—which are upon the hood <note>original: "toca," a head-covering or turban</note> of the sign of Aries, have power over this stone, and from them it receives its virtue. And when these are in the ascendant or in the midheaven, then this stone will show its works most effectively.

Concerning the stone they call Beruth: the thirteenth degree of the sign of Aries is the stone they call Beruth, though it has another name, which is **Agut**. It is found in a mountain in the land of Egypt. They speak of it in this way: the Egyptians call it the *marrow* <note>original: "mef," likely "meollo" or "medulla," referring to the inner substance of a bone</note> of Aries, and this is because it has a white color, and there are many yellow veins in it. It is a stone that is very light and easy to break, for it shatters very easily with whatever it is struck. And one finds upon it a color that resembles the dust found upon the walls of a mill. It receives this from the nature of the sea dew near where it is found. By its nature, it is hot and dry. And although it is not good for burning <note>original: "pruar," possibly "probar" (tasting/testing) or "purgar" (purifying)</note>, it is good when placed upon the tongue, where it makes a sensation as if it bites because of the sharpness within it. It also does another very powerful thing: if a very heavy man carries it with him, it thins the vital spirit <note>original: "ayma," meaning "alma" or soul. Therefore, it is good for overly heavy men who wish to become thin quickly and without trouble. ### Concerning the stone which they call the Stone of Cin

<image-desc>A historiated initial 'D' featuring two men: one in a green hooded robe and another in a light tunic raising an axe to strike a rock. In the margin, a small figure in a green and red tunic is shown kneeling.</image-desc>

Concerning the stone they call the Stone of Cin: the fourteenth degree of the sign of Aries is the stone they call the Stone of **Cin** <note>original: "cin," referring to China</note> because it is found in that land which has that name. And the people of that place call it **Tariz**, which means as much as "inner mouth." By its nature it is hot and dry and of a purple color with black veins. It is strong and hard to break. And when they do break it, they find it varied or mottled inside. It has such virtue that if it is hung around the neck of one who suffers from the swelling called quinsy <term>esquinancia: a severe inflammation of the throat or tonsils</term>, he is healed immediately; and if they grind it and give it to him to drink, it does this same thing. Furthermore, it has another very strange property: for flies flee from the place where it is present. Because of this, the people of that land make vessels and bowls from it in which they keep their food. And even besides this, it does another thing: if it is placed in olive oil, it dissolves immediately and incorporates itself with the oil. And the star that remains toward the northern part—which is in the hand of the Lady who is seated upon the chair <note>The constellation Cassiopeia</note>—has power over this stone, and from her it receives its virtue. And when this star is in the ascendant, this stone shows its works most manifest.

# CONCERNING ARIES

## ->Concerning the stone that attracts gold<-

<image-desc>A decorative initial letter 'E' containing a miniature painting of two men. A man in a green robe holds a small object, presenting it to another man dressed in a red tunic. The initial is framed with colorful blue and red leafy flourishes.</image-desc>

In the fifteenth degree of the sign of Aries is the stone that attracts gold. And it is by its nature hot and dry. It is of a yellow color that leans slightly toward purple; and when a man takes it in his hand, he feels it is smooth <note>original: "lezne," meaning slippery or polished</note> and soft. This stone attracts gold and makes the metal obey it, just as the magnet <term>jman: lodestone</term> attracts iron. And if one were to file gold and mix its filings with earth or with something else, and then bring the stone near it, the gold would separate from the other things with which it was mixed and all of it would stick to the stone. And goldsmiths use this stone often, as do those who wish to purify <term>apurar: to refine or cleanse of impurities</term> gold. And if they burn it in the same way as the stone we said attracts iron, it has an even greater power of burning. This stone also has another virtue: it gives very great joy to the heart, so that he who carries it in the morning will never encounter any great thing that makes him sad. And the middle star of the three that are in the area of the "turn of the river" <note>Referring to a section of the constellation Eridanus, the River</note> has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its virtue. And when this star is in the ascendant, this stone shows its works most clearly.

## ->Concerning the stone that sucks blood<-

<image-desc>A decorative initial letter 'E' containing a miniature painting of two men. One man stands wearing a red and blue robe, while the other kneels before him, appearing to work on the standing man's leg. The initial is surrounded by ornate red and blue leaf scrollwork.</image-desc>

In the sixteenth degree of the sign of Aries is the stone that sucks blood. This is by its nature hot and dry. And it is found in certain places in the regions of the East. Its color is green, and there is a red spot upon it <note>This description corresponds to the Heliotrope, commonly known as Bloodstone</note>. And whoever takes it in his hand finds it rough and light because it is very porous. In shape, it is flat on one side and round on the other, in the form of a half-sphere <term>media espera: hemisphere</term>. Its property is such that if the skin of any animal is broken and the stone is placed there, it pulls the blood out with very great force. And it does this to a living body, but not so much to blood that has already been separated. And whoever wishes to know the quantity of blood it has drawn should weigh the stone after it has drawn it, and then place it in hot water; all the blood it has drawn will come out of it and it will remain as it was before. Then weigh it again, and he will know the quantity of blood it drew. And the star called "the one on the southern side" that is in the breast of the Chained Woman <note>The constellation Andromeda</note> has power over this stone, and the stone receives its virtue from her. And when she is in the ascendant, this stone shows its works most clearly.

## ## Concerning the stone that appears in the sea when Mars rises.

<image-desc>An ornate illuminated initial 'E' featuring a miniature of a man sitting in a blue vessel representing the sea, looking up at a red star (Mars) in the sky. The letter is surrounded by intricate red and blue scrollwork with a hybrid creature at the base.</image-desc>

**T**he nineteenth <note>original: "dieziecheno," meaning nineteenth</note> degree of the sign of Aries belongs to the stone that appears in the sea when the planet they call Mars rises; it appears in the east just as the planet ascends. This stone is by its nature hot and dry, and it is found in the sea near the coasts of the East. Its color is a bright red, clear in the manner of fire. It is always found in a round shape and in no other way. And when Mars appears above the earth, this stone rises to the surface of the sea and floats upon the waves. But when the planet sets, the stone descends and goes to the bottom of the water, and it always behaves this way, rising and falling. One can never take this stone except when Mars is above the earth. It possesses a brilliance that looks like lightning or a glowing coal of fire. The finest among them give off light at night like a candle. This brilliance lasts as long as Mars is above the earth; when the planet sets, the stone immediately becomes like any other stone, dark and dim. This is one of the great wonders that testifies to the "prophecy" <note>The medieval concept that planets dictate the fate or properties of earthly objects</note> that the planets hold over stones and mines, through the power that God placed within them. This stone also possesses such a property that he who carries it will have the lions obey him <note>original: "olerte[n] le," likely a scribal variant for "obedecerle"</note> so that he may take them by hand, and they will do him no harm; for when the lion sees the stone, it loses all its strength and has no power. And the star that is in the middle of the Bear <note>original: "uesa," referring to Ursa Major</note> at the vertex of the triangle <term>Triangulum: a small constellation in the northern sky</term> has power over this stone, and from it the stone receives its virtue. When that star is in the middle of the heaven, this stone shows its workings most clearly.

<image-desc>A square illustration containing a gold-colored triangle with a central dot, representing the constellation Triangulum.</image-desc>

<column-break/>

## ## Concerning the stone that tints glass.

<image-desc>An ornate illuminated initial 'E' containing a miniature of a figure in red robes standing beside a circular apparatus, possibly representing the process of glassmaking. The initial is decorated with floral motifs and a grotesque figure stretching from the top.</image-desc>

**T**he nineteenth degree of the sign of Aries <note>The manuscript assigns this stone to the same degree as the previous one</note> belongs to the stone that tints glass. This stone is by its nature hot and dry. Its color is brown, and it has black veins within it. It is heavy and has a rough "wind" <note>original: "uiento asp[er]o," likely referring to internal fissures or a porous grain</note> such that certain iron-like marks <note>original: "ferreduras"</note> can be seen in it. This stone is not found in any other place except on a mountain in Arabia called Vulcan <note>original: "uulca," likely referring to a volcanic region</note>, which burns forever. Its property is such that fire cannot burn it, nor can any force change its color, even if kept in the flame constantly. It has another great property: glass obeys it and is refined by it, just as the magnet <term>aymante: lodestone</term> holds iron; it draws the glass to itself and purifies it entirely. For this reason, it is counted among the virtuous stones. If a piece of this stone touches any work made of glass—be it a vessel or something else—it will break immediately. If they place it at the mouth of the furnace in which the glass is kept, it makes the glass jump out, whether it be hot or cold. This stone performs this feat according to its size and weight. Furthermore, it has another property: he who carries it with him is safe from having "the drop" <term>gota: a historical term for gout or joint inflammation</term>, neither in his feet nor in his joints. This is because the stone destroys those humors from which the gout originates. If the gout has already joined the body, although the stone may not be able to take it away entirely, the illness improves greatly; if he carries it for a long time, he can be cured of it. And the star that is at the end of the spine of the sign of Aries, and the other which is in the right foot of the Chained Woman <note>The constellation Andromeda</note>, have power over this stone and from them it receives its virtue. When both are in the middle of the heaven, this stone will show its works most fully.

<image-desc>An illustration of a ram (representing the zodiac sign Aries) standing next to a small, semi-submerged human figure, representing associated celestial or mythological themes.</image-desc>

# OF ARIES

### Concerning the stone called *annoza*.

<image-desc>An historiated initial 'E' contains a scene of two men engaged in stonework. One man is seated on a bench, using a hammer and chisel to shape a square block of stone. Behind him stands another man. In the background, there is a landscape with a building or tower under a patterned sky.</image-desc>

The nineteenth degree of the sign of Aries belongs to the stone they call *annoza* <note>original: "annoza," likely derived from the Arabic "al-nura," meaning lime</note>. This name means the same in Chaldean <note>The language of the ancient Near East, frequently cited in this text as the source of lapidary knowledge</note> as "limestone" does in our language, for this is the stone from which they make lime. Its nature is hot and dry. It is found in most places on earth, and in all the heavy construction that men must perform, they rely greatly upon it because it joins stones together very strongly and seals up holes in such a way that water cannot escape. For this reason, men use it to repair conduits and to caulk ships, and they apply it to any other thing where they believe water must not pass through. When this stone is burned, it traps the fire within itself until water is poured over it; only then does it manifest the heat it has held enclosed, for smoke rises from it as if from a fire. And if it is placed upon something, heat comes from it that burns, though not as much as the other "burning stones" <note>likely referring to quicklime or sulfurous minerals</note> of which we have named some and will name more later in the appropriate place. Furthermore, when this stone is mixed with arsenic <term>azarnech</term> <note>original: "azarnech," a Persian-derived term for arsenic minerals like orpiment, often used in depilatory creams</note> and rubbed onto the hair of any animal, it strips it all away in a short time. If it is left to sit for too long, it flays the skin. It is like a toxic grain; if these stones are ground and mixed together as they should be, and the water from them is given to someone to drink, it pierces the bladder, creates sores in the intestines, and causes great damage to the liver. Yet in this aforementioned stone, there is also great benefit, for if it is ground with oil to make an ointment and applied to large and wide wounds, they close very quickly and heal well. The star located on the ankle of the hindmost foot of the sign of Aries holds power and dominion over this stone, and from it the stone draws its strength and virtue. When that star is in the middle of the sky, this stone will manifest its effects most clearly.

### Concerning the stone called *vsk*.

<image-desc>An historiated initial 'E' depicts a scholarly scene. On the left, an older bearded man in a hooded robe sits and gestures authoritatively. The twentieth degree of the sign of Aries belongs to the stone called *vsk* <note>original: "vsk," a transliteration of the Persian word for Jasper, "yashk"</note>, which is the one we call jasper. This stone is hot and dry in its nature. It also comes in many varieties, of which these are the best. The first of these is the color of green prase <term>prasme</term> <note>A leek-green variety of quartz</note>, which some men mistake for an inferior emerald because its color is not as clear; in this they err in their judgment, for this stone has its own nature that does not resemble the emerald at all. The same is true of the green jasper that looks like prase; it is not of that same nature or temperament, nor does it share its properties, as will be shown later in this book. The second kind of jasper is the color of thick wine, and it is clear so that sight passes through it. The third kind is the color of the air. The fourth is the color of smoke, and this is the most common and least valuable of all. The fifth is of many colors and markings, and it has white and blackish veins through which sight can pass. We shall speak of each one in its place regarding its specific property and which stars it is associated with, from which it draws its power. But first, we shall speak of the property found in this green jasper which...

->Concerning the stone named tumnon<-

<image-desc>A large illuminated initial 'E' containing a circular miniature of two men. One man in a grey robe sits on the left; the other, in a red tunic, strikes a rock with a pickaxe. This depicts the extraction of the stone.</image-desc>

The twenty-first degree of the sign of Aries belongs to the stone they call <term>tumnon</term> <note>A specific variety of jasper described in this tradition</note>, which we intend to discuss in this book; it is the second type of jasper. And this one is the color of white wine leaning towards yellow, and this yellowness is mixed somewhat with red. And they find it on the bank of the river of Çamundin. And its shape is round, but not perfectly so. And it is very beautiful and very clear, and sight passes through it. And this kind of jasper is more prized than the others we have spoken of. And it has such virtue that whoever carries it with them is protected from that disease called the falling sickness <note>original: "caduca," a historical term for epilepsy</note>. And likewise, it is good for those diseases that come from melancholy <note>in medieval medicine, "melancholy" was an excess of black bile thought to cause sadness or madness</note>, for it removes them by strengthening the heart and making it joyful. And it does another thing: if they grind it and give it as a drink to one who has wounded intestines <note>original: "entrennos llagados"</note>, it heals them very quickly. And for this reason, physicians put it in <term>electuaries</term> <note>medicinal pastes made by mixing powders with honey or syrup</note> and in other medicines to strengthen the arm and to remove melancholic diseases. And the star that is on the knees of the woman who is seated in the chair <note>referring to the constellation Cassiopeia</note> has power over this stone, and from her, it receives its strength and virtue. And when she is in the ascendant, the works of this stone will appear more clearly.

# Of the stone they call Afarunz

<image-desc>Historiated initial 'E' containing a miniature of two men in a rocky landscape; one is crouched and using a pickaxe on the earth while the other stands behind him, pointing and observing. The initial is decorated with colorful scrollwork and a bird perched on top.</image-desc>

In the 22nd degree of the sign of Aries is the stone they call Afarunz, which means "likeness of a star." It is the third kind of jasper we have mentioned, among which there are softer varieties that are translucent. And because these veins <note>original: "uias," referring to the internal streaks or inclusions</note> always shine like a star, they gave it this name. It is found in the same river we mentioned before where these jaspers are found, and it is more noble than any of them. Men prize it more because it is more luminous and larger than all the others. It is of such a nature that when it is placed in fire, the longer it remains there, the purer its light becomes and the more beautiful it grows; for the fire does not damage it, but rather purifies it and increases its brightness, unlike other stones that shatter in the fire.

It is necessary for whoever wishes to work with this stone to know the mastery of making the fire with which the stone must be treated. This is done by placing the stone in a crucible <note>original: "alhor"</note>, covering it with another from above, and sealing it well with mud. Then, two small furnaces <note>original: "formellos"</note> should be made: one to provide fire from below and the other from above, so that both heat it equally. When they wish to see if the stone is properly treated, they should uncover it, and if it is not yet as it should be, they must let it remain. When it is refined, they should not remove it immediately, but let it stay in the furnace until it cools on its own; for when the heat of noble stones is very intense and they are brought quickly into the air, they absorb the cold so suddenly that they crack and break. When the stone cools by itself, this does not happen.

The virtue of this stone is that whoever carries it finds their heart strengthened and it gives them joy, and it makes a man accomplish his deeds with ease. If they hang this stone on a man who has pain in his belly or liver, it takes it away immediately if the illness is new; if it is an old illness, it provides great benefit by not allowing it to grow further. And the star that is the last of those at the base of the angle formed at the straight turn of the figure of the Dragon <note>referring to the constellation Draco</note> has power over this stone, and from it, the stone receives its virtue. When this star is in the ascendant, this medicine manifests its effects.

<column-break/>

<image-desc>A circular miniature depicting a green serpent or eel-like creature coiled within a golden disk, set against a dark background.</image-desc>

# Of the stone named Belyniz

<image-desc>Historiated initial 'E' containing a miniature of two figures; one sits on the left, possibly a physician or sage, holding an object, while a smaller figure or child on the right reaches out toward them. The scene is set in an interior or grotto-like space.</image-desc>

In the 31st degree <note>Though the text says .xxxi., a zodiac sign only has 30 degrees; this is likely a scribal error for the 21st or 23rd degree</note> of the sign of Aries is the stone they call Belyniz. This is the other kind of jasper we mentioned, which has the color of clear air <note>original: "arzediao," likely a corruption of "aire diáfano"</note> and is clean in its light. For this stone is very bright, like the air through which one's sight passes. It has no color of its own, just as the air has none of itself, but it receives every other color it comes near. In this same way does this stone: as the air is clear, the stone is clear; and as the air is cloudy, the stone is cloudy. It is found on the bank of that river where the other jaspers we have spoken of are found.

It has such virtue that it takes away the pain that occurs in half of the head, which they call in Arabic <term>xaqueca</term> <note>Modern Spanish: jaqueca; English: migraine</note> and in Latin <term>migranica</term> <note>Modern English: migraine</note>. It does this by hanging it over the part where the pain is. Likewise, if it is hung over children while they are being raised, it is of very great benefit to their upbringing, for they grow better and healthier because of it, and it further ensures they are not easily startled <note>original: "uozados," likely meaning "frightened by loud voices or sudden noise"</note>. And the star that is the middle one of the three in the body of Cetus <note>original: "cap toz," a corruption of the Arabic "Kaitos," referring to the constellation of the Whale</note> has power over this stone, and from it, the stone receives its strength and virtue. When that star is in the middle of the sky, the effect of this stone will be stronger and of greater virtue.

In the 28th degree of the sign of Aries is the stone called gaguz, which means "smoky" <note>original: "fumenza"</note>. This is the fourth kind of jasper <term>iaspis: jasper</term> of which we have spoken, which has the color of smoke and a smoky appearance.

## The stone botimax
<image-desc>A circular miniature set within a square decorative frame with pink and blue borders. Inside, an elder in a hooded yellow robe and blue tunic stands holding a book, gesturing towards a younger man in a yellow tunic who is bowing or kneeling on the ground. At the eighteen degrees of the sign of Aries is the stone that they call botimax <note>original: "botimax," likely derived from the Arabic "buṭmāsh," meaning sleeplessness</note>; which means as much as "snatcher of sleep." And it is by its nature hot and dry. And they find it in the western regions on a mountain that is near the dark place where it is shadowy for most of the year. And it is a stone that tends toward the color black and resembles a shining coal <note>original: "luco," possibly referring to a lychnis or a dark, glowing mineral</note>. This stone is hard and very heavy, so much so that in its weight it resembles lead. And it is so strong that it cannot be broken except with the juice of the aytonio plant <term>juice of the aytonio: original "gumo aytonio," likely referring to a specific herbal extract or a corrupted reference to goat's blood, which medieval alchemists believed was the only substance that could break the hardest stones</term>. And its virtue is according to the name it has: for if a person hangs a weight of ten drachms <term>drachms: original "dragmas," a unit of weight roughly equal to 3.5 grams</term> of it upon themselves, they would never sleep as long as they held it, whether by night or by day. However, the wakefulness that a person undergoes because of this stone does not result in such great harm as that which a person does to themselves by forcing their own nature while they endure it. And the wakefulness that this stone causes is pleasant, unless it is excessive in a way that nature cannot endure by any means. And this wakefulness pleases the one who holds the stone so much that even if they hang it upon themselves for a very long time, they will not be able to sleep as well as they did before. And it even has another virtue: that if they grind about a quarter of a drachm of it and mix it with some liquid and put it into a cat's nostrils, it heals it the first time, provided that the leprosy <note>original: "gaffetat," a term used for leprosy or severe skin diseases that cause limbs to wither or "claw" (gafo)</note> is not so strong that it has already taken away some limb; for that cannot be recovered by the virtue of the stone. But as for the rest that remains in the body which causes the leprosy, it removes it and does not allow the disease to pass beyond that point. And the star that follows the things that are together after the winding of the river <note>original: "tortura del ryo," referring to the constellation Eridanus, the Celestial River</note> has power over the aforementioned stone and from it receives its virtue. And when it is in the ascendant, it shows the works of this stone more clearly.

At the thirty degrees of the sign of Aries is the stone that they call in Arabic annoratar <note>original: "annoratar," from Arabic "an-nūshādir"</note>, and in Latin, sal armoniaco <term>sal armoniaco: Sal Ammoniac or ammonium chloride, a salt known in antiquity for its cleansing properties</term>. And this stone is by nature hot and dry at the end of the third degree. And it is a type of salt that is divided into many kinds. Thus, there are some that are whole, and they extract it like small and very hard pebbles, and it is a salty form such that it grips the tongue very strongly when it is placed upon it. There are others among them in which they find black drops, and in others white drops, and others that are gray. But the greatest of all is another kind that is white and clear, resembling crystal. But all these aforementioned kinds have one nature and one virtue: and it is this—to draw out substances from the depths to soften them, not from the outside. And with this power of drawing that it possesses, it thins the substances with which it is mixed; and for this reason, the physicians put it in the eye-powder <term>eye-powder: original "alcohol," referring to kohl or finely ground medicinal powders for the eyes</term> that they make for the eyes, and likewise in the powders they make to clean the teeth. And it even has another virtue: that if they sprinkle the house with brine made from it, snakes and vipers will not gather there...

- **Outer Ring:** Divided into thirty segments, each containing an illustration of an angel with a red halo seated within a blue arched frame.

# OF THE SIGN
<note>original: "DEL SIGNO"</note>

**Prologue:**

These are the thirty types of stones that are associated with the sign of Aries. Each one is shown with the specific star to which it has its connection <note>original: "atamiento" – a binding or astrological link</note>, and through which virtue and power its influence directs its works in this lesser world <note>The "microcosm" or the earthly realm of humanity</note> from the heaven of the highest help. The ancients set down general rules so that men could work with more certain knowledge. They commanded that for each sign, one should also observe the planet that held the greatest power over it, and depending on what they understood its state to be, they should perform their works: using the good for well-being and the bad for harm, as set forth in this book for each planet in the place where it is appropriate. He who does not fully know this cannot understand the connection the stars have with one another, nor the power they hold over earthly things, nor how their states change from one manner to another. Therefore, they deemed it right that in all works pertaining to the degrees of the sign of Aries, one should pay close attention to the planet of the star they call Mars. Likewise, one must observe the Lord of the Face <term>decan: a sub-division of a zodiac sign spanning ten degrees, ruled by a specific planet</term> in which that degree resides, so that at the hour one wishes to perform a work with that stone, it is in one of its dignities <note>astrological positions of strength</note>, and above the eastern horizon in such a way that it has no hindrance; for all of this must be observed in works intended for good, and the opposite for those of evil. When all these things are observed, the virtues of the stars will join with those of the stones so that they will perform their works completely, allowing the worker to fulfill his will in whatever he wishes to achieve.

**Of the stone they call diamond:**

Aries is this second sign of the twelve of which we spoke. It is likewise divided into thirty degrees, and each degree has its known stone and a connection with it, whose virtue you shall see as will be shown hereafter. 

The first stone of these is the one called *meza* <note>original: "meza" – from the Arabic "al-mās" for diamond</note> in Arabic and *diamant* in Latin. This stone is by its nature cold and dry in the fourth degree <note>a reference to the highest intensity of these qualities in medieval medicine</note>. It is found in the river called Urabiçen that flows through that land they call Boraam; and it is not born there except in the land where it is six months day and six months night. No man can reach the place where that river originates because there are many snakes and other poisonous beasts of many kinds; and there are the vipers that kill by sight alone <note>a reference to the mythical Basilisk</note>. For this reason, men do not dare go there. But when that river rises, many channels and gullies flow from it, bringing these aforementioned stones with them. Although very large and small stones are born where the river begins, just as with other stones, these flash-floods can only carry the smaller ones. 

It has a color resembling clear *azogratir* <note>likely a transliteration of an Arabic term referring to the metallic luster of lead or quicksilver</note>, and it resembles polished iron. Some lean toward the color of purple, and others toward yellow, but the best of them is the one that resembles *vizno* <note>original: "uizno" – meaning clear or white</note>. Some men make counterfeits of them out of glass. He who wishes to prove which is true or false should put both in the fire; the glass one will melt, but the diamond will not, for the fire never does it harm. This is the stone that breaks all others that are pierced, or at least it marks them, and no other stone can make a mark upon it. This stone does even more: if other stones are carried with it, it grinds them all down. But there is a nature...

...lead, which is called *açobra* in Arabic and *estāno* <note>original: "estāno" — tin</note> in Latin, which breaks this type of stone in this manner: if they wrap the tin around the hardness of the stone and strike it with a hammer, it yields immediately, as if the tin had broken it. If one were to make a mortar and pestle out of this lead, they could grind the stone therein and make a powder of it. And if they mix this powder with something and give it to one who has a stone in the bladder, it will break it immediately. And it does all this if one takes a small piece of it and places it upon a thin piece of iron and moves it toward a man who has a stone in his anatomy <note>a reference to the urinary tract</note> in such a way that it touches him; it will break it immediately. But this should not be done unless the man is in great pain or in doubt of recovery. And those who wish to engrave or carve other stones take a small, very thin, and sharp piece of this stone and place it upon a handle of iron, silver, or copper, and they drill or carve with it the stones they wish to engrave or work with designs <note>original: "mafes" — possibly relief work or settings</note>. This stone is thus disfigured because of those poisonous animals that dwell where it is born; for these stones are always square and sharp, just as those animals have teeth to bite with. Thus, when men put them in their mouths and keep them there for a long time, their teeth fall out. It also has this property: if one grinds a weight of one drachma <term>drachma: an ancient unit of weight, roughly 3.4 grams</term> of it with the lead we mentioned and gives it to a man to drink, he dies. Although its nature is cold and dry, its sign <note>astrological signature</note> is such that he who carries it with him becomes angry and is moved to quarrel, and to do other things involving boldness and strength. And the bright star that is in the right thigh of the arm of Perseus <note>original: "p̄fio" — Perseus</note>, the one who carries the head of the ghoul <note>original: "dā l’gola" — Algol, from the Arabic 'al-ghul', the Demon Star</note>, and the other star which is the sun of the head of that same figure, have power over this stone, and from them it receives its virtue. And when they are in the mid-heaven <note>the highest point in the sky</note>, this stone shows its workings most clearly.

## Concerning the stone they call Camozica :-

<image-desc>A historiated initial 'E' containing a miniature of two figures: a scholar or alchemist in a green robe holding a flask, and a seated assistant in red. They appear to be in a laboratory or study.</image-desc>

The third degree of the sign of Taurus belongs to the stone they call *camozica*, which means "vinegary" in Chaldean <note>original: "caldeo"</note> just as it does in this Spanish language. It is named thus because when it is ground, that which comes out of it smells and acts like a very strong vinegar. It is by nature cold and dry, and its color is reddish. It is also airy, as it is very porous; however, despite this, it is very hard to break. It is found in the land of the Medes <note>original: "mediatōz" refers to Media, an ancient region in modern-day Iran</note> on the mountain they call Abdar, in certain caves found there; some of these stones are large and some are small. When men grind them and mix them with water, after six days, it becomes a very strong vinegar, and they use it in their food. Physicians <term>physicians: medieval doctors who balanced the body's four humors (blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile)</term> put it into syrups and other things to cut through the humors <note>original: "talar las humores" — to break down or purge excess bodily fluids</note> because it cleanses them better than regular vinegar. If one pours it over cloths made of linen or wool, it washes and cleanses them, because it dissolves "strong bodies" <note>likely referring to metals or hardened minerals in an alchemical context</note> and removes their filth. Those who labor in the art of alchemy also use it. The two stars—the one to the south and the other to the north—that are in the front line of *Azorayu* <note>original: "azorayu" refers to the Pleiades star cluster</note>, which they call the "Seven Little Goats" <note>original: "ſiete cabrellas"</note>, are located in the figure of Taurus. They have power over this stone, and from them it receives its strength and virtue. When these two are in the ascendant, this stone shows its works most clearly.

<image-desc>A circular diagram containing the zodiacal figure of Taurus, a bull, colored in ochre and brown with a gold star on its shoulder.</image-desc>

## Concerning the stone they call Fuludia. :-----:

<image-desc>A historiated initial 'E' containing a miniature of a shepherd (pastor) in a blue tunic holding a staff and a vessel, standing near another figure or animal.</image-desc>

The fourth degree of the sign of Taurus belongs to the stone they call *fuludia*, which means "gatherer of milk" <note>a reference to its curdling properties</note>. Its nature is cold and dry, and it is very strong in these two complexions <term>complexions: the combination of primary qualities (hot, cold, wet, dry) that determine a substance's nature</term>. Its color is so white that it resembles a piece of snow; water does not penetrate it, nor does the wind pass through it. It is so hard that no other body can conquer it except for the diamond. This stone is found on Mount Azar, which is in the land of Egypt; it is far from any settlement, a good hundred miles. There are caves there where vipers and other evil beasts dwell. The stone is found outside of them because the serpents bring them out, and the herdsmen who guard the flocks find them. They take them and bring them to be sold. If one rubs it with milk, the residue that comes off curdles <note>original: "quaiā" — to coagulate or set</note> all the milk it is placed in; therefore, the people of that land use it in their cheeses and in every other milk dish they wish to curdle. Physicians use it often in the medicines they make for the "bloody flux" <note>original: "menazo de sangre" — dysentery or internal bleeding</note> or for sores of the intestines <note>original: "estēnos"</note>. It has such virtue that he who carries it with him cannot be harmed by a viper. Therefore, the people of that land make vessels and small bowls <term>testudiellas: small terracotta or stone cups</term> out of it, from which those who have the illness of being unable to retain their urine eat. And the star that is in the left foot of *Fanoz*—which means "inflamed" or "burning," and is also called "The Shepherd"—has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its virtue. When it is in the ascendant, the stone shows its works more clearly.

# Concerning the stone they call Abarquirid :-

<image-desc>An illuminated initial 'D' containing a miniature of two men in medieval dress (one in a green robe, one in red) standing in a landscape with a tree.</image-desc>

The fifth degree of the sign of Taurus belongs to the stone they call *abarquirid*. It is found in the land of Africa in sulfur mines. It is lightweight <note>original: "māna," likely meaning *liviana*</note> and hard to break. Its color is a deep henna <note>original: "allēna"</note> mixed with green and a little bit of yellow.

It is flat in shape, and when one looks closely at it, the figure of a scorpion appears upon it. If they break the stone, they find the stone inside shaped in that same manner. By its nature, it is cold and dry. It possesses such a virtue that whenever any woman carries it with her, her desire for a man increases so much that she cannot be restrained <note>original: "endereçar"</note> except by very great force; any female animal that possesses it will behave in this same way. Those in India who work extensively in the art of necromancy <term>necromancy: a form of magic traditionally involving communication with the dead or the manipulation of occult forces</term> work often with this stone. It has such a power that if they give this stone, ground into a powder, to a woman to drink, her belly will swell in such a way that she appears to be pregnant. When the time for birth arrives, the swelling disappears. The necromancers make people believe through their art and knowledge that this pregnancy is created and removed by them. The bright star that is in the right side of the figure of Perseus <note>This likely refers to the star Mirfak in the constellation of Perseus</note> has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its virtue. When that star is in the ascendant <term>ascendant: the sign or degree of the zodiac rising over the eastern horizon at a specific time</term>, this stone shows its effects most clearly.

<column-break/>

# Concerning the stone that is called Racomez :-

<image-desc>An illuminated initial 'D' containing a miniature of a man in a red cap and white tunic working with a stone on the ground.</image-desc>

The sixth degree of the sign of Taurus belongs to the stone they call *racomez* in Chaldean <note>original: "caldeo"</note>. It is found in the land of Spain, and specifically in the region of Barcelona. Its color is brown, and it has blue-colored crescents <note>original: "lunnas"</note> hidden within it so that they only appear very slightly, and only when the air is very clear; otherwise, they cannot be seen. By its nature, it is cold and dry. Its property is that it flees from oil, such that when they place it near it, the stone jumps very forcefully away from the place where the oil is kept. If they grind it and mix it with any liquid, and afterward add olive oil, all the ground powder moves away to one side. By this, they know that the stone is of good quality. If they give a person one drachm <term>drachm: an ancient unit of weight, roughly 3.4 grams</term> of this ground stone, they will immediately go mad <note>original: "rrauia," implying rabies or violent madness</note>. The same will happen to any man unless he is helped in this way: give him olive oil to drink before twenty-four hours have passed. The middle star of the three that follow the two at the belt of the River <note>This refers to the constellation Eridanus, often depicted as a winding river in the sky</note> has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its virtue. When that star is in the midheaven <term>midheaven: the highest point on the celestial meridian, representing the peak of a star's path</term> or above, this stone shows its effects most clearly.

OF THE SIGN [OF TAURUS]

# Of the stone that draws out bones.

<image-desc>An illuminated initial 'E' containing a figure of a man in a blue and yellow tunic standing on a rocky shoreline with waves and mountains in the background.</image-desc>

The seventh degree of the sign of Taurus belongs to the stone that draws out bones. It is found on the coast of Sardinia; when the sea churns in its characteristic way, the waves cast these stones onto the shore.

Its color is brown, leaning slightly toward yellow, and it is light in weight. When someone carries it or takes it in their hand, it feels like a hollow object, yet its virtue <note>virtue: in medieval texts, this refers to the inherent medicinal or magical power of an object</note> is present throughout its entire being. It is hard and square-shaped when broken, and inside one finds a very white substance <note>original: "cuerpuzũ," a small body or core</note> that can be ground between the fingers like flour. Its nature is cold and dry. It possesses such a property that when it is brought near any bone, it draws it very strongly, just as other attractive stones <note>This likely refers to magnets (lodestones) which "attract" iron</note> act upon the bodies over which they have power. This stone is useful in the art of surgery for extracting bones that are broken within human bodies due to a wound or a fracture, for it draws them out very easily. To do this, a plaster is made of the stone mixed with honey and placed over the wound at the site of the break. It is also used in the art of medicine <term>physic: the medieval term for internal medicine, as opposed to surgery</term>; if three drachms <note>drachm: an ancient unit of weight, roughly 3.5 grams</note> of the white flour-like substance found inside is given in a drink to someone suffering from numbness in a limb, they are healed immediately. The star located on the right shoulder <note>original: "rochella," likely referring to the axilla or shoulder area</note> of the figure of Taurus has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its virtue. When this star is in the midheaven, the stone demonstrates its effects most clearly.

<column-break/>

# Of the stone they call Menessi.

<image-desc>An illuminated initial 'E' containing a figure of a man in a red hood and robe gesturing toward a white city or castle with several towers.</image-desc>

The eighth degree of the sign of Taurus belongs to the stone they call *menessi*. This is found in the land of Egypt near the city called Menessi <note>original: "Menessi," referring to Memphis</note>, from which it receives its name. They are small stones, and in each one there are many different colors; however, those that appear most prominently are red, yellow, and black. It is a hard stone and of strong substance; it is average in weight, being neither very light nor very heavy. By its nature it is cold and dry. The Egyptians call this stone *maridican*, which means "to torment," <note>This may be a corruption of an Arabic or Coptic word related to anesthesia or numbing</note> because it has such a virtue that when it is ground and mixed with some liquid and placed upon a human limb, it immediately numbs it <note>original: "atormenta," here used in the sense of causing a loss of sensation or "putting to sleep"</note> in such a way that the person does not feel it. It is useful in the art of medicine, working upon those areas that a physician wishes to cauterize or cut, or likewise for those in great pain; for by placing it upon those sites, it so strongly dulls the senses that afterward the patient feels nothing done to them by force, nor do they feel the pain they previously had in that place. The middle star of the three in the northern ear of the figure of Taurus has lordship over this stone, and from it the stone receives its strength and virtue. When this star is in the ascendant, the stone demonstrates its works most manifesty.

TAURUS

### Of the stone they call zumberic . xxxvii :

<image-desc>Illuminated capital 'E' containing a figure of a person in a tan habit, possibly a monk or scholar, holding a small object and looking toward the text. The background of the initial is blue with gold flourishes.</image-desc>

The ninth degree of the sign of Taurus belongs to the stone which is called *zumberic* <note>original: "zumberic" (Arabic); "esmeri" (Latin)</note> in Arabic and emery in English. This stone resembles coarse sand or clumps of clay joined together. It is composed of small grains and is heavy. It is of medium weight and hardness. Its color is a tawny brown that tends toward an olive hue. It is found in many places, but the best of all is that which is found near the Sea of Gin <note>Likely referring to the China Sea (Qin), often cited in medieval lapidaries as a source of rare minerals</note>. Its nature is cold in the second degree and dry in the third. Its property is to "eat" <note>In this context, "eat" refers to the abrasive power of the stone to grind down other materials</note> the bodies of all other stones. No matter how hard or strong they may be, all precious stones are polished with this stone, ground upon a plate of copper, lead, or wood. This craft is especially prized for making the surfaces of gems clear and beautiful. When used on those plates, it can grind away whatever is desired or even pierce the stones, for there is no stone that can resist it except for the diamond alone. The sharpness <note>original: "jdur," likely referring to the "hardness" or "edge" of the abrasive</note> that this stone applies to other stones is better and stronger when its powder is wet than when it is dry. Those who work with metal also use it in their craft because it is an excellent substance for cleaning the surfaces of metal objects and removing their grime; once they are cleaned, they receive a better color and weight. To the physician who wishes to heal another, it has the virtue that when its powder is cast into old and putrid wounds, it remedies the "bad flesh" <note>This refers to the debridement of necrotic or infected tissue</note> and heals it completely and more quickly. The southern star of the two that are in the front mouth of the square on the chest of the figure of Taurus has power and lordship over this stone, and from that star the stone receives its virtue. When this star is in the ascendant, this stone shows its effects more clearly.

<column-break/>

### Of the stone zamorat . xxxviii :

<image-desc>Illuminated capital 'E' containing a figure of a person in a blue and red robe looking upward with hands raised in prayer toward a white tower and a star above it. The background is gold and the initial itself is decorated with blue and red scrollwork.</image-desc>

The tenth degree of the sign of Taurus belongs to the stone they call *zamorat*; it is likewise called the "stone of the brothers." It is found on the shores of the sea called *alcuzana* <note>The Red Sea (Erythraean Sea)</note>, that same sea which Moses <note>original: "moysen"</note> and the children of Israel crossed. Near the city called Toatiz, on the shores of that sea, when the water churns in a storm, it casts these stones onto the beach. Its color is a deep yellow, shining like bright gold, and it dazzles the sight. It is difficult to break. Some are found large and others small, and they are always found in the shape of a chestnut. Its nature is cold and dry and very strong in these two complexions <term>complexion: the balance of the four qualities (hot, cold, moist, dry) that determines a substance's nature</term>. They prize it greatly in that land and wear it in rings and in sashes. This is because the man who carries it with him loses all desire for the pleasure of women; even if he begins the act, he cannot finish anything as long as he has the stone upon him. For this reason, the ancient sages gave it to religious men, hermits, and those who took vows to maintain chastity. Even some of the gentiles <note>non-Christians or pagans</note>, who had laws forbidding them from lying with their wives except at certain times—so as to impregnate them more readily and produce children who were more agile and strong—would carry the stone with them at all other times, except when they wished to conceive. If a man is given three drachms <note>drachm: a unit of weight, approx. 3.5 grams</note> of this stone ground into a drink, he will never again have the power to lie with a woman. Therefore, when the kings of India wished to castrate certain men so they might guard their wives, they gave them this stone to drink out of mercy, so as not to have to remove their members; it was as effective as if they had been castrated. The star in the nose of those stars in the face of the figure of Taurus has power and lordship over this stone and from it receives its strength and virtue. When that star is in the ascendant, this stone clearly demonstrates its works.

### Of the stone whose name is coral: XI

The eleventh degree of the sign of Taurus is the stone which they call coral in Latin. In Arabic, they call its root *murgan* <note>original: "murgan"</note> and its branches *becer* <note>original: "becer"</note>. This stone hardens from the water of the sea and grows like a tree; it resembles in color the stone they call sea-grass <note>likely referring to a type of seaweed or calcified marine plant</note>. It has many branches. While it is under the sea water it is soft, and as soon as they take it out into the air, it hardens. It is found in many places, but the best of all is that which is found in the Sea of England or on the island of Sardinia. It is not transparent enough for the sight to pass through it. Its color is red, and the more redness it has, the better it is. By its nature, it is cold and dry. Its property is to constrict <term>constrict</term> <note>original: "estennir," meaning to staunch or tighten tissues</note> quickly. If ground up and mixed with wine or something cold and given to drink to those who spit blood, it helps them greatly; it does the same for those who cannot pass urine. Whoever holds it with some liquid, it reduces the abscess <note>original: "postema"</note> that forms in the groin <note>original: "bago"</note>. The star that is between the one in the nose of Taurus and the other in the southern eye of this same image has power over this stone and from it receives its virtue. And when

->it is in the ascendant, this stone shows its works more clearly.<-

<column-break/>

### Of the stone they call black coral: XII

The twelfth degree of the sign of Taurus is the stone they call black coral. It has the same name in Arabic as the other. Like the other, it is soft under water and hardens when taken out into the air, but its scent is stronger than the other's. By nature it is cold and dry, but its dryness is greater than that of the other. It has all the virtues of red coral completely, and in addition, if it is worn ground up, it helps the sores of the intestines and the trembling of the heart; it is also used in medicines made for leprosy <note>original: "legra," likely a variant of "lepra"</note>. When it is burned and made into powder, it helps greatly to dry the tearing of the eyes; therefore it is good to include in eyeliners <term>eyeliners</term> <note>original: "alcoholes," from the Arabic *al-kuhl*, referring to medicinal eye salves or powders</note>. The star in the northern eye of the figure of Taurus has power over this stone and from it receives its virtue. When this star is in the ascendant, then this stone shows its works more clearly.

## Of the stone whose name is netzech

<image-desc>A large ornamental initial 'E' featuring a miniature of a scholar in a blue robe and white headgear gesturing towards a smaller figure who is excavating a rocky bank with a pickaxe.</image-desc>

The thirteenth degree of the sign of Taurus belongs to the stone they call *netzech* <note>likely from the Hebrew "Netsach," meaning victory or endurance</note>, and others call it *belmuz*. Its nature is cold in the second degree, and it reaches the fourth degree at its peak. Its color is red, but a very faint redness. Within it are subtle and very thin lines, so fine they do not appear unless one examines them closely in the sunlight. At first glance, it appears only to be of a reddish color. Those lines we mentioned are not straight, but look as if someone had painted dots who did not know how to paint well. They are clear and possess great brilliance when the sun strikes them, for they cast rays upon the ground similar to crystal. These stones are found in large and small pieces and in many shapes, but most are found in the shape of an egg.

The best of them are found on the island of *Çaramdin* <note>Serendib, the medieval Arabic name for Sri Lanka</note>, where other very noble precious stones are found. Goldsmiths use this stone frequently to make necklaces or to set it in rings. The most noble among them are found on that mountain of the aforementioned island near the monastery <note>original: "abbad," likely referring to a temple or religious site</note> called *Tarhun*. Its test is this: if they place it in running water, the water parts to the right and to the left so that it does not pass over the stone. And according to this reasoning,

<column-break/>

the ancient sages give it a property, saying that whoever carries it with them can never die in water. This is because it always provides a pocket of air <note>original: "aluna," likely meaning it creates a space or illuminates a path for breath</note> in such a way that the water recedes before the person, allowing them to breathe so they cannot drown. This is one of the noble virtues found in the mines of stones. The star that is in the southern eye of the figure of Taurus, which is called Aldebaran <note>the brightest star in the Taurus constellation</note>, has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its virtue. And when this star is in the ascendant <term>ascendant</term> <note>the degree of the zodiac rising over the eastern horizon at a specific time</note>, this stone manifests its works most clearly.

# Of the cotton stone:

<image-desc>A large illuminated initial 'D' containing a miniature scene. A seated master figure in a blue robe and white turban is gesturing toward a kneeling student dressed in red.</image-desc>

The twentieth degree of the sign of Taurus belongs to the stone they call "of cotton" <note>This refers to asbestos, which was known in the Middle Ages as "salamander’s wool" or "stone cotton" because of its fibrous, fire-resistant nature.</note>. This is cold and dry in nature. It is white in color, but translucent so that it tends toward the color of clear crystal. And 

they are found both large and small. It is light in weight, but despite all this, it is strong and hard to break; and when they do break it, they find within it a substance like cotton in texture and color. The virtue <note>In medieval science, "virtue" refers to the inherent medicinal or magical power of an object.</note> of this cotton is such that it does not burn in fire. It can be spun, and they make cloth from it just like from regular cotton; and when it becomes soiled, they put it in the fire and it comes out clean and clear as if it had been washed. The longer it stays in the fire, the whiter and more beautiful it becomes. And the physicians of that land burn this cotton and grind it into powder to put in the eyes, because it removes tearing and all the moisture within them. They are found in many sizes—some large and others small—and in many shapes. They are found in the Mountains of the Moon, there where the Nile is born, at the bottom of certain caves that are so deep that anyone who descends into them, if he stays too long, either dies or remains paralyzed. And those who are experts at taking them, as soon as they enter and reach where the stones are, they take

**I**n the twenty-fifth degree of the sign of Taurus is the stone they call **atanar**. And this creature has such a nature that specifically when the sea rises and makes great waves, and flows up the Nile and muddies the water, it then comes out and opens its mouth and swallows as much of that turbid water as it can swallow. And after it has swallowed it, it stands in the sun on the bank of the river, and with the great heat that animal has in itself, and with the other heat it receives from the sun, that water goes on curdling in its body. And when it feels that it is curdling, it enters the sea, and afterward returns to the river and comes out onto the land; and it does this so many times until it understands that the water is curdled in its body and made into stone. And when they <insert>the hares</insert> understand that they are quite hard and dry, they come out onto the land and void them; and therefore they are found on those banks of the Nile and of the sea. with various colors. And the wise men spoke of each of these in its place: and they said where they were found, and the virtues and properties they possessed. These properties we have mentioned are possessed by all five kinds of *ahaza* you have heard of.

At the twenty-second degree of the sign of Taurus: is the stone they find in the head of the hare that we spoke of. So it is that when they kill it, they remove the head and carefully open it: they find it inside in the marrow <note>original: "meollo"; referring here to the brain matter.</note> or attached to the bones. At the twenty-seventh degree of the sign of Taurus: is the stone of man. And it is counted just like this other one we spoke of among those of animals. But there is this much difference between this one and the others: that the stone of man is formed within the body, such as in the bladder or in the kidneys; whereas in other animals, it is formed in the head or in the outer members. And as the sages have explained: other animals besides man have wide passages through which the thick humors <term>humors: the bodily fluids (blood, phlegm, yellow bile, black bile) thought to govern health and temperament.</term> flow and exit with the urine. But man has narrow passages, and they cannot flow out so easily. And in this delay, when they reach that place where the heat is greatest: the fluid congeals because one humor is layered upon the other. And for this reason, when the stone is large: they find it like layers <note>original: "cortezas"; literally "barks" or "rinds," describing the laminated structure of a bladder stone.</note>, one over the other. And it is brittle <note>original: "cruda"; here meaning unrefined or easily crumbled.</note> and easily breaks apart. Of these stones, there are some that are very red in color, and others white, and others like yellow, and others like brown. It is not formed in all men in the same way, for in some it is white, and in others red...

Even here there is variety: sometimes they change into other colors according to the parts of the body where [the stones] form, or the foods <note>original: "uandas," likely a transcription error for *viandas* (foods)</note> they eat, or the humors <term>humors: the four fluids—blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile—believed to control health and temperament.</term> they have in themselves, or according to the seasons when it is gathered. And the virtue <term>virtue: the inherent medicinal or magical power of a substance.</term> it has is this: that when it is ground and sifted thoroughly, and put into the eyes of those who have the blemish called *nuf* <note>original: "nuf"; likely referring to a corneal scar or cataract</note>, it erases it. ### Of the stone they call lotarican. 35.

In the 35th degree of the sign of Taurus is the stone they call *lotarican*, which means "nature-retainer" <note>original: "retenedor de natura"; likely referring to its astringent properties that "hold back" bodily fluids.</note>. By its nature, it is cold and dry at the end of the fourth degree of each of these temperaments. Some are easily broken and they are not uniform in size, for some are large and others small. They are found in the land of Armenia in certain clay mines; when they dig there, they find

<column-break/>

this stone within them. Its color is mixed between red and yellow, and each one is faint, so that it resembles the color of the water that comes out of meat when it is salted. It is a stone that, when first taken from the mine, is very dull; however, when it is polished and prepared, it shines brightly, though not so much that the sight can pass through it <note>meaning it is opaque rather than transparent</note>. Its virtue is that if it is hung upon a man who has a flux <note>original: "menazon"; likely referring to dysentery or bleeding</note>, it causes it to stop immediately, so that while he wears it, he cannot suffer from it. And if they give the dust that comes off it when it is polished to be drunk, it does the same. If it is put in eyes that are runny with rheum <note>original: "rrema"; a watery discharge from the eyes or nose</note> or other moisture, it removes it likewise. For its power is marvelously great in retaining and shrinking <note>original: "enrugar"; literally to wrinkle, here meaning to contract tissues</note> all moist things. And the star that is at the tip of the horn that looks toward the south in the image of Taurus, and the other chain that is at the head of the figure of Orion—both of these have power over this stone, and from them it receives its force and virtue. When they are in the ascendant, this stone will demonstrate its work most completely.

# ON THE SIGN OF GEMINI

### Prologue on the degrees of the sign of Gemini

<image-desc>A large historiated initial 'M' featuring a central sun-like face with red and orange features, surrounded by intricate blue, red, and white vine scrollwork.</image-desc>

**T**he thirty natures of stones according to the thirty degrees of the sign of Taurus have been shown, and the forces they receive from the other fixed stars have been told—those which are in the figures of the other images <note>In this context, "images" refers to constellations.</note> that have a relationship and connection with this sign. But with all this, it is necessary for whoever wishes to use this work to pay heed <note>original: "jure mientes"; to pay close attention or take care</note> to the planet Venus, whose house is the sign of Taurus, and to see that she is well-received by aspect <term>aspect: the relative position of planets in astrology that determines their influence</term>, or by her placement in that location, or if the stars of that same degree are present. And let him also see that the Lord of the Face <term>Lord of the Face: the planet ruling a specific ten-degree segment (decan) of a zodiac sign</term> is in good condition at that hour and in one of its dignities <term>dignities: positions where a planet's influence is strengthened</term>. For all these things must be observed in works intended for good; and in those for evil, the contrary. But now we shall return to our intention: to speak of the thirty degrees of the sign of Gemini.

### Of the stone they call zarcán.

<image-desc>A historiated initial 'E' depicting a man in a green robe standing and holding a leafy plant, while another figure in red is kneeling and reaching toward the ground.</image-desc>

**T**he first degree of the sign of Gemini is the stone they call *zarcán* <note>original: "zarcán"; likely referring to Zircon or a similar bright mineral</note>. This is of a white color, of a clear whiteness, so that it resembles well-polished bone. It has a quarter-measure of clarity, but not so much that sight passes through it. It is light in weight and very smooth to the touch, and it is not strong or hard to break. By nature it is hot and moist. And there are many mines of it throughout the world, but the best are those from the land of Barbuna and of Espinna. And they are found on the shores of the sea and of the rivers. The vir-

<column-break/>

tue <term>virtue: the inherent medicinal or magical power of a substance</term> of this stone is such: that it greatly increases the milk of women who wear it. And it does the same for any other animal. And for this reason, the barbers make their wives wear them around their necks, according to what Alchofat <note>likely a reference to an Arabic author or a specific treatise on stones</note> says. And it also helps for this same purpose when they put it in electuaries <term>electuary: a medicinal paste made of powders mixed with honey or syrup</term> and give it to be eaten. And it is good against melancholy <note>original: "malanconia"; thought in the Middle Ages to be an excess of black bile causing sadness</note>, and it is very helpful for the abscesses that form in the eyes. And the star that is at the end of the Little Bear <note>the constellation Ursa Minor</note>—which they call the "Tailed One of Benanays"—has power and lordship over this stone, and from it the stone receives its force and virtue. And when this star is in the ascendant, this stone demonstrates its works most clearly.

### Of the stone of gold.

<image-desc>A historiated initial 'E' showing a man in a brown hooded robe standing and holding a golden disc, while another figure in a green tunic kneels and works the earth below.</image-desc>

**T**he second degree of the sign of Gemini is the stone of gold. By nature it is hot and moist: of all metals the most noble because the nobility of the sun’s virtue appears most clearly in it. It is a stone <note>The author classifies gold as a "stone" found in mines, consistent with medieval mineralogy.</note> that men love and prize greatly, and it is very heavy—more so than any other found in a mine or upon the earth—and they do not find large pieces of it, but always small grains in the sands of the sea or of the rivers. It is found in many parts of the world.

# OF GOLD

mas the best of all: is that which they find in Spain in the western part. In color it is yellow. And the more they clean it and burnish it: its yellowness increases more and it becomes clearer, yet not so much that the sight passes through it <note>meaning it remains opaque despite its clarity</note>. And if they burnish it much: it brightens so much that one can see oneself well in it as in a mirror. And it has such virtue that when they file it and give the filings with some other thing to eat or to drink to one who has tremor of the heart or weakness: it helps him. It does the same for one who has fear: by reason of melancholy <term>melancholy: in medieval medicine, an excess of "black bile" thought to cause irrational fear or sadness</term>. And likewise it heals or provides great benefit: to one who has the mange <note>original: "annoso"; likely referring to a skin disease or ringworm</note>: or to another sickness where the hair is plucked out which they call "lopina" <term>lopina: a term for alopecia or "fox-mange," a condition causing patchy hair loss</term>. And it is good likewise for making a cautery <note>original: "quema"; a medical procedure using heat to treat a wound or infection</note> with it: and this is: because it does not cause blisters and they heal from it more quickly. And the nature of the "stone" of this metal is that when they mix it with copper <note>original: "arambre"</note>: it becomes like the nature of glass and breaks. But nonetheless: it incorporates with it. And likewise if they mix it with tin: it turns black, and if with silver they mix it: its whiteness turns green, and thus it does with every metal. And therefore those who occupy themselves with alchemy, which they call the Great Work <note>original: "obra mayor"; the process of creating the Philosopher's Stone or perfecting metals</note>: must take care that they do not mistake the name of knowledge. For "alchemy" means as much as: mastery to improve things and not to worsen them. Among those who take the noble metals and mix them with the base ones, not understanding the knowledge nor the mastery, they cause the base not to be improved: the noble is ruined: and thus they commit a great error in two ways. One, that they go against the knowledge of God: and the other, that they do harm to the world. But if gold should be tainted with another base body, they should put sulfur <note>original: "suficre"</note> into the melting: and mix with it some of the stone they call marcasite <term>marcasite: a metallic mineral (iron disulfide) often used in alchemy for its sulfur content</term>, for this separates it from all other metals and cleanses it of all filth. And this is because sulfur burns all other bodies if it stays long with them: except for gold. And likewise marcasite has in itself the nature of sulfur: and for this reason they tint copper red with it in the color of gold. And it does the same to silver: if they know how to mix it well with it. But these works: are not lasting. As we were saying, the nobilities and the virtues of gold are so many: that they would be a long story, but some are manifest just as men see gold: such and reason and they hold to it more

<column-break/>

than with any other thing they can have: and furthermore all the things they wish to make noble and rich: they make from it more than from any other metal: and it serves for many things in the art of medicine <note>original: "fisica"; referring here to the study of natural properties and healing</note>: which it is not fitting to tell all in this book. And it has one property: alone: very marvelous. That if they make from it a ring: where the stone is of the same material <note>a ring made entirely of gold, including the "gem" part</note>: and they heat it and burn with it the wings of pigeons when they put them in the dovecote. They will never go from there to dwell in another place: even if their wings grow back. But some spoke against this reasoning, saying they feared more it was the carving <note>original: "tajjamiento"</note> of the figure on the ring: rather than the gold itself. For if it were in the gold: it would do it in whatever form it had. But he who composed this book: said that he holds that the virtue comes from both: because the ring could not do this being made of another metal if not of gold. And some others that have a bad color by their fixation, some of the sages who occupied themselves with the Great Work: [say] that if they take that yellow stone which is very well known to the goldsmiths <note>original: "orebzes"</note>, of which we shall speak later in this book in its place, that whoever grinds it and throws its powders over the poorly colored gold: when it is melted: it turns it to a good color: and it is one of the works of right and true alchemy: because it makes the bad good. And the star that is on the right shoulder of the figure of the Holder of the Reins <term>Holder of the Reins: the constellation Auriga (the Charioteer)</term> has power and lordship over this stone and from it receives its virtue. And for this reason, when this star is in the ascendant: this stone shows its works more clearly:—
