# OF GEMINI

### Of the stone they call batradunithaz.

<image-desc>A rectangular miniature with a blue background and white dots. A figure in a green robe stands on the left, holding a small jar and pouring a liquid onto a brown stone or object held by another figure in a reddish-brown robe. Both figures stand on a grassy ground.</image-desc>

The third degree of the sign of Gemini: is the stone they call batradunithaz, which means in Chaldean "oil swallower" <note>original: "tragador de ollio"</note>. This stone is very hot and moist: but not excessively so. Its virtues are found in many places: and although the one found in the land of Baratan is good, better is the one found in the Promised Land <note>original: "tierra de promission"; referring to the region of Palestine</note>, as it shows its virtue more clearly. And it has many open pores within it, so that it is rough on the outside: but despite this, it is heavy of body and strong and hard to break. And when they break it: it resembles a sponge inside. And they find very large ones, others of medium size: and others smaller. In color it is yellow, tending somewhat toward brown. The virtue it has is this: when they place it near oil of any kind, it seizes it as if it were alive and eats of it: according to its size and its weight. And based on this, it draws the oil from far or near: but if they leave it near the oil for a long time and the stone is of good quality: it draws more than its share <term>reason: here meaning its proportional or expected capacity</term>. And this they know by trial: weighing the oil on its side first and the stone on its own: for then they clearly see that it has drawn its full measure and more. And whoever wishes to extract the oil from this stone after it is incorporated within it: should place it in a vessel containing vinegar: and it will all come out immediately. And those who grind it and make powder of it and mix it with water: it removes every stain from cloth of whatever kind that has been stained with oil. And it does another thing: if they grind it and mix it with its weight in oil: and cook it over a gentle fire: it incorporates with it: and becomes like an ointment. And such medicine is very good for wounds: for it makes them ripen quickly and come to a head <term>venom: the original "uenino" refers to the pus or discharge that indicates a wound is healing or "ripening"</term>, and it eats away the "bad flesh" <note>necrotic or infected tissue</note> that forms in them. And it is also very helpful when it is well ground and sifted: for the sores that form in the eyes. And the two stars—one southern and the other northern—that are in the head of the Charioteer <term>the Charioteer: the constellation Auriga</term>: though the northern one is outside the head: both of these have power over this stone and from them it receives its force

<column-break/>

and its virtue. And when they are in the ascendant: this stone shows its works more clearly.

<image-desc>A circular diagram (tondo) containing a line drawing of a male figure. He is standing, holding a bow in his left hand and an arrow in his right. He wears a short tunic and a crown or headpiece decorated with stars/flowers. The circle is framed with a double-line border.</image-desc>

### Of the stone that draws flesh.

<image-desc>A small square miniature with a decorative border and blue background. Two figures are depicted: one on the left in a blue robe, seated, and one on the right in an orange tunic, standing. They appear to be in a moment of interaction, possibly an exchange or healing act.</image-desc>

The fourth degree of the sign of Gemini: is the stone they call "the flesh-drawer" <note>original: "la carne"</note>. And this is found in the sea they call Al-Aycun: which is the one the children of Israel crossed <note>likely referring to the Red Sea</note>. The color of this stone is like bruised flesh: and it is soft to the touch: and light in weight. And by its nature, it is hot and moist. And it has such virtue that when they bring it near the flesh of any living animal: it draws it toward itself: but if the animal is dead: it does not do this. And in this it differs from the other stone we mentioned, the *catriga* <term>catriga: a type of stone described previously in the text</term> of the hare: for the other sticks to flesh both living and dead: and draws it with pain and draws blood and makes a bad wound: but this stone does not do that. However, if one wears it for a long time: even if one wears it over cloth: once the body warms up: one finds the flesh directly beneath it is somewhat swollen and itchy <term>mordaça: a stinging or biting sensation</term>. This virtue was found in this stone by those who tested it: and no other. And the star that is at the end of the tail of the figure of the Hare <term>the Hare: the constellation Lepus</term> has power over this stone: and from it, it receives its force and virtue. And therefore when that star is in the ascendant: this stone shows its works more clearly.

### Of the stone they call margul in Chaldean:--

**T**he fifth degree of the sign of Gemini: is the stone they call *margul* in Chaldean. Its nature is hot and moist. And its mine is in the Mountains of the Moon where the Nile is born. It is a stone that is strong and hard to break, and heavy. And it has a color within it that is substantial, yet not so bright that it overwhelms the sight <note>original: "mas non que la pisse el uiso"</note>. And its color is like the yolk of an egg. And when it is broken, they find within it a camphor <note>original: "alcafor"</note> in the form of a moisture that sticks to the hands and smells very sweet. And if one anoints sores with this, or the blemishes <note>original: "panno"; referring to melasma or dark patches</note> that form on the face, it dissolves them and makes the skin smooth and radiant. And it even has another virtue that is very good for men: for when they are to lie with their wives, if they anoint that member with which they father children with it, it makes it grow by extending and thickening it. All these things are caused by the moisture that is inside. But the outer part, which is like limestone <note>original: "calco"</note>, if one grinds it into powder and puts it into the medicinal electuaries <note>original: "leernianos"</note> that are made to clear the passages of the liver: it is of great benefit. It causes them to open and removes the obstructions <term>opilaciones: blockages of the internal organs or "humors"</term> that form in them, and heals more quickly one who suffers from liver disease due to the closing of the passages. And when they place it in the fire: it does another very strange thing

<column-break/>

that it dissolves and flows like water: and if afterwards they take it out to cool, and then put it back into the fire: it returns to its original nature. And it does this as many times as they put it in the fire: for at the first heat it dissolves, and at the second it congeals. However, each time it is refined, such that a small amount of it is diminished. And the leading star of the two that are in the rudder, which faces North in the figure of the Ship <note>original: "naf"; referring to the constellation Argo Navis</note>, has power over this stone and from it receives its virtue. And when it is in the ascendant: this stone shows its works more clearly. ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

### Of the stone they call bezoar: it is the 2nd kind.

The thirteenth degree of the sign of Gemini is the stone of the second bezoar <note>original: "bezahar"</note>. And this is found in the land of [China?] <note>original: "an"; likely a truncated reference to "Sin" or "Sian," meaning China</note>. Its color is yellow, and for this reason they call it the yellow bezoar; and it has no obstruction <note>original: "obstanant"; meaning opacity or impurity</note> nor any other thing that hinders the color. By nature, it is hot and moist in both these two complexions <note>the medieval medical theory of the four humors/qualities</note>, but it is stronger than the other bezoar, and harder to break, because it is not composed of such subtle parts of the elements as the other. And it has a great power <note>original: "uertud"</note> that is useful against some poisons <note>original: "tossicos"</note>, such as the scorpion; for by touching it upon the wound of the one who is stung, he heals; and it does the same if they give it to him to drink. And it does another thing: to the one who carries it with him, the bite of a rabid dog or other poisoned beast does not hurt nor do him harm. And for this reason they include it among the other precious stones. And the star that is in the heel of the right foot of the Greater Dog <note>original: "can mayor"; the constellation Canis Major</note> has power over this stone and from it receives its strength and virtue. And therefore, when it is in the ascendant, this stone will show its works most clearly.

<insert>Large historiated initial E featuring a person seated in a landscape with a blue background and floral borders.</insert>The thirteenth degree of the sign of Gemini: is the stone that contains the **child** <note>original: "nino"; the name likely refers to its internal structure or a transliteration of an Arabic term</note>. # Of the stone named Quedontoz

<image-desc>A large historiated initial 'D' depicting a seated figure in a scholarly or royal robe and hat, gesturing towards a smaller standing figure. The background of the initial is gold with decorative patterns.</image-desc>

From the fifteenth degree of the sign of **Gemini** <note>original: "gemmi"</note>: is the stone that is called **Quedontoz** <note>original: "quedontoz"; likely a corruption of the Arabic *qayd al-dud*, meaning "bond or trap of worms"</note>, which means "love of worms" <note>original: "amor de guianos"; "guianos" is a scribal error for "gusanos" (worms)</note>. And the **Alans** <note>original: "alannics"; likely referring to the Alans, a nomadic Iranian people known to medieval writers</note> prize them highly, and wear them in rings; and their women put them in the necklaces they wear around their necks. And it has such virtue that if they put it in the mouth of one who has **leeches** <note>original: "sanguisuelas"</note> in the throat: it pulls them all out, just as the magnet pulls iron. And it does this same thing to one who has them in the intestines or has **worms** <note>original: "gusanos"</note>. For if they put it in the lower part <note>referring to the rectum</note>: it pulls them all out and heals the person. And whoever wears it in the belt with which he girds himself every day is safe from having **worms** <note>original: "lomvrizes"</note> inside the body. 

And the star that is in the right foot of Gemini, representing the front of the two that is in the left jaw of the **Greater Dog** <note>original: "can mayor"; referring to the constellation Canis Major</note>: and more than one of that nature have power over this stone and from them it receives its virtue. And when both are in the ascendant: this stone shows its works clearly.

# Of the stone named siphe . 12 . ——

The twelfth degree of the sign of Gemini is the stone called **siphe** <note>original: "siphe"; likely from the Arabic *shifa’*, meaning "cure" or "healing"</note>, which means **healing**. This stone is hot and moist in its nature. It is yellow in color, but within it are purple crescent shapes <note>original: "lunnas cardenas"</note> that resemble trees; in however many pieces it is broken, this figure is always found within them. Its essence is of a radiant color. They are found both large and small, but they are very light, possessing no heaviness. And its virtue is this: it heals pain of the stomach and the intestines for anyone who wears it hanging from their neck. And if they should possess it before the illness strikes, it is certain they will not suffer from it; and if someone has already fallen ill, they are healed immediately. Because such great health comes from it, they gave it this name. For this reason, it was counted as one of the most precious stones. And the star located to the south of the three that are in the head of the **Greater Dog** <note>original: "can mayor"</note>, near **Procyon** <note>original: "proer"; the star Procyon in the constellation Canis Minor</note>, rules over this stone and from it the stone receives its power and virtue. Therefore, when that star is in the ascendant, this stone demonstrates its effects most clearly.

Its virtue is to appear above the sea and hide beneath it, and to grow clear or cloudy, just as the other stones do, each according to its own planet. However, it seems to those who observe closely that this stone obeys Mercury more than other stones obey the planets they must follow. For when Mercury is alone and away from the Sun, it does not make the stone clear even if it is on land; and when it is out of the Sun's rays, even if the stone is alone and exposed, there is clarity within it. This stone is a mixture of many visible colors and possesses great brilliance and a strength that is hard to break. It is heavy and found in many shapes, but all of them are small. ### Of the stone that they call texvza

<image-desc>A historiated initial 'E' depicting a figure in a grey habit sitting on a bench and pointing toward a collection of small stones on a raised platform or table. The background is red with a white decorative pattern.</image-desc>

The seventeenth degree of the sign of Gemini is the stone they call **texvza** <note>original: "texvza"; likely a variation of a name for a Bezoar stone</note>. This is counted as one of the types of **bezoar** stones <note>original: "tezahar"; from the Arabic "bāzahr", meaning an antidote to poison</note> that resist poison. It is a noble and very precious stone, and they find it in the land of **Yemen** in mines located there. Some are large and others are small; they are strong and hard and possess a great radiance. Its color is a green that leans slightly toward yellow, which is believable because it changes just as the air does: when the air is clear, the stone is clear, and when it is murky, the stone is dark. It is agreeable and divine in its nature. And its virtue is such that if they place it near any vessel containing **poison** <note>original: "tossico"</note> of whatever nature it may be, the stone loses the clarity it possesses and becomes cloudy

<column-break/>

within, and it becomes dark like a **cloud** <note>original: "nuf"; likely "nube"</note>. For this reason, men prize it greatly, because they are protected by it from the harm of poisons. They also test it in another way: if they grind it and place its dust upon poison, it seethes like water over a fire; and the stronger the poison is, the more the stone increases in its boiling. It also has another very good virtue: if they give it ground to drink with some liquid to a person who passes blood or vomits due to an **abscess** <note>original: "postema"</note> in the veins, the bladder, or the **vessels** <note>original: "cannas"; referring to anatomical ducts or tubes</note>, they will be healed **immediately** <note>original: "ozyma"; likely a corruption of the Arabic "ayna", meaning "at once"</note>. And the star located in the mouth of the **Greater Dog** <note>original: "can mayor"; the constellation Canis Major</note>, which they call **Alahabor** <note>original: "alahabor"; the star Sirius</note>, has power and lordship over this stone, and from it the stone receives its virtue. For this reason, when this star is in the **ascendant** <note>the degree of the zodiac rising over the eastern horizon</note>, this stone shows its works most clearly.

### Of the stone that they call kologuid.

**T**he twentieth degree of the sign of **Gemini** is the stone that they call **kologuid** <note>original: "kologuid"; possibly a corruption of the Greek 'chamaileon' (chameleon) stone, known for changing colors</note>. And they find it on the shore of the land of the blacks [Sub-Saharan Africa] in the sands. And some are large and others small. It is strong and hard to break. And it has such virtue in that place where they are created that those who take them see phantoms appearing to them that they must endure. And therefore no one dares to enter that place where they are to take them, unless he is very brave and bold, and such that he believes that what he sees is not the truth, but is nothing but a **fantasy** <note>original: "antojança"; a visual hallucination or illusion</note>. This stone is of a hot and humid nature. And this property that is described does not appear in any other place except where it is born, except at night. For if the person who has it keeps it with him at night when he sleeps, he will see in dreams figures that approach him, so that by force he will have to wake up and get up from the place where he lies. But if he carries it by night, the virtue by day will make him safe from having that illness that comes from the demons. And it does yet another thing: if they put the stone called **affa fenda** in water, and they put this stone [kologuid] in that water and leave it there for a day and a night, it dissolves and turns into the nature of the water. And if afterwards they dip a comb in that water and comb their hair with it, the hair turns black from a dye that lasts a very long time. And the star that is between the ears of the **Greater Dog** <note>original: "can maior"; the constellation Canis Major</note> has power over this stone and from it receives its virtue. ## Concerning the stone they call Carnicon.

<image-desc>A circular illustration within an illuminated initial E. A man in a blue tunic and red hat holds a red object, presenting it to another person standing beside a small tree.</image-desc>

**The** twenty-first degree of the sign of Gemini belongs to the stone they call **Carnicon** <note>likely carnelian, though the descriptions of its properties here are specifically focused on its use as a sexual aid</note>. This name in the Chaldean language means the same as *assaluez* in Arabic, which in **Latin** <note>original: "latin coitidura de mugier"</note> means "intercourse with a woman."

Its nature is hot and humid. Its color is red, but a faint redness, similar to the watery fluid that leaks from meat when salt is applied to it. It is strong and hard, such that it cannot be broken except with a large hammer. If it is placed with silver [and lead], it almost fuses them together, but the stone breaks immediately and the silver takes on the color of copper. This stone is found in the **Land of Promise** <note>the Holy Land</note> in mines located atop a mountain they call Reteh in that land. The virtue of this stone is such: if a man puts it in his mouth, for as long as he keeps it there, his male member will be erect, and he may perform with a woman as many times as he wishes, for it will not lower, nor weaken, nor cause any harm. And if one grinds it with something moist and anoints that member with it, it performs its work even more powerfully. And the star located in the chest of **Canis Major** <note>the Greater Dog constellation; the star is likely Sirius or one nearby</note> has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its virtue. And when that star is in the **midheaven** <term>midheaven: the highest point the star reaches in the sky during its daily cycle</term>, the stone shows its effects most clearly.

## Concerning the stone they call Gemezt.

<image-desc>A circular illustration within an illuminated initial E. A person in red clothing stands while another figure stoops to gather stones from the earth in a rural setting.</image-desc>

**At** the twenty-second degree of the sign of Gemini is the stone they call **Gemezt** <note>possibly amethyst, though the description of it causing rather than preventing drunkenness is the reverse of traditional amethyst lore</note>. It is of a hot and humid nature in the third degree and of a yellow temperament. It is soft with open pores, light in weight, rough to the touch, dark, and without any brilliance. Its color is yellow, leaning somewhat toward red. It is found in many places, such as the Land of Promise, and from Liximen to Ana, and on the island of Santenaren, and other lands. Its virtue is such that if a man holds it in his mouth or on an empty stomach and drinks a sip of wine, he immediately becomes intoxicated by it, and it brings about all those things that a great **drunkenness** <note>original: "embriago"</note> causes <note>likely referring to nausea or loss of physical control</note>. And if they grind this stone and throw some of it into a vessel containing wine, all the virtue of the stone [enters the wine] and intoxicates just as if the stone itself were present. However, this power lasts only a short time, and the body does not remain broken or hungover as it does from other wine. And the star located in the right **knee** <note>original: "rohella"</note> of the first **Twin** <note>the star Castor in the constellation Gemini</note> has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its strength and virtue. For this reason, when that star is in the midheaven, the stone demonstrates its works most clearly.

### Concerning the stone named camyulicas.

<image-desc>A large ornamental initial 'D' containing a miniature illustration of a man in yellow and blue garments kneeling or sitting beside a brown horse. The initial is decorated with green, red, and gold filigree on a blue background.</image-desc>

**The** twenty-third degree of the sign of Gemini belongs to the stone they call **camyulicas**, which means "horse-restrainer" <note>original: "retenedor de cauallo"</note>. This stone is found on the island of **Çarantun** <note>a legendary or unidentified island often appearing in medieval lapidaries</note>. Its nature is hot and moist, but not excessively so. It is strong, hard, and light in weight, with a green color mixed with a ray of redness, appearing much like the feathers on a peacock’s neck. When they take it from the mine, it possesses no brilliance at all, but it acquires it later when polished. Its power <note>original: "uertud"</note> is such that when a horse sees it, the animal cannot bear to leave it; instead, it remains there neighing and fixating its mind upon it <note>original: "rremetcol mientes" - likely "remetiendo las mientes," meaning to focus or lose one's senses in contemplation</note> until it dies, unless the stone is hidden or removed from its presence. It also has another power: if one grinds it and gives it to a paralytic to drink, or to one suffering from the illness called **stupor** <note>a medical state of numbness or loss of sensation</note>, they are healed immediately. The star located between the shoulders of the leading twin of Gemini has power over this stone, and from that star, the stone receives its strength and virtue. When this star is in the **ascendant** <note>the point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at a specific time</note>, the stone demonstrates its works most clearly.

<image-desc>A circular diagram at the bottom of the first column depicting the constellation Gemini as two nude male figures standing side-by-side, holding hands. The figure on the left has a golden eight-pointed star (sunburst) on his chest.</image-desc>

### Concerning the stone called avecetucan.

<image-desc>A large ornamental initial 'D' containing a miniature illustration of a man with a white turban and robes holding up a golden vessel or plate. The initial is decorated with red, green, and gold scrollwork on a red patterned background.</image-desc>

**The** twenty-fourth degree of the sign of Gemini belongs to the stone they call **avecetucan**, which in the **Chaldean** language <note>an ancient Semitic language of Mesopotamia</note> means "dissolver of nature." Its nature is hot and moist, and it is firm in the way these two temperaments are joined. It is light in weight, soft, and brittle, such that it breaks very easily. Its color is green, leaning toward yellow. When it is first taken from the mine, it is radiant, but once it is handled, it loses that luster; it only recovers its clarity if it is polished again. Because frequent polishing causes it to steadily decrease in size, it is valued highly. They find it in the land of **Arabia** in the mines located there. Its name matches its power, for whoever carries it upon themselves will never lose their "output" <note>original: "rrendimentze" - referring to the body's ability to evacuate waste</note> as long as they have it. If one puts its powder or filings into a **purgative draught** <note>original: "feg" - likely a corruption of a term for a medicinal drink</note>, it performs the same function, as it purges the humors. If they give a **drachm's weight** <note>a medieval unit of weight, roughly 3.5 grams</note> of it to drink, it draws out each of the humors one by one: first the **phlegm**, then the **melancholy** <note>black bile</note>, then the **choler** <note>yellow bile</note>, and finally the blood from abscesses. If, while drawing out these humors, it causes a **flux** <note>original: "menazon" - diarrhea or excessive bowel movements</note>, the patient will not heal quickly except with the stone we have previously mentioned called **lenuican**; for what this stone dissolves, the other retains, and what the other retains, this one dissolves. Thus, the last stone given to drink overcomes the effect of the previous one; therefore, if this stone causes a flux in a sick person while they hold it, giving them the other stone to drink will heal them. If this stone is ground in the juice of the herb called **asafoetida** <note>a pungent plant resin used in medieval medicine</note>, it loses its power; but if it is then placed in **sheep's blood**, it recovers it. The star in the head of the leading twin of Gemini and the star on the left side of the trailing twin are both of the same nature; they have power and lordship over this stone, and from them, it receives its strength and virtue. For this reason, when they are in **mid-heaven** <note>the highest point in the sky reached by a celestial body</note>, this stone shows its works most clearly.

### Concerning the stone that draws out fat. :7

<image-desc>A decorative square initial 'E' containing a miniature painting of two men in a rocky landscape; one figure appears to be working the stone with a hand tool. The frame is surrounded by green foliate scrolls.</image-desc>

**In** the 30th <note>While the transcription reads "xxx" (30th), in the sequential order of the Lapidary this stone typically corresponds to the 25th degree of Gemini</note> degree of the sign of Gemini: is the stone called **seno** <note>original: "seno," likely a variant of "cenon"</note>. This stone is very white in color, though some specimens tend toward gray. It is light in weight and has open pores. By its nature, it is hot and moist. It is found in the mines located at the edge of Spain, toward the West. Its power <note>original: "uertud"</note> is such that if one places it with a thousand weights of fat <note>original: "seuo" - tallow or suet</note> of its own size, it consumes forty of them; it moves the fat and makes it boil as if it were placed over a fire, and it consumes it according to the amount of time it is left there. If they weigh the stone afterward, they find that it weighs twice what it weighed before. If the fat is later extracted from it, it returns to its original weight; by this, one knows that it draws the weight into itself. Furthermore, it does another thing: if one holds it in the hand or places it upon the flesh, those who watch will find that place as if it were greased, because the stone draws the fatness found within the flesh through the pores in such a way that the person feels that which he is lacking. And if one mixes the fat with wax or another substance and places the stone therein, it dissolves the fat by making it boil, but the wax does not dissolve. And if they give some of this stone

<column-break/>

ground up to a man so that he might have strength in his service <note>this may refer to physical labor or, given the context of medieval lapidaries, sexual potency</note>, so much fat would leave him that he might even die from a flux <note>original: "menazon" - a term for a discharge or dysentery</note> unless they aid him with some remedy, for this stone draws out all the grease. And the star located in the right shoulder of the leading twin of Gemini has power over this stone and from it, the stone receives its strength and virtue. When that star is in mid-heaven, this stone manifests its works most clearly.

### Concerning the stone that is the tooth of the sea crab.

<image-desc>A decorative square initial 'E' containing a miniature painting of a seated figure in a blue robe and white cap, possibly a scholar or lapidary, examining an object. The frame is surrounded by red and green foliate scrolls.</image-desc>

**In** the 26th degree of the sign of Gemini: is the stone that is the tooth of the sea crab, and it is counted as one of those stones originating from animals. By its nature, it is hot and moist. Its color is exactly like that of a crab's shell. Its power is such that if one grinds it and applies the resulting powder to the eyes, it strengthens the sight, heals "the itch" <note>original: "sarna" - likely referring to blepharitis or scabies of the eyelids</note>, and removes the itching sensation within them. For this reason, when both of these stars are in the ascendant, this stone manifests its works most clearly.

### Concerning the stone called batorita. .2.

<image-desc>An illuminated initial 'E' containing a scene of two men. A standing man in grey-blue robes and a cap leans forward to hand a small object to a man in a red robe who is seated on the ground. The background of the initial is gold and blue with white filigree.</image-desc>

**In** the 27th degree of the sign of Gemini: is the stone they call **batorita** <note>This name likely derives from the Greek *batrachites* (frog-stone), though the text provides a different etymology.</note>. This name means "tail like a beaver of reeds" in the Chaldean language <note>The "Chaldean" language in medieval texts often refers to Aramaic or Syriac, though etymologies were frequently imaginative.</note>. By its nature, it is hot and moist. It is found in the land of Ethiopia, within the gold mines. Its color is green like an emerald, but there is this distinction between them: the emerald shines in such a way that the sight passes through it, but this stone does not. However, once it is polished, rays emerge from it like a mirror, which then turn back into itself. There is also another distinction: the emerald is very heavy and hard to break, while this stone is very light and breaks easily. Those who wish to commit evil and fraud rub it with oil <note>original: "vntenla," to smear or grease</note> to use in place of an emerald for those who do not recognize it. Its power <note>original: "uertud"</note> is such that if one carries it before turning gray, it prevents gray hairs <note>original: "canas"</note> from appearing until a very long time has passed. And if they grind it and boil it <note>original: "fizieren estudiar," likely meaning to decoct or steep in this context</note> and soak a comb in the water that comes from it and comb the head with it, it prevents more gray hairs from growing and dyes those that have already grown in a way that lasts for a very long time. This water has another power: if they give it to a man to drink who has pain anywhere in his belly, he is healed immediately. In this matter, it has

<column-break/>

as much power as in the treatment mentioned; furthermore, if it is seen <note>The text here is slightly ambiguous, possibly referring to the stone's appearance or its exposure to light</note>, it is of a cold nature. If they give its powder to drink, diluted with some liquid, it does the same thing, though not as effectively as the water. The two stars—the one at the end of the head of Gemini <note>likely Pollux</note> and the other on the shoulder of this same image—have power over this stone, and from them it receives its strength and virtue. When both of these stars are in the ascendant, this stone demonstrates its effects most clearly.

<image-desc>A circular diagram representing the zodiac sign Gemini. Inside the circle, two nude male figures stand side-by-side. One figure has a six-pointed star on his forehead, and the other has a star on his left shoulder.</image-desc>

### Concerning the liver stone. .7.

<image-desc>An illuminated initial 'E' containing a scene of a man in long red robes holding a large, red, organ-shaped object (the liver stone). To his left is a smaller figure behind a low white table or block. The background of the initial is blue with a white circular motif and the number '8' appears in the right margin of the box.</image-desc>

**In** the 28th degree of the sign of Gemini: is the **liver stone** <note>original: "piedra del higado," often known as hematite or a variety of jasper</note>. This stone is of a reddish color that leans slightly toward black. It resembles a liver in both color and shape, for on one side it is round and on the other it is as if sliced; it has no clarity at all. It is strong, hard to break, and heavy. When it is broken, water comes out of it the same color as the stone itself. By its nature, it is hot and moist. It is found in mines in the lands of Egypt, in very desolate places called **Leruntar** <note>This may refer to a specific desert region or a corruption of a Greek or Arabic place name</note>. This is a land where there are many lions and other fierce beasts. Its power is such that if one hangs it over the liver of a sick person, they are healed; and if they drink the water that comes from the stone, it does the same and cures them.

much so. By its nature, it is hot and moist. ### Of the stone they call "pine-nutted" ateliemeh:

# Of the stone they call green atehenich.

<image-desc>A historiated initial 'E' contains a miniature of two figures: an older man in a tunic holding a staff or tool, and a smaller figure who appears to be working or kneeling. The background is blue with white dots, framed by red and blue decorative patterns.</image-desc>

The third degree of the sign of Cancer <note>original: "cancro"</note> belongs to the stone they call green **atehenich** <term>Atehenich: Likely derived from the Arabic "al-dahnaj," referring to malachite or similar green copper-based stones</term>. This is the third variety of these stones. It shares a common nature with all the others in being cold and moist <note>According to the medieval theory of the four humors, things that were "cold and moist" were often used to counter "hot and dry" illnesses</note>. In color, it resembles the **verdigris** <term>Verdigris: A green pigment (uerdet) traditionally made by exposing copper to acetic acid, like vinegar</term> with which artists paint, and it is like it in another way: if it is ground with linseed oil, it produces a finer and clearer color than verdigris itself. Furthermore, physicians put it into plasters because it has the property of taking away the pain of "hot" swellings <note>original: "postemas calientes," referring to inflamed abscesses or tumors</note> and their redness, especially the swelling they call **erysipelas** <note>original: "alhumbre," from the Arabic "al-humrah," a bacterial skin infection known for its bright red rash</note>. It does even more: if they grind it and mix it with water and rub it on **scald-head** <note>original: "tiña," a fungal infection of the scalp or skin</note>, it heals it in one or two applications. The star located in the hind foot on the northern side of the figure of Cancer has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its virtue. When this star is in the ascendant <note>The point of the zodiac rising over the eastern horizon at a specific moment</note>, this stone manifests its works most clearly.

# Of the stone named atehenich which is painted.

<image-desc>A historiated initial 'E' contains a miniature of a seated figure in long robes gesturing toward a standing youth. The scene is set against a blue background with white scrollwork, within a decorative red frame.</image-desc>

The fourth degree of the sign of Cancer belongs to the stone of the painted **atehenich**. It is called this because so many colors and patterns appear in it in so many ways that it seems to one who does not know it that it was painted by hand. By its nature, it is cold and moist like the others, but it differs in this: it is in itself a very powerful **poison** <term>Tossico: A deadly toxic substance</term>. For if someone is given two **drachms** <note>A unit of weight roughly equal to 3.5 grams</note> or more of it to drink, it ruptures the intestines and the stomach, and it immediately kills whoever drinks it. There is no other remedy for it except the **bezoar** stone <term>Bezoar: A mass trapped in the gastrointestinal system of animals, highly prized in the Middle Ages as a universal antidote to poison</term>, which works against all mortal toxins. However, if one keeps this stone of atehenich with them, it helps against the sadness that comes from the humor of **melancholy** <note>The "black bile" which, in excess, was thought to cause depression and gloom</note>. The northern star of the two that are in the **spar** <note>original: "uiga," referring to a structural beam or yardarm of a ship</note> at the turned-back end of the figure of the **Ship** <note>Argo Navis, a large ancient constellation representing the ship of Jason and the Argonauts</note> has power and lordship over this stone, and from it the stone receives its strength and virtue. Therefore, when that star is in the ascendant, this stone manifests its works most clearly.

The fifth degree of the sign of Cancer <note>original: "cancro"</note> is the three-colored stone of **atchehanch** <term>Atchehanch: A variation of "atehenich," likely a type of malachite or jasper</term>. It is the fifth variety of this stone and the most valuable of them all. By its nature, it is moderately cold and dry. It is always found in three colors: green and white <note>Though the text mentions three colors, it only names green and white; the third may be a mixture of the two or a variation in shade</note>. If one places it for three days and three nights in enough **aged wine** <note>original: "uino anieio"</note> to cover it, it dissolves completely and mixes with the liquid. If one then mixes that wine with **henna** <term>Alhenna: A dye prepared from the plant Lawsonia inermis, traditionally used for hair and skin</term> and washes the hair with it, the hair turns a deep black dye that never fades unless new hair grows in. In this same way, it dyes any part of the human body upon which it is placed. The northern star of the two that form the front line of the rectangle in the body of the figure of **Ursa Minor** <note>original: "ossa menor," the Little Bear constellation</note> has power over this stone, and from it, the stone receives its strength and virtue. When this star is at its **ascendant** <note>The point of the zodiac that is rising on the eastern horizon</note>, the stone shows its works most clearly.

<image-desc>A drawing of a bear, likely representing the constellation Ursa Minor (the Little Bear). A prominent star is drawn on its side. The bear is enclosed in a square frame within a circular border.</image-desc>

### Of the stone that attracts silver

<image-desc>A rectangular illumination showing two figures. One figure on the right appears to be handing or showing something (possibly a stone) to another figure on the left. They are framed within a circular border with decorative corners similar to the first illumination.</image-desc>

The sixth degree of the sign of Cancer is the stone that attracts silver. It is found in the West, in the rightmost part where the sun sets. By its nature, it is cold and moist; its color is white, tending somewhat toward gray. It is white both inside and out. When a person takes it and bites it between their teeth, it feels soft. It is quite heavy and "alive" <note>original: "uiua," suggesting it has an active, potent quality</note>, though it has no clarity or transparency in it. It possesses such virtue that whoever carries it set in gold or brass will be safe from the disease called **palsy** <term>Perlesya: A medieval term for paralysis or tremors, such as those caused by a stroke or Parkinson's disease</term>. Its specific property is to attract silver, just as other attracting stones called **magnets** <term>Magnetes: Lodestones or magnetic minerals</term> attract the bodies that are suited to them; however, this stone attracts more powerfully than any of the others, for its pull is of great strength. Thus, even if the silver is attached to something, the stone pulls ten times its own weight, for its attraction is ten times its own quantity. This stone is very soft: when pressed between the teeth, it sounds like **tin** <note>original: "estanno"</note>, though it contains no mixture of it. When it is burned, it turns into lime and retains the heat of the fire, like other magnets. The two stars in the right knee of the leg of **Ursa Major** <note>original: "ossa mayor," the Great Bear constellation</note> and the other in the hock of the same figure have power over this stone and from them it receives its strength and virtue. Therefore, when these are at the ascendant, the stone shows its works most manifest.

## Of the stone that attracts lead ~~~~~~

**The** seventh degree of the sign of Cancer belongs to the stone that attracts lead. This is found in the land of the West. It is ugly to look upon, each piece being white in color; these stones attract lead, yet the stone is not as heavy as the metal itself. It has the nature to attract it in a <unclear>certain</unclear> quantity, though not as much as any of the other <term>magnets</term> <note>original: "miante," a medieval variant for magnet or lodestone</note> do. By its nature, it is cold and moist, and it has a very foul odor, for it smells like <term>asafoetida</term> <note>Asafoetida: A pungent plant resin known for its strong, sulfurous, and often unpleasant smell, used historically in medicine and cooking</note>. However, people make use of it just as they do with other magnets; for if it is burned, it traps the fire within itself and turns into a substance like lime. Those who labor in <term>alchemy</term> <note>Alquimia: The medieval practice of transforming matter, particularly the attempt to turn base metals into gold</note> include it in their works. For if, after it is well burned, they take one part of it by weight and twelve parts of <term>quicksilver</term> <note>original: "argant uiuo," meaning mercury</note>, and place them in the fire and blow upon them as goldsmiths do, the quicksilver hardens in such a way that it can withstand the hammer and the fire. The bright star in the stern of the **Ship** <term>Naf: From the Arabic 'al-safina', referring to the constellation Argo Navis</term> <note>original: "naf"</note> has power over this stone, and from it, the stone receives its strength and virtue. For this reason, when that star is in the ascendant, this stone demonstrates its effects most clearly.

## Of the stone called Solonica ~~~~~~

**The** eighth degree of the sign of Cancer belongs to the stone they call **Solonica**. This is found on the bank of a river atop a mountain named **Sollorac**, from which it receives its name. By nature, it is cold and moist, and its color is white like crystal. It is not clear when it is first taken from the mine, but if it is later polished, it becomes somewhat transparent. it is light in weight and easy to break; they cut it with iron tools and make vessels, bowls, and other things from it. However beautiful it may be to look upon, its power is very harmful. For if a man is given a drink containing its shavings or its dust, he loses his mind and remains as if foolish and tormented until he is restored by something very hot that has the power to take away the coldness and the harm caused by the chill of this stone. There is another use for it that is beneficial: if they grind it and mix its <gloss>powders</gloss> with oil of roses and rub the head of one suffering from a great fever, the severe fevers are reduced and the person is healed. The northern star of the three front stars that form the rectangle in the body of the **Crab** <term>Nuf: A term likely referring to the shell or main body of the constellation</term> <note>original: "nuf dela figura del cangreio"</note> has power over this stone, and from it, the stone receives its virtue. And when that star is in the ascendant, this stone shows its effects most clearly. :-

# Of the stone that appears in the sea when the moon sets
<image-desc>A circular illustration containing a red crab with six legs and two pincers, set against a plain background.</image-desc>

<image-desc>A historiated initial 'E' depicting a seated king or noble on the left wearing a crown and a green robe, observing two figures in a body of water on the right. One figure is submerged up to the chest, while the other appears to be lying in or floating on the water.</image-desc>

**The** ninth degree of the <term>sign of Cancer</term> <note>The zodiac sign associated with the crab, ruling midsummer</note> belongs to the stone that appears in the sea when the moon sets and hides when the moon shows itself. This is found in the sea among rocks, in the same places where other stones are found that clearly manifest the <term>virtue</term> <note>Virtue: In medieval science, this refers to the inherent power or magical/medicinal property of an object</note> of the planets. By its nature, it is cold and moist, light in weight, and very black in color. And when the moon shows itself, the stone recedes and goes to the bottom; and when the moon sets, it rises up and floats upon the water. And once it is taken from that place, it darkens when the moon is above the earth and brightens when it is below the earth; it always behaves in this way. It is a great marvel of its making that, while being as black as can be, one's sight passes through it just as it does through crystal. It has a very marvelous and strange virtue: he who wears it hanging between both eyes can see as well by night as by day, without a candle or any other light. The star that is on the southern side of the two in the front of the <term>quadrangle</term> <note>Referring to the central box-like shape in the constellation of Cancer</note> in the body of our figure of Cancer, and the other star in the front horn <note>original: "cuerno," likely referring to the pincer</note> of this same figure, both have power over this stone and from them it draws its virtue. When they are in the <term>ascendant</term> <note>The sign or planet rising on the eastern horizon</note>, this stone shows its works more clearly.

# Of the stone they call African
<image-desc>A circular illustration containing a light orange or yellow crab with six legs and two pincers, set against a plain background.</image-desc>

<image-desc>A historiated initial 'E' depicting two men engaged in stonework. The man on the left, dressed in green, holds a mallet, while the man on the right, kneeling or sitting, uses a tool to work on a block of stone.</image-desc>

**The** tenth degree of the sign of Cancer belongs to the stone they call African. It has this name because it is found in the land of Africa on the banks of a river that descends from a mountain and runs through all that land. Some are very large and others small. Its color is that of yellow <term>orpiment</term> <note>original: "azarnech," a yellow arsenic sulfide mineral used as a pigment</note>; it is not very shiny but rather dark. It is strong and hard to break. By its nature, it is cold and moist. When it is broken, one finds inside a <term>core</term> <note>original: "cieruo," literally 'deer,' but here describing an internal inclusion or nucleus</note> that resembles an egg yolk in color, in feel, and in all its qualities. If they take this and rub <term>hemorrhoids</term> <note>original: "amorroydas"</note> with it, they heal very quickly. And if they put some of it into a <term>clyster</term> <note>An enema or medicinal liquid injected into the body</note> prepared for a man who is bleeding from broken veins, he is cured. And if they grind the stone—which is hard so that it does not crumble away—and mix it with the things used for writing or painting, it brightens them and gives them a good color; however, it only does this for yellow, green, or red, for it spoils all other colors if mixed with them. The northern star of the two in the chest of <term>Ursa Major</term> <note>original: "ossa mayor," the Great Bear constellation</note> has power over this stone, and from it the stone draws its strength and virtue. Therefore, whenever that star is in the ascendant, this stone shows its works more clearly.

### Of the stone named Tarmicaz.

<image-desc>Miniature within an illuminated initial 'E' showing two figures; one is seated on a bench holding a small red stone while gesturing toward a standing figure.</image-desc>

**The** eleventh degree of the <term>sign of Cancer</term> <note>The zodiac sign ruling midsummer, associated with water and the Moon</note> belongs to the stone they call Tarmicaz. This stone has a streaked color, mixed in such a way that it appears green when in small pieces. Even the largest of these stones weighs no more than half a <term>drachma</term> <note>A small unit of weight, roughly 3.5 grams</note>. These stones are consistent in their size and are always found in a three-cornered <note>triangular</note> shape. It is very light in weight in all its parts. By nature, it is cold and moist, and it is found in the sea called <term>Uermea</term> <note>The Red Sea (original: "mar uermea")</note>, where the children of Israel crossed, growing inside certain <term>shells</term> <note>original: "caxas", referring to the shells of mollusks</note>. From these stones, <term>pearls</term> <note>original: "fonzellas", likely referring to small pearl-like or scale-like growths</note> are made, resembling the scales found on a fish. The larger the shell, the larger the stone that grows within it, although it never exceeds its natural size limit. Its <term>virtue</term> <note>The inherent magical or medicinal power of the stone</note> is such that if it is placed in "physician's water"—called *azaitatona* in Arabic <note>likely a mineral oil or a specific distilled solution</note>—it softens like dough or wax while it is warm. If a woman drinks a mixture made of this softened stone, she will never become pregnant unless she already was. This same effect occurs in any female animal that drinks it. The northern star of the "foundations" in the quadrangle of the heavens, called <term>Lumetm</term> <note>An Arabic-derived name for a specific star in medieval astronomy</note>, has power over this stone and provides it with its virtue. When this star is in the <term>ascendant</term> <note>The point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon</note>, the stone shows its effects most strongly.

### Of the stone called Argent or Silver

<image-desc>Miniature within an illuminated initial 'E' showing a man in a blue tunic striking a rock face with a hammer and chisel, while a second figure observes.</image-desc>

**The** twelfth degree of the sign of Cancer belongs to the stone that everyone commonly calls <term>argent</term> <note>Silver (from the Latin "argentum")</note> or silver. The Moors perform various castings with this stone, just as they do with other stones that are metals. It holds its shape under hammering more firmly than iron or copper, but not as firmly as gold. Because these metallic stones share a nature in their whiteness and strength, they "love" one another and merge when mixed together. Some among them can even purify others, just as silver is often purified by the scent of the smoke that comes from lead; <term>quicksilver</term> <note>Mercury (original: "argent uiuo")</note> does this same thing. Salt is very good for this stone, for it washes it and makes it bright because of the whiteness and beauty within it. This stone is cold and moist by nature. It is lighter than gold, but heavier than iron or copper. If its filings are used with medicines for the "flame" <note>likely referring to inflammation or a specific feverish condition</note> called *vitreum menere* <note>A Latin pharmaceutical term for a glass-like mineral preparation</note>, it is beneficial. It is also useful for all diseases caused by <term>phlegm</term> <note>One of the four humors of medieval medicine, thought to cause sluggishness or respiratory issues</note>. If it is placed in a vessel and buried underground in such a way that nothing touches it, it will last for a very long time.

# Of the stone they call cazuura. 222

The fourteenth degree of the sign of Cancer belongs to the stone they call <term>cazuura</term> <note>Likely a type of lead ore or galena, though the name is derived from Arabic</note>. It is found in **Spain** in the western part near the riverbanks more than in any other place. When they take it from its earth, it resembles lead in color and weight, but it is softer than lead, for it breaks when pressed between the fingers. By its nature, it is cold and moist. However, when it is burned, it loses that moisture and the softness it had before, and it becomes hard like other stones that are difficult to break. And if, after it has been burned, they <term>quench</term> <note>original: "amataten"; to cool a hot mineral in liquid to change its properties</note> it many times in wine—putting it in and taking it out—it becomes light in weight and its luster increases somewhat. And that wine in which it is quenched acquires a very evil quality; if they give it to someone to drink, it closes the urinary tracts and does not let the urine pass, so that it kills the one who drinks it unless they quickly provide <term>theriac</term> <note>a famous ancient "universal" antidote</note> or the stone they call **texaruz**. If this burned stone is made into powder and placed in the nostrils of one who is bleeding, it stops the blood from flowing; it does the same for wounds or sores. And if they grind it without burning it and mix it with wax and rose oil <note>original: "rrosafina"</note> and make a plaster of it, it is very good for maturing wounds, growing new flesh in them, and healing them. And the middle star of the three that are in the front of the **Naf** <note>The Ship, referring to the constellation Argo Navis</note> has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its strength and **virtue**. And when that star is in the ascendant, this stone shows its effects most clearly.

# Of the stone that flees from honey.

<image-desc>A large decorative initial 'E' containing a miniature painting of two men. One man, wearing a blue robe, holds up two dark blue round stones while the other man looks on.</image-desc>

The fifteenth degree of the sign of Cancer belongs to the stone that flees from honey. This stone is cold and moist by nature. It is found on the island called **Mantiat**, which is in the **Red Sea** where the children of Israel passed. Though this island is uninhabited, ships pass near it in their coming and going. There are many kinds of stones there, some of which we will name in this book, each in its proper place as is fitting. But this one of which we speak is hard and heavy, and of a deep violet-blue color like <term>azure</term>, except that it tends somewhat toward green. They find some that are large and others that are small. Its property is such that it hates honey; so much so that when they place honey near it, the stone jumps and flees as much as it can. There is another test: if they grind this stone and mix it with water, it incorporates with the water in such a way that they cannot be separated, unless one takes honey and mixes it in; for then the stone casts out the water and separates from it. This stone is very beautiful to the sight; if a man is not a good judge of stones, he might think it is one of those very clear **sapphires** through which the sight does not pass <note>Meaning an opaque or very deep-colored sapphire</note>. And it has a very evil quality: he who carries it with him loses his <unclear>fuerças</unclear> <note>Likely "strength" or "potency"</note>.

### Of the stone they call scopetina of the moon.

<image-desc>A rectangular miniature framed by decorative floral borders, showing a man in a brown robe standing and gesturing toward a younger man who is bowing or kneeling. The background is gold leaf.</image-desc>

The seventeenth degree of the sign of Cancer belongs to the stone they call <term>scopetina de la luna</term> <note>Likely selenite or a variety of gypsum, which has a pearly luster and was traditionally associated with the moon</note>. And it has this name because they do not find it except at night, and specifically when the moon is full. By its nature it is cold and moist, white in color, and very light in weight; it takes into itself all the colors that are placed near it. It is found in the lands of the West more than in any other part, in some caves located in a wilderness, and they never find them except at night when the moon is full. Because of this, the people of that land have said that the moon creates it at that time and season, and therefore they give it the name we have already mentioned. However, others call it <term>moon foam</term> <note>original: "espuma dela luna"</note>. And those of Chaldea call it <term>cedahiqueuat</term>, which means the same thing. And the virtue of this stone is such that if they give

<column-break/>

its powder in a drink to one who is possessed by a <term>demon</term> <note>In the medieval context, this usually refers to epilepsy, fits, or mental illness</note>, they are healed immediately. **T**he 17th degree <note>The manuscript repeats the seventeenth degree here, though the previous page also described a stone for the seventeenth; this may be a scribe's error or a variation in the source material</note> of the sign of Cancer belongs to the <term>milk stone</term> <note>original: "lechar"; likely galactite, a mineral such as smithsonite or a type of calcium carbonate that produces a milky runoff when wet or crushed</note>. ## Of the stone named indega

### Of the stone they call baciz. 20th

The 20th degree of the sign of <term>Cancer</term> <note>original: "cancro"</note> is the stone they call <term>baciz</term>. This is found on the island of <term>Cathay</term> <note>original: "catayoz"; likely referring to China or the Far East</note> in a river that passes through there called the Sea, from which the stone takes its name. Its shape is quadrangular, but its four corners are triangular and meet at a single point, narrowing downward like the shape of a pinecone. Its color is light yellow, bordering on white. It is so brilliant that sight passes through it. It aligns with the red <term>bloodstone</term> <note>original: "sangonera uermeia"; likely hematite or heliotrope, known for its deep red spots or color</note>; they have a nature such that when they are placed together, each of them is harmed, but this stone receives the greater damage because it loses more of its luster than the other. Indeed, if it stays with it for long, it breaks and is ruined; the damage the other stone receives will be told later in the place where the book speaks of it. And so its virtue is that whoever holds it in their mouth loses the thirst they have; they feel no thirst as long as they hold it there. For this reason, it is good for the sick who have very high fevers. And if they grind this stone and give it to be drunk, its virtue is even more powerful in this act. ### Of the stone that appears in the sea when the moon rises

The 21st degree of the sign of Cancer is the stone that appears in the sea when the moon rises and <term>blooms</term> <note>original: "aflo rece"; likely meaning it surfaces or becomes visible</note> when the moon sets. Its shape is very round and large of body. By its nature it is cold and moist. #### Of the stone that has the name plomenna:—

## Of the Stone of the Tortoise.
<note>The heading reads "galapago" (tortoise), but the text describes the "Stone of the Rooster," known in Latin as Alectoria.</note>

The 28th degree of the sign of **Cancer** <note>original: "cancro"</note> is the **Stone of the Rooster**. It is one of those stones that comes from animals. It is found in this way: they watch for the first egg that a hen lays, and if they find it is large, they must leave it for eight months <note>This likely refers to letting the bird hatch and grow</note> and then kill it. Once it is dead, they will find in its belly a white stone that resembles crystal in color; it is as large as a bean, or a little larger.

By its nature, it is cold and moist. It has such virtue that if they give it ground up in a drink to a man when he has a "foul grain" <note>original: "grano feo"; likely a term for a pustule, cyst, or perhaps a specific type of fever</note>, it takes it away. If they carry it before it is ground and give that wash-water <note>Water in which the stone has been rinsed</note> to drink, his spirit will be gladdened, and the sadness will be removed from his sight if he has any; the stone does the same for the one who simply carries it with him. And if children carry it, they lose that fear they are accustomed to having when they are small.

And the star following the two that are at the root of the neck of the figure of **Draco**, which is the **Dragon** <note>original: "serpient"</note>, has power over this stone, and from it the stone receives

<column-break/>

its strength and virtue. And when that star is in the midheaven: this stone shows its works more clearly.—

## Of the Stone of Magnesia.
<note>original: "almagreia"; the text identifies it as Magnesia.</note>

The 29th degree of the sign of **Cancer** is the stone they call **magnesia**; there are three kinds of it. One is brown in color, another black, and the third green. It is called in Greek by the general name <term>amart dinuza</term> <note>original: "amart dinuza"; a medieval corruption of a Greek term, possibly relating to hematite or magnetic stones</note>. In these three kinds, there is no difference in nature nor in virtue, but only in the color. They are found in many places.

By nature, it is cold and moist. Its virtue is such that it causes glass—which is "spirited" <note>original: "espiritado"; referring to the airy, powdered state of silica sand before melting</note> in the likeness of sand—to join together; this is because it has a quantity of lead mixed into it. The wise men erred regarding this stone, for they believed it was the one that attracted iron and released that which was nailed <note>The magnet or lodestone</note>, because they saw it "nail" the body of the **aurochs** <note>original: "uro"; an extinct species of wild cattle. This may refer to a specific alchemical or medicinal process</note>. Likewise, this stone moved [missing word] in the powders they make to wash their flesh.

And the star following the three that are on the tiller of the stern of the **Ship** <note>The constellation Argo Navis</note> has power over this stone, and from it the stone brings its strength and virtue. And when it is in the midheaven: this stone shows its works more completely.—

### Of the Stone of Quicksilver. 25th [degree].

The 25th degree of the sign of **Cancer** <note>original: "cancro"</note> is the **Stone of Quicksilver** <note>original: "argent uiuo"; we know this today as mercury</note>. And its mine is in the land they call *Aduzegen*, or in that of *Sennert*, or in Spain. It is found both loose <note>as liquid mercury</note> and in solid stones <note>cinnabar ore</note> by burning that stone; once it is released, it is used in many works. That which is called "stone" is the ore they extract from the mine before it is burned. By nature, it is cold and moist; it is like silver that has "fallen ill." It also has a foul odor and causes trembling.

By its nature, it kills lice. The "earth" or residue of the stone after it is burned kills mice if it is mixed into their food. For the man who is reached by its smoke <note>mercury vapors</note>, it makes him paralyzed, causes his limbs to tremble, and makes him lose his hearing, along with many other diseases. From the place reached by its smoke, snakes and other reptiles flee, and those that remain die. When mixed with **marcasite** <note>original: "marcassita"; iron pyrite</note> and prepared with quicksilver as is appropriate, it will whiten and refine iron according to the work being done. And if they burn the quicksilver and give it to drink to one who is rabid <note>original: "rrabico"; suffering from rabies</note>, he is healed. However, quicksilver by itself, without being burned, kills whoever drinks it. And the star that follows the two that are in the

<column-break/>

left "cobbler’s foot" <note>A medieval name for a specific star in the constellation</note> of the **Great Bear** <note>original: "ossa mayor"</note> has power over this stone, and from it, the stone receives its strength and virtue. And when it is in the midheaven: this stone shows its works most clearly.—

### Of the Stone Called Gaacgaleritz.

The 26th degree of the sign of **Cancer** is the stone they call **gaacgaleritz**. This is found in the land named *Carce Daquia*, in the waters that descend from a very high mountain there; some of these stones are large and others small. It is white in color, somewhat yellowish on the surface, and it is shiny and heavy. When it is broken, the inside is found to be very white; if the yellow layer on the surface is scraped away, the stone remains white.

They make vessels and small tablets <note>original: "estudiolas"; possibly writing tablets or small decorative boxes</note> from it. Its virtue is such that he who carries it with him does not fall in love; eating from or looking at vessels made of it does the same <note>The stone was believed to act as an "anti-aphrodisiac"</note>. And the leading star of the two that are at the end of the mast of the **Ship** <note>original: "naue"; the constellation Argo Navis</note> has power over this stone, and from it, the stone receives its strength and virtue. And when it is in the midheaven: this stone shows its works most clearly.—

# OF THE SIGN [CANCER]

<note>The image at the top of the page depicts the constellation Argo Navis, the celestial ship. In medieval astrology, specific stars within this constellation were believed to govern the powers of the minerals described below.</note>

->**Of the stone named onna**<-

The 24th degree of the sign of **Cancer** is the stone called **onna** <note>original: "onna"; likely a type of kaolin or medicinal clay</note>. This is found in the land of the **Argreos** <note>referring to the Argives or Greeks</note>, which is a very humid land of great cold and much rain. When the waters are plentiful in the winter time, large lagoons form in the fields there. Afterward, when the summer comes, they dry up with the heat of the sun, and then these stones are found, some large and others small. Most of them are white, though some have a certain yellowish tint. They are resplendent and spotted, and by nature soft and moist. And if one should grind them well and knead them with water and make of them whatever shape they wish and leave it to dry in the sun, it becomes very hard and shining, so much so that it does not look like a man-made thing. The women of that land use it on their bodies to make them soft and of a good color. Those who make **white pigment** <note>original: "piper"; likely referring to the preparation of white lead or "biacca" used by painters and parchment makers</note> put this stone into it, because it makes it white and more lustrous. And the southern star of the two that are in the middle of the **mast of the ship** <note>Argo Navis</note> has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its force and virtue. When this star is in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works most manifest.

<column-break/>

->**Of the bloodstone**<-

The 25th degree of the sign of **Cancer** is the stone named **sanguina** <note>original: "sanguina"; literally "bloodstone," though here described more like a mineral glue or resinous earth</note>. It is found in the land called **Daquitas** <note>likely Ethiopia or a region in the East</note> on the banks of a river called **Sagafonte**, from which it takes its name. Its color is green, tending toward a dark, livid purple. In color, it greatly resembles the stone of **alberuzach** <note>likely a reference to a type of turquoise or malachite</note>, but this one is very light and has open pores; it is easy to break, so much so that it crumbles between the fingers. When they break it, they find within the fracture a moisture that resembles glue. If they grind this stone and mix it with water, it makes a very strong **starch-paste** <note>original: "engrudo"</note>. Those in the **Promised Land** who bind books use it, as do carpenters when joining boards. Its virtue is such that if it is given to drink to one who has an **abscess** <note>original: "apostema"; an internal swelling or infection</note> in the chest or the sides—provided it is ground and kneaded with water in which **mallows** <note>a soothing medicinal herb</note> have been cooked—the person is healed in one or two doses. And the southern star of the three that follow the **neck of the well** <note>a specific medieval asterism</note> has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its force and virtue. When this star is in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works most completely.

# Of the stone they call sarquiduz. —

The thirtieth degree of the sign of **Cancer** <note>original: "cancro"</note> is the stone called **sarquiduz** <note>original: "sarquiduz"; likely a corruption of "sarcophagus," a type of limestone known in antiquity for its property of consuming the flesh of the deceased</note>. This is found on the island of **Almaquak** <note>original: "almaquak"; likely referring to the legendary island of Waq-Waq, often placed by medieval geographers in the Indian or Pacific Oceans</note> on the seashore. It is yellow in color, and there are black lines in it, set one upon another in the likeness of a tree <note>This refers to dendritic patterns, which are branch-like mineral inclusions</note>. This stone is very heavy, strong, and hard to break, such that it does not break except with a large **mallet** <note>original: "mallo"</note>. 

And if they put it in the fire, a very foul odor comes from it that smells like rotten meat. And if someone who had a **demon** <note>original: "demonio"; in medieval medicine, "possession" often categorized conditions like epilepsy or severe melancholy</note> should smell this smoke, it returns to him immediately <note>The text implies the stone acts as a diagnostic tool or triggers a relapse in those afflicted</note>; but for one who did not have one, smelling it causes no harm at all. 

By nature, it is cold and moist. And the dark northern star of the two front stars that are in the northern part of the **Body of the Well** <note>original: "cuerpo del pozo"; referring to the constellation *Puteus*, a grouping of stars traditionally associated with the celestial ship Argo Navis</note> has power over this stone; and from it, the stone receives its force and virtue. And when it is in the **mid-heaven** <note>original: "medio cielo"; the point where a celestial body crosses the meridian, reaching its highest altitude</note>, this stone manifests its works most clearly. —

# Of the stone they call sarquiduz. —

The thirtieth degree of the sign of **Cancer** <note>original: "cancro"</note> is the stone called **sarquiduz** <note>original: "sarquiduz"; likely a corruption of "sarcophagus," a type of limestone known in antiquity for its property of consuming the flesh of the deceased</note>. This is found on the island of **Almaquak** <note>original: "almaquak"; likely referring to the legendary island of Waq-Waq, often placed by medieval geographers in the Indian or Pacific Oceans</note> on the seashore. It is yellow in color, and there are black lines in it, set one upon another in the likeness of a tree <note>This refers to dendritic patterns, which are branch-like mineral inclusions that look like moss or trees</note>. This stone is very heavy, strong, and hard to break, such that it does not break except with a large **mallet** <note>original: "mallo"</note>. 

And if they put it in the fire, a very foul odor comes from it that smells like rotten meat. And if someone who had a **demon** <note>original: "demonio"; in the medieval context, this refers to various physical or mental illnesses believed to be caused by spiritual possession or influence</note> [were to be fumigated with its smoke, it would aid them].

# Of the stone called fustec, mixed of colors

<image-desc>Historiated decorative initial 'E' featuring two men seated; one holds a small bowl, and both appear to be engaged in the preparation or examination of its contents.</image-desc>

**The** 30th degree of the sign of **Leo** <note>original: "leon"</note> is the stone called **fustec** <note>original: "fustec"; likely a variegated mineral, perhaps a type of jasper or agate, though the name is also associated with yellow-dyed wood in other contexts</note>, which is mixed of many colors. This stone is of the **magnitude of M** <note>original: ".m."; likely a medieval classification for the size, weight, or quality grade of the gem</note>. It is found on the island called **Rynar**. Its nature is hot and dry, just like the other stones of this sign, but it has less color than they do. 

And if they grind it and mix it with **oil** <note>original: "olio"</note>, it is beneficial for the **mange** <note>original: "sarna"; a skin condition caused by parasitic mites</note> and for **itching** <note>original: "comezon"</note>, and for **catarrh** <note>original: "romadizo"; a common head cold or runny nose</note> and for the **cough**. It also heals the ailment that comes from the **dripping from the head** <note>original: "destellamiento dela cabeça"; a reference to the medieval medical belief that phlegm or humors "distilled" from the brain and dripped down into the chest</note>, from which **asthma** is created in the lungs. 

And the star that is in the wing of the **Raven** <note>original: "canaria"; in medieval Spanish astronomical texts, this often refers to the constellation Corvus</note> which looks toward the south, has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its **virtue** <note>original: "uertud"; the innate medicinal or magical power of the stone</note>. And when that star is at **mid-heaven** <note>the highest point in the star's path across the sky</note>, this stone shows its works more clearly.
