# OF THE SIGN OF VIRGO 41.

### Prologue
The thirty types of stones according to the thirty degrees of the sign of Leo have been described. And it is necessary for whoever wishes to use the knowledge of this book: that he pay attention to the state of the Sun; just as has been said of the other planets of the signs of which we have spoken. And likewise to the state of the **Lord of the Face** <term>Lord of the Face: the specific planet that rules the ten-degree section, or decan, of the zodiac sign</term> in that degree of the sign to which the stone belongs: for the better its state, the stronger the virtue of these stones will be to work for good, and for evil the contrary. And so now we shall return to follow our discourse: and let us begin the sign of Virgo:

### Of the stone they call venecin.
<image-desc>Historiated initial 'E' containing a scene of a man in a blue hooded robe standing and presenting a yellow/green stone to another man who is bowing before him.</image-desc>
The first degree of the sign of Virgo: belongs to the stone they call **venecin** <note>original: "uenecın"; possibly a type of green jasper or a variety of nephrite</note>. This stone is found in a river called Queneuinz that flows through an island called **Neybe** <note>likely a reference to an island in the Indian Ocean or Red Sea area frequently cited in medieval lapidaries</note>. This river has so little water that in times of dry heat it dries up. And then they find this stone there, which is green in color and has a clear light. It is hard to break, and it shatters like crystal when it is broken; they find it is white inside. Some of them are so long that they make knife handles from them. And if they grind it and mix it with wine and smear with it a spear shaft or any other piece of wood: it will never bend; rather, it will straighten if it were crooked. And if they smear hot **abscesses** <note>original: "postemas"</note> with it, they heal; and it does this because it is of a cold and dry nature. And likewise, when they place it upon the stomach, it stops vomiting. And if they sprinkle the wine made from it over the body of a dead man: it keeps it from rotting for a long time; but in itself it is a deadly poison, for if they give it to a man to drink, it kills him, and it will not protect the body of the one who dies from this poison. And the two stars, the northern and the southern, which are in the robe of the figure of the Woman <note>The constellation Virgo is depicted as a winged woman</note> have power over this stone and from them it receives its virtue. And when these are in the **ascendant** <term>ascendant: the sign or star rising on the eastern horizon at a specific moment</term>: it shows its works more effectively.

<column-break/>

<image-desc>A circular miniature depicting a winged angel (the personification of Virgo) with white wings, wearing a white tunic decorated with golden patterns. The angel holds two golden circular objects in its outstretched hands against a deep blue background.</image-desc>

### Of the stone that has the name dark ahaza. 2--
<image-desc>Historiated initial 'E' containing a scene of a woman in a blue dress and red cloak standing and watching a man in a light-colored tunic who is kneeling and using a mallet to work on a block of stone.</image-desc>
The second degree of the sign of Virgo: is the stone they call **dark ahaza** <note>original: "ahaza oscura"; "ahaza" usually refers to varieties of magnet or jet in this tradition</note>. And of this type, we have already named three kinds in the degrees of the sign of Taurus. It is said to show one virtue and deny the other: but now we will speak here of the one that is very dark, and is of a cold and dry nature. And it is found in the land of Dan. It is hard and strong of body. And in it are all the evil virtues that we said were in the other types of ahaza. For he who carries it with him, men wish him ill and quarrel with him willingly. From this stone they make vessels and bowls in which they eat and drink; but it has such a quality that for whoever uses them to eat or drink: wrinkles will grow upon him, and also the diseases that come from **melancholy** <term>melancholy: one of the four "humors" or bodily fluids; an excess was thought to cause sadness and physical ailments</term>. And the northern star that is in the mouth of the **jar** <note>original: "tinaia"; likely referring to the constellation Crater, the Cup or Jar, which sits near Virgo</note> has power over this stone, and from it receives its strength and virtue. And when it is in the ascendant: this stone enlivens its works more completely.

### Of the stone that has the name marbled ahaza.

<image-desc>A circular medallion at the top left contains a two-handled green amphora against a dark blue background. Below it, an ornate initial 'D' shows two men in a landscape using a pickaxe to break rocks or mine.</image-desc>

**Of the stone that has the name marbled ahaza.** The third degree of the sign of **Virgo** belongs to the stone they call **marbled ahaza** <note>original: "ahaza entreuetada"; "entreuetada" suggests a variegated or marbled appearance where colors are intermixed</note>. And it has this name because they always find it in two colors: one white and the other red. By nature it is cold and dry, and it agrees with the other stone [previously mentioned] in the virtues we spoke of before. In this manner, it is soft to the touch, more so than any of the others we have described. And the leading star of the three that are in the left hand of **the one who helps to set** <note>original: "del q̄ aiuda a poner"; this refers to the constellation Boötes, often called the "Ploughman" or "Shouter" in medieval astronomy</note>—it is from this star that the stone's virtue flows. And when that star is in midheaven, this stone shows its works most clearly.

### Of the stone they call white ahaza.

<image-desc>A circular medallion at the top right contains a man in a brown tunic, barefoot, holding a hooked staff against a dark blue background. Below it, an ornate initial 'D' shows two men in tunics, one of whom holds a round white stone.</image-desc>

**Of the stone they call white ahaza.** The fourth degree of the sign of **Virgo** belongs to that stone they call **white ahaza**. They find it in the land of **Yemen**. In color it is white, and its nature is cold and dry. And it is a stone that men should not carry with them, for it is in itself a **mortal poison** <term>mortal poison: "toſico mortal"; implies the stone is inherently toxic to the touch or if ingested</term>. It is such that if a man takes the weight of one **drachma** <term>drachma: a small unit of weight, roughly 3.4 grams</term>, it kills him. However, if before three hours have passed they give him to drink as much as half an **ounce** <term>ounce: "onça"; roughly 28 grams</term> of **molten gold** <note>original: "oro calient"; likely referring to gold that has been heated or a potable gold medicinal preparation</note>, he is cured. But if three hours pass, nothing can save him from death. The middle star of the three that are in the left hand of the figure of **the one who helps to set**—from this star the stone receives its virtue. And when this star is in the **ascendant** <term>ascendant: the degree of the zodiac rising over the eastern horizon at a specific time</term>, this stone shows its works most fully.

### Of the stone named sardicamer.

<image-desc>The decorative capital letter E contains a miniature illustration of two figures: a man in a brown monastic-style robe stands over a kneeling man in a blue tunic who holds a bowl or basket, possibly sorting or processing stones.</image-desc>

The 10th degree of the sign of **Virgo** belongs to the stone they call **sardicamer**, which means "tongue-retainer" in **Chaldean** <note>original: "caldeo"; refers to the ancient Semitic language of Babylon, often associated with occult knowledge in the Middle Ages</note>. This stone is very black in color, and one finds white droplets within it. By nature it is cold and dry. It is found in a land called **Achurugem** on the shores of the sea. These stones are small and found mixed with sand. It is light in weight and has open pores. It is so soft that it breaks when pressed between the fingers. However, when it is burned, it becomes as hard as other stones. And if one were to grind any amount of it and knead it with watered wine, shaping it into whatever form desired, and then place it in the fire, it becomes hard stone again and retains its color and its virtue. It demonstrates the virtue it possesses in this way: whoever carries it with them will be unable to speak; and if it is given to someone to drink, they will become mute. However, this does not last forever, but only as long as the stone remains in the stomach, which can be as long as seven days. The northern star of the two located in the bottom of the **vat** <note>original: "tina"; referring to a specific vessel-shaped asterism</note>—which are in the body of the figure called **Pozio** <note>likely a corruption of "Icarius" or referring to the constellation Bootes, the Herdsman</note>—has power over this stone, and from it the stone receives its strength and virtue. And when that star is in midheaven, this stone demonstrates its works most clearly.

<column-break/>

<image-desc>A circular medallion featuring a large, ornate green ceramic urn or vase with two handles, decorated with vertical ridges on its body.</image-desc>

### Of the stone that appears in the sea when Mercury sets.

<image-desc>The decorative capital letter E contains a miniature illustration showing a man in a blue robe standing and handing a small object to a man in a red tunic who is seated or kneeling before him.</image-desc>

The 11th degree of the sign of **Virgo** belongs to the stone that appears in the sea when **Mercury** sets and hides when it rises. It is found in the **Sea of Darkness** <note>original: "mar tenevrosa"; the medieval name for the Atlantic Ocean, thought to be thick with fog and mystery</note> where other stones are found that manifest the virtues of the other planets. This stone is the opposite of the one we named in this book in the 28th degree of the sign of **Gemini**, for this one is as clear as the other is cloudy. It is a very dry piece of stone and has no visible [image] of its own, but it reflects any other thing that appears before it <note>suggesting it acts like a mirror</note>. By nature it is cold and dry, and if it were dissolved, it would follow the state of the planet **Mercury**. It possesses such virtues that whoever carries it with them feels a weariness throughout their entire body, such that all physicians would find them to feel very heavy. And if it is given to a person to drink, it will dull the senses <note>original: "cortara la esso"; likely "seso," meaning brains or wit</note> even more severely. The last star of the three in the thumb of the left hand of the figure of **the one who shouts** <note>the constellation Bootes</note> has power over this stone, and from it the stone receives its strength and virtue. And when that star is in midheaven, this stone demonstrates its works most completely.

### Of the stone named azech

<image-desc>A large, historiated initial 'E' decorated with blue, red, and gold leaf. Inside the initial, two figures are shown: a man in a blue robe and a shorter figure in a green tunic. The taller man appears to be handing or showing an object to the other.</image-desc>

The seventh degree of the sign of **Virgo** belongs to the stone they call **azech** <note>original: "azech"; derived from the Arabic *al-zāj*, referring to vitriols or metallic sulfates such as copper or iron sulfate</note>. This stone is of four types. The first they call **tzon**; the second **chalcitis** <note>original: "calcatur"</note>; the third **chalcanthum** <note>original: "calcadiz"</note>; and the fourth **chalcant**. We shall speak of each of these in its proper place, but first it is necessary that we show the ways in which they agree with one another, which are these: their texture is smooth and dry, and they blacken any bodies upon which they are placed. They stanch the blood that flows from the nose and from all wounds, though they leave that place black. They heal the **nerves** <note>In medieval medicine, this term often included tendons and ligaments</note>, and they strengthen and tighten areas that are loose. If a man drinks a certain quantity of it, his lungs will suffer such great dryness that he will die unless he is aided with **pine** <note>original: "pyña"; likely referring to pine resin or nuts used as a medicinal counter-agent</note>. There are also waters that run through the places where these stones are born; whoever is accustomed to bathing in them will develop great and very long-lasting fevers, from which they recover only very slowly. And now we wish to speak of the first of these vitriols, which they call **tzon**, which is red in color. Its mine is in the land of **Spain**, and in another called **Cates**, but the best of all is that found in the land of **Egypt**. It has the appearance of a tile or pottery; when they break it, they find it black inside

<column-break/>

and with pits that have a certain fiery glow within them. Its power is so strong that it causes the soul to pass into death <note>original: "camnar en obito"; meaning to die or perish</note> quickly if it is drunk. It has a harsh taste. Because its nature is so piercing, if they grind it and use it in a **cautery** <note>A medical treatment involving burning or searing the flesh to treat a wound</note>, it is beneficial for sores on the legs. This type of vitriol is the most prized and most brilliant of all the others. And the star that is in the **mouth of the Vat** <note>original: "tinaia"; referring to the constellation Crater, depicted as a large vessel or jar</note> toward the south has power over this stone, and from it the stone receives its virtue. When that star is in mid-heaven, this stone demonstrates its works most clearly.

<image-desc>A circular miniature with a blue background depicting a large, green, two-handled ceramic jar or urn (tinaia) with vertical decorative ridges around its body.</image-desc>

### Of the stone they call marmunia

<image-desc>A large, historiated initial 'E' decorated with blue, red, and gold leaf. Inside the initial, a figure in a red tunic stands before a small, domed building or shrine with an arched doorway, possibly representing the cave or path mentioned in the text.</image-desc>

The eighth degree of the sign of **Virgo** belongs to the stone they call **marmunia**. By nature it is cold and dry. Its mine is in a town called **Sayre**. It is found inside a cave in which there is a path; at the end of that path there is a basin, in the middle of which is a pool into which yellow drops of water fall from above. These stones are hard and very strong, and they shine somewhat, though their light is matte when they are broken, or on the outer edge where they were broken off. This stone has the power to cause great **retching** <note>original: "retennir"; here meaning to vomit or expel from the stomach</note>, so that if any man drinks of it, he vomits.

### Of the stone named calcatar

<image-desc>An ornate illuminated initial "E" containing a miniature of two figures. A standing man in a grey robe presents a small yellow object (the stone calcatar) to a seated man. The initial is surrounded by vibrant blue and red scrollwork with gold leaf accents that extend into the margin.</image-desc>

The ninth degree of the sign of **Virgo** belongs to the stone of the **azeth** <note>original: "azeth"; a term derived from Arabic referring to vitriols or metallic sulfates</note> which they call **calcatar** <note>original: "calcatar"; likely Chalcitis, a copper sulfate or iron-copper vitriol</note>. This is the second type of those we mentioned of yellow colors. Of this stone there are four varieties, or they are cast into the water. And more often they find in these red **azeth** stones that come from **dyamos** <note>original: "dyamos"; likely referring to *misy*, another vitriol variety</note>, which when they have a film that has formed upon them, appear of a yellow tint. In this it is understood that in time the yellow becomes red, and the red yellow.

<column-break/>

But among those that appear yellow, that which has the color of brass and is easier to break is the best. However, there is another kind in which they find veins like the color of gold; this type is harder and tougher to break. When they do break it, it shines somewhat in the fracture; for this reason, the good variety is called **enno** <note>original: "enno"; possibly a corruption of a Greek term meaning shining or star-like</note> because that brilliance it has within itself appears like stars. In Latin it is called **virine** <note>original: "uirine"</note>. The best of this **azeth** is found on the island of **Cyprus** <note>original: "catros"; likely a corruption of Cyprus, famous in antiquity for copper vitriol</note>, yet despite this, it is found in many other places. Likewise, it appears with all the other **chalcites** <note>original: "calques"</note> of this nature. Because of the great force of sharpness <note>Acidity or corrosiveness</note> that it possesses, it lasts a long time and contains such heat that it burns the flesh upon which it is placed and forms a scab. But as this stone loses its sharpness [when processed], it is better to work with it when it is roasted <note>original: "qumada" (quemada); calcined or heated in fire</note> rather than raw. This variety is of a more subtle substance than the other we mentioned and is easier to "eat" <note>To dissolve or act upon the body</note>. For this reason, it is included in medicines made for moisture of the eyes and for the tearing that comes from them. Likewise, it helps with hot abscesses <note>original: "postemas"</note> when it is boiled and mixed with the juice of leeks. It also enters into medicines made for abscesses of the gums, and for the pustules and sores that form on the body, and for fistulas. And the leading star of the three that are in the northern right arm of the figure of **Virgo** has power over this stone, and from it the stone receives its strength and virtue. And when that star is in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works most manifesty.

### Of the lead stone

**The** 26th degree of the

### On the stone they call çumidumi

The 25th degree of the sign of Virgo belongs to the stone they call **çumidumi** <note>original: "çumidumi"; likely referring to stibnite or a similar metallic ore used in ancient cosmetics.</note>. Its color is black like ash. It is very heavy and hard to break; and when it is broken, one finds inside the seeds of hair-like fibers <note>original: "semente de cabellos de fustes"; literally "seeds of hairs of wood," describing fibrous or needle-like mineral inclusions.</note>. By nature it is cold and dry with a harsh spirit. Its mines are found on the shores of the Indian Sea, in **P.** <note>The abbreviation ".p." in the text likely refers to a specific port or region in India known to medieval geographers.</note>. It is a dark stone and without luster. And if it is washed as other stones are washed to heal wounds, this stone does so effectively and clears them. This stone has a great power to retain moisture so that it does not flow, and to join together things that are separated. For this reason, they make **eyeliner** <term>alcohol: from the Arabic 'al-kuhl', referring here to a fine medicinal powder or ointment for the eyes</term> from it to heal the **white spot** <note>original: "albun del ojo"; likely referring to a cataract or corneal scarring.</note> of the eye, which is a marvel; and likewise the **protrusion** <note>original: "minmella"; an ocular swelling or inflammation.</note> that emerges with great pain. And the northern star of the **fore-vine** <note>original: "uina delantera"; referring to the star Vindemiatrix (Epsilon Virginis), traditionally known as the 'Grape-gatherer'.</note> which is in the left leg of the figure of Virgo, has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its virtue. And when this star is in the ascendant, this stone shows its effects most clearly.

<column-break/>

<image-desc>A decorative initial 'E' with elaborate flourishes. Within the letter, two figures are shown against a blue background. An older man in an orange robe holds a stone, while a smaller figure in a red tunic strikes a stone with a pickaxe or hammer.</image-desc>

### On the stone named tyssirenez

The 27th degree of the sign of Virgo belongs to the stone they call **tyssirenez** <note>original: "tyssirenez"; the description strongly suggests pumice.</note>. This is found often on the seashore; it is porous and so light in weight that it seems it could hold itself up in the air; yet despite this, it is strong and hard to break. It is somewhat clear, and its color is like **magnetite** <note>original: "aymā"; the text compares its color to a loadstone or magnet.</note>, and for this reason some call it the *caimanet* stone. It is also found in the land of Spain, on the shores of the sea that faces the West <note>The Atlantic coast.</note>. By nature it is cold and dry in the third degree. And if it is ground and given to someone to drink, it draws out moisture from the stomach and prevents vomiting; it has such power of retention that it heals both **diarrhea** <note>original: "camara"</note> and **dysentery** <note>original: "menazon"</note>. It does even more: for whoever carries it in their mouth, it prevents excessive spitting and the **drool** <note>original: "liua"; saliva.</note> that flows from the mouth while sleeping, and it serves children likewise when they are small. And the southern star which is in the **fore-vine** of the quadrant that is in the left leg of the figure of Virgo, has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its virtue. And when that star is in the ascendant, this stone shows its works more completely.

**On the stone Carabe. Degree 30.**

The 30th degree of the sign of Virgo belongs to the stone called **Alcarabe** <note>original: "Alcarabe"; from the Arabic 'al-kahraba', meaning amber.</note>, which means in Greek: **"that which draws straw"** <note>original: "tuatorte pñnas"; likely a corruption of the Greek 'harpaga', referring to amber's electrostatic ability to attract light objects.</note>, and in this place it is called **amber** <note>original: "alabre"; a variant of 'ámbar'.</note>. This is found in a river called the **Axis** <note>original: "actiz"; likely the Oxus or a similar river in Scythia.</note> which is in the land of **Scythia** <note>original: "scia"; an ancient region in Eurasia north of the Black Sea.</note>. They also find it in the lands of the Western Sea on the island called **Baltar** <note>original: "baltar"; likely referring to the Baltic region, famous for amber.</note> to the east of Spain. Most of those found there fall from **Moorish palms** <note>original: "palmas moriscas"; likely a reference to fossilized resin from ancient trees.</note>. In color it resembles a yellowish **jargoon** <note>original: "iargura"; a variety of zircon.</note>, and others are the color of gold; when they are broken, the same color is found inside. In some of them, a hint of redness appears when they are cut. It gives off a scent like **camphor**. By nature it is cold and dry. Its virtue is to **draw straws** <note>This refers to static electricity; amber attracts light particles when rubbed.</note>. When it is ground and its powder is sprinkled over the body of a dead man, it keeps it from rotting; it does this because of the power it has within it to retain and to wrinkle. For this same reason, it stops blood that flows from the nose or from any other place in the body. It also reduces **diarrhea** <term>camara: a medieval term for bowel movements or flux</term>. And from it they make a medicine for the disease they call **"the burning"** <note>original: "cauzar"; likely a corruption of 'causis' or 'cauter', referring to a burning sensation or gas in the stomach.</note>, caused by wind in the stomach, and for all pain in the stomach; likewise for the **stiffness** or **hardness** <note>original: "scidum o q̄ritadum"; terms for hardness or blockages.</note> of the bones. The southern star in the second line of the **quadrate** <note>original: "quatrat"; a four-sided astronomical alignment.</note> which is in the left leg of the figure of **Virgo** has power over this stone, and from it the stone receives its virtue. When this star is in the middle of the sky, this stone shows its works most clearly.

<image-desc>A circular illustration at the bottom of the left column depicts a winged angel with golden wings and a brown robe, standing within a blue circular field.</image-desc>

<image-desc>A large decorative historiated initial 'D' containing a miniature of two men. **On the stone that is named Kinfar. Degree 30.**

The 30th degree of the sign of Virgo is the stone they call **Kinfar** <note>original: "kinfar"; likely referring to jet or a black variety of fossil resin.</note>. By nature it is cold and dry. It is the color of gold speckled with black drops, and there are some that have flakes instead of drops. This one is harder to break than the other [amber], for light does not pass through it; when it is cut, a bit of clarity appears at the edges of the cut. The color inside is black and very dark, and it is heavy. It is found in a river called the **Rhone** <note>original: "roys"; possibly the Rhone or a similar sounding river in the Iberian peninsula.</note> that flows through the land of Spain; it is not found in mines, but there are certain trees there called in Latin **populus** <note>original: "populus"; the poplar or aspen tree.</note> that have black leaves and black wood. From those trees flows a moisture that falls into that river, and from this, the stone is formed in the water. If it is ground and softened with any oil, it becomes soft like wax and burns in that same manner. If the bite of an **"alborozo"** <note>original: "alborozo"; likely referring to a venomous insect or a specific type of skin ulcer.</note> is anointed with it, it heals. If its powder is placed in eyes where an **ulcer** <note>original: "forado"; literally a hole or perforation.</note> is forming, it cures them. Also, when they grind it and dissolve it with **vinegar** <note>original: "umague"; likely a corruption of 'vinagre'.</note>, they make from it a good and very clear **ink** for writing. The star that is in the right leg of Virgo has power over this stone, and from it the stone receives its strength and virtue. When it is in the middle of the sky, this stone shows its works most manifesty.

<image-desc>A circular illustration at the bottom of the right column depicts a winged angel with red and yellow wings and a green robe, standing within a circular frame.</image-desc>

They also find it in the lands of the Western Sea on the island called **Baltar** <note>original: "baltar"; likely referring to the Baltic region, which has been the world's primary source of amber since antiquity.</note> to the east of Spain. Most of those found there fall from **Moorish palms** <note>original: "palmas moriscas"; a medieval belief that fossilized resin dripped from ancient trees, here compared to palms.</note>. In color it resembles a yellowish **jargoon** <note>original: "iargura"; a pale or yellowish variety of the gemstone zircon.</note>, and others are the color of gold; when they are broken, the same color is found inside. ### Of the stone they call tebelcuz

<image-desc>Illuminated initial 'E' featuring a scene where a figure in blue robes appears to be consulting with or healing a seated figure in a reddish-brown tunic. The initial is decorated with colorful floral and leafy motifs.</image-desc>

**T**he first degree of the
sign of Libra: is the
stone they call
<term>tebelcuz</term><note>A light, porous stone, possibly a type of coral or volcanic rock like pumice.</note>. This is a
stone of open
pores. And when
 a man holds it in his hand: it
seems as if a
breath <note>original: "cuito," likely meaning a puff of air or heat</note> passes through it. In co-
lor it is brown but even
somewhat green. In the Eastern sea they find it in
this way: when a great storm occurs there,
the waves lift this stone because of the lightness <note>original: "uiuaneas"</note> it has in itself.
And when they break on the shore: they cast it onto the sand.
And if the water cannot cast it out: then as soon as
the storm ceases it returns to the bottom of the water like <term>pumice</term><note>original: "pumerio"</note>. Its
nature is hot and moist. And its virtue is such that whoever
carries it hanging from the arm, tied with ten twisted threads
or more: cannot be defeated in a feat of arms. But on the
other hand it is a deadly caustic. For if one gives it to someone to drink:
it wounds the kidneys and makes the urine run with blood and poison in
such a way that if someone <note>original: "ayma," likely "alma" (soul/person)</note> does not help him with some remedy: for this there is
no cure except death. And the star that is
in the belt on the right side of <term>the one who shouts</term><note>The constellation Boötes, often called "The Shouter" in medieval texts.</note> has power over
this stone: from it and through it, it receives its strength and virtue. And
when it is in the ascendant: this stone shows
its works more clearly.

<header>OF LIBRA</header>

<image-desc>A circular miniature at the top of the left column depicting a man in a blue tunic and white hose holding a tall white staff or rod. He is positioned against a blue background, and the frame is decorated with stylized floral motifs in red, blue, and gold.</image-desc>

**Of the stone named alguenna**

<image-desc>Historiated initial 'E' depicting two men in a landscape; one is seated wearing blue and red robes, while the other, dressed in orange, stands before him, possibly presenting or discussing stones.</image-desc>

**T**he third degree of the sign of Libra: belongs to the stone they call <term>alguenna</term><note>Possibly a type of sea sponge or coral-like marine growth; the name is related to the Arabic "al-qanna."</note>. It is the second type of sea-foam. This is always found in the form of wool, but it is entirely bluish in color, mixed with a certain amount of deep violet. And it is perforated, much like the <term>pumice</term><note>original: poman</note> that we call <term>Peletries</term><note>likely a reference to Halcyoneum, a marine substance mentioned by Pliny and Dioscorides</note>, and it is of a thick nature. Its smell is like seaweed, and it takes its name from this: because they call it <term>alganna</term><note>derived from "alga," the Latin word for seaweed</note>, though in Arabic they call it <term>gacoza</term>. Most of those that are found are in the sea of the land called Galatia <note>An ancient region in central Anatolia, modern-day Turkey</note>. Its nature is hot and moist, but its heat is greater than that of the first foam we mentioned. When ground and taken in a drink with a little wine, it is of great value for <term>jaundice</term><note>original: yctericia</note> and for ailments of the liver and the spleen <note>original: bago</note>. And when they burn it and make medicine from it, it is good for the disease called <term>lopia</term><note>alopecia</note>, where the hair is pulled out, and also for the mange <note>original: sarna</note> that comes from humidity. The forward star of the two that are in the left leg—which goes as if in front of the three that are at the root of the tail of the figure of him who is half-man and half-horse <note>The constellation Centaurus</note>—has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its virtue. And when that star is in the midheaven, this stone shows its works most completely.

**Of the stone that is made from the foam of the sea:**

<image-desc>Historiated initial 'E' depicting two men in a rocky landscape; one stands holding a large brown stone over his head as if to strike, while the other crouches on the ground before him.</image-desc>

**T**he fourth degree of the sign of Libra: belongs to the stone that is made from the foam of the sea, which is named <term>farfin</term>. Its entire nature is formed in the shape of tiny worms. In color, it is greenish mixed with brown, and according to the name <term>phykos</term><note>original: .pxu</note> in Greek, they call it <term>mhuas</term><note>likely "amyos," referring to a type of marine mussel or sponge</note>. It is found in the sea of the land called Warnitas. Its nature is hot and moist, and it is of a more solid substance than the other we mentioned, and lighter in weight. It has such virtue that if they give it to drink to one who cannot pass urine, he is healed. It also helps against the ailment of the <term>stone</term><note>kidney or bladder stones</note>, and for the abscess <note>original: postema</note> that forms in the bladder <note>original: ueriga</note>, and for <term>ringworm</term><note>original: tinna</note> if they rub it with it. However, when they burn it, it has greater strength in each of these things. The following star of the two that are in the right leg of the <term>Centaur</term><note>original: cantoro</note> has power over this stone, and from it, the stone receives its strength and virtue. For this reason, when that star is in the midheaven, this stone shows its works most manifesty.

### Of the stone that is named lanemia. .2.

<image-desc>Ornate illuminated initial 'E' for the word "El" (The). The initial frames a miniature of a seated scholar in a habit gesturing toward a standing youth. The letter is decorated with elaborate blue and red foliate patterns that extend into the margins.</image-desc>

**T**he 7th degree of the sign of Libra: belongs to the stone they call <term>lanemia</term><note>A name likely derived from the Latin "lana" (wool), referring to a type of marine sponge or Alcyoneum</note>. This is the fourth kind of <term>sponge</term><note>original: esponia; here referring to Alcyoneum, a marine substance often classified between animal and mineral in medieval lapidaries</note> that we have mentioned. In its form, it resembles dirty wool and smells exactly like it; it takes its name from this resemblance. Its nature is like the others we have already described, but more tempered <note>original: humana, literally "human," but in this context meaning mild or balanced in its qualities</note> than any of them. Its hardness is such that it is difficult to break, and they call it <term>guzunmo</term> in Arabic. This stone is found on the seashore, and most notably on the island they call Baritona. By nature, it is hot and moist, and its heat is greater than any of the others we have mentioned, but its moisture is not as great as theirs; for this reason, it has the power to penetrate bodies and greatly heals the skin from above. Its virtue is such that if it is ground and mixed with water, and used to anoint the breasts of a woman who has an <term>abscess</term><note>original: postema; a localized collection of pus or a swelling</note>, it heals them. And the star that is on the right shoulder of the figure of the one who has his knees fixed <note>A reference to the constellation Hercules, historically known as "Engonasin" or "The Kneeler"</note> has power over this stone and from it, the stone receives its strength and virtue. And when this star is at mid-heaven, this stone manifests its effects most clearly.

<column-break/>

### Of the stone they call fequenna. .2.--

<image-desc>Ornate illuminated initial 'E' for the word "El" (The). The initial frames a miniature showing a person bending over another who is seated, performing a medical treatment on their leg or foot over a basin. The decoration consists of orange and blue foliate flourishes.</image-desc>

**T**he 8th degree of the sign of Libra: belongs to the stone they call <term>fequenna</term><note>likely another variety of Alcyoneum, possibly Halcyoneum spicatum, which resembles an ear of wheat</note>. This is the fifth kind of sponge among those that are most foamy, and it is hot and moist by nature. Its form is like that of wheat, and it owes its name to this. It has no smell at all. Its color is murky, but when it is broken, it is found to be rough inside. It is not as porous as the others, and for this reason, it is heavier. It is green in color and shines like ash, but the internal virtue burns more than the exterior suggests. It is found on the seashore on an island called <term>Zafuriucron</term>, and the people of that land call it <term>aluzabne</term>. It has as much power as all the others mentioned; whoever places it on the tongue feels a sharp, burning taste. If it is ground and used to anoint hair, it removes it <note>This indicates its use as a depilatory</note>; however, it is good for healing the disease they call <term>morphea</term><note>original: morfea; a skin condition characterized by painless, discolored patches on the skin</note> and other conditions that affect the skin. And the two stars—the middle and the last of the three that are in the <term>alcahatret</term><note>A transliteration of the Arabic "al-rāmiḥ" (the spearman), referring to the constellation Bootes or the star Arcturus</note>, which is at the end at four and a half degrees—have power over this stone, and from them it receives its virtue. And when this degree is in the <term>ascendant</term><note>The degree of the zodiac rising over the eastern horizon at a specific moment</note>, this stone manifests its works most completely.

### Of the fish stone

<image-desc>A square illuminated miniature at the start of the column depicting two figures. A standing man in a blue tunic and red cloak appears to be instructing or presenting something to a smaller, kneeling figure. The background is a solid deep blue. To the left is an ornate vertical border of acanthus-style leaves in blue, red, and green with gold highlights.</image-desc>

The 17th degree of the sign of Libra: belongs to the stone they call the fish stone. This is found on the island called Guimea <note>Likely a reference to an island in the Indian Ocean or a corruption of a known geographical name in medieval Arabic geography</note> on the shore of the sea in some mines that are there, which are very deep. Some are large and others small. It is light in weight and perforated both inside and out, and hard to break. But when they break it, they find it is soft <note>original: vezne, possibly meaning spongy or fatty</note> on the inside. And the color it appears on the outside is like that of seawater. When broken, it is found to be a yellow color inside that leans toward red. By nature, it is hot and moist. It is found on the island called <term>Aamueruz</term> <note>From the Arabic *ḥajar al-ḥūt*, literally 'fish stone'</note>, which means as much as "fish stone"; this is because it smells like fresh fish when it begins to spoil. And its virtue is such that if they throw it into a place where there are fish, they all gather together. And if a person suffering from <term>leprosy</term> <note>original: gaffo, referring to those with the 'claw-hand' deformity associated with leprosy</note> drinks it, taking a weight of three <term>drachmas</term> <note>A unit of weight roughly equal to 3.5 grams</note>, it heals them; and anointing oneself with it in the bath does the same. And the three stars—the one in the left shoulder, the other beneath the joint of the left leg, and the one belonging to the figure that is half-man and half-horse <note>Refers to the constellation Centaurus</note>—these both have power over this stone and from them it draws its virtue. And when they are in the ascendant, this stone shows its works more completely.

### Of the stone that they call elbehtu

<image-desc>A square illuminated miniature showing two figures seated on the ground in conversation or performing a task. One wears a blue robe and the other a red one. The background is a solid blue. A decorative border of swirling foliage in blue, red, and gold separates the two columns and frames the initial text.</image-desc>

The 18th degree of the sign of Libra: belongs to the stone they call <term>elbehtu</term> <note>From the Arabic *al-baht*, meaning 'the stunned' or 'the marvel'</note>, which means "congealing" or "stupefaction." This is of a hot and moist nature; and its color resembles golden <term>marcasite</term> <note>A metallic mineral often mistaken for gold or pyrite</note>, but this is clearer and more brilliant. They find it in the Eastern Sea in places where there is great cold, when there are great storms; for among those waves, these stones are cast upon the shore of the water in the sand. Some are found large and others small. And its virtue—beyond what the name implies—is this: that whenever anyone looks at it, it makes their eyes fixate, and they stand thus, fainting while staring at it, just as if they were congealed by the numbness of cold. They can never move their eyes from it until it is removed from before them or covered with something. And it even happens in that land where they find it that there are some birds the size of turtle-doves, and they are red and russet in color, with long black beaks; they call them <term>qulunten</term> in Arabic, and the men of that land eat them. Whenever one of these birds perches upon that stone, it makes it lose its virtue. And if they put this stone into human blood, it dissolves and mixes with it; and afterward if they put it to the fire, the blood congeals and the stone is purified from it, but it receives a great and very soft flexibility.

### Of the stone called Mihiraz
<image-desc>Decorative initial letter 'D' containing a miniature of two figures seated on the ground. An older man with a red cap and blue robes gestures toward a younger man in a brown tunic. The initial is framed by elaborate blue, orange, and gold foliate borders extending into the margins.</image-desc>
The 9th degree of the sign of <term>Taurus</term> <note>original: "taura"</note> belongs to the stone they call **Mihiraz**. It is a stone so strong and hard that no other body can make a mark upon it except for the **diamond** alone, nor does fire harm it. It is found in the land of <term>Media</term> <note>An ancient region of north-western Iran</note> in such a way that it lies upon the surface of the earth, and not in caves or any other deep place. It is a stone of great brilliance and resembles **fine gold** in color. Some are found large and others small, and of various shapes. By nature, it is hot and moist. And its virtue is such that **flies** flee from it, as does all foul company <note>original: "rrepañia," likely referring to vermin or pests</note>. And the sages even said that the devils remember <note>Avoid or fear</note> the one who carries it, and such a person has no desire to use **necromancy**, nor can any spells be cast

against them. And the star at the tip of the hand of the beast they call the **Centaur** has power over this stone, and from it, the stone receives its force and virtue. And when it is in the <term>ascendant</term>, this stone shows its works most clearly.

### Of the cleft stone
<image-desc>Decorative initial letter 'E' containing a miniature of two stonemasons. One man stands and swings a hammer at a chisel held against a large stone block, while a second worker is crouched at the base of the stone. The initial is decorated with intricate blue, green, and orange foliate scrollwork.</image-desc>
The 10th degree of the sign of **Taurus** belongs to the **cleft stone** <note>original: "piedra fendida"</note>. This is found in the land they call **Levna**. In color, it is like **saffron** or even more deeply tinted. It is cleft <note>Split or layered</note>, and because of this, it is easy to break and lighter in weight. In its characteristics, it entirely resembles **ammoniac** <note>original: "almonriaco," likely referring to *sal ammoniac* (ammonium chloride) or the medicinal gum of the same name</note>, but this stone is hot and moist in the third degree. It has such virtue that if it is ground and mixed with **woman's milk** and placed in the eyes, it heals the foul sores that form in them, as well as <term>acenias</term> <note>Possibly sties or similar ocular growths</note>; it also removes the swelling <note>original: "grossura," literally thickness or fat</note> that forms in the eye sockets. And if it is given as a drink to one who has an **abscess in the liver**, they are healed. And the two stars in the **Centaur** <note>original: "cantorio," a scribal variant for Centauro</note>—one in the right shoulder and the other on the horse's spine—both have power over this stone, and from them, it receives its force and virtue. And when it is in the <term>midheaven</term> <note>The highest point of the sun or a star's daily path</note>, this stone shows its works most clearly.

### Of the stone of the tanners

<image-desc>A large historiated initial D featuring two figures: one standing in a blue and red robe drinking from a bowl, and another kneeling on the ground over a basin.</image-desc>

The 51st degree of the sign of Libra belongs to the stone of the tanners, which they call **Monuue** <note>original: "monuue," likely a transliteration from Arabic</note>. It is called this for the reason that if it is placed in still water, it remains dirty and does not move; but if it is later placed in running water, it sinks to the bottom. It is found on the island called **Augenica** more than in any other place, along the seashore upon the surface of the earth, for it is not found in mines. Although it has open pores within it, it is nonetheless heavy. Its color is like ash, and they find them as pebbles and other small pieces. Its nature is hot and moist. Tanners use it for cutting leathers; also, if it is ground up and poured into the throat of one whose **uvula** <note>original: "uua," literally "the grape," referring to an inflamed or fallen uvula</note> has fallen, it heals them immediately. And if it is given as a drink to one who has poison in their stomach, it makes them recover quickly. The star that has power over this stone is the northernmost of the three located in the right limb <note>original: "rruido," possibly a corruption of a term for joint or limb</note> of the one who is **kneeling** <note>The constellation Hercules, known in the Middle Ages as "The Kneeling Man" or "Engonasin"</note>; from this star, the stone receives all its force and virtue. When this star is in the <term>ascendant</term> <note>the degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon</note>, the stone manifests its works most clearly.

### Of the stone of the serpent

<image-desc>A large historiated initial D featuring two figures: one in blue and orange robes raising a hammer to strike a stone on an anvil or rock, while another figure in blue stands behind him watching.</image-desc>

The 52nd degree of the sign of Libra belongs to the stone of the serpent; they call it **Tezaquid** in the <term>Chaldean</term> language <note>original: "catteo," referring to the language of ancient Babylon</note>, which means as much as "facial fleece" <note>original: "uelloꝛ de rrosto," perhaps referring to the stone's texture or its use for facial ailments</note>. These are found in gold mines or where veins of **emeralds** are found. Their color is like a worn-out thing <note>original: "contra gozada," likely meaning faded or weathered</note> with white spots. It is a stone much prized by the people of that land, and they find them both large and small. Neither fire nor iron harms it. Its nature is hot and moist. Its virtue is such that whoever carries it with them will be safe from having the disease of the face that forms on the body, and it improves the complexion greatly if one keeps it. If it is placed upon the wound of a **viper**, it will heal it just the same; it does this also if it is ground and given as a drink. The two stars that follow the bright one in the figure called the **Crown** <note>original: "esceta," referring to the constellation Corona Borealis</note>—one of which is further north than the other—gather power in this stone, and from them it receives its virtue. When these stars are in the <term>ascendant</term>, this stone shows its works most perfectly.

### Of the stone called zfetaidna.

<image-desc>Historiated initial 'E' depicting two men in a rocky, mountainous landscape. One man, dressed in a green tunic and a white turban, stands and points toward another man. The 13th degree of the sign of Libra belongs to the stone they call **zfetaidna** <note>original: "zfetaidna," likely a transliteration of an Arabic mineral name</note>. And they find it in the land of **Zen** <note>original: "tierra de zen," referring to China</note>, mixed among other stones where **sulfur** <term>azunbre: an archaic term for sulfur</term> is found, and it is easily broken. Its nature is very moist. It is blue in color with black drops, but in some of them, they find large stones instead of drops when they are taken from the mine. However, later they can be worked and shaped into any form one desires.

It has a specific virtue: if one melts **silver** <note>original: "plata"</note> or an equal amount of sulfur, and then joins the sulfur on its side and the silver on its own, and they read <note>perhaps "lay" or "align"</note> one more than the other, and they melt the silver again on its side and mix it with this stone, ground into powder, and they make a hammer and anvil of that silver—any work done with that hammer upon it in the place where it was before will stay in its place; it will not move at all from its position when one takes it in hand. And they find no other virtue in this stone but this. The star that is in front of the three located on the right side of **Centaurus** <note>original: "cancori," a common corruption in these manuscripts for the constellation Centaurus</note> has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its virtue. And when that star is in mid-heaven, its effects are manifested most clearly.

The 14th degree of the sign of Libra belongs to the stone they call **lamich** <note>original: "lamich," likely from the Arabic "lāmish"</note>. ### Of the stone named after pitch.

<image-desc>Illuminated decorative initial E. Inside the letter, a figure in white and grey clerical robes with a halo is shown touching the head of a small child in a pink tunic. The background is blue with a gold and white pattern.</image-desc>

In this degree of the sign of Libra <note>the 14th degree</note>: is the stone they call **black pitch stone** <note>original: "pez negra," likely referring to a type of bitumen or jet</note>. It is very rare, and it shines just like a mirror; however, it is not thick or rough. Its body is hard to break, such that it does not crumble except with great effort. It is found in the lands of the West more than in any other place. It is smooth to the touch, and it seems that a smoke rises from it by day; this is visible and resembles smoke but has no manifest smell, nor does it appear at night.

And it has such virtue that if they place it upon a thousand weights of pitch, it makes them boil by its own power, just as if they were over a fire. And this stone, once placed in the pitch, if it is later put into hot water, it makes the water flee <note>original: "foyr," meaning to move or stir rapidly</note> to the right and to the left; and it shows this same virtue in the springs of cold water. Its nature is to touch and master by sight. It does another very marvelous thing: **camphor** <note>original: "clahofur," likely a variant of the Arabic *kafur*</note>, which is so [unclear: lacking?] in color that it is not well-rounded—if they put it back into the pitch where this stone was, the stone will straighten its face and make it very round. And the bright star in the **Northern Crown** <note>original: "corona feptentrional," known today as Corona Borealis</note>, which they call **Alphecca** <note>original: "cetera á foter," transliterations of Arabic names for the star Alphecca</note>, is set in this stone, and from it, the stone receives its strength and virtue. ### Of the stone named Indiana

At the 26th degree of the sign of Libra is the stone they call **Indiana**. Its nature is hot and moist in the third degree. It is found in the land of Egypt more than in any other place, and also on an island called **Yoquiim** <note>possibly an island in the Indian Ocean or Red Sea</note>. ### Of the Bloodstone

At the 27th degree of the sign of Libra is the stone they call the **Bloodstone**. It has this name because of its virtue, for it stops blood. So much so, that if they place it in water, it remains there in such a way that they cannot take it out <note>perhaps suggesting it dissolves or settles heavily</note>, and they do not place it all in the sun or by fire. For then there comes out of it something that loses neither the taste of blood nor its substance, but only the color. And if this stone is put into a vessel containing blood, a portion of the blood changes according to the stone's size; and that which remains, it turns into the color of water. And although this stone and the other we mentioned are similar in color, there is a great distinction between them: for the other only stops blood in a dead animal, while this one stops it in the living. And in this stone, they find no virtue in medicine <note>original: "fisica"</note> nor in any other thing, except for this one which has been told.

### **Of the** stone found on Mount Sinai.-

<image-desc>An illuminated initial 'D' containing a miniature of a man in red robes kneeling in prayer or wonder at the mouth of a dark cave entrance in a craggy mountain. The initial is decorated with colorful scrollwork and floral patterns.</image-desc>

The 28th degree of the sign of **Libra** belongs to the stone found on **Mount Sinai**. By nature it is hot and humid, and very hard to break or destroy, so much so that no other substance can prevail against it except for the **diamond** <note>original: "dyamante"</note> alone. It is green like the color of an emerald, but it is more luminous and of such great radiance that those who look at it cannot keep their eyes fixed upon it, for the sight is overwhelmed by its clarity. It is found at the summit of Mount Sinai in a very deep cave; the entrance is very narrow, long, and frightening because it has many twists and turns. However, those who take heart and dare to enter find it wide and shadowy once they are inside, and from there they take these stones. It has such virtue that whoever carries it with them feels no fear and is not frightened, even if they are in great danger. And when sorrow or anger moves them, these feelings are dispelled; if the person finds strength and comfort in themselves, it causes them to increase in humility and to be modest. And the northern star that is outside the head of the one who holds the serpent <note>Ophiuchus, the Serpent-Bearer</note> has power and dominion over this stone and from it receives its virtue and strength. And whenever it is in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works most fully.

# Of the stone named Secantaca .

<image-desc>A historiated initial 'E' depicts a scene with two figures: a seated man in a gray habit gesturing toward a standing man in a red tunic and orange leggings who holds a walking stick. The background is blue with white floral accents.</image-desc>

The 30th degree of the sign of **Libra**: is the stone they call **Secantaca** <note>original: "secantaca"; derived from the Arabic *saqantāqā*, meaning "maker of pregnancy"</note>, which means "maker of pregnancy," because its virtue is such that the woman who carries it with her will conceive the first time a man

unites with her. It is found in the **Land of Promise** <note>A medieval term for the region of Palestine/the Levant</note> and also in the East. In color, it is red like a very deep rose, and it shines so much that it appears to sparkle to the eye. It is light in weight, and they find some that are large and others small, but most are found in the shape of an egg, and some even have a hole in the "belly" or middle of them. It is hot and moist by nature, and many men love this stone for its beauty, but they find no other virtue in this stone except the aforementioned one regarding pregnancy. And the star that is in the middle of **Azubene** <note>original: "azubene"; refers to *Al-Zubānā*, the Arabic name for the "claws" of the Scorpion which medieval astronomers used to form the scales of Libra</note> in the southern part, which is in the hanging part of the scale of the figure of **Libra**, has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its virtue. And when it is in the mid-heaven, this stone shows its works most completely.

# Of the stone of vinegar .

<image-desc>A historiated initial 'A' shows two men in discussion: one seated on the left wearing a blue robe and yellow cap, the other standing on the right in a red hat and reddish-brown robes. The background is blue with floral motifs.</image-desc>

At the 27th degree of the sign of **Libra**: is the **stone of vinegar**. Its color is yellow, tending toward green, but it is dark. It is porous to the touch and light in weight, and so brittle that it breaks if held with too much force. This

stone is found on the island of **Sardinia** on the seashore; they find them in small shapes, so that the largest of them weighs no more than four **drachms** <term>dragmas: a medieval unit of weight, roughly 3.5 grams</term>. By nature, it is hot and moist in the third degree. Its virtue is that it appears to hate vinegar and all sour things, so much so that when it is placed near them, it jumps and flees, distancing itself as much as it can. And if they grind it and mix it with another substance and pour vinegar over it, it separates itself. And if they give it ground to a man to drink, it heals every cough and **shortness of breath** <note>original: "angostura del fuelgo", literally "narrowness of the breath"</note>, and likewise the spitting of blood or **pus** <note>original: "uenino", used here to mean morbid humors or discharge</note> that comes from an **abscess** <term>postema: an internal swelling or gathering of fluid/pus</term> that forms in the side or in the lung. It also defeats any other sickness a man might have in the chest, or in the membranes of the lung, or in other respiratory organs. And if they mix it with some oil and anoint the aforementioned places or the sites of painful illnesses, it does the same. And the star located in the hind leg of the **Bear** <note>Referring to the constellation Ursa Major</note> of this constellation—the hand of **Canis**—has power over this stone and from it receives its virtue. And when it is in the ascendant, this stone shows its nature most clearly.

## Of the stone named Marina

<note>original: "arina" in the heading, "marina" in the body; the text describes it as a sea-stone found on the shore</note>

<image-desc>Historiated initial 'E' containing two figures in yellow and red robes, seated and engaged in conversation with expressive hand gestures.</image-desc>

The 25th degree of the sign of **Libra**: is the stone they call **Marina** <note>The Sea Stone</note>. This is found in the western regions on the seashore, because the waves of the sea cast it out upon the sand. In shape, it is like the spindle-whorls <note>original: "torrenos"; the small, heavy weights used to balance a hand-spindle during spinning</note> that are placed on the spindles with which they spin, and it is pierced through the middle. Some are large and others small; they are all shaped like spindles, like grains. In color they are yellow, and appear like dusty spindles; they are strong and hard to break, and dense in color. By nature they are hot and moist. And its virtue is such that whoever drinks a potion <note>original: "pozo"; likely a medicinal draft</note> of it in a large dose, it breaks the stone that forms in the bladder or in the kidney, and causes it to be cast out like fine sand. And if a little of this stone is placed in meat when it is set to cook, it softens the bones in such a way that they can be eaten just like the other flesh; it does the same to fish bones. And the southern star of the three that follow the arrangement of the neck of the serpent held by the **Enchanter** <note>The constellation Ophiuchus, the Serpent-Bearer, often called "the Enchanter" in medieval Spanish texts</note> has power over this stone; and from it, the stone receives its force and virtue. When the star is at mid-heaven, this stone shows its effects most clearly.

## Of the stone they call Tarinon

<image-desc>Historiated initial 'E' containing a seated figure in a blue robe, holding up a dark stone or object. To the left, a smaller figure is visible within a dark opening, possibly a cave.</image-desc>

The 26th degree of the sign of **Libra**: is the stone named **Tarinon**, which means "mother of leeches" <note>likely derived from the Arabic "umm al-'alaq"</note>. It is strong and hard to break, and of a dark color that leans somewhat toward red. It is always found in the shape of a flask <note>original: "redoma"</note>, and inside it there appears the figure of a leech. If it is broken, in every piece one finds another such figure. This stone is found at the foot of **Mount Sinai**, in a cave that is not very deep. By nature it is hot and moist; its heat is stronger than its dryness. And its virtue is such that if it is placed at the mouth <note>original: "atoca"; likely a scribal error for "a la boca"</note> of any animal that has a leech in its body or throat, it pulls it with such great force that it causes the leech to come out and stick to the stone. And if it is ground and made into powder and placed upon proud flesh <note>original: "carne que sea sobre sanada"; tissue that heals excessively, often causing a raised bump</note>, it removes it and heals it; it does the same for warts. Furthermore, it has great power to retain moisture so that it does not flow, and to join things that have been separated. For this reason, an eye-powder <note>original: "alchol"; from the Arabic *al-kuhl*, used here as a medicinal salve rather than a cosmetic</note> is made from it to heal the white of the eye when it is blemished; likewise it is used for <term>munneda</term> <note>Possibly a type of surgical tool or a specific skin condition; the term is obscure in this context</note> which is benefited by its great color. And the northern star of the one in front, which is in the left leg of the figure **Tenis** <note>A variant name for the figure of Ophiuchus</note>, has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its virtue; and when the star is at mid-heaven, this stone shows its works more fully.

### Of the stone named Armenian.

<image-desc>An ornate initial 'E' decorated with blue and red scrollwork, containing a miniature of two men seated on a bench, engaged in conversation.</image-desc>

**T**he 19th degree <note>original: ".cxix." refers to the 119th stone in the overall sequence of the Lapidary, corresponding here to the 19th degree of the sign</note> of the sign of **Libra**: is the stone called **Armenian** <note>likely Azurite, a blue copper mineral</note>. It has this name because it is found in the land of Greater Armenia, in a very far-off settlement, in sandy places mixed with the soil.

This stone is white, light, and brittle; when it is broken, the inside is found to be like sand joined together. Its color is blue, and it greatly resembles <term>lapis lazuli</term> <note>original: "al mucho," likely a transcription error for "al lapi" or "azul," referring to lapis lazuli</note>, but it is distinct from it in its natural virtue; the more deeply tinted it is, the better. Of this kind of stone, some very large ones are found and others small. **Goldsmiths** use them to dye fabrics, and **painters** likewise use them to paint on wood. Its power is in its blue color; when placed upon the eyes, it greatly clears the vision, causes <term>postemas</term> <note>abscesses or inflammatory swellings</note> to fade and diminish, and dries up the moisture of the limbs. It brings them to their proper <term>complexion</term> <note>the medieval balance of the four bodily humors</note> when it is turned into powder and applied over them. From the star located in the right arm of the figure holding the censer <note>original: "incieso," likely referring to the constellation Ara, the Altar</note> it receives its force and virtue. When this star is in the <term>ascendant</term> <note>the degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon</note>, this stone shows its works most clearly.

### Of the stone of the fish

<image-desc>An ornate initial 'E' containing a miniature of a figure kneeling and reaching into a pool of water, perhaps searching for the "fish stone" mentioned in the text.</image-desc>

**T**he 21st degree <note>original: ".cxxi."</note> of the sign of **Libra**: is the **stone of the fish**. This is taken from a fish found in canals; it is found near the **Red Sea** <note>original: "mar bermeio"</note> on the island called Achac. For there is a lagoon there that contains only certain fish about a palm's length; they have no scales and have round heads. When one strikes them, these black stones are found in place of the brain. They are strong and hard to break, and people avoid them because of their weight; some are clear, and of a brown color that tends toward yellow. By nature, it is hot and moist in the sixth degree. It has such virtue that if it is ground and given to drink to those suffering from <term>gravel</term> <note>original: "arenas" or "grauella," referring to kidney or bladder stones</note>, it removes the stone that forms in the veins. It also does another thing: if it is kneaded with white vinegar and placed in an earthen vessel with a narrow mouth, and buried in an orchard and left there for thirty days during the summer, at the end of this period a creature will be found that resembles a lizard in shape, but is green in color. If this creature is burned and made into powder, and any amount of it is given to someone to drink, they will die without any illness or sign appearing; it does the same through scent alone. Against this <term>toxico</term> <note>poison</note>, no remedy that man can make is of any use. From the star that is in the joint of the right foot of the figure who stands by the hand of the singer... <note>the text breaks off mid-sentence</note>

# OF THE SIGN OF SCORPIO

### Prologue of the degrees of the sign of Scorpio.

<image-desc>A small decorative initial D containing a miniature of a seated figure in red and blue robes, possibly the author or a scholar, gesturing with their hands as if in discourse.</image-desc>

The thirty degrees of the sign of Libra have been fully described, as well as the thirty types of stones found within it. Therefore, it is necessary that whoever wishes to work with this book should pay close attention to the planet **Venus** and to the **Lord of the Face** <note>In medieval astrology, each zodiac sign is divided into three "faces" or decans, each ruled by a specific planet. The "Lord of the Face" is the planet governing that specific ten-degree section.</note>, ensuring that both are well-received and in a good state along with the star being used. For then, by the pleasure of God, one shall achieve what they desire.

### Of the stone they call alazrob

<image-desc>A large circular illumination framed within a square. It depicts an artisan or alchemist in a workshop setting, wearing a red tunic and blue hood. He is working with a vessel and a tool, while another figure stands in the background. The scene is encircled by a blue border decorated with white quatrefoil patterns.</image-desc>

The first degree of the sign of Scorpio is the stone they call **alazrob** <note>original: "alazrob," likely a reference to a form of lead or lead ore, possibly galena</note>, and some call it **utar**. This is a type of lead, the vilest <note>original: "rruî," meaning low-quality or base</note> of all others. it smells foul and has in its nature a portion of very congealed earth, as well as a part of sulfur <note>original: "azre"</note>, though very little. Its nature is cold and moist. What shows it contains sulfur is that it dissolves quickly in fire with little heat. If placed in a moist location, it increases in weight, and for this reason, it is very heavy. If a mortar and pestle are made from it and used to grind moist things, it greatly purges those things according to its nature. It is put into medicines intended for abscesses <note>original: "postemas"; inflammatory swellings or tumors</note>, for which it is beneficial, and also for diseases that occur in the reproductive organs. Furthermore, if a thin plate <note>original: "lamina"</note> is made from it and tied to a man over his vein, it removes the "opinion" <note>A euphemism for nocturnal emissions or erotic dreams</note> that he conceives at night while sleeping. Its stars—one in the belly and the other in the leg of the constellation of the **Centaur** <note>original: "osso fela figura de cátonz"; a corruption of the Latin 'Centaurus'</note>—have power over this stone, and from them it receives its strength and virtue. When both of these stars are in the **ascendant** <note>The degree of the zodiac rising over the eastern horizon at a specific moment</note>, the stone manifests its works most clearly.

<column-break/>

<image-desc>A marginal illustration of a centaur with a human torso and a horse's body, holding a long-handled axe or polearm.</image-desc>

### Of the stone they call tacat

<image-desc>A square miniature depicting a scholar or physician in a grey hooded robe and a red hat, holding a stone or small object and showing it to a younger figure in a short red tunic who holds a small vessel.</image-desc>

The second degree of the sign of Scorpio is the stone they call **tacat**, which in the Chaldean language <note>The language of ancient Babylonia, often associated with deep astrological wisdom in the Middle Ages</note> means "water-breeder." This is because in the land of Chaldea, near a certain town, there is a spring of very pleasant fresh water that descends from a mountain. It falls into a very ancient lagoon, and in the winter, parts of it freeze. When it thaws in the summer due to the heat, certain congealed pieces remain like stones, and this happens every year. These stones are strong, hard, reddish-blonde, and clear—white in color, just like frozen water. It is a stone that never dissolves, and for this reason, it is counted among the earthy stones. Its nature is cold and moist. Its virtue is such that if it is ground with something and the palm of the hand is rubbed with it, one can hold fire in that hand without being burned or feeling it. Likewise, by rubbing it on the forehead and temples of one who has a fever caused by heat, it takes the fever away. It does the same for one who has a fever from sunstroke, and for this same reason, it is very helpful for hot abscesses. The star in the right thigh of **Ophiuchus** <note>original: "rruo freato," a medieval Spanish rendering of the Greek 'Ophiouchos,' the Serpent Bearer</note> has power over this stone, and from it, the stone receives its virtue. When this star is in the ascendant, the stone shows its works most perfectly.

### Of the stone they call annufez

<image-desc>A large historiated initial "E" containing an indoor scene. A figure in a blue robe appears to be performing a medical or alchemical procedure on the head of a person seated on the floor. This illustrates the text's mention of treating head pain.</image-desc>

The fourth degree of the sign of Scorpio is the stone they call **annufez** <note>original: "annufez"; likely a form of gypsum or selenite, which can be ground, heated, and reconstituted.</note>. This is found in the eastern part of Spain in certain mines that are near the town of **Mancelem** <note>likely a phonetic spelling of a Spanish location with an Arabic name, possibly related to "Manzil"</note>, which in Arabic means "salvation." These stones are so hard that they cannot be reached unless one uses iron tools. Some are found large and others small, and in many shapes. It is so clear that sight passes through it, but it breaks very easily. It has three colors: one side is white, the other green, and the stone itself is very clear. This is one of the stones loved for its beauty. Its substance is of a nature that is tender, cold, and moist in the third degree of both these complexions. And it has such virtue that whoever carries it with them is safe from having pain of the **migraine** <note>original: "media cabeza," literally "half-head," the traditional description of hemicrania or migraine</note>; and if they place it on one who has it, they are healed. And if they grind it and give it to drink in the weight of half a **drachma** <note>a unit of weight used by apothecaries, roughly 1.8 grams</note>, it is of great value to those suffering from the illness they call **syncope** <note>original: "staqui," referring to fainting or sudden loss of consciousness</note>, which is like a swoon; but if one takes more than the aforementioned weight, they may die from the suffocating nature of the illness. It also does another thing: if this stone is placed in sweet juice, it softens it. If it is then placed in the sun and left until it thickens, and then poured into any shape one desires and placed by the fire until it hardens, it turns back into

<column-break/>

stone and loses nothing of its clarity, nor its beauty, nor its color; however, it loses the nature and the virtue that it had before. And the southern star of those in the thigh of the right arm of the one who holds the **living serpent** <note>A reference to the constellation Ophiuchus, the Serpent Bearer</note> has power over this stone, and from it comes its virtue. And when that star is in the **midheaven** <note>the highest point in the sky that a celestial body reaches</note>, this stone shows its works most clearly.

<image-desc>A circular diagram containing a human figure in a brown tunic, kneeling or standing with one leg bent. The figure holds a sickle in the right hand, and a six-pointed star is superimposed on their chest. This represents another astrological figure.</image-desc>

### Of the stone they call Indiana . 2

<image-desc>A large historiated initial "E" showing two figures standing near a body of water with stylized hills in the background. One figure wears a red cap and brown tunic, the other wears a blue robe. This relates to the text describing stones found by riverbanks.</image-desc>

The fourth degree of the sign of Scorpio is the stone they call **Indiana**. This is born in the water, and they find it on the coasts of India in mines, and also among the sands of the riverbanks. It is always found in the shape of **handles** <note>original: "uas tantas," likely a corruption of "manubrios," meaning handles or sleeves</note>, which in Latin means **manguiar** <note>likely "manubrium"</note>. It is porous and very light in weight, and yellow in color, but not a very deep yellow. And its virtue is such that if they place it upon a person with **dropsy** <note>original: "idropico"; a condition of swelling caused by excess fluid (edema)</note>, it draws out the yellow-colored water and removes it from the body, according to its size. ->**Of the stone named Belmunicen .2, 2,**<-

<image-desc>A large decorative initial 'E' contains a miniature painting of two figures in medieval tunics bending over a large wooden chest or sarcophagus, appearing to search for or place something inside.</image-desc>

This 10th degree of the sign of Scorpio: is the stone they call Belmunicen. This is formed on the island called Argemea on the seashore, wrapped in the sand. It is lightweight <note>original: "Luuiana"; modern Spanish "liviana"</note> and heavy and rough on the outside: if they break it—and however much they break it—they find it smooth <note>original: "lezne"; slippery or polished</note> on the inside. Its color is reddish, but not very much, and they find it in various shapes. Its nature is cold and moist: when they place it upon something by itself or through a very thin cloth: it becomes so smooth that one can easily make a rouge <note>original: "rroio"; likely a red pigment or cosmetic</note> with it over whatever place they put it: and it makes it very clear and very beautiful. And if they grind it and knead it with water: they make from it a very good paste <note>original: "engudo"; a type of glue</note>: such that neither moth nor worm <note>original: "tinna ni danna gusano"</note> harms the wool that is treated with it. And this stone also has another virtue: if they carry it much across the floor of a ship when it is sailing <note>original: "tahent"; moving or under sail</note>: whoever sits there will be seized by a very strong sickness they call "couca" <note>original: "couca"; an archaic term for seasickness or vertigo</note> in such a way that if they do not move away from that spot: they may even die. And the forward star of the two <note>original: "tos"</note> that are in the hind leg of the figure of Scorpio, which are before its tail <note>original: "couajo"</note>: has power over this stone: and from it, it receives its virtue. ->**Of the stone they call Buritasten .2.2.2.2.2**<-

<image-desc>A large decorative initial 'E' contains a miniature painting of two figures; one is seated and appears to be holding or examining a round disk or vessel, while the other stands opposite him.</image-desc>

The 11th degree of the sign of Scorpio: is the stone they call Buritasten. This is the color of amalgam <note>original: "almagam"; a mercury-alloy, often appearing silvery-grey</note>. And its nature is cold and moist in the second degree: its property is such that it shuns water <note>original: "ante de la uer agua"; literally "before seeing water," implying an aversion or reaction</note>: and when they break it, they find the inside hollow: and all that vacuum is filled with a thin thing that resembles a spider's web. And if they grind this stone and mix it with ten times its weight of tin: and they melt them together: it will turn into silver: and it endures the hammer and fire and all other things that silver can endure: but it is not fine silver: because afterward, if they melt it many times: it returns to the state it was in at first. And if they give it, ground up, to a man to drink: it makes him pass much urine: in such a way that he cannot retain it: and if he drinks much of it: it kills him. But if he who has weak kidneys <note>original: "gritas flacos"; referring to the urinary tract or renal system</note> drinks it temperately: it makes him heal by passing urine: especially those in whom there is more phlegm than choler <note>This refers to the Four Humors; phlegm was considered cold and moist, while choler/bile was hot and dry</note>.
