And if they make a crucible from this stone to burn oil <note>original: "ouo"; likely "olio" or oil, though the word resembles "egg"</note> or a wax candle: and put it therein: it makes it last ten times longer in burning than it ought to last. It is found in the Promised Land: not in deep mines but upon the face of the earth in certain sandy places, and at times they find it on the island of Sardinia. And the forward star of the three bright ones that are in the body of Scorpio has power over this stone: and from it, it receives its virtue. And when it is in the ascendant, this stone shows its works most manifesty.

### Of the stone named astagoniz. 222.

<image-desc>A decorative historiated initial 'E' containing a scene of two men at a stone well. One man is leaning over to draw water, while the other stands nearby holding a bucket. The background of the initial is blue with gold filigree.</image-desc>

The 21st degree of the sign of Scorpio belongs to the stone they call astagoniz. In the Chaldean language <note>original: "caldeo"; referring to the ancient Semitic language associated with Babylonian astrology</note> this name means "the diamond of the sense of taste." This stone is found in the land of Greater Armenia, specifically in very large fields where there are very deep wells. When water is drawn from them, these stones come out with it. It is light in weight and its color is between white and yellow, appearing much like the color of the wax from a honeycomb or the juice of fresh grapes. It has such a virtue that from the time the sun sets until it rises, it becomes soft as wax, so that people can make of it whatever they wish, joining one piece to another or dividing it into as many parts as they see fit. However, from the time the sun rises until it sets, it hardens so much from within that it can be ground into powder. Its nature is cold and moist. And the name we mentioned first is very true, for whoever holds it in their mouth will not be able to taste anything they eat or drink. Furthermore, if it is placed among spices that have a bad flavor, it takes it away and makes them good, as long as the stone remains with them. The star located in the claw <note>original: "unỹ," likely for "uña"</note> of the left leg of the one who holds the staff <note>original: "pioio fira"; likely a reference to a figure in a constellation like Ophiuchus</note> has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its virtue. When this star is at mid-heaven, the stone's effects are shown most clearly.

### Of the stone that appears in the sea when Mars sets.

<image-desc>A decorative historiated initial 'E' containing a scene of two figures in a small, dragon-headed boat on turbulent blue water.</image-desc>

The 22nd degree of the sign of Scorpio belongs to the stone that appears in the sea when the planet Mars sets, and it hides itself when Mars rises. This stone is found in the Tenebrous Sea <note>original: "mar tenevrosa"; the medieval name for the Atlantic Ocean</note> where other stones are found that clearly show the virtues of plants. It is white in color, very shining and clear, so much so that at night it glows like a candle. Because of the great clarity it possesses, it catches the voice of anyone who speaks loudly before it. It is so hard that it will not break except by very great force. Its property is such that it shows a great enmity toward salt. If they are put together, the stone breaks and crumbles, and the salt loses the saltiness it possesses. It is light to the touch, and in it appears the same contrary nature mentioned in the twentieth degree of the sign of Aries. When the tide <note>original: "mar̃e"</note> rises, this stone sinks to the bottom of the water, and when the tide falls, it stays on top, floating. It also does another thing: the more it is out of the water, the more it brightens upon the land, and when it is submerged, it darkens. Furthermore, when the planet Mars is above the earth, whoever looks at the stone will see that it softens and can be easily broken; but when the planet is below the earth, it does the opposite.

# OF THE

If they give a drachm's weight <note>original: "peso de una dragma"; a drachm was a small unit of weight used by medieval apothecaries</note> of it to drink to anyone, it causes them to lose all the strength of the stomach’s retention and the appetite for eating. If they try to eat or drink anything by force, they must vomit it immediately. In this way, they remain until they die. And it does the same to the one who carries it with them; for in an instant it makes them lose the sense of smell, so that they smell nothing. And it not only does this to animals, but to all other things upon which they might place it. 

And the two stars—the one that is the hindmost of the other on the left, and the other morning star of the three that are in the left foot of the one who holds the *morio sicut* <note>Original: "morio sicut". **Of the stone they call tarnificen**

<image-desc>A historiated initial 'E' featuring a seated scholar or physician in a grey robe and blue cap, holding a small vessel and gesturing toward a standing young man in an orange tunic. The background is blue with gold decorative patterns.</image-desc>
**THE 18TH** degree of the sign of Scorpio belongs to the stone they call **tarnificen**. This stone is in the shape of a bowl, hollow on one side and round on the other; and some of them are large and others small. Its color is green turning toward yellow, spotted with red drops. It is found in a place they call the Cave of Paradise, which is at the beginning of the Promised Land,

<column-break/>

# SIGN

outside the bank of the river they call Larzon. And in this aforementioned cave, there are many kinds of snakes and serpents; and there are some kinds among them that are a palm’s length long, in the likeness of vipers. They have such a property that when the planet **Mars** rises above the earth, they give such frightening cries that whoever hears them dies immediately. Therefore, the men of that land who know the time refrain from passing by that cave in that season. 

And these stones that lie in that cave cannot be obtained except in this way: when the river rises by a great flood, it enters that cave and fills it; and when the water recedes, it carries these stones behind it. And according to the abundance of the water that goes out, the stones—large or small—remain on the riverbank. And in this way they can have them and not in any other, for they cannot enter the cave because of the dangers mentioned. 

Its nature is moist and warm in the third degree, and it is highly prized. And the more they put it into a fire that burns hotly, the more it loses its color. Any thing that is dirty, such as mud, or a base sword <note>original: "espada desgraciada"; likely referring to a low-quality or damaged blade</note>—if one puts a little of this stone over the iron or over any other thing at the time of melting and makes from it a sharp knife or any other weapon, if it should wound any animal in such a way that blood comes out, it can never recover and will die. 

It does the same if they give it to someone to drink; if it finds within the body any kind of vein or place where it can reach the blood, as soon as it reaches it, it kills, as has been said. And the star that is in the left shoulder of the one who holds the *morio sicut* has power over this stone, and from it, it receives its virtue. And when it is in the ascendant, it shows its works more abundantly.

# OF SCORPIO

<image-desc>A large decorative initial 'D' containing a miniature of two men in a rocky landscape. One man is seated on a rock, while the other stands and strikes the earth with a pickaxe. The initial is adorned with colorful flourishes in red, blue, and green.</image-desc>

**Of the stone they call ceminez**

<margin>
The 19th degree of the sign of Scorpio belongs to the stone they call *ceminez*, which means "flyer" in Chaldean <note>original: "caldeo"; in medieval texts, "Chaldean" often referred to Syriac or the ancient Babylonian language associated with magic and astrology</note>. This is because for the person who carries it: if they lose it, they will never again find themselves feeling sad. For this reason, those who know its nature loathe it <note>This implies the stone induces a state of chronic melancholy or dependency that is only relieved by its loss</note>.
</margin>

It is found on the island of *Caridin*, where they find the other very noble stones described in this book. In color it resembles a sapphire <note>original: "cafire"</note>, but not in its brilliance, for it is dark and without light, and it is strong and hard to break. Of these, there are very few, because men do not dare to venture out to extract them due to the evil influence <note>original: "mala uertud"</note> that is in them, as we have already said. Its nature is cold and moist. And if they grind it and mix it with the juice of purslane <note>original: "uerdulagas"; a succulent plant used in medieval medicine for its cooling properties</note> and wash the face with it, it heals the sores that form there and turn red because of a bad humorial complexion. And the two stars—the one in the first knot and the other in the second of the body's part in the figure of Scorpio—have power over this stone, and from there it receives its virtue. And when they are in the midheaven, this stone is at its strongest and has the most power in all its works.

**Of the stone named farunceen**

<margin>
The 20th degree of the sign of Scorpio is the stone they call *farunze*, which means "frightener of children" in Chaldean. It has this name because of its power: for if children see it or have it with them while they sleep, they will see things of great fear and much terror in their dreams, so much so that they are forced to scream, and some shriek very loudly.
</margin>

And when they grind this stone and incorporate it with another medium <note>original: "colador"; likely a base or straining agent for an ointment</note>, it makes a very good ointment to remove the itch <note>original: "pinote"; likely referring to a stinging skin eruption or pruritus</note> and the mange, and for the fever that grows from the heat of the sun. This happens because by its nature it contains moisture. Its color is black, speckled with yellow drops. These spots are clear and mirror-like, but not if the sight is divided <note>suggesting the spots have a reflective quality when viewed directly</note>. They find large ones and small ones of various shapes; it is strong and hard to break. It has such a property that if they put it in brine <note>original: "salmueera"</note> or water, it turns the liquid entirely yellow, the color of its spots. This stone is found in a river they call the *Turbes*, which is at the edge of the eastern part of Spain <note>original: "spaña"</note>; they find it at the bottom of that water mixed in the sand with other stones. And the last star of the three in the left foot of the one who holds the serpent <note>original: "rinoso"; likely a corruption referring to Ophiuchus, the Serpent-Bearer</note> has power over this stone, and from it, the stone receives its virtue. And when that star is in the midheaven, this stone shows its works most clearly.

# Of the stone called martiz

<image-desc>An illuminated miniature at the top of the column depicts two figures: a man in an orange tunic and dark leggings, and a smaller figure in a grey tunic. They are standing by a dark, jagged opening in the ground, appearing to observe or extract a dark mineral (martiz). The scene is framed by a decorative blue and red border with golden acanthus-style flourishes.</image-desc>

The 16th degree of the sign of Scorpio belongs to the stone they call *martiz*. Its color is very black, yet it is so polished that light rays reflect off it just as they do in a mirror. The body of the stone is streaked in form, and to the touch, it has certain indentations <note>original: "unnas"; literally "claws" or "nails," used here to describe curved, gouge-like marks</note> like those made by a winepress. It is soft to the touch, spongy <note>original: "huanar"; likely meaning soft or porous</note>, and full of holes.

It possesses such virtue that if it is ground and mixed with other substances and used to anoint the skin, it cures the itch and mange <note>original: "canna : z sannya"; common medieval terms for irritating skin diseases like scabies</note>. It also cures the disease called *alvafreila* <note>original: "aluafreila"; an Arabic-derived term for a type of erosive ulcer or skin lesion</note>, as well as the hangnails <note>original: "pinazos"</note> that form at the tips of the nails on the fingers and toes. Its nature is cold and moist in the second degree <note>Medieval medicine classified the "humors" or qualities of substances on a scale of one to four; the second degree indicates a moderate medicinal strength</note> of both these temperaments. It is found in the land called Artel, in a town called Crates, in very deep mines located on the ridge of a mountain near that place.

And the two stars—the one in the third joint of the tail of the figure of Scorpio, which is the northern one, and the other in this same joint toward the south—both have power over this stone, and from them it receives its strength and virtue. When these stars are in the ascendant <note>The "ascendant" is the zodiac sign or degree rising on the eastern horizon at a specific time, believed to be the moment of greatest astrological power</note>, this stone manifests its effects most clearly.

# Of the stone named gezaquifez

<image-desc>An illuminated miniature at the top of the column shows two men engaged in mining. One man, in a blue tunic, strikes the ground with a pickaxe, while another man in a long grey robe and a blue hat stands to the left, watching the work. The scene is enclosed in a decorative blue and red border.</image-desc>

The 17th degree of the sign of Scorpio belongs to the stone called *gezaquifez*, which in our language, from the Chaldean <note>In the Middle Ages, "Chaldean" often referred to Syriac or Arabic, the languages of ancient eastern learning</note>, means "of the creature." It bears this name because its virtue is such that if a pregnant woman carries it with her, it protects the creature <note>The unborn child</note> from harm until the time of birth; furthermore, it makes her give birth easily and without danger. It also helps a woman to conceive quickly, without the need for other medicinal aids <note>original: "sin taurio : z sin ugion"; likely referring to specific medieval poultices or specialized treatments</note>.

This stone is found in Lesser Armenia, in the city or town called Gurfen, in a dark place. Its mine is on the bank of a river that runs through a hollowed-out, sandy area. It is always found in a round shape, and at the bottom, it has indentations like washed-out claws. It is porous and very light, but smoother on the inside. It is shiny, and its color is that of refined gold, though slightly reddish. Its nature is cold and moist, and it dissolves very easily; if it is wetted or moved just a little, it breaks down. When placed in copper at the moment of melting, it turns the copper the color of gold—though not a beautiful gold—making it appear so in all its qualities, though it is not naturally gold, for if it is melted many times, it returns to its original state. If placed upon wounds, it makes them heal quickly.

The star located in the left foot of the one who holds the serpent <note>The constellation Ophiuchus</note> has power over this stone, and from it, the stone receives its virtue. When this star is in the ascendant, the stone shows its works best.

### Of the stone named tumen.

<image-desc>An illuminated initial 'D' featuring a miniature of a man in a red tunic standing in a small boat on blue water. He appears to be using a pole or spear to hunt a sea creature. The initial is bordered by ornate gold, blue, and red scrollwork.</image-desc>

**O**f the 22nd degree of the sign of Scorpio: this is the stone they call *tumen*. Its nature is cold and moist. It is found on the shores of the Red Sea <note>original: "mar rubio"</note> near a place in that aforementioned sea where certain fish dwell. These fish produce this stone in great abundance. They have no place for it to emerge into the light from the mud except through their mouths; therefore, this stone takes its shape inside the body. When the fish wishes to cast it out, it goes to the shore and ejects it there.

It possesses such virtue that if, after it has been ejected, another fish touches it, that fish dies immediately. Fishermen find these stones in that place and take many of them because when they place a piece on a hook, any fish that approaches it dies instantly, allowing them to be caught very easily. Its color is like that of leek leaves—a green that tends slightly toward white. It is light in weight, rough to the touch, and easy to break. If someone drinks the weight of one drachm <note>a medieval unit of weight, roughly 3.5 grams</note> of it, it greatly purges phlegm; therefore, it is good against all pains that occur in the joints <note>original: "artellos"</note> caused by cold humors <note>original: "tenacium fria"; likely referring to persistent cold ailments</note>. And the star located in the thigh of the left arm of the figure who holds the bolt <note>original: "el que tiene el uiro"; referring to the constellation Ophiuchus, often depicted holding a serpent or a staff</note> has power over this stone, and from it, the stone receives its strength and virtue. When this degree is in the ascendant, this stone shows greater power in all its works. —

### Of the stone they call catu.

<image-desc>An illuminated initial 'D' containing a miniature of two figures; one is kneeling and tending to a small ram-like animal. The initial is surrounded by decorative gold and colored foliate patterns.</image-desc>

**O**f the 23rd degree of the sign of Scorpio is the stone they call *catu*. This is created within the membranes <note>original: "telas"</note> of animals. It is found in this manner: in the heads of certain beasts, namely mountain rams that are small of body but have such great power for running that nothing can catch them. Therefore, they cannot be captured except by trickery. These rams are called *catu* in the Chaldean language <note>original: "caldeo"</note>, and from this, the stone takes its name. It happens that these rams carry a stone in the fontanelle <note>original: "fuent"</note> of that body. As it forms, it stretches the skin, and in this way, they feel that they have it. When it is extracted, it is found to be the color of a jujube <note>original: "iuziusa"; a reddish-brown fruit</note>.

Its shape is as follows: the part that sits against the bone is flat, and the outer part against the skin is high and rounded. The flat side shines like a mirror, but the other side does not. It is a strong stone and hard to break, but when it is broken, the inside is found to be made of layers like membranes. Its nature is cold and moist. Handles for knives and swords are made from it, as it is highly prized for such ornaments. Its scent is like that of ambergris <note>original: "ambar"</note>, and even stronger when it is placed over fire. If it is ground after being burnt, its powder is very useful. If mixed with rose water and placed upon a burn from fire, it heals it and leaves no scar. And the star that follows the horn, located at the fourth knot of the figure of the Scorpion, has power over this stone and gives it its virtue. For this reason, when it is in the midheaven, this stone manifests its works most clearly. —

## Of the stone named mazintarcan.

<image-desc>A large historiated initial "E" containing an illustration of two figures: one standing in a blue robe holding a red object (likely the stone), and another figure seated, possibly a scholar or patient.</image-desc>

The 17th degree of the sign of Scorpio belongs to the stone called *mazintarcan*, which means "a thing that is governed by foam" <note>original: "fuma"; likely referring to sea foam or frothy deposits</note>. This is a type of stone that grows <gloss>and is</gloss> maintained by the governance of all things. It forms in the depths of sand in very cold places during the winter time, and especially where rainwater gathers during rainy years. This stone is found in the mud in this manner: when the waters rise greatly and afterwards recede, and the earth wrinkles from the heat of the sun, small mounds are formed there. He who breaks these open finds stones inside them with "buds" <note>original: "ninnos"; literally "children," but used here to describe internal nodes or smaller stone formations</note> in the shape of coral, though it has nothing else in common with it. It is a very hard stone, such that it does not break except with a heavy blow; it is very heavy and of two colors: one green and the other white, and each is very lustrous in itself. Its nature is very cold and moist. Its "buds" are some thick and others thin, and they are so joined to one another that they resemble the knots of a tree. Because of this, it is most often hung around the necks of children, and also

<column-break/>

because of the virtue it possesses, it protects them from the illness they call *maseta* <note>likely a medieval term for a swelling or a specific childhood ailment</note>, from runny noses, and from excessive crying. If a woman also wears it, it is helpful for all ailments of the chest, for those who spit blood, for poison, and for those who suffer from urinary incontinence. When made into a plaster, it is of great benefit for "hot abscesses" <note>original: "postemas calientes"; referring to inflamed, painful swellings</note>. The two joined stars—the northern and the southern—which fall over the figure of this place, have power over this stone, and from them it receives its virtue. When they are at the midheaven <note>the highest point in the sky reached by a celestial body</note>, this stone manifests its effects most clearly.

->Of the stone they call ancalites<-

**The 33rd degree** of the sign of Scorpio belongs to the stone they call *ancalites*. Its nature is cold and moist in the second degree of both qualities. It is found on the shores of the Sea of Spain <note>The Atlantic Ocean or Mediterranean coasts of the Iberian Peninsula</note> toward the eastern part, and also on the shores of Bithynia <note>original: "Bituna"; an ancient region in northwest Asia Minor</note>. It is very heavy, smooth to the touch, and both porous and rough. When it is burned, it becomes very light and rough, and it hardens more than it was before; then it does not dissolve in water. And if after they

burn and grind it, they place it upon the wounds that occur on the feet from tripping or from the tightness of a shoe: it heals and cures them. It also cures ringworm <note>original: "tiñuenas"</note> and hangnails <note>original: "unnas de las uinnas"; referring to painful skin or slivers around the fingernails</note>. In color, it is yellow, at times turning toward green, and it is helpful for dyeing and painting. # OF THE SIGN OF SAGITTARIUS

It is fitting for anyone who <gloss>Prologue 2.</gloss> journeys through all thirty degrees of the sign of Scorpio: that they pay close attention to the planet that is received by the star which has power over the stone; likewise to the lord of the face <term>lord of the face: a planetary ruler of a ten-degree subdivision (a decan) of a zodiac sign</term> that it be placed in its proper location; and doing this, one will accomplish what they desire by the pleasure of God.

<margin>Of the stone they call zequerh</margin>

<image-desc>A rectangular miniature with a gold background. Two figures are depicted in a landscape; a man in a green robe stands pointing towards a smaller figure in a red tunic who is seated on the ground.</image-desc>

The first degree of the sign of Sagittarius: is the stone they call **zequerh**. This is found in the land of Lycia <note>original: "luquia," an ancient region in what is now Turkey</note>; likewise by the river that flows near the town they call Mitaz. This stone is **black in color** and **very light in weight**. And when they burn it, it creates a shimmering <note>original: "uamart," likely referring to a bright flame or a specific type of soot</note>; the smoke from it smells like pitch <note>original: "pez," a resinous substance used for sealing ships</note> when they put it in the fire. By nature it is **hot and dry**. And if its smoke is given to one who is possessed by a demon: they return to themselves immediately. And if they also smoke a woman with it who has pain in her nature <note>original: "su natura," referring to the reproductive organs or womb</note>: she is healed immediately because this stone is diffusive. And from the smoke of this when it is burned: oppressive spirits flee. And this stone is good when they put it into medicines to heal the sickness they call arthritis <note>original: "artetica," a general term for joint pain or gout</note>, which comes from the nature of phlegm <term>phlegm: one of the four bodily humors believed to cause sluggishness or cold illnesses</term>: because it is salty in its fourth degree. And the star that is in the left knee of the one who holds the bow <note>original: "el que tiene el proyo fuzado," a descriptive name for the constellation Sagittarius</note> has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its virtue <term>virtue: an inherent healing or magical power believed to reside within a natural object</term>. And when it is in the middle of the sky: this stone shows its works more clearly.

<image-desc>A figure with curly yellow hair, wearing a brown-purple tunic, holds a large curved sickle or blade in his right hand while extending his left arm.</image-desc>

<margin>Of the stone they call sedmech</margin>

<image-desc>A rectangular miniature showing an interior scene with a gold background. A figure in a blue robe is seated, holding a small object (likely the stone described) towards another smaller figure seated on the ground.</image-desc>

The second degree of the sign of Sagittarius: is the stone they call **sedmech**, which means **hematite** <note>original: "amatites," from the Greek for "blood-like" because of its red color</note>. This is found in the sands they call the ocean. And likewise they find it in the land of Egypt in the mines that are there. By nature it is **hot and dry** and easy to break: and it is of a **red color**: and the more dyed it is, the better it is; and likewise that which is clean and does not crumble. It is a very well-known stone. And its property is: that it has within itself a **retentive power with sharpness**: and for this reason they prepare it to thin the thickness of the eye sockets. And if they mix it with woman’s milk: it heals the sickness they call ophthalmia <note>original: "oytal," likely a corruption of the Greek ophthalmia</note>, as well as the sores that form in the eyes. And if they give it to be drunk with wine: it cures the ill that comes from the retention of urine. And likewise for women who have illness because their flow <note>original: "fior," referring to menstruation</note> comes too strongly: it makes them lose that excess. And if they give it to be drunk to one who spits blood: it provides very great and immediate benefit. And he who wishes for this stone to perform its virtue more strongly: should burn it and make it into powder and give it to be drunk with wine: and it will have greater strength and work more than in any other way. But do not let it burn too much, lest it lose the sign of how much it should be burned, which is this: pay attention that as soon as it begins to lose its <unclear>color</unclear>, one should take it out immediately. And when they rub this stone on a whetstone: a red color comes from it that is very good for healing the mange and the itching that occurs in the eyes. And the two stars, the northern and the southern of the three that are in the left arm of the one who holds the bow <note>Sagittarius</note>, have power over this stone and from them it receives its force and virtue. And when both of these are in the ascendant <term>ascendant: the sign or star rising on the eastern horizon at a specific time</term>: this stone shows more force and greater virtue in all its works.

The third degree of the sign of Sagittarius: is the mineral stone they call **copper**. By nature, it is **hot and dry**, and it appears in various colors. One type tends toward **red**, and this is the best, provided it is a clear redness; the other type tends toward **black** and is not as vivid. This red variety is found in the mines located in the land of *Chalcos* <note>original: "calcoz," the Greek word for copper</note>; and it possesses a "male" power within it. It has a hidden quality <note>original: "alconcha"</note> that does not appear unless it is brought into contact with vinegar or another sour substance. For then, **green verdigris** <term>verdigris: a green pigment or crust (copper acetate) formed on copper, brass, or bronze</term> is created upon it, which is a very strong poison. And if they join this stone with that other stone called *berenich* <note>likely a reference to calamine or a similar mineral used to make brass</note>, of which we have already spoken in this book, and melt them both together with **quicksilver** <term>quicksilver: mercury</term>, it causes the mercury to harden in such a way that it becomes brittle and breaks. And if they melt the **brass** <note>original: "aram bresco"</note> with a little *mono* <note>possibly a mineral flux or arsenic</note> or a little borax, and then quench it in cold water, it turns the color of **fine gold**; however, if it is later brought back to the fire, it turns black. And this damage is even greater if they use it to store any roasted fish of any nature, because that food absorbs a foul smell and becomes poisonous. And if these medicines are ground upon a tablet of **emery** <note>original: "amivre"</note> or in a mortar made of the same, they will be better and work more quickly. And when they grind the emery and wash it, they make medicines from it to heal wounds and to cure the aforementioned diseases. However, he who wishes to work with it must be careful: he should not use it on delicate or soft bodies unless it has been **burnt** <term>burnt: calcined or purified by fire</term>; but on strong bodies, it may be used raw. And the southern star of the three located in the **feather of the arrow** <note>original: "fuyar," referring to the tail or fletching of the arrow in the Sagittarius constellation</note> has power over this stone, and from that star, the stone receives its virtue. And whenever that star is in mid-heaven, this stone demonstrates its effects most clearly.

The seventh degree of the sign of Sagittarius is the stone they call **calyxon**. The Arabs call it *çemí*. The 12th degree of the sign of Sagittarius belongs to the stone they call **arsenic** <note>original: "azarnech"; from the Arabic "al-zarnikh," referring to arsenic sulfides</note>. It is called *zuntaich* in Chaldean, and in Latin they call it *orpiment* <note>original: "orpiment"; from "auripigmentum" or gold pigment</note>. This stone is divided into three kinds: one which is red in color, another which is yellow and is named *zeurech*, and the third is white. In this book, each of these is shown for what it is. But first, it is proper to speak here of what pertains to them all together, and afterward we shall speak of each one by itself. This stone is found in many places and many mines, but the greatest of all is that which is found in the land named Eticonton. Its nature is hot and dry in the fourth degree, and it possesses a very great bitterness. And if they burn it until it turns as white as lime, and they mix with the copper <note>original: "azumbre"; while this usually means a liquid measure, in this alchemical context it likely refers to "alambre" or copper, which was famously "whitened" or turned gold-colored using arsenic in medieval alchemy</note> a little oil, and they treat the copper and put a little earth with it and some of this stone; when they melt it, it draws out a gold color from within and without, and makes it lose the foul odor it possesses; however, it is not natural gold. And if they burn the arsenic and make it into powder and rub it upon the teeth, it brings great benefit to gums that are being eaten away; and this is because it becomes a more subtle substance upon burning. And if they place it upon the hair, it removes it all; indeed, if it is left too long during the rubbing, it burns the flesh. These properties are shared by all these arsenics we have mentioned. But as for the red kind specifically, let us say that it is very beautiful to look upon: of a red color, very clear, clean, and easy to break. And if they grind it and knead it with the juice of **henbane** <note>original: "uisquiamo"; from the Latin "hyoscyamus"</note> and anoint the place where hair has been removed, the hair never grows there again. And mixed with manna, it heals the disease called *lopina* <note>a skin condition, likely mange or a form of scaly lupus</note>. And taking it with pitch, it softens the white spots <note>leukonychia</note> that form on the nails. It also enters into the medicines used against all diseases of the nose, and of the *uirax* <note>likely a type of ulcer or lesion</note>, and of sores, and of **fistulas** <term>fistula: an abnormal tunnel-like passage in the body</term>, and likewise of **hemorrhoids** <note>original: "amoroydas"</note>. And it is good to put into the medicines made for those who have phlegm in the

<column-break/>

chest. And if they use it as a fumigant for one who has an old cough, it clears the phlegm; even if they eat a little of it mixed with honey, it greatly clears the voice. And the star that is in front of the two dark ones in the northern arch of the **Corona** <note>the constellation Corona Borealis</note> has power over this stone, and from it the stone receives its virtue. And when it is in the ascendant, this stone shows its effects most completely.

### Of the stone that they call natron

<image-desc>A square illustration with a circular inner frame. A figure in a red cap and tunic stands on the left, gesturing towards a seated figure in an orange-yellow tunic on the right. At the **17th degree** <note>The OCR 'Alexu' is a common transcription error for the Roman numeral XVII (17th)</note> of the sign of Sagittarius is the stone they call **natron** <note>original: "anatron"; a naturally occurring soda ash/sodium carbonate used in ancient cleaning and glassmaking</note>. This is a kind of earth; it is also a mineral like salt. It is found in the land called Thrace <note>original: "taratte"</note> or Drama <note>original: "driemos"</note>.

We have found that it is similar to the other **red nitre** <note>original: "uivunē uermeio"; likely referring to a red variety of nitre or borax</note> in flavor and color, but this one has less power. By nature, it is hot and dry. It cleanses and purifies the filth of wounds, making them clear and clean, and it removes the excessive moisture that is in them; for this reason, it is good for strengthening the **nerves** <term>neruios: in medieval medicine, this often included tendons and ligaments</term>. In this stone, there is great knowledge and great benefit that the wise men found for working in the **Great Work** <note>The "Great Work" (obra mayor) refers to alchemy, specifically the creation of the Philosopher's Stone</note>, because it enters into it often, and it creates very beautiful and precious things. It has the same benefits as the red nitre. And the power that is beneath the "arm" of the three stars that are in the curves of the bow of Sagittarius has power over this stone, and from them, it receives its virtue. And when it is in the mid-heaven, it shows the effects of this stone most clearly through its works.

### Of the stone of salt

<image-desc>A square illustration with a circular inner frame. Two figures, one in yellow and one in blue robes, stand in a rocky landscape near a body of water, possibly harvesting salt or minerals. This miniature serves as a decorative initial 'E' for the word 'El'.</image-desc>

At the **18th degree** of the sign of Sagittarius is the **stone of salt**. This exists in many forms, and they find it in many places. Some are created in the lagoons of the sea, and they dig for them as they do in Phoenicia <note>original: "Fenicia"</note> within the sand. There is another kind that is in the form of a stone. And another that they call **rock salt** <note>original: "sal gema"; halite</note>, which is stony. And yet there is another kind also called rock salt which is likewise hard. All these varieties are those that they cook in the lagoons of the earth, and they are made by fire or by the heat of the sun; this is called **solar salt** <note>original: "sal de amallar"; likely referring to Al-Mahar or salt produced by evaporation</note>, and men who trade in others use this one the most. Some of this is found in the sands and in specific wells. But it is not appropriate here for us to speak of any except these three which are counted as stones: the one they call **Indian**, another called **rock salt**, and the third... <note>text cuts off or refers to the previously mentioned types</note>.

The **Indian salt** of which we wish to speak first is of a purple color, spotted with black drops. It is found mostly in the land of Ethiopia <note>original: "moria"</note>. It is strong and very hard to break, and it is hot and dry in the third degree. It has a very subtle flavor, and because of this, it has the power to cleanse bodies and to greatly brighten **gold** and **silver**, each in its own color. It removes impurities and subterranean greases; for this reason, they place it in the **Great Work**.

In most stones, there is mixed a very salty substance, which is somewhat lightning-like <note>original: "fulminea"; perhaps referring to a sparkling or reactive quality</note>. Because this explanation is very long and does not suit this book of ours, we do not wish to speak of it here. But of salt, we say that if they put it in the flesh of any animal, it preserves it by drying it and making the moistures leave it. Thus, it makes the body last a long time so that it does not rot, nor smell bad, nor spoil. There is no other stone that can do this except this one. However, there are other things that do this, such as **aloe**, **myrrh**, **camphor**, and **balsam**. But these do not work except by making the moisture that lies within the bodies dry up inside themselves; whereas salt, by squeezing the moisture, makes it leave the bodies and dries them out. And for this reason, it is good for men...

<summary>This page describes the medicinal and alchemical properties of natron (17th degree) and various types of salt (18th degree) under the sign of Sagittarius. It highlights their ability to cleanse wounds, purify precious metals, and preserve organic matter by extracting moisture.</summary>
<keywords>natron, salt, rock salt, Indian salt, Sagittarius, alchemy, Great Work, preservatives, medieval medicine, astrology</keywords>

### Of the stone that they call rock salt .27th
<note>The OCR reads ".xxvii." (27th degree). While the book usually follows a sequential order, the degrees in this section of the manuscript are sometimes non-linear.</note>

<image-desc>Historiated initial 'E' containing a scene of a seated scholar or physician in orange robes handing a small object (perhaps a piece of salt gema) to a standing man in a short tunic.</image-desc>

At the **27th degree** of the sign of Sagittarius is the stone they call **rock salt** <note>original: "sal gema"; halite or pure mineral salt</note>. This is of a stony substance, as we shall describe. Most of it is found in the land of **Armumaqui** <note>likely Armenia</note>.

By nature, it is hot and dry. It strongly prevents **proud flesh** <note>original: "mala carne"; the overgrowth of tissue during the healing of a wound</note> from growing in wounds. It is good for postumes that come from phlegm and for those that occur in the **uvula** <note>original: "p’opios" followed by "uina" (uvula); possibly referring to the tonsils or throat area</note>. It is frequently used in medicines made for diseases of the **uvula**, and also for **quinsy** <term>esquinancia: a severe, painful inflammation of the throat or tonsils</term>, which is a postume that grows in the throat. It heals **impetigo** <note>original: "empietros"; scaly or eruptive skin diseases</note>. If mixed with **honey-mixture** <note>original: "melruto"; likely a specific preparation of honey and rue or a similar herbal syrup</note>, it makes a plaster

<column-break/>

that is very good for the **mange** <note>original: "sarna del canacan"; likely a type of severe skin irritation or "mange of the canker"</note>. Furthermore, in Egypt, they make a plaster from it for **flesh-wasting fever** <note>original: "febre dela caronçada"; caronçada refers to the flesh</note> because it is better for this than any other medicine. It has the nature to cause change. If a little of it is given to drink, it acts as a **laxative** <note>original: "laxa"</note> and purges phlegm. It is used often in the works of **physic** <term>fisica: the medieval term for medicine and natural philosophy</term>. The star located in the **spine of the turtle**—which they call **the flying vulture** <note>original: "totyar uolant"; a corruption of the Latin 'Vultur Volans', referring to the star Altair</note>—has power over this stone and gives it its virtue. When it is in the ascendant, this stone shows its effects most completely.

### Of the stone that they call aramçar

It helps greatly in **smelting gold** because it softens it; thus, when they put them together, the gold melts so quickly because of it that it seems to be afraid of it. This stone is very helpful for the **decay** of the teeth and gums, and it kills...

### Of the stone they call *arep*
<note>arep: a transliteration of an Arabic term for alum</note>

<image-desc>A historiated initial 'E' containing a scene with two figures. On the left, a man in a long purple robe and a light-colored cap stands or sits, pointing upwards with one hand. Facing him on the right, a younger man in a shorter orange tunic and yellow hose is bowed or kneeling, appearing to listen or learn. The background within the letter is blue, and the initial is decorated with ornate red and blue flourishes.</image-desc>

In the **fourth degree** of the sign of Sagittarius is the stone they call **arep** in Arabic and **alum** <note>original: "alumbre"</note> in Latin. This name is given because they **brighten** <note>original: "auibran"; from 'avivar', to enliven or make vivid</note> and clarify all things that are cooked with it, each according to its nature. For those things used for **dyeing**, it makes the colors very beautiful and clear. The best of these are found in **Egypt** in a land they call **Miletus** <note>original: "miles"; likely referring to the ancient center of wool and textile production</note>. They are also found in **Greece** in a land they call **Madume** <note>original: "madumē"</note> in their language, and in Latin they call it **Macedonia**. These stones are found in many forms, but the three best kinds are: The first is what they call **split alum** in Latin <note>original: "sentida"; referring to 'alumen schiston' or splintery alum</note> and **caritiz** in Greek <note>original: "caritiz"</note>. The second is **round**, and they call it **sagnam** in Arabic. The third is **moist** <note>liquid</note>, and they call it **uguina** in Greek <note>original: "uguina", likely from 'hygros' meaning moist</note> and **aluima** in Arabic. Of these, there are some in which virtue is apparent, others that look like earth, and others that lean

<column-break/>

toward a yellow color. But despite this, when one tests them with the tongue, one finds they lean toward a **sour taste**. They break easily and are very white in color. The best of these is the **split** type, and in it, the **hair-like fibers** <note>original: "azeitit"; likely a reference to trichites or the fibrous structure of certain alums</note> are more apparent than in any of the others. Of the round variety, the best is the one that leans toward yellow. And of the moist variety, the best is that which is clear and the color of milk, being uniform in all its parts and having a **smell of fire** <note>perhaps referring to a sulfurous or sharp odor</note>. Because all these varieties are similar in nature and have power, we speak of them all here together. We say they are hot and moist with **astringency** <note>original: "restriñimiento"; the quality of shrinking or constricting body tissues</note>. For this reason, they are good for removing the **film** from the eyes <note>original: "tela de los oios"; likely cataracts or growths</note> and the **excess flesh** <note>original: "carne sobrada"; proud flesh or polyps</note> from any place it may be. They are used in the medicines made for **scabies** <note>original: "sarna"</note> that comes from too much moisture, and they are helpful for the **ulcers** <note>original: "nagas"; sores</note> that form in the mouth. If it is burned and mixed with something else and rubbed on the armpits, it removes the **bad odor** found there. It is also helpful for **abscesses** <note>original: "postiemas"</note> of the gums and for the wounds caused by the **scab** <note>original: "sarna"</note> that they call **scrofula** <note>original: "scophiulas"; a swelling of the lymph nodes</note>. Furthermore, it purifies the bodies of metals and makes them bright. It does even more: if one dissolves the **arep** until it flows like water, it **burns iron**, and for this reason, they use it much in the **Great Work** <term>obra mayor: the ultimate goal of alchemy, the creation of the philosopher's stone</term>. The star that is between the **eyes** <note>original: "oyas"; likely a variant of 'ojos'</note> of the three stars in the figure of Sagittarius has power over this stone, and from it the stone receives its strength and virtue. When it is in the **ascendant**, this stone shows its works more clearly.

# OF SAGITTARIUS

<meta>Foliation mark '19' in pencil at the bottom left corner.</meta>

->Of the stone named red *susre*<-

<image-desc>Decorative initial 'E' containing a miniature of two men in medieval robes; one is seated and gesturing while the other stands before him, possibly discussing the mineral described in the text.</image-desc>

In the **21st degree** of the sign of Sagittarius is the stone they call **red *susre*** <note>original: "susre uermelo"; likely a transliteration of the Arabic "shusra"</note>. It is a variety of the *susrine* stones we have already mentioned. However, this *susre* is a red stone and not very dark. It is found in the land of **Africa** near the part of the West, close to the **Atlantic Ocean**. When this stone is in its mine, it glows so brightly that from within it resembles a candle; but when it is removed, it loses this power. This is because its **spirit of nature** <term>spiritu de natura: the vital essence or alchemical property inherent in the substance</term> is like the others, and it shares the same properties in all its quantities. It has such a power that if a little of it is placed in the nose of one who is **possessed by a demon**, it drives the devil out and heals them. It does the same for that illness called **apoplexy** <note>original: "apõpusia"</note>, and likewise for the ailment called **migraine** <note>original: "cefalea" from Greek kephalaia</note> in Greek. It is used extensively in the crafting of gold, for it tints white gold red and gives it a fine color; for this reason, those who work with the **works of nature** <note>referring to alchemists or skilled goldsmiths</note> mix it frequently into their creations. The middle star of the three that are in the northern **headdress** <note>original: "toca"; refers to the stars forming the crown or top of the archer's head</note> of Sagittarius has power over this stone, and from it the stone receives its virtue. When it is in the **ascendant**, this stone demonstrates its effects most clearly.

<image-desc>A circular diagram of the constellation Sagittarius, depicted as a centaur archer with a bow and arrow. Various stars are marked as gold dots within the circle.</image-desc>

<column-break/>

->Of the stone they call *bizach*<-

<image-desc>Decorative initial 'E' containing a miniature of a seated figure, likely a scholar or physician, working at a desk or table.</image-desc>

In the **22nd degree** of the sign of Sagittarius is the stone they call **bizach** <note>likely *bijadi*, a medieval term for a variety of garnet</note>. This stone is red in color, such that it resembles the **jacinth** <note>original: "langonça"; a common medieval term for hyacinth or zircon gems</note> in its hue, but it does not withstand fire as that stone does; rather, it breaks in the heat and loses its color. Its best mines are in the East, and when they are taken from the mines, they have no brilliance at all, but after polishing, they become beautiful and clear. Its nature is **hot and dry**, though its heat is less than that of the jacinth and its dryness is greater. Its virtue is such that when one carries a weight of it equal to three **barleycorns** <term>granelhos de ordio: a medieval unit of weight</term> or more, they will not dream fearful dreams. If it is placed in the rays of the sun and then the eyes are touched with it, it causes the vision to diminish greatly <note>The text warns that this stone can harm the eyesight if used this way</note>. If it is warmed by being rubbed against the hair of the head and then placed on the ground, it **attracts feathers** and small straws <note>a description of static electricity, a property often noted in garnets and ambers</note>. The best of all these is the reddest and clearest. There is another kind called **merbech** <note>perhaps a variety of marcasite</note> which is not as red, nor does it attract feathers or straws as much as this other one we have described, yet it possesses all the same virtues. The last two stars of the three that are in the northern part of the **headdress** of Sagittarius have power over this stone, and from them it receives its virtue. When they are in **midheaven**, this stone demonstrates its effects most fully.

# OF THE SIGN

### Of the stone named ayuriquit.

<image-desc>A large historiated initial 'E' contains a scene of two figures in medieval tunics; one stands while the other kneels, both appearing to examine the ground for stones in a rocky landscape.</image-desc>

The **26th degree** <note>original: "xxxvi"; likely a transcription or scribal error for "xxvi" (26), as Sagittarius has only 30 degrees</note> of the sign of Sagittarius: is the stone they call **ayuriquit**. It is found in the **land of the blacks** <note>Sub-Saharan Africa</note> in a place called **Quini**, which belongs to the town called **Ateyvultz**. Its nature is that it is found atop a steep mountain; it is hard to break and shiny, of a **dun color** <note>original: "parda"; a grayish-brown</note> that turns toward red, resembling bone. By nature it is **hot and dry in the third degree** <term>degrees of nature: a medieval medical classification of a substance's potency from one to four</term>. It cleanses many bodies that are washed with it; it markedly improves the face, increases strength, kills lice, and makes the hair very beautiful. If the whole body is washed with it, it cleanses it of the filth it contains and thins the skin, giving it a good scent. It dissolves **abscesses** <note>original: "postemas"</note> and tumors, especially those that form on the face. If vinegar is poured upon this stone, it blisters and grows; if they continue to treat it with this, it thickens and will not dissolve with anything except vinegar. When it is dissolved this way, it gives off a scent like **wild rue** <note>original: "ruda montefina"</note>. If it is placed near the nose of one who frequently **faints** <note>original: "amortecer"</note>, it helps them. It is also effective against the illness called **apoplexy** <note>original: "apoushia"; a corruption of the Greek 'apoplexia'</note>. The star located **between the horns of the turtle** <note>original: "gallapago"; in medieval astronomy, the constellation Lyra was often depicted as a tortoise</note> has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its virtue. When it is in the **ascendant** <term>ascendant: the degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon</term>, this stone shows its works most clearly.

### Of the stone they call beynebryz.

<image-desc>A large historiated initial 'E' depicts a standing figure in an orange robe holding a staff or walking stick, gesturing toward a smaller youth in a blue tunic.</image-desc>

The **27th degree** <note>original: "xxxvii"; likely for "xxvii" (27)</note> of the sign of Sagittarius: is the stone they call **beynebryz**, which means as much as **water-hater** <note>transliterated from Arabic; the text explains the meaning as "one who puts water away"</note>. By nature it is hot and dry. It is found in the **Promised Land** <note>Palestine</note> to the east, on the shore of the lagoon they call **Dead** <note>The Dead Sea</note>, which is at the end of that land. It is strong and hard to break, shiny and clear like <unclear>glass</unclear> <note>original: "urlo"; likely 'vidrio'</note>, and the color of the sky. They always find it joined with other sharp stones, so that each of them cuts like a knife. Most of those they find are at the bottom of a vein at the end of that lagoon, or where a stone is hollowed out in the shape of a **grave** <note>original: "fuessa criatu̅a"</note>. The name of this stone is certain, for if they place it in any boiling substance other than water, it sinks to the bottom; but if they throw it into water, it leaps out as if it loathed it. If a man is given the weight of a <unclear>grain</unclear> <note>original: "pelo d'una llagma"; likely an error for 'grana' or a specific small measurement</note> to drink, it strongly purges **yellow bile** <note>original: "colera"</note>. ### Of the stone they call Leplenzeech: 28.

<image-desc>An illuminated initial 'E' containing a scene of a person sitting in a wooden wash-tub while another person in red and yellow robes attends to them, possibly bathing or performing a medicinal treatment.</image-desc>

> The **28th degree** of the sign of Sagittarius: is the stone they call **Leplenzeech**. This name means as much in Chaldean <note>original: "caldeo"; referring here to Aramaic, the language of ancient scholarship</note> as **stancher of veins**. For it has such virtue that whoever carries it with them: it mitigates the flows <note>original: "uinas"; here meaning veins or bodily discharges</note> that run from a man while he sleeps. And it does the same for small children who wet themselves at night, in such a way that the urine <note>original: "uino"; likely a scribal error for "orina" (urine)</note> that passes through them appears to have a reddish color. It is smooth <note>original: "liniana"; possibly meaning light or smooth-textured</note> with a strong and hard color. But because of this: it breaks very easily when brought to the touchstone <note>original: "amagante"; a stone used to test the quality of metals or a polishing tool</note>. This stone is found at the bottom of the lagoon they call **Yez**, which is in the eastern part of the **Promised Land** <note>original: "tierra de promission"; referring to the region of Palestine, likely identifying the lagoon as the Dead Sea</note>. The water of this lagoon is very salty, and in color it resembles camphor <note>original: "acafarnada"; meaning translucent or whitish like camphor</note>. By nature it is **hot and dry**. And if they give it ground to drink, about half a drachm <note>term: "dragma" (drachm); an ancient unit of weight, roughly 3.5 grams</note> with a little vinegar: it heals the illness they call **gout**. And likewise it helps with pain of the stomach and the entrails, and it benefits the liver greatly when it is weak or chilled. And the two stars—the one in the right hind leg and the other which is in the front of the northern side, which is in the quadrangle formed at the root of the tail of Sagittarius—have power over this stone and upon it their virtue descends. And when it is in the **midheaven** <note>original: "medio cielo"; the highest point a celestial body reaches in the sky</note>: this stone shows its works most clearly.

### Of the stone they call Saruquz: 29.

<image-desc>An illuminated initial 'E' containing a scene of a person in blue and green garments standing in an outdoor setting, using a staff or tool to work with materials in a stone-lined pit or kiln.</image-desc>

> The **29th degree** of the sign of Sagittarius is the stone they call **Saruquz**. This is found in the land they call **Sarugua**, and from it the stone takes its name. And the place where they find it is called **Adrancz**, or a bath <note>original: "uano"; likely 'baño' or bath</note> in which there is a very long and hot cave by nature; thus the water falls there in rays <note>meaning jets or streams</note> through its joints and onto the stones, which are strong and hard, from which they make the balls <note>original: "pelotas"</note> that when they are taken from the cave are like soft and friable powder. But after they are brought out: they are very black in color and shine somewhat. And if one drinks it as a lethal poison in the weight of one drachm: it tears the entrails and kills by causing one to bleed. And if the dregs of the earth are burned and the fire is in it: then if they moisten it with water, it burns all things it finds that can be burned; and this fire cannot be extinguished <note>original: "amatar"</note> with anything else except with **vinegar**. By nature it is **hot and dry**. And if they throw it into water and it lies there for some time, it has benefit for all those things that the water of **caustic baths** <note>original: "uinos caucios"; likely 'baños cáusticos' or hot springs</note> has for the man who bathes in it. And the two stars—the one that follows the one on the northern side and the first one from the southern part, both of which are in the quadrangle formed at the root of the tail of Sagittarius—have power over this stone and from them its virtue descends. And when they are in the **ascendant** <note>original: "asceniente"; the degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon</note>, this stone shows its works most clearly.

# **Of the stone called muludyntas:**

<image-desc>A large historiated initial 'E' decorated in blue and gold with red accents. Inside the letter, two figures are shown against a blue background: a standing man in a light-colored tunic holding a vessel, and another man in a red-orange tunic bending down, possibly examining the ground or the stone mentioned. Perched atop the initial is a green dragon or basilisk with wings patterned in red and blue.</image-desc>

The **30th degree** of the sign of Sagittarius belongs to the stone they call **muludyntas**. This is found in the land of **Syria** more than in any other place, at the bottom of a river that runs near the city they call **Cairo** <note>original: "cayre"; while Cairo is in Egypt, medieval texts often used "Syria" to refer broadly to the Levant and surrounding regions, or may be referring to a different localized settlement</note>. Its nature is **hot and dry**. Its color is black, streaked with yellow veins. It is rough to the touch and light in weight.

And it possesses a strange property: when it is cast into water, it sinks to the bottom, but if it is cast into wine, it floats to the top <note>original: "anda aresuso nadando"; literally, it goes upward swimming</note>. And if they grind it and mix it with honey, it heals **hot abscesses** <term>postemas: inflammatory swellings or boils</term>. And if it is held upon the hair, it kills **lice**; and if any are born afterward, they are weaker than the first; and if they continue to anoint the hair many times in this manner, they are born no more. It is also good for medicines made for the eyes, for it soothes their tenderness <note>original: "muelle la blandura"; likely meaning it relieves inflammation or sensitivity in the eyes</note>.

And the star located on the southern side of the quadrangle formed at the base of the tail of **Sagittarius** has power over this stone, and from that star, the stone receives its virtue. And when this star is at the **midheaven** <note>original: "medio del cielo"; the highest point in the sky reached by a celestial body</note>, this stone manifests its effects most perfectly.

The figure is drawn in black ink with yellow-brown washes. Several stars are marked on the centaur's body: one on the tail, one on the hindquarters, one on the back, and others on the human torso, corresponding to astronomical positions.</image-desc>

# **OF CAPRICORN**

->Prologue<-

Many are the thirty kinds of stone according to the thirty degrees of the sign of **Capricorn**. It is necessary that whoever wishes to work effectively with these should observe the planet **Jupiter**, ensuring that it is well-received in that star with which he performs his work; and likewise the **Lord of the Face** <note>This refers to the planetary ruler of the specific ten-degree "decan" or face of the zodiac sign</note>, that it be in a good state for works of good, and the contrary for works of evil.

### Of the stone they call tutty

<image-desc>Miniature within the historiated initial 'E' depicting two men in a rocky landscape; one man is seated on a rock while the other stands before him, both appearing to examine the ground or stones.</image-desc>

The **first degree** of the sign of Capricorn belongs to the stone they call **tutty** <term>tutya: a mineral form of zinc oxide, highly valued in antiquity for medicinal uses</term>. This is of three kinds. The first is **white** and they call it **Indian**. The second is **green** and is named **marine**. The third is **yellow**, leaning toward **reddish**, and they call it **Spanish**. And of these we shall speak later in their place, but here we will speak first of that which is called Indian. This is found in the **Indian Sea**, and from this it takes its name; it is the best, though it is found in other places, such as the land of **Carnos**. It is white in color and resembles the dust of **vinegar-salt** <note>original: "sal acetillo"; likely a crystalline mineral deposit or an acetate salt</note>. It is very light in weight, clear in color, and by nature it is **cold and dry**. And if it is cast into **vinegar**, an odor like **camphor** comes from it. It has the power to **restrain and to comfort** <note>In medieval medicine, to "restrain" meant to act as an astringent, and to "comfort" meant to strengthen an organ or tissue</note> greatly; it makes flesh grow in **wounds** and joins them together; it cools the moisture of medications and removes the bad odor that forms there. And it also clears away **tears from the eyes** and prevents them from running. And when they grind it and wash it with **wine**, it does this much better. This Indian variety is the most praised of all stones of this nature. And the star that is in the **right shoulder of the Eagle**, which is called **Vaitaz Volant** <note>original: "vaitaz uolant," from the Arabic "al-nasr al-ta'ir," meaning "the flying eagle"; this refers to the star Altair</note>, has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its virtue. And when it is in the **ascendant**, this stone shows its works most clearly.

<column-break/>

<image-desc>Circular medallion containing an illustration of an eagle (representing the constellation Aquila) with its wings partially spread. A small green stone is depicted on its breast.</image-desc>

### Of the stone named green tutty

<image-desc>Miniature within the historiated initial 'E' showing a man in a red tunic standing and gesturing toward a seated figure who is using a mortar and pestle to grind materials on the ground.</image-desc>

The **second degree** of the sign of Capricorn is the stone they call **green tutty**, which is called **marine**. The mine for this is on the seashore of the land of **Anforran**. In color it is green and **rough to the touch**, and it is heavier than the first and of thicker substance. By nature it is **cold and dry**; it has the power to **cool**. Through its restorative power it removes the **film from the eyes** and is good for **cancerous wounds**, as well as for **blisters** and eye sores. And if they grind it and knead it with water and make **tablets** <term>tutios: medicinal pellets or lozenges prepared from the mineral</term> of it, and dry them in the shade, they will then be better for all these works. And the **southern star** of the two that are in the **Heart of the Tortoise** <note>original: "coro del galapago"; this refers to the constellation Lyra, which was often visualized as a tortoise-shell lyre</note> has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its virtue. And when it is in **mid-heaven** <note>The "Medium Coeli," the highest point the star reaches in the sky</note>, this stone shows its works most clearly.

<summary>This page introduces the sign of Capricorn and its first two medicinal stones, both varieties of tutty (zinc oxide). It details their origins in India and Anforran, their healing properties for wounds and eyes, and their astrological links to the stars Altair and Lyra.</summary>

# **OF THE SIGN**

### Of the stone named Spanish stone

The **fourth degree** of the sign of **Capricorn** belongs to the stone of **yellow tutty** <term>tutya: a mineral form of zinc oxide used in medieval medicine</term> which they call **Spanish stone**. And this is born in the land of **Spain**, from where it takes its name. And they also find it in **Arabia** from the district of **Mahra** <note>original: "an rordem de mayuaria"; likely referring to the Mahra region of the Arabian Peninsula</note>, but this one from Spain is coarser than the others, and heavier, and with less clarity. By nature it is **cold** and **dry**, and therefore it is retentive; it dries much, and there is in it a certain stinging quality. And it is a better medicine than any other for the sores that occur in the **private parts** <note>original: "partes uergonnosas"; a standard medieval medical term for the genitals</note>. And it prevents humors from passing through the membranes of the eyes, and strengthens the sight and sharpens it. And the star that is in the **notch of the arrow** <note>Referring to a star in the constellation Sagitta</note> has power over this stone, and from the stone the star receives its virtue. And when it is in **mid-heaven** <note>The point where a celestial body reaches its highest position in the sky</note>, this stone shows its works most clearly.

<column-break/>

### Of the stone they call zebeth

The **fourth degree** of the sign of **Capricorn** is the stone they call **zebeth** <term>zebeth: likely jet (azabache), a type of lignite used for jewelry and mirrors</term>. It is hard, of a very black color, light in weight, and easy to break; and it shines like a **mirror**, though the sight does not pass through it. In many places they find the mines for it, but the largest of them are those found in the **islands of India**. By nature it is **cold and dry** in the third degree. And if they grind it and mix it with the medicines made to strengthen the sight of the eyes, it helps much. And if they make a mirror of it and use it to look into, it strengthens the sight greatly, whether the eyes be weak from old age or from sickness. This stone, when they take it from the mine, is shaped like **slabs**, some thick and others thin. And afterwards they work it in whatever way they wish, but it is not good for a man to always carry it with him, because for the one who carries it, **sorrows** happen to him. And the leading star of those that are on the **left shoulder of the Eagle** <note>The constellation Aquila</note> has power over this stone, and from the stone the star receives its virtue. And when it is in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works more completely.

<summary>This page describes two minerals linked to the fourth degree of Capricorn: "Spanish" yellow tutty, used for treating sores and eye ailments, and "zebeth" (jet), a black stone used to strengthen vision but believed to cause sadness if carried.</summary>

# **OF CAPRICORN**

### Of the stone they call elima

The **fifth degree** of the sign of **Capricorn** belongs to the stone they call **elima**. This is found in many places, for they find it in **silver mines**, or in the **furnaces** where they are accustomed to smelt the ore. Some are found in **rivers** where the water runs very fiercely, because the movement of the sand and earth uncovers them, and they are found there wrapped within it. Others are found on the **riverbanks**, which are more natural than those we have mentioned, and are considered better among the good stones; and it is of these we wish to speak before the others. This stone is formed in the shape of a **bunch of grapes**, and for this reason, they call it in **Arabic** *ancoti* <note>original: "ancoti"; from the Arabic 'unqūdī, meaning grape-like</note>, which means the same as **grape-like** <note>original: "rrazimena"</note>. Its color is **black**, of a thick substance, and somewhat light in weight. Some of those found are **ash-colored**, and others are the color of **azingur** <term>azingur: likely referring to a blue-green or verdigris color, common in mineral slag or copper byproducts</term>, and these are the best. By nature, it is **cold** and **dry**, and therefore it greatly dries the things upon which it is placed. It retains the **humors** <note>In medieval medicine, humors were the bodily fluids—blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile—that governed health</note> so that they do not flow. For this reason, it is put into the **medicines** made for the **eyes**, or for other places where they do not want the humors to descend and cause harm. And the star that is in the **mouth of the hen** <note>The star Albireo in the constellation Cygnus (the Swan, often called the Hen in medieval texts)</note> is said to have power over this stone, and from it, the stone receives its virtue. And when that star is in the **ascendant** <note>The degree of the zodiac rising over the eastern horizon at a specific moment</note>, this stone shows its works most clearly.

<column-break/>

### Of the stone that is named carnelian

The **sixth degree** of the sign of **Capricorn** belongs to the stone they call **alaq** <note>original: "alaq"; likely a variation of the Arabic 'aqīq</note>, which in **Greek** and in **Latin** is called **cornelina** <note>Translated as Carnelian</note>. This is of a **reddish color** that leans somewhat toward **yellow**. It is clear and shining in such a way that the sight passes through it. The one that has these signs is the best and most noble, for others resemble the **watery fluid** that comes out of meat when it is pressed. Some are found that are whiter and appear very clouded. The **mines** of this stone are in many places, such as in the **River Vizmaya** <note>An unidentified geographical location, possibly corrupted from an Arabic source</note>, in **Yemen**, in the rivers of that sea, and also in the **land of Rome**, and in many other parts. This stone is of a **cold** and **dry** nature and is much loved by men for its beauty, and because it helps greatly through the **virtue** <note>In this context, "virtue" refers to a stone's inherent magical or medicinal power</note> it possesses. For it has within itself three great and good virtues: the first is that it helps those who have a **voice** for **public speaking** when they carry it with them, for it gives them the **courage** to reason without fear, and further helps them to do so elegantly. The second is that it is good for **stopping blood** when it flows too much, and especially for **women** when it flows more than it should. And the third virtue is that it benefits the **teeth**; when they grind it into **powder** and rub it over them, it **cleanses** them and makes them bright, and it makes the **flesh grow** <note>Referring to the healing or strengthening of the gums</note> upon them and makes...

likewise, it makes the gums very red. However, the variety that truly has the power to **stanch blood** seems stronger than all the others; and this is the one that has the **color of the water that comes out of meat when salt is applied to it** <note>This refers to the reddish brine or "juice" of salted meat</note>. This variety works better than the others on the **teeth**, just as we have said, and it does even more: it heals the **sores** <note>original: "aiouas"; likely dental abscesses or ulcers</note> that form at the roots of the teeth and stops the blood that comes from the gums. ### Of the stone named almarfac . 7

<image-desc>An illuminated initial 'E' depicting an interior scene where an older man in a blue robe and red cap gestures toward a younger man in a brown tunic who is working with a hammer on an object. The background is blue with white dots.</image-desc>
The **seventh degree** <note>The OCR reads "sereno," but contextually this is the "seteno" or seventh degree</note> of the sign of **Capricorn** belongs to the stone they call **almarfac** <note>From the Arabic "al-marqashitha," meaning Marcasite</note>. There are some of these that are **artificial** and others that are **natural**, of which we wish to speak now because they are counted among the others. The best of them are found in the land called **Tachitav Raue** <note>A phonetic transcription of an Arabic place name, possibly in the region of modern-day Iran or Iraq</note> and also in **India**. Its color is **reddish** and it looks like **soot** <note>original: "fomita"; likely referring to a dusty or carbon-like texture</note>. It is **hard**, yet it does not burn by itself from the heat of the earth, but it is **easy to break**. By nature, it is **cold and dry**, and therefore it dries things out greatly and preserves and cleanses the things upon which it is placed. However, its strength is not very great, nor is its appearance very remarkable; but with all that,

<column-break/>

it is very helpful for **itching** and for the **sores** that arise from it. And when they mix it with **honey**, a very good **medicine** is made from it which cools moderately, soothes pain, removes **rotted flesh** <note>Refers to necrotic tissue in a wound</note> from sores, and joins them together to heal. And when they **burn it**, it has even greater power in these things. This stone tightens and dries things out significantly. For this reason, when it is burned and mixed with a little **rock salt** <note>original: "sal gema"</note>, it becomes very white; because of this, they use it in the **work of alchemy** <note>The medieval precursor to chemistry, focused on the transformation of matter</note>. But how this is to be done is not put in this book, as it is not appropriate here. And the **following star** of the two that are in the **left shoulder of the flying vulture** <note>original: "uientre uolant" likely a scribe's error for "uultre uolant," referring to the constellation Aquila, the Eagle</note> has power over this stone and from it, the stone receives its virtue. And when the star is in the middle of its path, this stone performs its works much more clearly.

<image-desc>An illustration of an eagle (Aquila) with dark brown plumage and detailed feathers, shown in profile with its head turned to the left and wings partially spread.</image-desc>

### Of the stone they call almagra . 8

<image-desc>An illuminated initial 'E' depicting two men: one on the left in a blue hooded robe handing a small red stone or object to a man on the right dressed in a red tunic. The background is dark blue.</image-desc>
The **eighth degree** of the sign of **Capricorn** is the stone they call **almagra** <note>Red ochre or hematite</note>. This comes in three types. One is made from **burnt bricks**, of which it is not appropriate for us to speak; the other is the type we wish to speak of in this book. Although it is found in many places, the best of all is that which is found in a land named **Cefinnat** <note>Possibly a reference to Sinai or a specific mining region in the East</note>.

->**OF CAPRICORN**<-

Its color is like **liver**, and it is of **thick substance** and **very heavy**, with its qualities balanced in equal parts. Its nature is **cold and dry**. When it is stirred in water, it **burns** intensely <note>This likely refers to a chemical reaction or a sensation of heat when the mineral powder is mixed with liquid</note>. It is known by science and by rule that it is included in **medicines** made for **bloody fluxes** <note>original: "menazones"; refers to dysentery or excessive menstrual flow</note>. Also, because it is **drying** <note>original: "dessecatina"</note>, it effectively joins parts that have been separated. To make its effect stronger, its powder should be mixed into a **soft-boiled egg**; then it shows its power more and greatly aids **liver pain**. If hot **abscesses** <note>original: "postemas cauientes"</note> are anointed with it, it is very beneficial. Likewise, it is very good for **intestinal sores**, for those who **spit blood**, and it aids **chronic diarrhea** <note>original: "diarrenaçoes antiguas"</note>. If it is given to drink or administered as an **enema** <note>original: "cristel"</note>, it kills the **worms** that form in the intestines. The two stars—the **southern** and the **northern**—of the three that are in the **hind horn** of the figure of **Capricorn** have power over this stone, and from them it receives its strength and virtue. When they are in the **ascendant**, this stone shows its effects most clearly.
