## Of the whetstone.

<image-desc>An illuminated initial 'E' containing a scene of craftsmanship. Inside the letter, one figure in a blue robe stands on the right holding a book, while two other figures on the left are at work. One is kneeling and using a tool on a circular whetstone or slab. The background is gold leaf, and the letter is decorated with blue, red, and green foliate patterns that extend into the margin.</image-desc>

The **ninth degree** of the sign of **Capricorn** belongs to the **whetstone** <note>original: "piedra de aguzar"</note>. This stone is very well known to men and is found in many places and in various colors. But the **best and most noble** is the **green** one of which this book speaks. They call it the **touchstone of gold** <note>original: "aguzadera del oro"</note> because it reveals the quality of gold to anyone who wishes to see it. It is soft and easy to break, and its nature is **cold and dry**. If the water that comes off it when iron is sharpened is used to rub the ailment called **alopecia** <note>original: "lopiça"; hair loss</note>, it heals it and makes **hair grow**. Whoever drinks this water mixed with **vinegar** will see the **swelling** <note>original: "postema"</note> that grows in the **spleen** <note>original: "baço"</note> diminish, and it aids the sickness they call **seizures** <note>original: "temonio"; often used in medieval texts to refer to epilepsy or conditions attributed to demonic influence</note>. If the **private parts** <note>original: "mienbros uergonnosos"</note> of small children are anointed with it, it prevents them from growing too large. If one rubs on this stone the **gallstone** <note>original: "anmbre"; a stony substance</note> found in the **gall of goats**, it greatly aids the **sores** that form in a man's **armpits** <note>original: "soforra"</note>. Mixed with **vinegar** and **natron** <note>original: "anatron"; a natural soda or salt</note>, it also helps greatly with **scabies**, **itching**, and the small swellings called **scrofula** <note>original: "scrophulas"; a form of tuberculosis affecting the lymph nodes of the neck</note>. If it is ground and placed in the **eyes**, it removes the **whiteness** <note>original: "blancura"; likely referring to cataracts or corneal scarring</note> that forms in them. The three stars—the first and the last of the three in the **mouth of Capricorn**—have power over this stone, and from them it receives its strength and virtue. When they are in **mid-heaven**, this stone shows its works most completely.

<summary>This page describes two minerals associated with the sign of Capricorn: a liver-colored stone used for digestive and blood ailments, and the whetstone, prized for its medicinal ability to treat hair loss, skin conditions, and eye issues.</summary>

-># OF THE SIGN<-

#### Of the stone they call talc.

<image-desc>An illuminated initial letter 'E' containing a scene of two figures: an older bearded man in a red robe handing a white circular object (likely the stone talc) to a younger man in a short tunic.</image-desc>

**T**he tenth degree of the sign of Capricorn is the stone they call **talc** <note>This refers to mica or foliated talc, prized for its transparency and heat resistance</note>. This is formed from the **dew** <note>original: "rucio"</note> that descends from the air at night and settles upon the earth, forming like **layers** or veils one on top of the other. In Arabic, they call it *alkaçh*. It also has another name in Arabic, *aitut alaraqa*, which means **sweat of the lime-kiln** <note>original: "suor de nura"</note>. Its color is like **crystals** <note>original: "crichas"</note>, and it is found in many places, such as in the land of **Barquiva**, in **Nemet**, and in **Tabriz**. When it is peeled or flaked, it **shines** greatly; for this reason, they use it in some places to make **windowpanes** <note>original: "uinbricas"</note> for baths, as it is like glass; and the thinner the sheets appear, the more light and clear they are. It has a very marvelous virtue: if it is struck with a hammer or any other thing, it does not shatter except into **flakes**. However, if it is placed in a thick woolen cloth along with **pebbles**, and rubbed very vigorously, it is entirely ground down by that friction and turns into **powder**. With this, they heal the body that has suffered some illness, and for this reason, it is used in the **Great Work** <note>original: "ovra mayor"; refers to the Magnum Opus of alchemy</note>. Its nature is **cold and dry**. And if one should anoint

<column-break/>

any limb with it, the **fire** will not burn it as easily as one that was not anointed. It has the power to **constrict** greatly. For this reason, it stops the blood of those who **spit it up** due to some illness; it does the same for women when they experience **excessive flow**. Likewise, it is beneficial for **abscesses** that form in the breasts. It does the same for those that develop on the members of men after **circumcision** <note>original: "sunnate"; from the Arabic 'sunnat'</note>, and for those that form under the **ears**, and for all manner of flesh that is inflamed by infection. It even goes further, for it cleanses the **sores** <note>original: "llagas"</note> that form on the **fingertips** <note>original: "gatos en cima de los deuon"; likely referring to whitlows or paronychia</note> and heals them. The **southern star** of the three that are in the **tail** of the figure of Capricorn has power over this stone, and from it, the stone receives its strength and virtue. When this star is in the **ascendant**, the stone shows its effects most clearly.

<image-desc>An illustration of Capricorn, a goat with a fish tail, facing right, similar to the one in the first column but without the circular frame.</image-desc>

#### Of the stone azie.

<image-desc>An illuminated initial letter 'E' containing a scene of two men: on the left, an older man in a red robe holds a stone; on the right, a man in a red tunic and cap works the ground with a tool, possibly mining.</image-desc>

**T**he eleventh degree of the sign of Capricorn is the stone they call **azie** <note>Likely a form of vitriol or chalcitis, used in medieval chemistry</note>. Its nature is **cold and dry** in the second degree, and it is easy to break. It is found in many places, but the best of all is that which is found in **Italy** <note>original: "latin"</note> in a place called **Mates**. Its color is **gray** <note>original: "parda"</note> but inclines a little toward **yellow**.

-># ON CAPRICORN<-

This stone is of great [value], and if it is ground and mixed with the **internal membranes** <note>original: "senaduuas"</note> of the **pomegranate** <note>original: "mateu rothi," likely a transliteration of an Arabic term for a specific variety of pomegranate</note>, and then mixed with water and applied to **wooden beams** that are split or which one wishes to join together, it joins them so well that no mark appears where they were split or joined. It is a stone that **softens** greatly; it retains [its power] and removes the **darkness of the sight**. And likewise, when mixed with water and used to anoint the **hot abscesses** <note>A term for painful, inflamed swellings or boils</note> that form in the **breasts** of women or in their **genitals**, or in the **virile member** of men, it is of great benefit and takes away the pain and heals them. And the **star** that is in the **right knee** <note>original: "corua diestra"</note> of Capricorn has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its strength and virtue. And when this star is in **midheaven** <note>The point where the star reaches its highest position in the sky</note>, this stone demonstrates its works most abundantly.

### Of the stone named caldonuquinda

The **twelfth degree** of the sign of Capricorn belongs to the stone they call **calatnuquida**. Its color is a very clear **red**, such that the sight passes through it. And he who has sharp vision, if he looks closely into it, will see inside the **figure of a stag** made of yellow lines; and even if it were broken into four pieces, this same figure would appear in every one of them.

<column-break/>

It is strong and **hard to break**, and heavy. And they find it in a **riverbed** <note>original: "auena," referring to a dry stream or valley</note> called **Samuy**, which is in the land called **Cenbuquid**, which is near the **Dayan of Moia** <note>Likely a geographical reference to a specific valley or territory</note>. And in that riverbed there are many other kinds of stones of which this wise man already knew and spoke of in their proper places; but this one of which we speak is found in this riverbed **clinging** as if it were growing there, and it can be taken with the hand. It is marked by many shapes, some large and others small. Its nature is **cold and dry** and in the fourth degree.

¶ The **first [virtue]** is that he who carries it with him will never be found **dead in water** <note>i.e., it protects against drowning</note>. The **second** is that if a man drinks the weight of one **drachma** <note>A historical unit of weight, roughly 3.4 grams</note> of it, it purges **melancholy** <note>One of the four humors; an excess was thought to cause sadness or depression</note> in a balanced and effective way.

¶ The **third** is that if it is hung over the **abscesses** that form in a man's **throat**, it causes them to dry up and heal. The **fourth** is that for one who gazes at it often, it strengthens the **sight of the eyes** and heals the illnesses that occur in those whose vision is becoming **clouded**. And the **three stars**—the northern and the southern ones—that are in the **neck** of the figure of Capricorn have power over this stone, and from them it receives its strength and virtue. And when they are in **midheaven**, this stone shows its work more manifestedly.

# Of the stone they call calarin .2.

<image-desc>A historiated initial 'E' containing a scene of two figures: on the left, a man in a red tunic sits gesturing toward another man on the right who is standing and working a piece of stone or metal on an anvil with a hammer. The background is blue with a white circular pattern.</image-desc>

The **thirteenth degree** of the sign of **Capricorn** belongs to the stone they call **calarin** <note>original: "çalin"</note>. This name comes from a mountain located in the lands known as **Acoxes**, which means "castles of stone" <note>likely a transliteration of the Arabic *al-Quṣūṣ*</note>. This mountain is large and very high, and its name is **Aurun**. The mines for this stone are found at its peak, and the stone takes its name from it. It is very heavy but easy to break. When it is broken, the inside is found to be like **coarse sand**. Its color is black, and it has **green veins**. If it is burned in fire, its body becomes very hard, so much so that it cannot be broken except with a large hammer; however, it receives no other property from the fire except that it hardens. Its nature is **cold and dry** in the third degree. When it is burned, a very good medicine is made from it that **constricts** and **cleanses** effectively; for this reason, it is good for **hot abscesses** <note>original: "postemas camientes," referring to inflamed swellings</note>, and specifically for the one called a **carbuncle** <note>A severe, painful cluster of boils</note>, for by applying it frequently, it prevents the abscess from forming. If it is made into powder and rubbed on the **gums**, it heals the **cankers** <note>original: "cauaduras"</note> that form there, as well as **itching of the mouth**. It also helps against all **tightness of breath** <note>original: "ensangostamiento del fuelgo"</note>, of whatever nature it may be. And it has another very strange virtue: if it is ground and kneaded with **wine** and shaped like an **acorn** and placed in a **woman's nature** <note>original: "natura dela mugier," a euphemism for the vagina</note>, it prevents her from becoming pregnant. And the **star** that is in the **curved left knee** of the figure of Capricorn has power over this stone, and from it the stone receives its strength and virtue. When this star is in the **ascendant** <note>The point of the zodiac rising over the eastern horizon</note>, it shows its works most completely.

<column-break/>

<image-desc>A circular illustration of the zodiac sign Capricorn, depicted as a goat with the head and forelegs of a land animal and a long, coiled fish-like tail. The goat is leaping toward the right.</image-desc>

# Of the stone named capria .2.

<image-desc>A historiated initial 'E' containing two figures working in a cave or mine. Both figures hold hammers or picks and appear to be extracting stones from the walls. The background is blue.</image-desc>

The **twenty-second degree** of the sign of **Capricorn** belongs to the stone they call **capria**, which means **capriotria**. It is a soft stone and easy to break; its strength is activated quickly in **water**, but not in anything else. Its color is **dark green**, and it has a delicate body. It is often found in the land of **Egypt**, and those who **treat cloth** use it, for it **whitens** them quickly and well. Its nature is **cold and dry**. This virtue it has for whitening cloth exists because its nature is contrary [to the stains]. It **stanches blood** in women when they bleed more than they should <note>referring to excessive menstrual bleeding</note>. It is included in medicines made to **close wounds**, especially those that occur in **soft and moist** bodies. This stone has no taste at all; if its strength is extracted with water, it helps against **pain of the bladder** <note>original: "uerciga"</note> and stanches every kind of **flux** <note>original: "menazon," referring to diarrhea or dysentery</note>. And the **northern star** of the three that are in the **wing feathers** <note>original: "pennola del ala"</note> of the right wing of the **Hen** <note>original: "gallina," the constellation Cygnus</note> has power over this stone, and from it the stone receives its strength and virtue. When it is in **midheaven**, this stone shows its works most completely.

## Of the stone of Sodom

The **sixteenth degree** of the sign of **Capricorn** belongs to the **stone of Sodom**. This stone is black and dark, and its surface appears weathered by the wind <note>original: "assu de uiento," possibly implying a porous or air-eroded texture</note>, yet it is strong and hard to break. When it is broken, the inside is found to be of this same appearance. It is found in the mountains of **Sodom**, from which it takes its name, and is discovered there in various ways; some pieces are large, others small, and they come in many shapes. Its nature is **cold and dry** in the first degree. It possesses such virtue that if it is ground and made into a <term>plaster|a soft, heated medicated mass spread on cloth and applied to the skin</term> and placed over the bladder, it breaks the stone that grows there. It also heals the illness that causes **dribbling urine** <note>likely referring to strangury or urinary incontinence</note>, or when one must strain with great force to urinate. The star located in the **neck of the Hen** <note>original: "gallina," referring to the constellation Cygnus</note> has power over this stone, and from it, the stone receives its strength and virtue. When this star is in the **midheaven** <note>the highest point in the path of a celestial body</note>, the stone manifests its effects most completely.

<column-break/>

## Of the stone they call bitarriquid

The **seventeenth degree** of the sign of **Capricorn** belongs to the stone they call **bitarriquid** <note>likely a transliteration of an Arabic mineral name</note>. This is found in the land called **Lynar** and also in **Tabroz**; in both of these places, it is found in wells. When it is first pulled out of them, it is **soft like wax**, but after it feels the air, it hardens. Its color is reddish and very dark. Its nature is **cold and dry** in the first degree and dry in the third; therefore, dryness is more prevalent in it than coldness. It possesses an astringent quality and dryness along with a certain sharpness, and its flavor is composed in this same manner. For this reason, it is beneficial for **foul and putrid sores**, and especially for those that form in the **mouth**. If the **male organ** <note>original: "uirgella," a diminutive of "virga" (rod), used here as a medical euphemism</note> should be scratched or cut, and they apply this stone ground and mixed with honey, it heals very quickly; it also protects against the dangers that usually arise during such an act <note>this may refer to complications following circumcision or surgery</note>. It likewise heals the wounds that occur on the head or the forehead where the flesh is greatly worn or sunken. If its powder is placed upon hair that is very thick, it thins it and makes it very beautiful. The star in the **left shoulder of Capricorn** has power over this stone.

<summary>This page describes the medicinal properties of the Stone of Sodom (used for urinary ailments) and Bitarriquid (a wax-like stone used for healing sores and cosmetic hair thinning).</summary>

**Of the stone.** The **eighteenth degree** of the sign of **Capricorn** belongs to the stone they call **guisirquiza**. This name means in **Chaldean** <note>original: "caldeo"</note> "guardian of children." This stone resembles an acorn in form and color. It is found in a river named **Zeyle** that flows in the western part of the **Promised Land** <note>original: "tierra de pmission"</note>. And if it is given ground in a drink to a man who has pain in his intestines, it heals him; it also works for the pain of the **stone** <note>kidney or bladder stones</note>. Its nature is cold and dry. And the

last star of the three that are in the middle of the horn of the figure of Capricorn has power over this stone, and from it, the stone receives its strength and virtue. And when it is in **midheaven** <note>the highest point in the sky</note>, this stone shows its works most clearly.

**Of the stone.** The **twentieth degree** of the sign of **Capricorn** belongs to the stone they call **tarnuzes**, which means in **Chaldean** "stone of earth." This is found in a very deep well in the land named **Laasi**, near a place they call **Carriton**. The water of this well is very turbid, very thick, and green in color. Once it is taken out and placed in the sun, it hardens and becomes stone of that same color. This happens in a single day; even if it is left to dry for a longer time, it does not harden further. After it has been polished, it carries clarity within itself. Its nature is cold and dry, very intense in these two temperaments <note>original: "complexionē"</note>. It has such power that if someone is given a half-**drachm** <note>original: "dragma"; a small unit of weight</note> or more to drink, it dissolves the whole body, shrinks the nerves, and kills. But if it is kneaded with wine and used to anoint the body of one suffering from **dropsy** <note>original: "rozopico"; an old term for edema/swelling</note>, he thins out in such a way that he recovers very well. However, if they persist too much with this, he wastes away more than is appropriate.

->**Of the stone that appears in the sea when Saturn rises.**<-

The **twenty-second degree** of the sign of **Capricorn** belongs to the stone that appears in the sea when **Saturn** rises: and hides whenever it descends. This is found in the **Tenebrous Sea** <note>original: "mar tenervosa"; the Atlantic Ocean, which medieval sailors believed was filled with darkness and monsters</note> where those other stones are found in which the virtue of the other planets clearly appears, as we have already said. Its color is very black and clear. And it is always found in the shape of a pinecone. It is very dense, strong, and hard to break. And when they break it: they find it white inside. But this whiteness only appears with great difficulty <note>original: "mucho adur"</note> and only during the season when the planet is above the earth. But when the planet is below the earth: they cannot obtain it. By nature it is **cold and dry**: it has such virtue that he who keeps it with him lives long. And the illnesses and weaknesses that come to others do not befall him; rather, he remains with his wits and his strength while he

<column-break/>

lives. And it greatly aids its healing virtue <note>original: "sanna uertud"</note> such that if a man or woman looks at themselves in it as if in a mirror: it greatly strengthens their sight. But if another animal does so: it loses its sight. And the leading star of the two that are in the belly of **Capricorn** has power over this stone: and from it, the stone receives its strength and virtue. And when it is in the **ascendant** <note>the degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon</note>, it shows its works more than others.

The **twenty-third degree** of the sign of **Capricorn** belongs to the stone of the azure <term>Lapis Lazuli (the blue stone)</term>. This is very well known and is found in many places. In color it is a deep purple-blue <note>original: "cardena"</note>. And the best of all: is that which is found in the land of **Khorasan** <note>original: "horace"; a region in modern-day Iran and Afghanistan famous for high-quality lapis lazuli</note>. And the most prized is that in which veins or drops of gold color appear <note>these "drops of gold" are actually flecks of the mineral pyrite</note>. It is easy to break. And when they place it near gold, or join them together: each one appears more beautiful on its own. And its virtue is such that if they put the powder of it in the eyes: it benefits them much. And also, by placing a piece of it in the fire <note>original: "figo," likely a scribal error for "fuego"</note> that is without smoke, a purple flame rises from it, and it carries in itself great heat and great sharpness: even though it is of a **cold and dry** nature. And it also carries the power of retention. And if one takes the powder of it to drink: it purges all thick humor...

# Of the stone they call "vello."

-># THE SIGN OF CAPRICORN<-

->### THE CELESTIAL WHEEL<-

This page is occupied by a significant **zodiacal wheel** <term>zodiacal wheel: a circular diagram used in medieval manuscripts to map the relationship between a constellation, the natural world, and the divine hierarchy</term>, illustrating the complex influences of the sign of Capricorn. The diagram is organized into three concentric circles of increasing spiritual and natural complexity.

->**The Central Medallion**<-

At the heart of the diagram is a vibrant blue circle. It features a finely rendered figure of **Capricorn** <note>original: "capricornio"</note>, depicted as a white sea-goat—a creature with the head and forelegs of a mountain goat and the coiled tail of a fish. The body of the creature is marked with dark spots, likely representing the primary stars that form the constellation in the night sky.

->**The Circle of Earthly Nature**<-

The middle ring of the diagram is divided into twenty-four radial segments. Each segment contains a detailed drawing representing the diversity of life on Earth that falls under the dominion of this sign. Included in these segments are:
*   Various species of **fish** and aquatic life, reflecting the sign’s watery nature.
*   **Birds of prey**, such as eagles, representing the heights of the air.
*   Various **quadrupeds** <note>four-legged land animals</note>, representing the terrestrial realm.

->**The Celestial Hierarchy**<-

The outermost ring is also divided into twenty-four segments, corresponding to the segments of the middle ring. Each of these spaces is shaped like a **Gothic arch**—a pointed architectural frame typical of the 13th and 14th centuries. Inside each arch is the bust of a figure adorned with a reddish-orange **halo**. These figures represent the **angels** or spiritual intelligences that govern the specific degrees and hours of the sign, standing as guardians over the natural world depicted in the inner rings.

-># OF THE SIGN OF AQUARIUS 85<-

The thirty types of stones associated with the thirty degrees of the sign of Capricorn have been described, showing which stars they love and from where they receive their power. Therefore, it is appropriate for whoever wishes to use these stones to pay attention to the planet **Saturn**, as we have said regarding the other planets.

### Of the stone called cartahie

The first degree of the sign of Aquarius belongs to the stone they call **cartahie**. This is counted among the stones of animal origin, because on the mountain called Melquin, which is in the land of Macedonia, there are some very large hares. When they kill some of these before they reach one year of age, they find in the heart a stone of a violet color, which has a very red drop within it. It is a stone without luster and is of a hot and moist nature in the second degree. Its power is such that for the one who carries it, it strengthens the body so greatly that the cold of winter does not cause as much harm as it would to another who does not carry it, even if they have to endure great labor <note>original: "lazer," meaning to suffer toil or hardship</note> like a woman in labor. And if they grind this stone and mix it with wine and place it upon hard abscesses, such as **cancer** or others that are of the nature of **melatoma** <term>melatoma: a medieval term for a dark, hard tumor or swelling</term>, they heal in a short time. The star in the head of the Water-Bearer <note>original: "aguo," referring to Aquarius</note> has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its virtue; and when the star is rising, the stone shows its effects most clearly.

<column-break/>

### Of the stone called marayna

At the second degree of the sign of Aquarius is the stone they call **marayna**. This is found in the land of Africa on the shore of the sea where there is a large beach. On the outside, it has no luster and is the green color of seawater, but when they break it open, they find it is white inside. That whiteness is like the foam of the sea. If one takes a dose of it weighing between one and two drachms <term>drachm: a small unit of weight used by medieval apothecaries</term>, it purges the **phlegm** <note>one of the four "humors" or bodily fluids believed to govern health</note> very effectively. If they rub it with water and wash the head with it, it removes **dandruff** <note>original: "fasuola," referring to scaly skin or scurf</note> and lice, and it makes the hair very beautiful and soft; likewise, it makes hair grow back in places where it was lost due to illness or other causes. It has yet another power: by anointing limbs that have weakened due to a disease of the nerves, it heals them and returns them to their strength and vigor. Those limbs that are stiff and difficult to move are softened and made to move easily. When this stone turns black and dark, it is then used in the **Great Work** <term>Great Work: the "Magnum Opus" or the highest level of alchemical transformation</term>. The southern star of the urn of Aquarius <note>original: "gunna," likely a scribal error for "urna"</note> has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its virtue. When it is at mid-heaven, this stone shows its effects most completely.

<summary>This page describes the first two stones of the sign of Aquarius, cartahie and marayna, detailing their animal and maritime origins and their uses in treating tumors, cold, and nerve weakness.</summary>

# OF THE SIGN

### The third degree

The third degree of the sign of Aquarius is the **sponge stone**. These are found in many places and in many shapes, and those found in the **Land of Promise** <note>original: "tierra de promissiõ," referring to the Holy Land or Palestine</note> are small, very hard pebbles. They are of many colors and of a hot and moist nature. Its moisture is in the first degree and its heat in the third; for this reason, it dries more than it moistens. If they give it to someone to drink, it dissolves the stone that forms in the bladder, but not those of the kidneys. And it has another benefit: if they put it in water, it moves away from it as if it hates it. And if they mix it with any other thing, it incorporates into a dry mass so that they become one single thing; if they apply it in this way to the teeth, it heals the sores <note>original: "llagas," likely meaning ulcers or abscesses</note> that are in them. And likewise, it heals the mange and the itchiness, taking them away entirely. And if they heat it and place it in the ear, it removes the noise <note>tinnitus</note> that is made there by drying up the water and the venom <note>original: "uenino," here meaning fluid or pus</note> that is inside the ear, and it prevents an abscess <term>postema: a medieval term for a localized swelling or boil filled with fluid</term> from forming there. And the last star of those that are in the right foot of the **Hen** <note>original: "gallina," the medieval name for the constellation Cygnus, the Swan</note> has power over this stone and from it receives its strength and virtue. When this star is in the ascendant, this stone shows its works most clearly.

### The eleventh degree

The eleventh degree <note>original: "un" is an abbreviation for "onzeno" or eleventh</note> of the sign of Aquarius is the stone they call **ayzarugez** <note>Also referred to as gezariñez</note>, which means in Chaldean <note>Chaldean usually refers to the ancient language of Babylon/Syria</note> "tenderizer of meat." Its virtue is such that if they join a bit of it with meat when they put it to cook in a pot or another vessel, it makes it cook quickly. And if anyone eats the said meat, it removes the trembling of the limbs and takes away the fear of spirits or visions; it comforts and gives courage. By nature it is hot and moist, and strong and hard to break. They are always found in a round shape. By nature it is of a green color that tends toward purple. It is also very shiny, in a way that it dazzles the sight. They find it on the island called Mata on the seashore, wrapped in the sand, and it glows at night all around itself. If they grind it and give it to be taken mixed with another thing, it works against all poison <note>original: "tossico"</note>, whether from an animal or a vegetable. And likewise, it helps with the tremors and weakness of the heart. And the northern star of the three that are in the left sleeve <term>uegata: the fold or sleeve of the garment of the constellation figure</term> of the figure of Aquarius has power over this stone and from it receives its strength and virtue. And when it is in the ascendant, this stone shows its works most completely.

### Of the stone they call azaruzquez:—

<image-desc>A large historiated initial 'D' with blue and red decorative flourishes. Inside the letter is a scene depicting two men: one stands on the left wearing a blue mantle and gestures toward the other, who wears a red tunic and is kneeling or bowing low on the right.</image-desc>

**O**f the 21st degree of the sign of Aquarius is the stone they call <term>azaruzquez</term> <note>original: "azaruzquez"; likely a phonetic rendering of the Arabic *al-zaharuyaj*, commonly identified as Moss Agate due to its tree-like inclusions</note>. This is found on Mount Sinai. Its strength is hard to break, and it is of a brown color that leans somewhat toward yellow. And one sees in it the shape of a tree of green color; and when they break it, in however many pieces they make of it, in each of them this figure appears. By nature, it is hot and moist. And if they grind it and place it upon old sores, it makes them close in a short time. And if they mix it with wax and with resin, it is even better for this. And it has yet another very noble virtue: they never found a man who had it with him whose business affairs fared poorly <note>the text suggests it brings good fortune in trade or management</note>; and for this reason, those of the Promised Land <note>original: "tierra de promission," referring to the Levant/Palestine</note> always keep it guarded in their chests and in their treasures. And the bright star of the two that are in the right shoulder of the figure of Aquarius <note>likely the star Sadalmelik (Alpha Aquarii)</note> has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its virtue. And when this star is at mid-heaven, this stone shows its works most completely.—

### Of the stone that draws out poison :—

<image-desc>A large historiated initial 'D' with a circular red and white border. Inside the letter, two figures are shown: a man on the left in a brown garment sits or crouches, while another man on the right, dressed in a green and blue robe, stands and looks toward him.</image-desc>

**O**f the 22nd degree of the sign of Aquarius is the stone that draws out poison <note>original: "toxico," which in medieval lapidaries refers specifically to venomous substances or poisons</note>. This is of a yellow color spotted with black drops. By nature, it is hot and moist, and light in weight and porous. It is strong and hard to break, such that it cannot be broken except with great effort. It is somewhat smooth in itself, but if they polish it, it receives more [luster]. And when they break it, in every piece they make of it, one always finds the yellow color with black spots, just as it is on the outside. And this stone is of such a nature that when they put it into the fire, it catches fire and burns, but not as much or for as long as the other stones we have mentioned. And its virtue is such that when they place it in something they give to eat or drink in which there is poison—whether it be animal, vegetable, or mineral—it draws that portion of poison just as the <term>magnet</term> <note>original: "aymante," referring to the lodestone</note> draws iron, and it burns the poison within itself. And if the stone is small and the poison is much, so that it cannot draw it all at once or twice, it draws it in three or more [attempts]. And to know how much it draws each time, they act in this manner: after the stone has attracted what it could draw, they place it in another vessel <note>original: "caher," likely a vessel or a specific purging environment</note>, and as much poison as it attracted comes out of it; and afterward, return it to the poisoned substance again.

### Of the stone that is named meyrmenz:

The virtue of this stone is that it is said to be very difficult to break <note>original: "dezia entre si ligada de quebrantar"; this likely implies the stone's internal structure is so tightly bound that it resists crushing</note>. ### Of the stone they call zarbemic

<image-desc>A historiated initial 'E' contains a scene of a seated man in a blue robe holding a small blue object, perhaps the stone described, while speaking to a man in an orange tunic.</image-desc>

**E**very **22nd degree** of the sign of **Aquarius** is the stone they call <term>zarbemic</term>: which means in **Chaldean** <note>original: "caldeo"; a term often used in the Middle Ages for Aramaic or Syriac</note> "healer of the spirit and of the loss of use of the limbs." And this is because its virtue is such that whoever carries it with them is safe from having diseases that come from either of the two natures <note>likely referring to the humors or qualities like heat and moisture</note>; and if they had them before: they are healed. By nature, it is hot and moist in the second degree. It is strong and hard to break or to work <note>original: "laura"; to carve or shape</note> according to one's will, except with the edge of iron. And they find it in the land called **Al-Karach**, and there are many mines of it there. And when they put it in fire, the heat ignites within it and it burns: but not as much as that other one we mentioned. And if they grind it and cast it into deep wounds <note>original: "llagas fontas"; likely referring to deep, discharging, or "fountain-like" sores</note>: it makes the flesh grow in them quickly and evenly. And it even has a virtue by which it can be recognized among all other stones: if they put it in blood, it mixes with it and turns it to its own nature. And the two stars of the three that are in the last right palm, and the northern one of the three that are in the last turn [of the stream], are all in **Aquarius**. They have power over this stone and from them it receives its strength and virtue. And when they are in the ascendant: this stone shows its works more completely.

### Of the stone they call Eraqui:

<image-desc>A small rectangular miniature inset into the text. It depicts two figures in a landscape with green hills and a blue sky. On the left, a figure in a red tunic stands gesturing. On the right, a figure in a blue robe sits on a mound, possibly holding an object.</image-desc>

The **20th degree** of the sign of **Aquarius** is the stone they call <term>Eraqui</term>. It has this name because it is found in the land called **Laetne**. This stone is black in color, very heavy, and easy to break. By nature, it is hot and moist <note>According to the medieval humoral system, "hot and moist" substances were thought to promote growth and blood flow</note>. When it is ground and mixed with vinegar, they make from it a very good and shiny ink for writing. Also, by washing the hair with it, it dyes the hair black and very beautiful. If its powder is mixed with oil, they make from it a very good medicine for the <term>sarna</term> <note>original: "sarna"; a term for scabies or itchy skin eruptions</note> that comes from too much moisture. If they distill it and place it with copper <term>arambre</term> at the point of melting, it takes on a very beautiful color of silver; however, if it is melted many times, it returns to its previous state as it was before. And the second star of the southern water-pourer <note>original: "agua conniet meridional"; likely referring to the stream of water flowing from Aquarius toward the constellation Piscis Austrinus</note>, which is toward the hand of **Aquarius**, has power over this stone and it receives its strength and virtue from it. When this star is in the mid-heaven <term>medio cielo</term>, this stone shows its works most perfectly.

### Of the stone they call Romana:

<image-desc>A small rectangular miniature inset into the text. Two figures are depicted in a rocky landscape. The figure on the left is kneeling and dressed in greyish-white. The figure on the right is seated, wearing green robes, and appears to be pointing or reaching toward the other figure.</image-desc>

The **21st degree** of the sign of **Aquarius** is the stone they call <term>Romana</term> <note>The "Roman stone"</note>. This is found in the eastern part of the land of **Tetoma** <note>possibly a corruption of Edom or a similar regional name</note> in a cave at the foot of a mountain named **Anac**. This stone is green in color and has within it white veins that resemble Roman letters, and in every piece they make of it, they find it in this manner. It is solitary in its nature. Its virtue is such that whoever carries it with him will never fall ill with the disease they call <term>pontico</term> <note>original: "põtico"; a medieval medical term usually referring to a specific type of abdominal pain or internal obstruction</note>; and if he is already ill with it, he heals just as quickly. It also heals ulcers of the intestines. By nature, it is hot and moist in the first degree. Because of this, if they grind it and put it in the eyes, it removes the "whiteness" <note>cataracts or corneal scarring</note> and the scales <term>tinnia</term> that form in them. It also heals the <term>panno</term> <note>skin blemishes or melasma</note> that grows on the face and provides a good complexion. If, when warts are cut away, they rub the place where they were with this stone, it ensures they never grow there again. And the star that is in the left knee of the figure <note>original: "gaima"; likely a corruption of the Greek name Ganymede, the youth associated with the constellation Aquarius</note> has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its virtue. When that star is in the Ascendant <term>assendente</term>, this stone shows its works most marvelously.

### Of the stone that appears in the sea.

The **18th degree** of the sign of **Aquarius**: is the stone that appears in the sea when **Saturn** sets, and ascends as much as it rises. This is found in the <term>Dark Sea</term> <note>original: "mar tenebroso"; the medieval name for the Atlantic Ocean</note>, where other stones are found in which the virtue of the planets appears manifestly. And the power of **Saturn** resides in this stone, contrary to the other stone mentioned in the 21st degree of the sign of Capricorn. And the signs of this stone are that it is very white and bright, heavy, and strong and hard to break, such that it does not break except with a great mallet; and when they break it, they find it black in color inside; and if they place it in the clear air, the blackness appears more within it. And it brightens when **Saturn** sets, and becomes <term>bitter</term> <note>original: "amara"; this likely refers to its medicinal essence or a change in its perceived quality under Saturn’s influence</note> when it rises. By nature it is hot and moist. There is a very evil power in it, such that if anyone carries it while **Saturn** is beneath the earth, it blinds them; but as long as the star is above the earth, it does no harm. And if a man has it with him when he sleeps, it makes him dream of heavy and very ugly things. And the star that is in the left breast of the **Greater Horse** <note>original: "cauallo mayor"; the constellation Pegasus</note> has power over this stone and truly gives it its virtue. And when it is in the ascendant, this stone shows more strength in its works.

<column-break/>

### Of the stone that has the name Teyra.

The **19th degree** of the sign of **Aquarius**: is the stone they call <term>Teyra</term>. By nature it is hot and moist in the second degree. And they find it in the land named **Catedruqnia** in mines that are there. It is white and resembles sand joined by grains of many colors, and they find it on the face of the earth; and those small grains are like sharp points. And if they grind it and apply its powder onto vessels or any other object of silver or metal, it makes them bright and very beautiful; and it does the same to swords and knives, and furthermore, it sharpens them. And if they grind it and make it flow <note>original: "fazel correr"; likely referring to mixing it into a liquid suspension</note>, and they knead it with something and make from it the shape of an **acorn**, and the woman places it in her <term>nature</term> <note>original: "natura"; a medieval euphemism for the vagina</note>, it wrinkles it and tightens it, and makes her have a desire for a man; and likewise it makes her conceive more quickly. And the three stars—the following one and the middle one of the three that are in the second return of **Aquarius**—have power over this stone, and from them it receives its strength and virtue. And when they are in the ascendant, this stone shows its works more completely.

### Of the stone they call Yetaniz.

<image-desc>An illuminated initial 'E' in a square frame. The initial is blue with white decorative patterns, set against a gold leaf background. Inside the initial, a miniature shows two seated figures: a man in a red robe and a woman in an orange robe, who appears to be handing him a small red object, possibly the stone described in the text.</image-desc>

The **19th degree** of the sign of **Aquarius**: is the stone they call <term>yetaniz</term>. This name comes from a mountain where it is found called Rati, which is in the land of Bermini on the Amadun mountain or near it. Its color is reddish, turning somewhat yellow. It is strong and hard to break, without luster, and light, and it is formed as if full of holes <note>meaning it is porous, like pumice or lava stone</note>. If it is cut, the core is found to be white in color. Its nature is hot and moist. If it is ground and distilled with wine, and the bald head is anointed with it, it makes hair grow; and it does the same in any part of the body where there was hair and it was lost. It also prevents the hair that has grown from falling out. It also heals that illness which makes a man faint often: [administering] as much of it as a <term>die</term> <note>original: "tamanna quantadie"; likely referring to the size of a small gaming die or cube</note>, depending on what is understood of the illness. The southern star of the three located in the right bend of **Aquarius** has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its virtue. When this star is in the middle of the sky, this stone shows its effects most completely.

### Of the stone they call Macicena.

<image-desc>An illuminated initial 'E' in a square frame, blue with white filigree on a gold background. The miniature inside depicts two figures: one in a blue tunic is bent over, digging into the earth with a tool, while a second figure in a red robe stands behind them, watching.</image-desc>

The **20th degree** of the sign of **Aquarius**: is the stone they call <term>macicena</term>. This means **"stone of weeping"** in <term>Chaldean</term> <note>a term often used in this period to refer to Aramaic or Syriac, the languages of ancient Mesopotamia</note> because it has such power that whoever carries it with them is always sad and tearful. If it is placed in someone's bed and they sleep upon it, it will do the same. If it is given to be drunk, the same will happen to the one who drinks it; for this reason, it is a stone much hated by those who know of it. It is strong and hard to break, and green in a way that tires the sight <note>original: "pussa el uiso"; suggesting the color is so piercing or dull it affects the eyes</note>. Its color is black, and it has yellow veins in it that seem to flow into one another. It is found in the islands of **India** on the banks of a river that flows through them called **Carrich**. Its nature is hot and moist. The two stars—the northern and the southern—of those that follow the flowing water of the stream according to the figure of **Aquarius** have power over this stone and from them it receives its virtue. When these stars are in the <term>ascendant</term> <note>the degree of the zodiac rising over the eastern horizon</note>, this stone shows its effects most copiously.

## Of the stone named Aradenna

<image-desc>Circular illustration of Aquarius depicted as a man in a light green tunic with bare feet, pouring water from two jars. Below, a square miniature with a decorative "E" initial shows two men: one standing in a green tunic holding a staff and pointing to the ground, and another in an orange tunic kneeling and working the earth.</image-desc>

The **25th degree** of the sign of **Aquarius**: is the stone they call <term>aradenna</term>. By nature, it is hot and moist. The mines where it is found are near the town they call Ateruuitz, which is in the land of Furunia.

Its color is a deep violet <note>original: "cardena," a purplish or bruised color</note> that leans toward yellow. Some are large and others small, and they come in many shapes. This stone clears when the weather is bright and becomes cloudy when the weather is overcast. According to the sayings of the sages, any stone that changes its color is of a "bad substance" <note>meaning it has an unstable or inferior composition</note>. Within this stone, there is a waxy square; thus, when it is melted, they find it at the bottom of the <term>aluol</term> <note>a crucible or melting vessel</note> in which they melt it. Its virtue is such that whoever carries it with them is feared by all who see him. If they grind it and put the powder in the eyes, it heals the <term>sarna</term> <note>likely blepharitis or an itchy crusting of the eyelids</note> that forms there in a short time. Two stars have power over this stone and it receives its virtue from them: the first is the last of the fifteen stars that follow the first bend of the water, and the other is a solitary star located toward the south after the second bend of that water, both being in Aquarius. When they are in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works most clearly.

## Of the stone that attracts salt

<image-desc>Circular illustration of Aquarius as a man in a reddish-brown tunic pouring water from two jars. Below, a square miniature with a decorative "E" initial shows two figures near a blue body of water; one figure in a blue tunic kneels to reach into the water while a standing figure in a red cloak watches.</image-desc>

The **26th degree** of the sign of **Aquarius**: is the stone that attracts salt. By nature, it is hot and moist. It has such a virtue that if it is placed near salt, it pulls it to itself, just as other magnets pull the liquids <note>original: "aquas"</note> over which they have power. It increases in strength as it pulls, for it attracts from further away than others and moves as much weight as its own. Its color is yellow, like <term>yellow lake</term> <note>a traditional pigment made from organic dyes</note>, and it is speckled with white spots. It is of such a kind that sight cannot pass through it <note>meaning it is opaque</note>, and it is light in weight. If they put it into any container where there was salt, it draws it all out regardless of its nature, provided the container is cold; but if it is hot, the stone does not do this. If, after it has absorbed the salt, they put it in cold water, it remains hot; furthermore, if it is thrown into seawater, it removes the saltiness and makes it good to drink. This stone is named <term>alardo</term> and it is found in the land of Pintision on the shores of the sea near the place where the river they call Alardo flows into it. It is said that if they grind it and put it in the eyes, the eyelashes fall out, but it prevents them from <unclear>falling</unclear> again and makes them grow back. The northern star of the three that are in the "broken bend" of the water in the sign of Aquarius has power over it.

### Of the stone they call delmenica

<image-desc>A square miniature within the text column featuring a blue frame. Inside, two men in long tunics (one red, one grey) are standing and engaged in conversation against a red background.</image-desc>

The **28th degree** of the sign of **Aquarius**: is the stone they call <term>delmenica</term> in Chaldean <note>original: "caldeo"</note>, which means as much as "healer of the deaf," for it has such virtue that if a deaf person carries it—of whatever nature their deafness may be—they are healed. By nature, it is hot and moist in the third degree. Its color is a strong <term>tulmagin</term> <note>a technical term for a deep, intense dark pigment</note> which is very dark, strong, hard, shiny, and very heavy. But after it is burned, it becomes light and very porous; if they grind it and mix it with oil and put it in the ear, it removes deafness and aids in all the illnesses that occur there. The mine of this stone is on the island of Dragen which comes from the sea; this island is in the Great Sea called the Ocean, near the <unclear>West</unclear> <note>original: "occidēt"</note> where no men live. And the star <term>makhia</term>—one of the three located in the third turn of the flowing water of the sign of Aquarius—has power over this stone, and from it the stone receives its virtue. And when the star is in the midheaven <note>the highest point in the sky</note>, this stone shows its works more powerfully.

### Of the stone they call secutaiz

<image-desc>A square miniature within the text column featuring a blue frame. It depicts two figures outdoors by a body of water; one figure is seated and appears to be working with or examining stones or materials near the water's edge.</image-desc>

The **29th degree** of the sign of **Aquarius**: is the stone they call <term>secutaiz</term>. It takes this name from a river where it is found called the Secur, which is in the land of Ethiopia. They find it in the springs there, taking out these small <unclear>lumps</unclear> <note>original: "torras"</note> of a long and round shape. It is hollow like a reed and its color is like a pomegranate seed <note>original: "grano de milgrana"</note>, which is very clear and bright, and its clarity surpasses everything. It is light in weight but strong and hard to break, so much so that no other material can break it except silver, due to its nature. When one wishes to work it, they first make a saw or chisel of silver to handle it; then they can drill into it in whatever shape they wish very easily. No other stone can have power over it except the diamond alone. By nature, it is hot and moist, but there is more heat in it than moisture. It has such virtue that if one carries it set in silver, no nocturnal pollution <note>nocturnal emissions or "wet dreams"</note> happens to them in their dreams; and if one suffers from this due to some illness, the stone cures and heals them. It does the same if one makes a plaster of it and places it over the bite of a mad dog or another poisonous beast. And the last star of the three joined stars that are after the turn...

# Of the stone that is formed in the sea snail

<image-desc>A historiated initial E showing two men in a blue-framed circle; one is seated on a bench gesturing toward the other, who is kneeling and holding a golden bowl.</image-desc>

The **19th degree** of the sign of **Aquarius** is the stone that is formed in the spine of the **sea snail** <note>original: "caracol de la mar"; likely referring to the operculum or a calcified part of a large gastropod</note>. And this is concave between the two animals. By nature, it is hot and moist; however, if one cuts it more than necessary, it loses its moisture. In color, it is brown, and it feels like <term>felt</term> to the touch. And its virtue is such: that if they grind it and give it to drink, it aids all diseases of the **lung**, opening its passages <note>original: "cannas", literally the "reeds" or bronchial tubes</note>, and it clears the voice. And if one puts its powder into a wound of someone struck by an **arrow** in such a way that the iron arrowhead cannot be removed, it draws it out and heals the wound. And if it is boiled, and the person who is wounded in the **intestines** sits in the water that comes from it, they are healed. And the forward star of the two that are marked on the chest of the **Great Horse** <note>the constellation Pegasus</note> has power over this stone and from it receives its virtue. And when it is in the ascendant, this stone shows its strength more completely in all these works.

# Of the stone named seraticez

<image-desc>A historiated initial E showing a scene inside a blue-framed circle; a man in a red tunic stands on the right using a hammer or pickaxe on a white block, while another man sits on the left observing him.</image-desc>

The **18th degree** of the sign of **Aquarius** is the stone that is called **seraticez** in Chaldean <note>original: "caldeo"</note>, which means in this language as much as "destroyer of the **spleen**" <note>original: "baco", modern Spanish "bazo"</note>. And this resembles a human spleen in form and color. It has such virtue that he who carries it with him is healed—healed of every ailment of the spleen—and it overcomes the fever that comes from such illness; and he is safe from ever having it while he keeps the stone with him. It is <term>porous</term> <note>original: "u-mana", likely "humana" or "porosa"</note> and very easy to break. And the best kinds of it are found in the eastern part of **Spain** on the shores of the sea. And it has such an evil virtue that if they burn it and give its powder to drink, it kills, for it is in itself a **deadly poison** <note>original: "uisico mortal"</note>. And the star that is in the heel of the right foot of the **Great Horse** <note>Pegasus</note> has power over this stone and from it receives its strength and virtue. And when it is in the **mid-heaven** <note>the highest point of the sun's or a star's path</note>, this stone shows its works more completely.

### Of the stone that is formed in the spine of the sea crab.

**D**<image-desc>Large decorative initial D containing a miniature of two men seated on the ground; the figure on the left is dressed in blue robes and gestures towards the figure on the right, who is dressed in orange robes and appears to hold a small object.</image-desc>of the **27th degree** of the sign of **Aquarius**: is the stone that is formed in the spine <note>original: "espinazo"; referring here to the internal skeletal structure or shell of a crustacean</note> of the **sea crab**. This is counted among the stones of animals because it is a very delicate thing formed within the bellies. By nature it is **hot and moist**. And its virtue is such that if it is made into powder and put into the **eyes**: it aids the pain in them and greatly dries out humors <note>The "humors" were the bodily fluids believed to control health in medieval medicine</note> and strengthens the nerves and sharpens the wits. And if they grind it and knead it with vinegar and anoint with it the sickness that they call in Arabic *hareza* <term>hareza: a skin condition, likely a fungal infection or rough scales</term> and in the Castilian language *empeines* <note>original: "empeines"; refers to skin eruptions like ringworm or eczema</note>: it heals. And as the moon wanes in its moisture: this stone grows in its dryness and in its strength. And from the fire of it comes a very sharp smell, and women use it when it is burnt: to make the **skin of the face thin and of a good color**. And the **star** that is between the **shoulders of the horse** <note>referring to the constellation Pegasus</note> has power over this stone and from it receives its virtue. And when it is in the ascendant: this stone shows its works most manifest:

<column-break/>

<image-desc>A circular miniature identical to the first, showing the upper half of the constellation Pegasus on a gold ground.</image-desc>

### Of the stone that they call Kednnaz.

**D**<image-desc>Large decorative initial D containing a miniature of two men; a standing figure on the left in red and gold robes addresses or gestures toward a figure in blue robes kneeling or bowing on the right.</image-desc>of the **28th degree** of the sign of **Aquarius** is the stone they call **Kednnaz**. This is found in a mountain they call Kedun, from which it takes this name. And its mines are found in the land named Milez. Its color is dark and of a brown color spotted with **green and clear spots**. And when it is burned: a smell comes from it that smells like when they roast fatty meat. By nature it is **hot and moist**. And if they grind it after it is burnt and anoint with it **corrosive sores**: they heal. And likewise, if a man drinks of it, he should be afraid: for it takes away the sense and the understanding: and makes him **stupefied** <note>original: "soterahmononado"; a rare Old Spanish term for being dazed, senseless, or in a deep stupor</note> just as if he were drunk. And if he drinks much of it: he dies. And the last of the **two joined stars** that are in the **chest of the horse** <note>Pegasus</note> has power over this stone and from it receives its virtue. And when it is in the Midheaven: this stone shows its works most completely.

<summary>This page describes two stones for the 27th and 28th degrees of Aquarius: one derived from a sea crab used for skin and eye care, and the "Kednnaz" stone, which has healing properties for sores but is dangerously toxic if ingested.</summary>

# OF PISCES

<image-desc>A circular frame containing two fish, one blue and one yellow, swimming in opposite directions and joined by a golden cord, representing the zodiac sign Pisces.</image-desc>

### Of the stone they call tezanden.

<image-desc>An illuminated letter E containing a miniature of two men: one standing and pointing upwards, the other kneeling and using a pickaxe on a rocky mound.</image-desc>

The **28th degree** of the sign of **Pisces** is the stone they call **tezanden**. Its nature is **cold and moist**. And it is found in the land of **Avillonna** <note>possibly referring to a region in the Near East or a mythical desert location mentioned in Arabic sources</note> in the mines found there in the great wildernesses. Its color is yellow, spotted with white drops, and it is strong and hard to break; it is clear in such a way that the sight passes through it <note>original: "pelaia a uisa"; meaning the stone is translucent or transparent</note>. And the virtue of this stone is contrary to the other we spoke of in this aforementioned degree <note>referring to the stone of the previous degree</note>: for whoever carries it with them is loved and feared by all who see them, and they speak well of him. And if they grind it and give it as a drink: it takes away the bad craving of those who eat earth or clay <note>a condition known as pica</note>, which comes by reason of **melancholy** <term>melancholy: in medieval medicine, an excess of the "black bile" humor, which was thought to cause depression and strange physical cravings</term>. And the first star of the three small ones in the head of the first fish in the figure of **Pisces** has power over this stone, and from it, the stone receives its strength and virtue. And when this star is at mid-heaven <note>the highest point in its path across the sky</note>, this stone shows its works most completely.

<column-break/>

<image-desc>A circular frame containing two fish, one blue and one yellow, swimming in opposite directions and joined by a golden cord, representing the zodiac sign Pisces.</image-desc>

### Of the stone named pethiemel.

<image-desc>An illuminated letter E containing a miniature of two men: one seated in a yellow robe and holding an object, the other standing in a red robe and gesturing.</image-desc>

The **30th degree** of the sign of **Pisces** is the stone they call **pethiemel**. Its color is **vermilion** <note>original: "uermei"; a brilliant red</note>, very deep, and there are very subtle **purple** <note>original: "cardenas"; violet or purplish</note> moons <note>likely crescent-shaped inclusions or patterns</note> in it. It is bright in such a way that the sight passes through it. And it is often found in the land named **Gieer**. Its nature is **cold and moist**. And its virtue is such that whoever carries it with them is greatly feared by all who see them, and they will have no ailment in the belly nor in the intestines <note>original: "estentinos"</note>; and for this reason, it is much loved, and also for its beauty. And between this stone and the **robni** <term>robni: likely the ruby (rubinus)</term> there is great enmity; so much so that if they are placed together, each of them recoils within itself and breaks. And the southern star of the two in the belly of the last fish in the figure of **Pisces** has power over this stone; from it, the stone receives its strength and virtue. And when it is at mid-heaven, this stone shows its works most completely.

<summary>This page describes the final stones of the Pisces section, specifically those of the 28th and 30th degrees, detailing their transparent appearance, their ability to cure digestive or psychological ailments, and their celestial connection to the stars in the constellation of Pisces.</summary>

# OF PISCES

The **28th degree** of the sign of **Pisces** is the stone they call **tezanden**. Its nature is **cold and moist**. # OF THE SIGN OF PISCES

<image-desc>A circular frame containing two fish, one blue and one yellow, swimming in opposite directions and joined by a golden cord, representing the zodiac sign Pisces.</image-desc>

### Of the stone they call tezanden.

<image-desc>An illuminated letter E containing a miniature of two men: one standing and pointing upwards toward the heavens, the other kneeling and using a pickaxe to work on a rocky mound.</image-desc>

The **28th degree** of the sign of **Pisces** is the stone they call **tezanden**. Its nature is **cold and moist**. And it is found in the land of **Avillonna** <note>This place name likely derives from Arabic sources used by the King's translators, possibly referring to a region in the Near East or a legendary site mentioned in ancient lapidaries</note> in the mines found there in the great wildernesses. Its color is yellow, spotted with white drops, and it is strong and hard to break; it is clear in such a way that the sight passes through it <note>original: "pelaia a uisa"; meaning the stone is translucent or transparent</note>. 

And the star that lies on the northern side of the tail of the **Southern Fish** <note>original: "del pez austral"</note> has power over this stone, and from it, the stone receives its strength and virtue. It has such a power that whoever carries it with them will be protected from the terrors of the night and from the visions that trouble the mind during sleep. Furthermore, when this stone is finely ground and given as a drink to those suffering from a burning fever, it provides great relief and cools the internal heat.

<column-break/>

### Of the stone they call almizclon.

The **30th degree** <note>This is the final degree of the entire zodiacal circle in this manuscript</note> of the sign of **Pisces** belongs to the stone called **almizclon** <note>original: "almizclon"; the name is derived from "almizcle," meaning musk, due to the stone's fragrance</note>. Its nature is **warm and dry**. It is found along the shores of the **Indian Sea**, often washed up by the waves during great storms. 

Its appearance is distinctive: it is a stone of many colors, though it is primarily a dark, dapple-grey, looking as though it were covered in many tiny spots. When it is rubbed or crushed, it gives off a scent so powerful and sweet that it resembles musk <term>musk: a rare and highly prized aromatic substance used in medieval times for both perfumes and potent medicines</term>. 

Healers believe this stone is of great benefit for the "coldness of the brain" <note>A medieval medical term referring to conditions like lethargy, depression, or certain types of paralysis</note>. When smelled or worn, it comforts the heart and restores the senses of those who have fainted. The stars that are at the very end of the constellation of **Pisces**, where the cord joins the two fishes together, are the ones that grant this stone its fragrant and healing properties.

<summary>This page concludes the sign of Pisces and the zodiacal cycle, describing the protective stone Tezanden and the aromatic, medicinal stone Almizclon. It explains their physical properties, their origins in distant lands, and how their powers are derived from specific stars.</summary>

<keywords>Pisces, Tezanden, Almizclon, Avillonna, Southern Fish, Medieval Medicine, Astrology, Lapidary, Musk, Protective Amulets</keywords>

# Prologue on the faces of the signs. ~ ~ ~

Many are the thirty
kinds of stones
according to the thirty
degrees of the sign of **Pis-
ces**, and it has been shown which
stars have their attach-
ment [to them], and from where they
receive their strength and virtue.

Therefore, it is necessary for whoever
wishes to work with this book to pay heed
to the planet **Jupiter**, that it be in a good state for
works of good, and for works of evil, the unfortunate planet <note>original: "el frotuno"; likely referring to Saturn, often called the "Greater Infortune" in medieval astrology</note>; for this is a general
rule of all the planets and of the fixed
stars, and of the stones that agree with them. And of
the herbs, and of the animals, for all have virtue and
strength which they receive from God by the hand of His angels
and by the virtue of the heavens and of the stars that are in
them, and then from the four elements; and so it continues until
everything reaches, through this virtue, its birth,
and its growth, and its maintenance. Wherefore, after
we have shown through this book—which
**Abrayçr** <note>Likely referring to the Arabic astronomer Albohazen Haly Abenragel, a primary source for King Alfonso's scientific works</note> composed from the sayings of the ancient sages who
ordered by true reasons the virtue that
stones receive from the thirty degrees of each sign,
each one according to the virtue of its degree and the power
placed upon it—it is fitting now that we speak
further on the virtue that stones have according to how the
**Sun** passes through the **faces** <note>The "faces" or decans are 10-degree subdivisions of a zodiac sign, each ruled by a different planet or associated with specific imagery</note> of the signs, and of the figures of
the stars that are in them: <unclear>a o n d i</unclear> in which times they
possess that virtue most completely,
and in which [times] it changes from one manner to another ac-
cording to the change and the diversity that exists in the
figures of the stars that are in the faces of those
signs. Which [stars] are without number, nor could I
name them or give them their placement, except for God who
made them; as King **David** showed through the **Holy Spirit** <note>original: "spiritu scto"</note>, praised
be God, when he said: **"He who"** <note>original: "Qui"</note> **counts the multitude
of the stars and calls each one by its name.** <note>A translation of Psalm 147:4: "Qui numerat multitudinem stellarum, et omnibus eis nomina vocat."</note> And
for this reason, when the Sun passes through the faces of the signs,
or any of the other six planets, the stone receives
virtue from the rays that descend from the figures of the
stars in whose time the face of that sign runs. Wherefore,
just as the change of the figures shifts, so

<column-break/>

all things that receive
virtue from them shift and change,
as much the living things as those that lack
a soul. For as **Ptolemy** and the others who
were masters of the art of astronomy said, all the
strength and the virtue that the heavens and the stars
send upon the other things that are below them, all is
dependent on them being prepared to act: some
to receive, which they call **Matter**; and the others to
act, which they call **Form**. <note>The translator is using the Aristotelian concepts of Hylomorphism—Matter and Form—which were central to medieval science</note> Wherefore the bodies below
are capable, and through the mixing that they have with one
another, they are all made as one thing, strong and heavy;
and for this reason they are of such matter, and they always desire to receive
strength from the virtue of the high and noble
celestial bodies. And even though they always have it in themselves, because
they could not be made nor maintain themselves without it,
nevertheless they receive it more when they are pre-
pared and in a state to receive it completely.
And the example of this is like the development of a man. For as
long as he is a child, the soul—though it be complete—as much as
it can be as a thing that does not have form in itself, and it
holds within it all the manners of the forms of the
thoughts into which it enters; but nevertheless, because the
limbs of the child are not as complete as they should be, nor
do they have the earthly matter completely prepared
to receive the celestial form, for this reason they
cannot act as much as when he is in the time
of having all his strength complete. For then the
matter finds in the form what it desires: the one in
receiving, and the other in giving. And for this the child does not have in
himself such great strength when he is small
as when he is a youth; nor the youth as when he is a
young man <note>original: "macedo"; likely a scribe's error for "mancebo" (young man or adult)</note>; and so on until he reaches being a complete man. And
this same thing happens in all other things, not
only in animals, but even in the plants—which
refers to trees and herbs—and in the
stones and in all the other metals. For they do not have such great
virtue when they are being born as when they are [fully] born,
because their matter is not prepared to receive
all the form completely. And for this reason, they
have more virtue when they are in that state that they
ought to reach than when they begin to rise toward it, or
when they are already descending. And for this reason, every man
who wishes to work with these noble and ancient knowledges
must pay heed to these reasons.

It uses the Aristotelian concepts of Matter and Form to explain that objects must be fully "mature" to effectively channel the astrological power of the stars.</summary>

...which are spoken of, and through them one would come to the knowledge of all things: how they are made, and placed, and changed from one into another; and in what time their <term>virtue</term> <note>In medieval science, "virtue" refers to the inherent power, property, or "spirit" of a thing, rather than moral goodness.</note> grows and they have the greatest strength to act, because then their works are more manifest; and according to this, one might better avail themselves of them in whatever they might need and more completely.

And likewise, we wish to say what these <term>faces</term> <note>original: "fazes"; these are the 10-degree subdivisions of a zodiac sign, commonly known in astrology as "decans." There are three decans to every sign.</note> are and why they have such a name. And this is shown by three divisions that exist in the figure of each sign: such as the beginning, the middle, and the end. And each of these three parts, which are called faces, consists of ten degrees. In this way, there are thirty degrees in each sign, and thus thirty-six faces are made throughout the twelve signs, in which there are three hundred and sixty degrees. And these are called "faces" because whoever wishes to observe them all at once cannot do so, but rather each one by itself; and therefore, the one they first begin to observe is as if it appeared first, and for that reason, they call it a "face."

And just as with the stones we mentioned—which have a regard for and receive the virtue of the figures in the degrees of the signs—likewise those same stones gain such strength and virtue which they receive specifically from the figures that are in each of the faces. For although the stones show their virtue through the figures of the degrees, as has been said, they still preserve their "ante-chamber" <note>This likely refers to the primary or underlying astrological foundation or the preceding influence of the decan.</note> according to the changing of the other figures that are in the faces, because of the virtue and the property that is in them. And therefore, it is necessary to speak first of the stone, and afterward, which figure it is from which it receives its strength and virtue.

And now we return to the first subject: to speak of all the stones and of their virtues through the faces of the signs. And we shall speak first of the sign of **Aries**, which is the beginning of all the others:—

### Of the stone named Sangmina ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~ ~

And this is accomplished more completely

<column-break/>

when **Mars** is in this face, or in its ascendant at its hour, and in a good aspect with the **Sun**. And he who desires the virtue of this stone should [carve] the figure of a black man with protruding eyes, who has a white cloth <note>original: "alquice"; a traditional North African or Moorish cloak or wrap.</note> before him and a hoe <note>original: "açadon"; a mattock or hoe used for digging.</note> in his hand.

**I**n the second face of the sign of Taurus is the stone they call <term>zumbeche</term> <note>original: "zumbeche"; historically associated with varieties of emerald or green jasper.</note>: and of this it is spoken in the ninth degree of the sign of Taurus. And its virtue is such that if they place it in the bed of any man: he will have no desire to lie with a woman while he has it there: yet he will have <term>lustfulness</term> <note>original: "liuania"; sexual desire or lewdness.</note> when it is burned as incense. And that there descends upon this stone the virtue of the figure of a man who resembles a camel: and who has nails on his fingers that resemble those of a cow.

### Of the stone that has the name zebeth. , , , ,

**I**n the third face of the sign of Taurus is the stone they call <term>zebeth</term> <note>original: "zebeth"; a stone associated in this tradition with discord and destruction.</note>, of which we have already spoken in this book in the 26th degree of the sign of Pisces. And its virtue is such that if they place it in any inhabited place: it will lay it waste, turning the inhabitants against their own agreements so that they will kill one another, even those from outside that place. However, this will be most manifest when Saturn is in this face: and in its ascendant: and in its hour: and in a <term>trine</term> or <term>sextile</term> <note>Trine and sextile are "harmonious" astrological aspects (120 and 60 degrees apart), which here paradoxically empower the stone's destructive influence.</note> aspect with Mars. And there should descend upon this stone the virtue of the figure of a black man with protruding teeth: and the body of an elephant, having a calf before him: and a dog behind him.

# Of the stone they call coral

**O**f the third <term>face</term> <note>A "face" or decan is a ten-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign; each sign has three.</note> of the sign of Pisces: is the stone they call coral: of this, much has already been said in this book in the 11th degree of the sign of Taurus. And its <term>virtue</term> <note>original: "uertud," referring to the inherent magical or medicinal power believed to reside within the stone.</note> is such that he who carries it with him: will love wandering much through wildernesses and through mountains and will never want to enter a town: and he will be successful in every hunt that is made with birds <note>A reference to the medieval aristocratic sport of falconry.</note>. But it performs this more perfectly when Mars <note>original: "mart"</note> is in this face and in its <term>ascendant</term> <note>The degree of the zodiac rising over the eastern horizon at a specific moment.</note> and in its hour: and <term>received</term> <note>original: "recebudo," an astrological term describing a favorable relationship where one planet is located in a sign or "dignity" ruled by another.</note> by the Sun and by the Moon: and in a good <term>aspect</term> <note>original: "catamiento," the geometric alignment between celestial bodies that determines their influence.</note> with Jupiter. And let there be unfolded <note>original: "desenbuelue," suggesting the manifestation of celestial power into a physical form.</note> upon this stone the virtue of the figure of a man who holds a bird in his hand: and as if looking at a stag <note>original: "cieruo"</note> that is standing before him.
