-> ON SATURN <-

Having finished the second <term>lapidary</term> <note>A book or treatise describing the medicinal and magical properties of gemstones.</note> in which the properties that stones possess through the power they receive from the figures in the <term>eighth heaven</term> <note>In medieval cosmology, this was the sphere of the fixed stars, located beyond the seven spheres of the planets.</note> are fully shown, according to the temperament of the faces of the twelve signs—though the sun runs through them all year, both by night and by day—it is now appropriate to show the work of the third lapidary. In this, we speak of how the <term>virtues</term> <note>original: "uertudes"; the inherent medicinal or occult powers of the stones.</note> of stones change many times according to the state of the planets and the figures in the eighth heaven from which they receive their power. And first, we shall begin with Saturn, because he is the highest planet of all others, and we shall descend in order until we reach the Moon, which is the lowest, through whom we receive the virtue of the other planets as God placed it within her.

### Of the stone named ademuz in Greek

**S**aturn has power over the stone named <term>ademuz</term> in Greek, and <term>almez</term> in Arabic, and in our language, the **diamond**. And this stone has already been mentioned in the first degree of Taurus. And if, when Saturn is well <term>received</term> <note>original: "recebudo"; an astrological term where a planet is in a sign or "dignity" ruled by another planet that is making a favorable aspect to it.</note> by the moon and in its <term>ascendant</term> <note>The degree of the zodiac rising over the eastern horizon at a specific time.</note> and in its hour, one takes this stone and keeps it with them, the power of the figure of the stars will descend upon it. In these stars are figured the eight "mayoral lions" of the ark of Saturn, which men found before any other letters could be known. And if they enter any place where there are people who love each other well, they will soon wish each other ill for as long as the stone remains there.

### Of the stone they call serzuzech in Arabic

**T**o the second stone of Saturn, they say **serzuzech** in Arabic. And its virtue is such that he who carries it with him when Saturn is in its <term>exaltation</term> <note>The specific sign where a planet's influence is most powerfully manifested.</note> and received by the moon, and in its hour, and when the first face of Capricorn is ascending—and if the power of the figure of a man who stands on a stool <note>original: "escanno"</note> descends upon this stone, holding a <term>rock-goat</term> <note>original: "rocaz"</note> above his head and in his right hand a sickle as if he wishes to harvest—he will live long and will be healthy in his body from any mishap that might occur from the outside. And even this same stone has another virtue according to the movement of Saturn. If someone carries it with them when Saturn is in the third face of Aquarius, and in its ascendant and its hour, and received by the sun in <term>trine</term> or <term>sextile</term> aspect <note>Geometric angles of 120 and 60 degrees respectively, considered harmonious in astrology.</note>—and if the power of a man standing on a very high roof descends upon this stone—it heals the stone that forms in the bladder or in the kidneys, and the burning that comes from the dripping of urine. Likewise, it makes the blood stop when much of it comes from women after childbirth.

### Of the stone they call jandera. 2-2-2

They call the third stone of Jupiter <term>Pandera</term> <note>original: "jandera" in the heading, "Pandera" in the body text; likely referring to the *Aetites* or "eagle-stone," famous in medieval lore for containing a smaller stone that rattles inside.</note>, because it makes one give birth easily. **M**ars has power over the stone they call <term>magnetite</term> <note>original: "almagnites"; loadstone or magnetic iron ore.</note>. Its virtue is such that whoever carries it with them while Mars is in its <term>exaltation</term> <note>A specific sign where a planet's influence is strongest; for Mars, this is Capricorn.</note> and in good aspect with Jupiter—and when the second face of Aries is the <term>ascendent</term> <note>The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at a specific moment.</note>—shall accomplish all the deeds they desire, whether good or evil. Its power is even greater for evil deeds than for good ones, and in struggles and battles. As long as one carries this stone, they shall never be defeated or overcome by any man. But it performs this more perfectly when the virtue of the figure of a knight upon a lion descends upon this stone, holding a naked sword in his right hand and the head of a man in his left.

# Of the stone they call agate. 2 2 2

**A**gate <note>original: "alaaquec," from the Arabic "al-aqiq."</note> is the name of the second stone of Saturn. It has such virtue that whoever carries it while Mars is in its <term>house</term> <note>The zodiac sign naturally ruled by a planet; for Mars, these are Aries or Scorpio.</note> and in its hour, shall be well-received by the Sun and the Moon. And if the first face of Scorpio is the ascendent, all who see him shall fear him. But this is greater when there descends upon this stone the virtue and figure of a man standing on his feet, dressed in <term>hauberk</term> <note>original: "loriga"; a shirt of mail armor.</note> and holding a sword hanging from his neck, and in his right hand another naked sword, and in the left the head of a man. Furthermore, this stone has another virtue: when worn over a wound or any other place from which blood flows, it makes it stop immediately. This it does more effectively when Mars is in its exaltation and in the ascendent, and well-received by the Moon, and when the virtue of the figure of a lion—which has these letters before it—descends upon the stone. Additionally, this agate stone has another virtue: he who carries it in the hour of Mars, and in its ascendent, and in the third face of Scorpio—being well-received by the Sun and in good aspect with Jupiter—shall be valiant, daring, and bold. Though he be fearful by nature, he shall have no fear of kings, nor of evil thieves, nor other wicked men or dangerous beasts. But it performs this more perfectly when there descends upon this stone the virtue of the figure of a man with a crown on his head, holding a naked sword in his right hand upon which are written the letters of the figure of Mars.

## Of the stone they call copper. ~~~~~

*Alcalce* <note>original: "Alcalce"; likely from the Arabic *al-khals*, meaning pure copper.</note> in Arabic and *alambre* <note>original: "alambre"; a medieval Spanish term for copper or copper alloys like brass.</note> in this <term>Romance</term> <note>Referring to the vernacular Spanish language used by the translators, as opposed to the original Arabic or Latin sources.</note> is the name of the eighth stone of the Sun. And it is also good for those who travel and fear thieves or enemies who might harm them, and it is very helpful to those who are bitten by snakes or scorpions, or by any other poisonous creature.

## Of the stone named Bobi: —

*Bobi* is a stone that, although it belongs entirely to the Sun, Venus has a very large part in it. Therefore, whoever carries this stone with them in the hour of Venus, while she is in her <term>exaltation</term> <note>The specific sign where a planet's influence is considered most powerful; for Venus, this is the sign of Pisces.</note> and in her ascendant, and receiving a good <term>aspect</term> <note>original: "catamiento"; literally "looking," referring to the favorable angular relationship between planets; here, a positive connection between Venus and Jupiter.</note> from Jupiter: they shall be loved and well-regarded by men, and people will speak well of them. But this is manifested more completely if the virtue of the figure of a woman descends upon this stone, who holds an apple in her right hand and in her left a comb made like a tablet, upon which are such figures as are shown here. And let the woman's face be like that of a bird, and her feet like those of an eagle.

<meta>This page transitions from the third lapidary (dealing with celestial figures) to a new book or section, likely the fourth lapidary of the Alfonsine collection. It moves from the powers of constellations to the inherent properties of stones based on their creation, color, and scent. This page introduces the stone "Hyontis."</meta>

Having finished the third lapidary, in which is shown the virtue of stones according to how they receive it from the figures of the sky that descend upon them, and likewise from the positions in which the planets are found; it is now appropriate to show another way <note>The text says "dua manera," likely "duna" or "de una" (of one way), marking the beginning of the fourth book of the Lapidary.</note> that speaks of their virtues according to the <term>constellation</term> <note>In this context, referring to the specific planetary alignment at the moment of the stone's "birth" or creation.</note> in which they are created. It also speaks of the form they receive in their creation, and even of the color they have by their nature, and of the scent that comes from them when they are rubbed vigorously against something with water. Furthermore, it shows how this comes to them through the virtue of the planets that engender and create these things by the power of God, who made them, ordered them, and maintains each one in its state. And this lapidary was composed by **Mahomat Abequich** <note>Likely a reference to the 11th-century Arab physician and pharmacologist Ibn Wafid, known in the West as Abenguefith.</note> according to the knowledge he found in the books of the sages, and he proved it by his own hand. He organized them by the letters of the Arabic alphabet, though here they are organized by the Latin ones.

->**Hyontis** is the<-
->first stone<-
->of the letter **A**, and it is of<-
->seven types,<-
->each of which<-
->has its own color,<-
->and its work is<-
->distinct, whether<-
->for good or<-
->for evil. These<-
->colors are:<-
the first, black; the second, grey; the third, red; the fourth, yellow; the fifth, white; the sixth, sky-blue; the seventh, green. And each of these likewise belongs to its planet. For the black is of **Saturn**, and the grey is of **Jupiter**, the red of **Mars**, and the yellow of the **Sun**, the white of **Venus**, the sky-blue of **Mercury**, and the green of the **Moon**. ### Regarding the second type of the stone Anyontz

The second of the seven types found in this aforementioned stone called **Anyontz** <note>This name likely refers to a variety of jasper or agate; in medieval lapidaries, stones were often classified by their planetary associations rather than modern mineralogy.</note> is spotted by the nature of **Jupiter**, and he is its planet, and its ruler is Thursday. **Atacrifes** is its name in Greek; the fifth stone of the letter D. ¶ This one is of two colors: one is vermilion like a lobster <note>original: "langosta" — can mean locust or lobster; vermilion suggests the latter</note>, and the other is brown, which possesses such clarity at night that a person can see with it as if by the light of a fire. ¶ And the virtue of this stone is useful for the coldness of the kidneys, by drinking its rubbing.

**Axerites** is what they call the sixth stone of the letter D in Greek. It is vermilion in color, and however much one rubs it, its rubbing comes out vermilion, tending toward the color of gold. ¶ And if they weigh it after it has been turned to powder, they will find that its weight has not decreased by any amount. ¶ And this stone has such a property that if a woman who has a flow of blood [hemorrhaging] takes some of its powder on a bit of wool—that is, if she holds it for an hour in her nature <note>a period-appropriate euphemism for the vagina</note>—it will stop it for her. ¶ And for he whose vein is blocked—that is, if he hangs it upon himself—it will be released.

**Amesidicatiz** is the name in Greek for the seventh stone of the letter D. And it is found in Armenia; it is blue in color. ¶ And its virtue is this: its rubbing is helpful for pain of the liver.

**Ambrosis** is its name in Greek: the eighth stone of the letter D. ¶ And its property is such that if someone places it in a pond where there are frogs, they will all gather around it. ¶ And the ancients made images from it that were beneficial for pain of the throat.

**Aquioz** they say in Greek for the ninth stone of the letter D. Its color is that of dark brazilwood <note>original: "bresil" — a reddish-orange dye derived from wood</note>, and it is easy to break. ¶ And

**Auardemuz** is its name in Greek; the tenth stone of the letter D. ¶ This stone has the color of iron, and when it is rubbed, its rubbing comes out vermilion. And with this stone, they clean **seed pearls** <note>original: "alioffar"</note>, round off glass, and polish stones. ¶ And its virtue is: it is helpful for pain in the entrails and for removing excess flesh that grows on a man's body, such as a wart, by carrying it hung upon oneself, for he who has this ailment.

**Aburez** in Greek, **Mabe** in Arabic, and **Crystal** in Latin <note>original: "cristal en latin"</note>—because it exists in many varieties—is the name of the eleventh stone of the letter D. ¶ There are some of these that tend toward brown, and it is useful against **Greek fire** <term>Greek fire</term> <note>In a medical context, this often refers to Erysipelas (a skin infection) or other burning rashes, though it also names the famous incendiary weapon.</note>. ¶ And its virtue is: that he who has the ailment of Greek fire, and rubs this stone with oil and anoints the site of the fire, will be healed. ¶ And whoever has pain in the fingernail, if they keep it hung upon them: it will kill the pain.

**Almelim** is what they call the twelfth stone of the letter D in Greek. ¶ And it is a mineral stone, and it has a brightness like silver. ¶ And this stone is the one they call **Talc** <note>original: "Atalch"</note>. ¶ And the wise men spoke much of it, and some of them said it was the alum that does not melt in fire, but if anyone knew its solution <note>how to dissolve it into a liquid state</note>, its depth <note>its hidden secrets or true power</note> would be revealed. ¶ And some said that if they soak it in very strong vinegar made from wine, it softens until it becomes like a mass, and then they can make a stone that is useful against poisons and for driving out bad swellings <note>original: "testiglos malos" — likely referring to growths or tumors</note> from wherever they wish. ¶ And he who knows well how to dissolve it and anoints the place he desires with it, fire will not take hold there.

**Alyounza** is the name in Greek of the thirteenth stone of the letter D.

### Of the seventh stone of the letter T

**Tous** is the name in Greek for the seventh stone of the letter **T** <note>original: ".t."</note>. And in Arabic it is called **auaca**. ¶ And the aforementioned Mahometh said that if they rub the skin with it, it scrapes the hair from it. ¶ And likewise, workers rub wineskins with it to make them smoother. ¶ If they rub the body with it, the hair will die. ¶ And it had another **virtue** <term>virtue</term> <note>original: "uirtur" — a hidden medicinal or magical power inherent in a substance</note>: that if one who has a fever carries it hanging upon them, it will take the fever away without sweating. ¶ And if they give to drink the water resulting from its rubbing to one who has a fever, it will take it away.

### Of the 8th stone of the letter T

**Tous** they call this 8th stone in Greek. And they call it in Arabic: **adelin**. ¶ It is white in the likeness of marble, and they make vessels from it for kings. And it does not want any ointment to touch it, for whatever place on it that is touched, it turns black immediately. ¶ It never clears up. ¶ And if they grind this stone ¶ and mix it with **white apostolicon** <term>white apostolicon</term> <note>original: "apostoligon blanco" — a renowned medieval healing plaster or ointment used to treat wounds</note>, it will dissolve **abscesses** <term>abscesses</term> <note>original: "postemas"</note> and wounds in which there is much poison, and it will gather the matter. And if any woman holds it: her milk will dry up. ¶ They say that it stops the **woman's flower** <note>original: "tura la flor de la muger" — a common medieval euphemism for menstruation</note>. ¶ And the woman who holds it: it will hinder her pregnancy. ¶ And the drink made from it is the weight of one drachma, or more or less according to the woman's **complexion** <term>complexion</term> <note>original: "complexion" — the specific balance of the four humors (blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile) in an individual</note>, and the hour of the time in which it occurs. ¶ And this shall be according to the sense and the wisdom of knowing the time, and the season, and the age of she to whom it is given to drink.

### Of the 9th stone of the letter T

**Tozyn** they call the 9th stone of the letter **T** in Greek. And it is white in the likeness of crystal, but it is a little darker. And it is set in rings, because it has such **virtue** that he who carries it with him will be well-received

### Of the first stone of the letter Y

### Of the second stone of the letter Y

**Yenctatiz** is the name in Greek for the second stone of the letter **Y**. And it resembles the heart of a bird they call **caerroz**. ¶ And whoever rubs this stone ¶ and gives to drink what comes from it to one who has pain in the liver, it will take it away.

### Of the third stone of the letter Y

**Yalenturnios** they call the third stone of the letter **Y** in Greek. ¶ And it is blackish, tending toward green. ¶ And it aids the **distressed** <note>original: "cupados" — likely meaning those suffering from obstructions or melancholy</note> and those with sadness; when a man carries it with him, such is its **virtue**. letter Kheth. Its color is like a rose, and it has a scent like 
musk <note>original: "ala" — likely referring to an aromatic substance like aloeswood or musk</note>. And its virtue is that if they hang it 
upon a man who is mad, he will be healed immediately on that day.

### Of the second stone of the letter Kheth

The second stone of the letter Kheth they call **Xdyeceyn** 
in Greek <note>original: "xdyeceyn"</note>, and in Arabic *kaceten*. And this is 
one of the three building stones <note>original: "pariapules" — likely referring to stones used for walls or parapets</note> that we shall mention. In 
color it is white; and they use it much in building 
abbeys, towns, and castles. And its 
virtue is that if they grind it and place it upon a 
wound or a cut <note>original: "tmadura" — likely "tajadura"</note> of a nerve or a vein from which blood 
is flowing, it stops it immediately.

->Here begins the book of the forms and of the images that are in the heavens, and of the virtues and of the works that come from them into the bodies that are below the moon’s heaven <note>The "moon's heaven" refers to the sublunary realm—the Earth—which medieval science believed was influenced by the movements of the celestial spheres</note>, which the most high and honored Lord **ALFONSO**—lover of sciences and of knowledge, by the grace of God, **KING** of Castile, of Toledo, of Leon, of Galicia, of Seville, of Cordoba, of Murcia, of Jaén, and of the Algarve, and son of the most honored **KING** Don **FERNANDO** and of **QUEEN Lady BEATRIZ**—ordered to be compiled from the books of the ancient philosophers. And this book was begun in the twenty-fifth year of his reign, in the Year of Caesar: one thousand three hundred and fourteen years <note>The "Spanish Era" or Era of Caesar was a dating system used in Iberia; to find the AD date, subtract 38 years. 1314 minus 38 equals 1276 AD</note>. And in the year of our Lord Jesus Christ: in one thousand two hundred and seventy-six years. And it was finished in the twenty-eighth year of his reign, in the Year of Caesar: in one thousand three hundred and twenty-five years <note>1325 minus 38 equals 1287 AD</note>. And in the year of our Lord Jesus Christ: in one thousand two hundred and seventy-six years <note>The original text repeats the year 1276 here, though the regnal year and the Era of Caesar suggest the completion was actually in 1287 AD</note>.<—

So that this book of ours may be clearer and better understood, and so those who read it may more quickly know the works within it to help themselves when they need them and find them prepared, we have placed here at the beginning of this book its parts and the works of each part individually, just as the ancient sages said and proved. And first we speak of the parts of this book: which are eleven parts.

The first part is by Abolays <note>Abolays: A mysterious figure, likely of Chaldean or Arabic origin, credited with the primary "Lapidary" text Alfonso translated</note>, which speaks of the images and their works made in stones according to the degrees of the twelve signs <note>The twelve signs of the Zodiac</note>; and it has three hundred and sixty chapters.

And the second is by Amtim, which speaks of another manner of images made by the degrees of the signs in stones and with metals mixed together; and it has three hundred and sixty chapters.

And the third is by Pythagoras <note>The famous Greek philosopher, though here associated with astrological magic</note>, which speaks of other kinds of figures that rise in these same degrees that operate in the births of men; and it has three hundred and sixty chapters.

And the fourth is by Yluz, which speaks of the images made in stones according to the faces of the signs <term>faces: also known as "decans," these are ten-degree subdivisions of a zodiac sign</term>. And it has eighty-six chapters.

The fifth is by Telfenus and Yluz, which speaks of many kinds of images made in stones by the planets when they are in their dignities <term>dignities: specific positions in the zodiac where a planet's power is strengthened</term> and in their hours; and it has <note>Space left for number</note> chapters.

And the sixth is by Pliny and Vetrenus and other sages; and it speaks of images made in stones by making rings from them; and it has <note>Space left for number</note> chapters.

The seventh is by Utant; and it speaks of seven images made by the seven planets in seven specific stones, and rings are made of them; and it has seven chapters.

And the eighth is by Ragiel, which speaks of twenty-four images that should be made in specific stones; and it has twenty-four chapters.

The ninth is by Nicoch, which speaks of the waters and the places that are necessary in this work of the stones; and it has seven chapters.

<meta>This page serves as the formal prologue to the Lapidary, transitioning from the specific lists of stone properties found on the previous pages to a historical and philosophical explanation of the work’s origins. It introduces the intellectual lineage of the text, tracing it from Aristotle and ancient Chaldean wisdom through Arabic translations to the court of King Alfonso X of Castile.</meta>

# ON THE SIGN OF ARIES.<note>original: "DEL SIGNO DE ARIES." This heading introduces the first section of the book, which organizes stones according to the degrees of the zodiac sign Aries.</note>

---

Aristotle, who was more accomplished than the other philosophers and who most naturally demonstrated all things through true reason, and made them understood completely as they are, said: that all things that are under the heavens move and are directed by the movement of the celestial bodies, by the <term>virtue<note>In medieval science, "virtue" (vertud) refers to an inherent power, strength, or medicinal property a thing possesses by nature.</note></term> they receive from them according to the order of God, who is the first virtue and from whom all others proceed. And he showed that all things in the world are as if linked together, and receive virtue from one another; the lowliest from the most noble. This virtue appears more manifest in some, such as in animals and in plants, and more hidden in others, such as in stones and in metals. Concerning these, the sages wrote books in which they spoke of the celestial bodies, which are not composed of the four elements, and likewise of the others that are composed of them, such as animals—which are all living things that have a soul to feel and to move—and also of plants, which are the fruits that are born from the earth, such as trees and herbs. They spoke also of the harder things that are made from the earth, such as stones and metals; and of each of these they made books.

But those who wrote of stones—such as Aristotle, who wrote a book in which he named seven hundred of them and told of each one, what color it was, and what size, and what virtue it had, and in what place it was found—so did many other sages who touched upon these matters. Yet among those, there were some who strove further to know the facts about them; they felt it was not enough to know their color, size, and virtue unless they also knew which were the celestial bodies with which they had a connection, and from which they received the virtue by which they were directed to perform their works, according to the alignment of the states of the bodies above in every work of good or evil.

And among the sages who labored most in this was one named Abolais. Although he held the law of the Moors <note>original: "ley de los moros"; meaning he was Muslim.</note>, he was a man who greatly loved the <term>gentiles<note>In this context, "gentiles" likely refers to the ancient pre-Islamic or pre-Christian peoples, specifically the pagans of antiquity like the Chaldeans.</note></term>, and especially those from the land of Chaldea, because his ancestors were from there. And because he knew how to speak that language and read its script, he took great pleasure in searching for their books and studying them, for he had heard it said that in that land were the greatest sages in the world. But because of the great wars and many other occurrences that happened there, the people died out and their knowledge remained as if lost, so that very little of it could be found.

This Abolais had a friend who searched for these books for him and helped him obtain them. Among those he found for him, he discovered this one, which speaks of three hundred and sixty stones, according to the degrees of the signs that are in the <term>eighth heaven<note>In the Ptolemaic system, the eighth heaven (octavo cielo) is the sphere of the fixed stars, beyond the seven spheres of the planets.</note></term>. And it told of each one, what color and name and virtue it has, and in what place it is found, and of the star of the figure that is in the degree of 

<column-break/>

that sign from which the stone receives its force and virtue. And this is according to how the sun runs throughout the entire year through the degrees of the figures of the twelve signs, which total three hundred and sixty. These are all figured with tiny stars and many other figures that are in the eighth heaven, which are also figured with stars—some in the northern part, which is by the star they call the <term>Trasmontana<note>The North Star or Polaris.</note></term>, and others in the southern part. Some of these are within the signs and others outside of them, so that there are forty-eight in all including the signs.

Therefore, when Abolais found this book, he was very joyful with it, for he felt he had found in it what he had desired to find regarding this knowledge of stones. After he had read it much and understood what was in it, he translated it from the Chaldean language into Arabic. During his life, he strove to test those things that lay within it and found them certain and true, for he was a master of the art of astronomy and of the nature of knowing stones.

After he died, this book remained as if lost for a very long time, in such a way that those who had it did not understand it well, nor did they know how to work with it as was fitting, until God willed that it should come into the hands of the noble King Don Alfonso, son of the very noble King Don Fernando and Queen Donna Beatriz, and Lord of Castile, Toledo, León, Galicia, Seville, Córdoba, Murcia, Jaén, and the Algarve. He found it while he was still a prince <note>original: "infante"; the title for the son of a Spanish monarch who is not the direct heir, though Alfonso would become king.</note>, during the life of his father, in the year he won the Kingdom of Murcia, which was in the era of <unclear>year omitted</unclear>.

And he obtained it in Toledo from a Jew who had kept it hidden, who did not wish to make use of it himself nor for it to be of benefit to any other.

And once he had this book in his power, he had it read to another of his Jews who was his physician; they called him Judah Mosca the Younger, who was very learned in the art of astronomy and knew and understood well both Arabic and Latin. When the King, through this physician of his, understood the goodness and the great profit that lay within the book, he commanded him to translate it from Arabic into the Castilian language <note>Spanish.</note>, so that men might understand it better and know how to benefit from it more. In this translation, he was assisted by Garci Pérez, one of his clerics, who was likewise very learned in this knowledge of astronomy. The translation was finished in the second year after the noble King Don Fernando, his father, won the city of Seville.

This book is very noble and very precious. Whoever wishes to benefit from it must keep three things in mind. First, that they be learned in astronomy, so they know how to recognize the stars, in what state they are, and in what season the greatest virtue comes from them to the stones, according to the virtue they receive from God. The second thing is that they know how to recognize the stones and their colors and features, and also that they certainly know the designated places where they grow and where they are found, and to distinguish the counterfeit from the natural, and also to tell apart those that naturally resemble one another...

->DEL SIGNO<-

...recognizing them by weight, and by hardness, and by the other signs by which they can be recognized by a man who is skilled in this knowledge.

The third thing is that he be knowledgeable in the art of <term>physic<note>original: "fisica." In the Middle Ages, this referred to the study of nature and medicine.</note></term>, for much of it is enclosed within the virtue of the stones, as is shown in this book; and that he knows how to work with them as it commands: and that he be of good sense so that he knows how to help himself with the things that do good, and guard against those that cause harm. And working in this way, he will reach what he wishes to do through them, and see marvelous things of their virtue which they receive from God; for which he will have to praise and bless His name, which is blessed forever and ever. Amen.

### **Of the stone they call Magnetat in Chaldean and Arabic; and in Latin, Magnetes; and in the Castilian language, Aimant [Magnet].** <note>1 vuelto: This indicates the reverse side of the first leaf of the manuscript.</note>

From the first sign, which is Aries—which means the figure of a ram, and is the house of Mars and the exaltation of the sun—and according to the <term>complexion<note>In medieval science, a "complexion" is the specific balance of the four qualities: hot, cold, moist, and dry.</note></term> it shows in all its works, it is hot and dry. And the stone that is in its first degree is called Magnetat in Chaldean and in Arabic, and in Latin *Magnetes*, and in the Castilian language *Aimante* <note>original: "Aimante," the lodestone or magnet.</note>.

And this stone is black in color, but leans a bit toward reddish. And there are some in which a purple color appears, like blue; and these are the greatest. And although the mine of these stones is found in many parts, the greatest of all is that of the land of India, which they find near the sea. And this stone has a natural virtue within it to pull iron with very great force. And because it seems a great marvel to those who do not know the nature of the properties of things, that this stone—which is by its nature hot and dry—can pull iron, which we say is cold and dry, they should not marvel at it: for if they look closely at the words of the sages, they will find that all things that pull one another do so in two ways: either by similarity or by contrast.

And of this, the sages showed many reasons which it is not necessary to put in this book, for what is said here is quite enough for any knowledgeable man, if he knows how to pay attention to what they said: for by the property of this stone they can know all the others. And the pulling that this does is according to its size relative to the iron it pulls: so that, in the land of India, in the mountain where they find them, which is near the sea, it pulls all the nails from the ships that pass near it by the force of the part where the rock is: so that it makes them fly like arrows. And if they are well-riveted, so that it cannot stretch and pull them out, it makes the ships go toward it so fast that they strike the rocks and perish. And it is a great marvel that iron, which overcomes all other metals by the strength it has in itself, is overcome by this stone through its property, and makes it come obediently toward it. And by this, it is shown that this pulling is more by the force of contrast than similarity. And so great is the virtue that iron receives from this stone when it joins with it—if it is very fine—that it pulls other smaller irons toward itself, so that they stick to it as to the stone: and in this way, it can pull many irons sticking to one another in as great a quantity as it can suffer. And this virtue is so proven and manifest that, besides what a man sees with his eyes, holding the stone in one hand and the iron in the other, he feels how it goes to stick to it, and one iron to the other. And if a man wishes for this stone to lose its virtue, let him put it in the juice of garlic or onions, so that it is entirely covered for three days and three nights, and it will lose it. And if he wishes for it to recover it, let him put it for another three days and three nights in the blood of a goat, so that it is also entirely covered, and it will recover it, changing the blood every day. And in this stone, there is also another great marvel: that if they put it in an earthenware vessel, in a furnace with a strong fire, and do this four times, changing the vessel each time for a new one; and once it is burnt and they take it out of the furnace and place a bit of sulfur near it, and sprinkle the stone

<column-break/>

with water, fire will come out of it such that it will burn very far away anything it reaches that can burn. And it does this because it is hot and dry: and when they burn it, the virtue of the fire is enclosed within it, and hidden: and therefore it flees from water, which is its opposite, cold and moist; and it joins with sulfur which is its similar, hot and dry. And in this way, fleeing very fast from its opposite, which is stronger than itself, and joining with great force to its similar, it burns from afar, as was said above. And if a man wishes for it to lose this burning, let him pour upon it oil of whatever nature he wishes, and it will lose it. And this stone has a virtue in it that he who carries it with him, if he is a man weak of heart, it will give him courage; and if he is courageous, it will give him more. And in the art of physic it is very useful: for if they give any man iron filings to drink, or any other kind of poison in which iron is mixed, or if he is wounded with poisoned iron, by grinding this stone and making it into powder, and mixing it with whatever oil he wishes, and giving it to drink to the one who is poisoned, the poison will come out from below <note>A polite medieval way of referring to excretion or purging.</note> and he will be healed immediately. It will do the same if they put it ground upon the wound of the one who is poisoned. And he who wishes to know with which stars this stone has its connection, and from which it receives its strength and virtue, know that they are those three that are in Aries and follow the knot of the line of the figure of Pisces; and one of them is at the end of the tail of one fish. And the property they have of pulling iron is by the virtue they receive from these stars. And when the middle one of them rises on the eastern horizon, it will have greater force and more virtue in all these works that we have mentioned.

### **Of the stone they call Zurudica.** <note>2 vuelto: The reverse side of the second leaf.</note>

From the second degree of the sign of Aries is the stone they call Zurudica, which means the destroyer of the liver. And this stone is purple <note>original: "cardena," a dark, bruised-looking purple.</note> in its color; so that it resembles the sapphire in its purpleness, but not in its light; for the sight does not pass through this one as it does with the sapphire; for its color is very thick and turbid, but there are some in which they find white grains, like drops; and these are the largest. And they find them in the Promised Land on the bank of a river they call *Alberich*, which flows between two mountains, far from any settlement. This stone is by its nature hot and dry: and its property is that he who carries it with him has great fear without reason, without seeing a cause for it. And according to the nature of physic, to do harm it has such a virtue that when they polish it or grind it and give a known quantity of those polishings or grindings to someone to drink, it will destroy the entire liver, blood coming out from below so that it will never stop until he dies. And if they put the liver of any animal in a basin and the stone with it, it will destroy it all, and turn it into flowing blood. And the middle star of the three that are in the belt of the <term>Chained Woman<note>This refers to the constellation Andromeda.</note></term> has power over this stone and from it, it receives its strength and its property. And when this star is in the ascendant, this stone will have greater force and show its works more manifestly.

### **Of the stone they call Gagatiz in Chaldean and in Latin Gagates.** <note>2 vuelto.</note>

From the third degree of the sign of Aries is the stone they call Gagatiz in Chaldean and in Latin *Gagates* <note>Commonly known today as Jet.</note>. It takes this name from a river where they find it called Gaga, and they also call it the River of Hell, and it flows near the house of the Temple. The sight does not pass through this stone, for it is the color of turbid clay: and they find it also in Spain in some mountains that are near Zaragoza in a place they call Diche. And also in the mountain that is near Granada they call Soler in some caves that are there. But those from Zaragoza as well as those from Granada are few and are not as good as those found in the River Gaga. This stone is by its nature hot and dry and has such a property that when they polish it and give what comes from it to a man whose body smells bad because of sweat, to drink, it reaches him and makes him smell good. And even besides this, it has another property: if they gird it upon the belly of a man who has in his intes[tines]...

...certain worms that they call "pumpkin seeds" <note>original: "simiente de calabazas." ### Of the stone they call Miliztiz. (3.)

Belonging to the third degree of the sign of Aries is the stone they call Miliztiz, which means in the <term>Chaldean<note>A term often used in the Middle Ages to refer to Aramaic or ancient Babylonian languages.</note></term> tongue "ripener of abscesses." This stone is of a deep purple color that resembles blue; it breaks easily and can be crumbled between the fingers. This stone is found in the mountain that is near the House of the Temple <note>Likely referring to the Temple in Jerusalem.</note> in certain places there that resemble caves: and whoever enters inside feels a heat like that of a bath, and a smell like smoke. There are both large and small versions of these stones: and those that have white mixed with the purple are the best. When this stone is polished, it becomes clear and bright, just like other stones. It has such a property that it attracts the stalks of <term>hemlock<note>original: "ciguda." A highly toxic plant.</note></term>, just as the Magnet attracts iron. In the art of <term>physic<note>original: "física." Medieval natural philosophy and medicine.</note></term> it provides great benefit; for he who grinds it and kneads it with any liquid and places it upon an abscess causes it to ripen immediately: and if he hangs it over the area, it does the same. And should anyone wish to use it for evil and gives someone six <term>drachmas<note>A unit of weight; approximately 3.5 grams.</note></term> to drink, the person will die as venom is expelled from below: but if he drinks less than this amount, he will escape. And for the one who is known to have drunk it, if they give him any oil to drink, it will not harm him and he will recover very well. This stone is by its nature hot and dry, and the virtue and force it possesses comes from the southern star of the three that are upon the belt of the Chained Woman who never knew a husband <note>The constellation Andromeda.</note>. And when this star is in <term>mid-heaven<note>The highest point the star reaches in the sky.</note></term>, the stone shows its work most effectively.

### Of the stone they call Ceritiz. (3.)

Belonging to the fifth degree of the sign of Aries is the stone they call Ceritiz. It is found in the land of India on an island where a river of the same name flows; they find it on the banks of that water, and it is of a green color so dark that it borders on black. This stone is very strong; and they weigh one hundred and twenty drachmas. When they clean and polish it, men can see themselves in it as if in a mirror of <term>al-binde<note>original: "espeyo dalbinde." This likely refers to a high-quality glass or polished metal mirror, possibly of Persian or Arabic origin.</note></term>. It is likewise by its nature hot and dry, and has in itself such a property that if a woman keeps it hung upon her or set in a ring when she lies with a man, she will never conceive anything but a male. This same effect will happen to any animal upon which it is hung. This virtue is received from the star that is in the turn of the River <note>The constellation Eridanus.</note>, the one that touches the chest of <term>Cetus<note>original: "Caitoz." The constellation of the Sea Monster.</note></term>. And when this star is in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works most clearly.

### Of the stone they call the Mover. (3 verso)

Belonging to the sixth degree of the sign of Aries is the stone that is called the Mover, and it has this name because when they polish it and take the powder that comes from it and give it to a pregnant woman to drink, the child will die immediately, and she will expel it from herself, dead or alive, in whatever state it may be. It does the same if she merely keeps it hung upon her. It will do the same to any animal that drinks of it or has it hung upon them. This virtue is bad for women who have living children in their wombs and do not wish to lose them, but good for those who have dead children and cannot expel them, or who are so weak that they cannot give birth. The color of this stone is a mixture of green and red; but its greenness is so faint that it tends toward yellow: and likewise, the redness is so slight that it resembles the water of meat when it is put into salt. Its mine is on the shores of the islands of the sea in the land called <term>Cin<note>China.</note></term>. By its nature, it is hot and dry. And the star that follows the one in the turn of the River has power over this stone, and from it

<column-break/>

the stone receives its force and virtue. And when that star is in the ascendant, this stone shows its works most clearly.

### Of the stone they call Goliztiz. (3 verso)

Belonging to the seventh degree of the sign of Aries is the stone they call Goliztiz. This name comes from a river so called where it is found on the shores of the Indian Sea. Because it is found in no other place but there, it has no other name but that of the river. By nature, it is hot and dry. Its color is gray mixed with yellow, but the yellowness is greater than the gray. Its property is that if they take ten drachmas' weight of it, it will attract half a drachma of copper or brass, just as the magnet attracts iron: and according to this proportion, it attracts more or less. It also has another virtue: if they take half a drachma of it by weight and throw it upon ten drachmas of molten silver, it will turn it a yellow color. And if they do this three or four times, it will turn the color of pure gold and will endure the melting of fire forever after: but it is not natural gold. This happens because it has within it the nature of red sulfur. In the art of physic, it has this virtue: if they take two barley-corns' weight of it, grind it, mix it with fresh water, and put it into the nostrils of one born with the sickness they call "the demon" <note>This likely refers to epilepsy or perhaps severe mental illness, which were often attributed to demonic influence.</note>, he will be cured the first time, or at the latest, the second. The leading star of the two in the horn of the sign of Aries, and the other in the neck of this figure, have power over this stone, and from them it receives its virtue. When these stars are in the ascendant, this stone shows its works most clearly.

### Of the stone they call Telliminuz. (4.)

Belonging to the eighth degree of the sign of Aries is the stone they call Telliminuz. This stone is by its nature hot and dry, and its dryness is in the fourth degree <note>Medieval medicine categorized qualities in four degrees of intensity; the fourth was the most extreme.</note>. It is black in color and there appears in it a certain amount of redness, so that it resembles grains of pepper. It is strong and very hard, so that it cannot be broken by anything except yellow brass that is dyed with the dye of Alexandria: and this breaks it in such a way that when the brass touches the stone, it breaks immediately. This is found in the land of the Blacks, on the bank of a river that passes through those places where these stones are: and they find them there in various colors and shapes; but they are always found in a round and flat form, made like a small cake: some large and some small. Its virtue is very useful in the art of physic; for if they place it over a wound or a sore, it heals very quickly, without venom or abscess forming in it. If they hang it over the area, it does the same. And the star that is over the head of the figure of the Woman seated in the chair <note>Cassiopeia.</note> and the other that is in the elbow area of that same figure, which they call the "stained palm" <note>original: "palma tinta." A traditional name for the star Beta Cassiopeiae (Caph), which in Arabic tradition was part of a "stained hand."</note>, have power over this stone, and from them it receives its force and virtue. When they are in the ascendant, this stone shows its works most clearly.

### Of the stone they call Milititaz. (4.)

Belonging to the ninth degree of the sign of Aries is the stone they call Milititaz. This is by its nature hot and dry. They find it in the islands of a land named Cin <note>China.</note>, in a place where a river runs that they call the River of Honey. This stone is light in weight and very porous; it is never found except in a square shape. It is red in color, but not very much, for a large part of it tends toward yellow: and there are some that are found entirely yellow. Its property is such that if they polish it with anything, a sweet taste like honey comes from it. In the art of physic, this is of great benefit; for if they give it to drink to a man who has a cough or other ailment of the chest, it is of very great help and heals him immediately. And if they hang it over the place where the ailment is, it will do the same, though not as quickly. And the leading star of the three following stars in the figure of the River <note>Eridanus.</note> has power over this stone, and from it the stone receives its force and virtue.

## Of the stone that flees from milk. (4 verso.)

Belonging to the tenth degree of the sign of Aries is the stone that flees from milk. This is hot and dry in its nature. It is black in color and porous, in such a way that it is very light in weight. It is rough to the touch and easy to break. It is found on the bank of a river named Disla, which is in the land of Egypt. And its property is such that if they place it near the milk of any animal whatsoever, the stone leaps and flees very forcefully from it; so much so, that in no way does it wish to be joined with it. And this is because of the enmity it has with milk according to its nature. This stone is very good in the <term>art of physics<note>Medicine or natural science.</note></term>, for if they grind it and temper it with vinegar and smear it upon any of the <term>morpheas<note>original: "morfegas." Chronic skin conditions that cause discoloration, such as vitiligo or types of leprosy.</note></term>, whether white or black, it heals them immediately. And the star that is in the right knee of the <term>Chained Woman<note>The constellation Andromeda.</note></term> has power and lordship over this stone, and from it, the stone receives its force and virtue. And when that star is in the <term>ascendant<note>The point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon.</note></term>, this stone will demonstrate its works more clearly.

## Of the stone they call Aliofar <note>original: "Aliofar." An archaic Spanish term for pearl, derived from Arabic.</note>. (4 verso.)

Belonging to the eleventh degree of the sign of Aries is the stone they call Pearl. This is by its nature hot and dry. They find it in many parts of the great sea that surrounds the world, inside very large shells in which they are grown in this manner: when the north winds blow, the shells open and catch that moisture which the winds bring; and with those drops of dew that fall into them, they close, and go by night to the bottom of the water. When day comes, they emerge and place themselves against the sun, and open, and catch a great portion of its heat; afterward, they descend to the bottom, and they do the same in the evening when the sun sets. And once they understand that the water is congealed, they become light; so much so, that the waves of the sea push them so strongly that they cast them onto the shore. When the waves recede, they pull the shells with them, and when they extend, they send them outward. By being moved in this way, the pearls become round, beautiful, and shiny. The larger, whiter, and clearer they are, the more they are worth. And although this stone is very white, the sight does not pass through it because its whiteness is thick; but it is very lustrous of itself, as if it were polished. Those that come out with a bad color, or cloudy, or of a bad shape—not being well-rounded or smooth—this is only because of a fault in the growth of the shells, which did not receive as much air or heat from the sun as they should, nor at the proper season, or were not allowed to be moved by the waves to become round. This stone is very noble and highly prized by men, and there is great virtue in it; for all who see it love it for its form and for the beauty it has of itself, and it has no need for help from a craftsman. Great lords prize it highly, for it is counted as one of the noble stones. In the art of medicine, it is very good, for it is very helpful for the trembling of the heart, and for those who are sad or fearful, and for every illness that comes from <term>melancholy<note>In medieval medicine, an excess of "black bile," thought to cause sadness and physical ailments.</note></term>; for it cleanses the blood of the heart and brightens it, and removes all cloudiness from it; and for this reason, it is beneficial for the things mentioned. Therefore, physicians put them in their medicines and in the <term>electuaries<note>A medicinal paste made of honey or syrup mixed with powdered herbs or minerals.</note></term> with which they heal these diseases, giving them to be eaten. Furthermore, they make powders from them to put in the eyes, because it greatly clarifies the vision, strengthening the nerves, removing vapors, and drying up the moisture that descends to them. If this stone is dissolved in such a way that it turns to water, and one smears the <unclear>...</unclear> with it, it will heal it the very first time. It will do the same by putting it in the nostrils of one who has a headache caused by the movement of the nerves of the eyes. He who wishes to dissolve this stone should grind it thoroughly, and then knead it with the juice of a bitter citron, and place it in a glazed earthen vessel, and cover it with that juice, and hang it over another vessel of very strong vinegar; and close the mouths of the vessels very well, and bury them in moist manure, and let them stay so for fourteen days; and at the end of that

<column-break/>

period, he will find that stone turned into water. The star that is in the southern part of the Triangle, which is in the third turn of the figure of the Dragon, and the other star that is in the breast of the one who is seated in the chair <note>Cassiopeia.</note>, these have power over this stone, and from them, it receives its virtue. And when these stars are also in the middle of the sky, this stone will demonstrate its works more clearly.

## Of the stone they call Anetatiz. (5 recto.)

Belonging to the twelfth degree of the sign of Aries is the stone they call Anetatiz, which means "bloody stone" <note>likely Hematite.</note>. By its nature, it is hot and dry, and it is of a dark red color that tends toward blood-red. It is so thick that the sight does not pass through it, and it is strong and very heavy. When they polish it, what comes off it resembles blood in color and in all its qualities. Its virtue is such that if they hang it over the <term>apostemes<note>Abscesses or inflammatory swellings.</note></term> that break out, it dissolves them in one day; and especially if they smear them with the polishings that come from it. If they cast this substance, which resembles blood, into eyes that are tearing, it stops the tears. It is helpful for all diseases of the eyes that are caused by moisture, and this is because of the great heat and dryness that is in it. It does even more, for he who looks at it every day when he rises in the morning is safe from having an abscess in his eyes. The two stars—one toward the north and the other toward the south—which are over the mouth of the sign of Aries, have power over this stone, and from them, it receives its virtue. When these are in the ascendant or in mid-heaven, then this stone will demonstrate its works most.

## Of the stone they call Beruth. (5 verso.)

Belonging to the thirteenth degree of the sign of Aries is the stone they call Beruth, and it has another name by which they call it, Azuz, because they find it in a mountain in the land of Egypt that is named thus. The Egyptians call it the "Snow of Acin" <note>original: "Nief de Acin."</note>, and this is because it has a white color, though it has some yellow veins in it. It is a very light stone and easy to break, for it breaks very easily with whatever hits it. They find upon it a color that resembles the dust found on the walls of a mill. This it receives from the nature of the dew of that sea near where they find them. By its nature, it is hot and dry. When they want to test if it is good, they place some of it on the tongue, and they feel as though it bites, because of the sharpness it has in it. It has such virtue that when they grind it and put its powder on abscesses, it makes them open in one day. If they put it on a wound in which there is rotten flesh, it removes it in the same way. It also does another very powerful thing: if a very fat man carries it with him, it will make him thin quickly without doing him any harm. Therefore, it is good for men who are excessively fat and wish to become thin quickly and without labor. The middle star of the three that are in the mouth of <term>Caitoz<note>The constellation Cetus, the Sea Monster.</note></term>—which is the one in the center—and the northern one of those that are over the eye, and the eyebrow of that same figure, the one that appears to be over the hair, these stars have power over this stone, and from them, it receives its virtue. When they are in the ascendant, this stone demonstrates its virtue most.

## Of the stone they call the Stone of China. (5 verso.)

Belonging to the fourteenth degree of the sign of Aries is the stone they call the Stone of China <note>original: "Piedra de Cin."</note>, because they find it in that land which is so named. The people of that place call it Tatiz, which means as much as "hollow inside." By its nature, it is hot and dry, and of a brown color with black veins, and it is strong and hard to break. When they break it, they find it empty inside. It has such virtue that if they hang it around the neck of one who has the abscess they call <term>quinsy<note>original: "esquinancia." An inflammation of the throat or tonsils.</note></term>, he heals immediately; and if they grind it and give it to him to drink, it will do the same. Furthermore, it has another very strange property: for flies flee from the place where it is. Therefore, the people of that land make vessels and bowls from it in which they keep their food. And besides this, it does another thing: if they put it in olive oil, it dissolves.

### Of the stone that attracts gold. (6.)

Belonging to the fifteenth degree of the sign of Aries is the stone that attracts gold. It is hot and dry in its nature; and of a yellow color that leans toward brown. When a person takes it in their hand, it feels smooth and soft. This stone attracts gold and makes it obey just as the magnet attracts iron. And if one were to file gold and mix the filings with earth or any other thing, and the stone touches it, it will separate the gold from the other things with which it was mixed, and it will all cling to the stone. Goldsmiths <note>original: "orebes"</note>, or those who wish to purify gold, use this stone often. And if they burn it—just like the stone we mentioned that attracts iron—it will have a greater power to burn than that one. This stone also has another virtue: it gives great joy to the heart, so much so that he who looks upon it in the morning will go about happily all that day, unless some great excess occurs to make him sad. And the middle star of the three that are in the space of the "Return of the River" <note>The constellation Eridanus.</note> has power over this stone and from it receives its virtue. And when this star is in the ascendant, this stone shows its works more clearly.

### Of the stone that sucks blood. (6.)

Belonging to the sixteenth degree of the sign of Aries is the stone that sucks blood. This is hot and dry in its nature, and it is found in certain places in the eastern parts. Its color is green with a red spot <note>This describes the mineral Heliotrope, commonly known as Bloodstone.</note>. He who takes it in his hand finds it rough and light, because it is very porous. In shape, it is flat on one side and round on the other, in the figure of a hemisphere. Its property is such that if the skin of any animal is broken and the stone is placed there, it pulls the blood out with very great force; and it does this in the living body, but not when the blood is already separated. And he who wishes to know the quantity of blood it pulls should weigh it after it has pulled the blood, and then place it in hot water; all the blood it has pulled will come out of it, and it will remain as it was before. Then he should weigh it again, and he will know the quantity of blood it drew. And the star that descends toward the midday part, which is in the right foot of the Chained Woman <note>The constellation Andromeda.</note>, has power over this stone and from it receives its virtue. And when it is in the ascendant, this stone shows its works more clearly.

### Of the stone that appears in the sea when Mars rises. (6 verso.)

Belonging to the seventeenth degree of the sign of Aries is the stone that appears in the sea when the planet called Mars rises, and it hides when that planet sets. This is hot and dry in its nature, and it is found in the western sea. Its color is red and clear, in the manner of fire. It is always found in a round shape and in no other way. And when Mars appears above the earth, this stone rises upon the sea and floats upon the waves; and when the planet sets, the stone descends and goes to the bottom of the water. It always goes about in this way, rising and descending; and this stone can never be taken except when Mars is above the earth. There is a brilliance in it that appears like lightning, or a coal of burning fire. Those that are of good quality give light at night like a candle, and it has this brilliance when Mars is above the earth; but when the planet sets, it immediately turns murky like any other stone and darkens. This is one of the great wonders that appears through the power that the planets have over stones and mines, through the virtue that God placed in them. Furthermore, this stone has such a property that he who carries it is obeyed by lions, so much so that he can take them with his hands and they will do him no harm; for the lion, when it sees the stone, loses all its strength and has no power in itself. And the star

<column-break/>

which is in the middle of the three that are at the bottom of the triangle <note>The constellation Triangulum.</note>, has power over this stone and from it receives its virtue. And when it is in the middle of the sky, this stone shows its work most fully.

### Of the stone that attracts glass. (6 verso.)

Belonging to the eighteenth degree of the sign of Aries is the stone that attracts glass. This is hot and dry in its nature. Its color is brown and it has black veins in it; it is heavy, rough to the touch, and cracks form within it. This stone is found in no other place but a mountain in Sicily called Vulcan <note>Mount Etna.</note>, which is always burning. Its property is such that fire cannot burn it, because it always dwells within it, nor can fire ever make it change its color. It also has another property: that glass obeys it, and it attracts glass just as the magnet attracts iron. This attraction is in proportion to its own size, and therefore it is counted among the "attracting stones." And if it is brought near any work made of glass—vessels or anything else—they break immediately; and if it is placed at the mouth of the furnace where glass is kept, it makes the glass leap out, whether it be hot or cold. It performs this virtue according to its size or weight. Furthermore, it has another property: he who carries it with him is safe from having <term>gout<note>A form of inflammatory arthritis; in the Middle Ages, often used to describe various joint pains.</note></term> in the feet or in the joints. This is because it strengthens those places where the gout might come; and if the gout has already arrived, although it may not take it away entirely, the person improves much in their illness; and if they carry it for a long time, they may be healed of it. And the star that is at the end of the spine of the sign of Aries, and the other that is in the right foot of the Chained Woman, have power over this stone and from them it receives its virtue. And when these two are in the middle of the sky, this stone will show its works more clearly.

### Of the stone named Annora. (7.)

Belonging to the nineteenth degree of the sign of Aries is the stone they call Annora, which means "limestone" in <term>Chaldean<note>A term often used in this period to refer to Aramaic or related Semitic languages.</note></term>. This is the stone from which they make lime. Its nature is hot and dry; and it is found in most places on the earth, for in all the heavy works that men must do, they help themselves much with it. It joins stones together very strongly and seals pierced places in such a way that water cannot escape; therefore, men repair pipes with it, seal ships, and put it in every other thing they wish to keep from leaking. When this stone is burned, fire is locked within it until water is thrown over it, and then it demonstrates the heat it has enclosed within itself, for steam comes out of it like smoke. And if sulfur is placed near it, fire comes out that burns; however, not as much as the other burning stones we have named or will name later in the proper place. When this stone is mixed with <term>azarnech<note>original: "azarnech." Orpiment, a yellow arsenic sulfide mineral used as a pigment and depilatory.</note></term> and smeared upon the hair of any animal, it scrapes it all off in a short time. And if it is left there for long, it flays the skin. It is like a great poison; for if these stones are ground and tempered together as required, and the water from them is given to someone to drink, it punctures the bladder, makes sores in the intestines, and damages the liver with great harm. But in this stone, which has been described, there is also great benefit; for if it is ground with oil to make an ointment, and large and wide sores are smeared with it, they join together very quickly and heal very well. And the star that is above the ankle of the hind foot of the sign of Aries has force and lordship over this stone, and from it the stone receives its force and virtue; and when it is in the middle of the sky, this stone will show its works more clearly.

It is also of many kinds, but the best are five. The first of these is of the color of <term>Prasme<note>Prase, a leek-green variety of quartz or chalcedony.</note></term> green...

The same is true of the green Jasper <note>original: "Yaspio"</note>, which resembles Prase <note>original: "Prasme"; a leek-green variety of chalcedony</note>, but is not of its nature or its complexion, nor does it have the same properties, as will be shown later in this book. ### Of the stone called Tuminon. (7 verso.)

Belonging to the twenty-first degree of the sign of Aries is the stone they call Tuminon, which we have already mentioned in this book, being the second kind of jasper. This one is the color of white wine that leans toward yellow, and this yellowness is mixed somewhat with red. It is found on the shore of the island of Zarandin. Its shape is round, but not perfectly so; it is very beautiful and very clear, and sight passes through it. This kind of jasper is more prized than the others we have mentioned. It has such virtue that he who carries it with him is guarded from that illness called the "falling sickness" <note>original: "caduca"; epilepsy</note>. Furthermore, it is good for those illnesses that come from melancholy; for it removes them by strengthening the heart and making it great. It does another thing: if they grind it and give it to be drunk by one who has ulcerated intestines, it heals them very quickly. For this reason, physicians put it into electuaries <note>term: electuary <gloss>a medicinal paste made of honey or syrup and powdered herbs/minerals</gloss></note> and other medicines to strengthen the heart and remove melancholic diseases. And the star that is upon the knees of the woman seated in the chair <note>The constellation Cassiopeia</note> has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its strength and virtue. And when she is in the ascendant, the works of this stone appear most clearly.

### Of the stone they call Astarnuz. (8.)

Belonging to the twenty-second degree of the sign of Aries is the stone they call Astarnuz, which means "star-like," and it is the third kind of jasper we mentioned which has white translucent veins. Because these veins always shine like stars, they gave it this name. It is found in that river we already mentioned where these jaspers are found; it is more noble than any of them, and men prize it more because it is more shining and better than all the others. It is of such a nature that when they put it in the fire, the longer it remains there, the purer its light becomes, and it grows more beautiful; for the fire does not harm it, but rather purifies it and increases its light, just as it does to other stones that are brightened by fire. Therefore, it is necessary that whoever wishes to work with this stone should know the skill 

<column-break/>

of making the fire with which the stone must be tempered. This is how it is done: when they put the stone in the crucible <note>original: "albot"; likely an alchemical vessel or pot</note>, they should cover it with another from above, seal it well with mud, and make two furnaces—one to provide fire from below and the other from above—so that it receives the heat equally. When they wish to see if the stone is tempered, they should uncover it, and if they see it is not yet as it should be, they should let it remain. When it is refined, they must not take it out suddenly, but let it stay in the furnace until it cools by itself; for when the heat of noble stones is much inflamed and they are taken quickly into the air, they desire so much to receive the cold of the air that they split and break. When the stone cools by itself, it does not do this. The virtue of this stone is that he who carries it with him finds his heart strengthened, it gives him joy, and makes a man perform his deeds with ease. And if they hang this stone on a man who has pain in his belly or his liver, it takes it away immediately if the illness is new; and if it be old, it brings him great benefit, for it allows it to grow no further. And the leading star of the two that are at the base of the triangle, which is formed in the third turn of the figure of the Dragon <note>The constellation Draco</note>, has power over this stone and from it receives its virtue. And when it is in the ascendant, this stone shows its work more fully.

### Of the stone called Belinniz. (8.)

Belonging to the twenty-third degree of the sign of Aries is the stone called Belinniz. This is the other kind of jasper we mentioned that has the color of clear and clean air in its light; for this is very shining like the air, so that sight passes entirely through it. But it has no color of its own, just like the air, which has no color itself but receives every other color it comes near; this stone behaves in the same way, for when the air is clear, the stone is clear, and when the air is cloudy, it is cloudy. It is found on the bank of that river where the other jaspers we have spoken of are found. It has such virtue that it takes away the pain in half of the head which they call in Arabic *jaqueca* <note>original: "jaqueca"; modern Spanish for migraine</note> and in Latin *migranea* <note>original: "migranea"; migraine</note>. It does this by hanging it over that part where the pain is. Also, if they hang it on young boys while they are being raised, it brings them great benefit in their growth; for they grow better and healthier because of it, and furthermore, it makes them so they are not criers. And the middle star of the three that are in the body of Cetus <note>original: "Caitoz"; the sea monster constellation</note> has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its strength and virtue. And when it is in the middle of the sky, the work of this stone will be stronger and of greater virtue.

### Of the stone called Gaciuz. (8 verso.)

Belonging to the twenty-fourth degree of the sign of Aries is the stone they call Gaciuz, which means "smoky"; and this is the fourth kind of jasper of which we have spoken, which has the color of smoke, so that it appears smoky. It is the most common of all the other jaspers we mentioned. It is a dark stone that has no clarity nor receives a polish. It is found on the bank of that river where the other aforementioned stones are found. By its nature it is hot and dry, and it has such virtue that if they give four drachmas <note>A unit of weight</note> by weight of its powder in a drink to one who has pain in the intestine called the colon, he is healed immediately. And if they gird it or hang it over the belly, it will do the same, but not so quickly. Of this kind of jasper, they find in the island of Zarandin some small stones and others so large that men make pillars or door-sills and beds for sleeping from them. And the star that is in front of the two against the spine of the tail of Aries has power over this stone, and from it receives its virtue. And when it is in the ascendant, this stone will show its works most clearly.

### Of the stone called Abietitiz. (9.)

The stone called Abietitiz belongs to the 26th degree of the sign of Aries; its name means <term>Vulture-stone<gloss>original: "Boitrenna"</gloss></term>; and it has this name because the female vulture carries it to her nest so that she may give birth to her young more easily. Its nature is hot and dry, and it is the second type we mentioned, which is called Cabroci. It is found in the shape of an acorn, though some are somewhat longer. It is soft, easy to break, light in weight, and tends toward white, though not greatly so. When broken, another harder stone is found inside that tends slightly toward yellow; and sometimes they also find other small yellow stones inside, which are easy to break like the others. This stone has such virtue that when it is placed in deerskin and tied to a woman’s left thigh when she is in labor, she gives birth immediately, easily and without danger, and the children are born without injury, provided nature did not err in forming them beforehand. The star that is the middle of the three in the tail of Aries has power over this stone and gives it its strength and virtue. And when it is in the middle of the sky, this stone shows its works most clearly.

### Of the stone named Lubi. (9.)

The stone called Lubi belongs to the 27th degree of the sign of Aries. Its nature is hot at the beginning of the first degree and dry at the beginning of the second. It is the third type we have mentioned, called Lubi; it is found in the land of Libya in a cave at the base of a mountain called Mount Corcor. These stones are small and the color of sand. They are light and soft to the touch, and easy to break. When broken, another white stone is found inside that is very hard and difficult to break. Whoever takes this stone, grinds it, and knows how to turn it into liquid can make a very strong glue from it to join leathers with such a powerful bond that the seam where they were joined cannot be seen. For this reason, they make the fine <term>adargas<gloss>Leather shields used in Iberia and North Africa</gloss></term> in that land, which neither iron nor anything else can pierce. Glue made in this manner is also good for joining wounds before any venom or abscess forms; for afterward, it would not be able to do so. This stone has another virtue: if it is tied with a crimson silk thread around the neck of a pregnant woman so that it touches her belly, it protects the child until the time of birth, so that it receives no harm or damage except by extreme force. The purple star at the end of the right hand of <term>Perseus<gloss>original: "Persio"</gloss></term>, he who carries the <term>head of the demon<gloss>original: "cabeza dalgol"; referring to the star Algol</term></term>, has power over this stone and gives it its virtue. ### Of the stone named Zeraquiz. (8 verso.)

The stone called Zeraquiz belongs to the 28th degree of the sign of Aries, and it is the fourth type of the stone we mentioned called <term>Azufaratiz<gloss>Likely a corruption of a Greek or Arabic mineral name</gloss></term>; this is the one they call the Antiochene. ### Of the stone Bedunaz. (10.)

The stone called Bedunaz belongs to the 29th degree of the sign of Aries, and its name means <term>Driver-away of Sleep</term>. This wakefulness so pleases the one who holds the stone that even if they hang it on him for a very long time, he will not be able to sleep as well as he did before. It has yet another virtue: if they grind a quarter of a drachma of it and mix it with some liquid and put it into a <term>leper's<gloss>original: "gafo"</gloss></term> nostrils, he is cured the first time, provided the leprosy has not been so strong as to have already destroyed a limb; for that cannot be recovered by the stone's virtue. But as for the rest that remains in the body causing the disease, it removes it and does not let the sickness proceed further. The second star of the two that are together after the bend of the river has power over this stone and gives it its virtue. And when it is in the ascendant, this stone shows its works most clearly.

### Of the stone they call Camorica. (12 reverse.)

Belonging to the third degree of the sign of Taurus is the stone they call Camorica, which in <term>Chaldean<gloss>An ancient Semitic language; often used in this text to mean "Aramaic" or "ancient Eastern"</gloss></term> means the same as "vinegary" in our common tongue. Physicians put them in syrups and other things to "cut the humors," for it cuts them better and faster than any other vinegar. If it is poured onto linen or wool cloth, it cuts and breaks them. Because it dissolves strong bodies and cleanses them by removing their filth, those who work in the art of <term>alchemy<gloss>The medieval forerunner of chemistry, focused on transforming matter</gloss></term> use it. The two stars—one southern and the other northern—located in the front line of <term>Azoraya<gloss>The Arabic name for the Pleiades star cluster</gloss></term> (which are called the <term>Seven Little Nanny-Goats<gloss>original: "siete cabriellas"</gloss></term>) and which are within the figure of Taurus, have power over this stone; from them, it receives its strength and virtue.
