### Of the stone they call Fuludia. (12 reverse.)

Belonging to the fourth degree of the sign of Taurus is the stone they call Fuludia, which means "Milk-gatherer." By its nature, it is cold and dry and very strong in these two <term>complexions<gloss>The combination of qualities (hot, cold, wet, dry) believed to govern health</gloss></term>. Its color is very white, so much so that it resembles a piece of frozen snow; it has no clarity, nor can sight pass through it. It is so strong that no other body can conquer it except for the <term>diamond</term>. This stone is found in Mount Acir in the land of Egypt, which is far from any settlement, a good hundred miles; there are caves there where snakes and other evil beasts live, and the stone is found outside them. Those serpents bring them out, and the herdsmen who watch the livestock manage to take them and bring them to sell. If it is rubbed with milk, the result curdles all the milk it is placed upon; therefore, the people of that land use it in their cheeses and in every other milk product they wish to curdle. Physicians include it often in the medicines they make for the "flux of blood" (hemorrhaging) or for sores in the intestines. ### Of the stone that is called Raconic. (13.)

The star above the right knee of the figure of Taurus has power over this stone, and from it, the stone receives its virtue. When it is in mid-heaven, the stone shows its works more.

### Of the stone they call Zumberic. (14.)

Belonging to the ninth degree of the sign of Taurus is the stone they call *Zumberic* in Arabic and <term>Esmerl<gloss>Emery (a form of corundum used as an abrasive)</gloss></term> in Latin. And they cut from them whatever they wish, or drill them; for there is no stone that can defend itself against it, save for the <term>diamond<gloss>original: "diamante"</gloss></term> alone. And the polishing that this stone performs on others is better and stronger when its dust is wet than when it is dry. Those who work in <term>alchemy<gloss>The ancestral science of chemistry and transformation</gloss></term> use it in their work because it is good for cleansing "bodies" <note>In alchemy, "bodies" usually refers to metals</note> by removing their impurity, so that after they are cleaned, they receive greater color and weight, according to what a man wishes to give them. And it even has another virtue: when its powder is thrown into wounds that are old and rotten, it eats the bad flesh, and they heal more quickly because of it. And the southern star of the two in the front line of the quadrant in the neck of the image of Taurus has power over this stone, and from it, the stone receives its virtue. And when this is in the ascendant, this stone will show its works more clearly.

### Of the stone Zamorat. (14.)

Belonging to the tenth degree of the sign of Taurus is the stone they call *Zamoricaz*; and it is also called the "stone of the hermits." It is found on the shores of the sea called <term>Alcuzun<gloss>The Red Sea (from the Arabic 'al-Qulzum')</gloss></term>; and that is the sea through which Moses led the children of Israel, near the city called Bocaliz. The waves of that sea, when there is a storm, cast them onto the shore. It is very yellow in color and shines like clear oil, and sight passes through it <note>Meaning it is transparent</note>. It is difficult to break, and there are large and small ones, but they are always found in the shape of a chestnut. By its nature, it is cold and dry and very strong in these two <term>complexions<gloss>The balance of qualities (hot, cold, wet, dry) in a substance</gloss></term>. They prize it highly in that land and use it in rings and necklaces, for the man who carries it with him has no desire for the "pleadings of women" <note>A euphemism for sexual intercourse</note>; even if he begins the act, he cannot finish anything while he has the stone with him. And for this reason, the ancient sages gave it to religious men, to hermits, and to those who promised to maintain chastity. And some of the Gentiles, who had a law not to lie with their wives except at certain times for the sake of impregnating them more quickly and making the children wealthier and stronger, carried these stones with them at all other times, except when they wished to conceive. And if they give three <term>drachmas<gloss>An ancient unit of weight, about 3.5 grams</gloss></term> of this ground stone to a man to drink, he will never again have the power to lie with a woman. Therefore, the kings of India, when they wished to castrate some men to guard their wives, gave them this stone to drink

<column-break/>

out of the grief they felt at having to cut off their members; and it was as effective as if they had been castrated. And the star in the nose of those in the face of the image of Taurus has power and lordship over this stone, and from it, the stone receives its strength and virtue. And when this star is in the ascendant, it shows the works of this stone more clearly.

### Of the stone named Coral. (14 reverse.)

Belonging to the eleventh degree of the sign of Taurus is the stone they call *Coral* in Latin; in Arabic, they call its root *Margen* and its branches *Becet*. This stone congeals from the water of the sea and grows like a tree; in color, it resembles the herb called "sea herb." It has many branches, and while it is under the seawater, it is soft, but as soon as they take it out and the air hits it, it hardens. It is found in many places, but the best of all is that found in the Sea of England or on the island of Sardinia. It is not clear so that sight may pass through it, and its color is red; the more redness it has, the better it is. By its nature, it is cold and dry. Its property is to be moderately <term>astringent<gloss>original: "estrennir" — a substance that contracts body tissues and stops bleeding</gloss></term>. If they mix it, ground, with wine or some other thing and give it to drink to those who spit blood, it helps them greatly. It also helps those who cannot pass urine. Whoever drinks it with some liquid dissolves the <term>abscess<gloss>original: "postema"</gloss></term> that forms in the arm. And the star located between the one in the nose of Taurus and the other in the southern eye of this same image has power over this stone, and from it, the stone receives its virtue. And when it is in the ascendant, it shows the works of this stone more clearly.

### Of the stone they call Black Coral. (14 reverse.)

Belonging to the twelfth degree of the sign of Taurus is the stone they call Black Coral. It has the same name in Arabic as the other one; and like it, it is tender under the water and hardens when taken into the air, but its scent is stronger than the other. By nature, it is cold and dry, but its dryness is greater than the other's. It has all the virtues of red coral completely, and additionally, it has this: if it is drunk ground, it helps wounds of the intestines and tremors of the heart; it is also included in medicines given for joy. When they burn it and make it into powder, it helps greatly to dry the tears that come to the eyes; therefore, it is good to put into <term>eye-salves<gloss>original: "alcoholes" — referring to kohl or medicinal powders for the eyes</gloss></term>. And the star in the northern eye of the image of Taurus has power over this stone, and from it, the stone receives its virtue. And when this star is in the ascendant, then it shows the works of this stone more clearly.

However, they are clear and of great brilliance when the sun strikes them, for they cast rays upon the ground like crystal. Of these stones, they find large ones and small ones and of many shapes, but most are found in the shape of an egg. The best ones are found on the island of <note>Zarandin is Serendib, modern Sri Lanka</note>, where other very noble precious stones are found. Goldsmiths use this stone often to make necklaces or to set in rings. The most noble are found on that mountain of the aforementioned island near the city called Tarhan. ### Of the stone they call Debaran. (15.)

Belonging to the fourteenth degree of the sign of Taurus is the stone they call the Debaran stone. It is found in some places in Africa in mines that exist there; and when they take it out it is soft <note>original: "muelle"</note>, and after they have taken it out and the air hits it, it becomes hard and very strong. Its color is brown, and in some of them they find veins that resemble gold, and others silver: but those which are largest and have the color of gold show the greatest virtue. By nature it is cold and dry. And it has such a property that if they hang it over a sore or wound from which blood is flowing, it stops it immediately. Likewise, when they grind it and knead it with vinegar and make pellets <note>original: "bellotas," literally "acorns," referring to the shape of the medicinal suppository</note> of it and place them upon the <term>nature of the woman<gloss>A medieval euphemism for the vagina or womb</gloss></term>, it stops the flow. And <term>physicians<gloss>Practitioners of medicine</gloss></term> also put it, ground up, into the powders they make to tighten teeth and gums that are in poor condition. And the star that is in the thigh of the left arm of the image of Taurus has lordship over this stone, and from it the stone receives its strength and virtue. And when this star is in the ascendant, this stone will show its works more clearly.

### Of the stone that appears in the sea. (15 verso.)

Belonging to the fifteenth degree of the sign of Taurus is the stone that appears in the sea when the planet <term>Venus<gloss>Associated in lapidaries with beauty, desire, and moisture</gloss></term> rises, and hides when it sets. And this stone and the other which we spoke of before regarding Mars, and those we will speak of later for each of the other planets—in what manner the virtue of that planet from which it takes its strength appears in it—all are found in the sea they call <term>Tenebroso<gloss>The "Sea of Darkness," or the Atlantic Ocean</gloss></term>: but each one in its own place; for they are not all in one spot. But this one, which belongs specifically to Venus, has a white color that tends somewhat toward yellow. It is a shining and clear stone and gives off a great splendor. It is light in weight, yet strong and very hard to break; so much so, that no other metal breaks it, except gold in this manner: when gold is brought near it, the stone breaks immediately. And in every way the <term>complexion<gloss>The specific balance of qualities (hot, cold, wet, dry)</gloss></term> of Venus is shown in it; but its nature is cold and dry. It is a very beautiful stone to look upon; and those who know it prize it greatly. And its property is such that all kinds of poisonous serpents flee from it. And it has yet another great property: that he who carries it with him has a great desire for women, and even if he indulges often, it does not do him as much harm as it would another. And the star following the two that are in the crown of <term>Perseus<gloss>The constellation representing the Greek hero</gloss></term> has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its virtue. And when this star is in the <term>midheaven<gloss>The highest point the star reaches in the sky</gloss></term>, it will show its works more clearly.

### Of the stone named Zamorat. (15 verso.)

Belonging to the sixteenth degree of the sign of Taurus is the stone they call *Zamorat* in Arabic, and <term>Emerald<gloss>original: "Esmeralda"</gloss></term> in Latin. This stone is green, of a very beautiful greenery, and the greener it is, the better it is. It is a mixture of the nature of earth and stone. And by nature it is cold and dry. And it is formed often in gold mines. And they find it in the land of the West more than in any other place. Its virtue is such that it protects against all deadly poisons <note>original: "tosicos"</note> and wounds or bites from poisonous beasts: for if they take one <term>drachma<gloss>A unit of weight</gloss></term> of it and grind it and sift it, and give it to drink with wine or with water, it heals the poisoned man so that he does not die, nor does his hair fall out, nor does his skin peel. And it has another virtue: that he who carries it with him escapes the sickness they call the <term>demon<gloss>Likely referring to epilepsy or "falling sickness," often attributed to demonic influence in the Middle Ages</gloss></term>, provided he holds it before

<column-break/>

he has an attack, and for this reason, and because it is very beautiful, men love it, and especially honorable men. And in that land where they find the best ones, they hang them around the necks of children, so that it may protect them from having the aforementioned sickness. And if they have it from the beginning and they tie it to the muscle of the arm or the left leg before the sickness becomes old <note>i.e., chronic</note>, they are cured. And the star that is at the root of the northern horn of the figure of Taurus has power over this stone, and from it the stone receives its virtue. And when this star is in the ascendant, this stone shows its works more clearly.

### Of the stone named Zavarger. (16.)

Belonging to the seventeenth degree of the sign of Taurus is the stone they call *Zavarget* in Arabic, and <term>Prasme<gloss>Prase, a leek-green variety of quartz</gloss></term> in Latin. This resembles the emerald in color. And it is found in those same gold mines where the others are found; but sometimes they find it in others. It is earthy and stony in complexion. By nature it is cold and dry. And its greenery and its splendor are much better than that of the other emerald. And its virtue is such that if they tie it to a woman’s thigh at the time of birthing, she gives birth easily and without danger. And it does yet more: he who carries it with him loses the fear that men have at night when they are alone, and this is because it greatly strengthens and comforts the heart. This stone has a great enmity with the other we mentioned called *Abechenie* in Arabic, and <term>Green Jasper<gloss>original: "Yaspio verde"</gloss></term> in Latin; though both are of one color, the better and more beautiful of them is this Prase. And when they want to prove how they dislike each other, they take these two stones and bring them close to one another, and in a short time they find black spots on the Prase. And the emerald does the same thing with the stone called *Dihenit*. And the star that is in the heel of the right foot of the image of Perseus has power over this stone, and from it the stone receives its strength and virtue. And therefore, when this star is in the ascendant, it will show its works more clearly.

### Of the stone named Alambari. (16.)

Belonging to the eighteenth degree of the sign of Taurus is the stone they call *Alambari*. This is cold in the third degree and dry at the beginning of the second. And it is found in clay mines. Among these stones there are large ones and small ones: but they are always found in a round shape. Its color is a very pure yellow, but there are some in which they find green drops, and those are the best and of greater virtue. It is a strong stone and very hard to break. And it has such virtue that he who has it in his mouth does not become intoxicated by any wine he drinks, nor does the wine do him harm as it does to one who does not carry it; and he has this property by carrying it with him, but not as much as if he held it in his mouth. And if he puts it in a cask or a jar or any other thing that holds wine, it takes away its power to intoxicate; but it does not take away the flavor that it has: and it does the same to whatever a man drinks. And therefore, those from the land of the West where they find them usually hang them around children's necks, so that wine does not do them harm, and they might grow better and more quickly while drinking it. And for this same reason, they would set it in their vessels and in the other things from which they drank, because the wine tasted good to them and did not harm them. And the star that is at the root between the horn and the northern ear of the image of Taurus has power over this stone and from it receives its virtue. And when it is in the ascendant, this stone shows its works more clearly.

### Of the stone of cotton. (17.)

From the twentieth degree of the sign of <term>Taurus<gloss>The constellation of the Bull</gloss></term> is the stone they call Cotton <note>The description of a non-flammable, fibrous stone that can be spun into cloth identifies this as asbestos</note>. This is cold and dry by nature. It is white in color, but only slightly: so much so that it tends toward a light ash color. Large and small ones are found. It is light in weight; yet, despite that, it is strong and hard to break; and when they do break it, they find inside it a substance like cotton in both texture and color. And the virtue of this cotton is such that it is not consumed by fire, and it can be spun, and they make cloths from it as they do from other cotton; and when it becomes soiled, they put it in the fire and it comes out clean and bright as if it had been washed; and the longer it stays in the fire, the whiter and more beautiful it becomes. And the physicians of that land burn this cotton and make it into powders and put them in the eyes, because it removes tearing and all the humidity that is in them. And some are found large, and others small, and in many shapes. And they find them in the Mountain of the Moon where the <term>Nile<gloss>The great river of Africa</gloss></term> is born, at the bottom of some caves that are there. But they are so deep that he who descends through them, if he stays long, either dies or becomes paralyzed. And those who are skilled in taking them, when they enter inside, as soon as they reach where the stones are, they take those they can and leave with them, and once those have left others enter, and in this way they find them, and not otherwise. And the two stars—the southern one and the northern one—that are in the front line of the quadrant, which is in the ears of the figure of the <term>Hare<gloss>The constellation Lepus</gloss></term>; and also the star that is in the left heel of the figure of the one who holds the reins <note>The constellation Auriga, the Charioteer</note>, have power over this stone, and from them it receives its virtue. And when these stars are in <term>mid-heaven<gloss>The highest point the stars reach in the sky</gloss></term>, this stone will have greater strength in its works.

### Of the stone that flees from wine. (17.)

From the twenty-first degree of the sign of Taurus is the stone that flees from wine. It is cold at the end of the fourth degree, and dry at the beginning of the second. It is hard and difficult to break. And it is resplendent and of many colors: so much so that to those who see it, there appear to be letters written upon it because of the mixed coloring that is within it in many ways. And they find it on the island in the sea called <term>Alcuzun<gloss>The Red Sea</gloss></term>, near the island they call <term>Vacuac<gloss>Waq-Waq, a legendary island in medieval Arabic geography</gloss></term>. And it has this name because, according to what <term>Ptolemy<gloss>Claudius Ptolemy, the famous 2nd-century astronomer and geographer</gloss></term> says, there grow in that land trees with fruits in the shapes of women that hang by their hair; and while they are on the trees green, they are alive, and they do nothing else but say "vacuac," and once they are ripe they fall and die. And near that island which is so named, there is a place where one can go on foot for twelve miles along the shore of the sea, and there they find these stones wrapped in sand. Some are large and some are small;

<column-break/>

and they are of diverse forms. And they are very prized in those lands for their clarity and for their beauty; and kings put them in crowns and in rings, and in other noble ornaments that they make. And it has such virtue that he who carries it with him does not experience the hallucination <note>original: "imaginacion"</note> that men call a demon, nor is he afraid when a man is alone at night in the darkness. And it has another virtue: that it so hates wine by its nature that when they place it near it, the stone jumps and flees from it very forcefully. And it performs yet another marvel: when they burn it and turn it to ash, all those colors that the stone showed before all appear in the ash after it is burned. And this ash has such a property that if they take a vessel of it and throw it into a vat of wine, no matter how strong it may be, it spoils it all and turns it into the substance and color of water. And also: by kneading it with dog urine and anointing any sign of a wound with it—provided it has not entered the bone—it erases it by the third time they apply it. And the two stars—the northern one and the southern one—that are in the horn on the southern side of the image of Taurus, have power over this stone, and from them it receives its virtue. And when these are both in the ascendant, then this stone shows its work more.

### Of the stone they call Atarráz. (17 back.)

From the twenty-two degrees of the sign of Taurus is the stone they call Atarráz. It is cold and dry by nature and very strong in these two complexions; but the people of that land where it is most commonly found call it the "stone of the hare" for this reason: in that place where the great river Nile enters the Mediterranean Sea, there is bred an animal that resembles in its limbs and all its features the land hare; and for this reason they call it the <term>sea hare<gloss>Aplysia, a type of sea slug known since antiquity</gloss></term>. And this creature has such a nature that it watches for when the sea rises and makes great waves and moves up the Nile, churning the water that then comes out; and it opens its mouth and swallows as much of that turbid water as it can swallow; and after it has swallowed it, it stands in the sun on the bank of the river. And with the great heat that the animal has in itself, and with the other heat it receives from the sun, that water begins curdling within its body. And when it feels that it is curdling, it enters the sea and from there returns to the river and comes out onto the land; and it does this many times until it feels that the water has curdled in its body and turned to stone. And when they feel they are quite hard and dry, it comes out onto the land and voids them <note>original: "camialas"</note>, and therefore they find them on those banks of the Nile and the sea. And they are very green in color, and so hard they cannot be broken with anything; and for this reason the <term>Chaldeans<gloss>Ancient people of Mesopotamia, often associated with secret wisdom and astrology</gloss></term> call it <term>Rofolez<gloss>A transliterated term meaning "unbreakable" or "indivisible"</gloss></term>, which signifies something that cannot be split. And it is heavy in itself according to the size it has, but the largest they find does not weigh more than two <term>drachmas<gloss>An ancient unit of weight, roughly 3.5 grams</gloss></term>. Some of them are found round and some a bit more oblong; and these are the largest. And the wise men tried many ways by which they might break or dissolve this stone, and they found only one, and it is this: they take this hare and crush it while it is alive, and squeeze it hard, and extract as much juice as they can from it, and put it in a vessel of glass or tinned copper or silver, and throw those stones into it so that they are covered by that water. And afterward they close the vessel well so that no other moisture enters except that; and once they have done this, they hang it in a well of fresh water, so that it does not reach the water, and then they close its mouth well so that the heat of the sun nor any other thing can touch it, and they leave it there for forty days, and afterward they take it out; and they will find that all those stones will be dissolved and turned to water. This has such virtue that if they anoint with it the places where they have plucked or shaved hair, it will never grow there again. And therefore the physicians of that land use it to cure men who have a disease where hairs grow in the eyes <note>likely trichiasis, where eyelashes grow inward</note> that prevents them from sleeping and seeing. And the two stars—the southern and the northern—which are in the quadrant of the ears of the figure of the Hare, have power over this stone, and from them it receives its strength and virtue. And therefore, when these stars are in the ascendant, then this stone shows its works most clearly.

### Of the stone named Aliaza. (18.)

The stone called Aliaza belongs to the 23rd degree of the sign of Taurus. There are five types of this stone. The first is white; the second, black; the third, green; the fourth has the color of tin; and the fifth is variegated, mixed with many colors. The sages spoke of each of these in their proper place, describing where they are found and the virtues and properties they possess. However, above all the natures they found in it, they said it was a very hard body—so much so that few stones were found harder than it. It is of such a quality that when it is ground and its dust is rubbed over other stones being polished, it brightens them and gives them a fine color.

This name, *Aliaza*, in the language of the land where they are found, means something like "the diminishing of good." This is because the common virtue of all these types is that whoever carries it experiences a very great and irrational fear, without knowing why. Furthermore, it causes the person to be hated by others, leading people to speak ill of them without reason, to despise them, and to shun their company. These properties belong to all five types of Aliaza mentioned; however, the one specifically discussed here is the very black and shiny variety. It is cold and dry in nature. Whoever carries it will find their worries and sorrows constantly increasing, and at night, their dreams will be foul and terrifying. Beyond all this, it is a mortal poison. If a quantity of the ground stone is given to a man or woman diluted with wine, it shreds the entire lung, causing it to come out in pieces; this continues until they die, and very few can survive past two days. 

The star located on the thigh of the left arm of the one who holds the reins—which is called the <term>Goat<gloss>The star Capella in the constellation Auriga</gloss></term>—and the two other stars on that same arm called the <term>Kids<gloss>The stars Zeta and Eta Aurigae</gloss></term>, have power over this stone, and from them it receives its virtue. When these stars are in the Ascendant, the stone shows its effects most strongly.

### Of the stone they call Iron. (18 verso.)

Iron belongs to the 24th degree of the sign of Taurus. This is a mineral stone, for it is a metal, and it is born in many parts of the world. There are many mines for it, and men put it to use in most things they wish to craft, such as weapons of many kinds. When they wish to work it, they place it in the fire to heat it, and afterward, they shape it however they desire. It is among the best-known stones that men use. 

There are types of a soft nature and those of a strong nature; some, when placed in hot water, become even harder, while others become softer the longer they remain there. There is a type of iron that, when smelted, has certain "medicines" <note>This likely refers to alloys or fluxing agents used in the smelting process.</note> added to it, making it so strong that it cuts other irons; the Moors call this *Albinde*, and in some lands, it is called *Andaüico* <note>original: "Albinde... Andaüico." These terms refer to high-quality crucible steel, often known as Wootz or Indian steel.</note>. There is another type that is not made through such mastery but is strong by its own nature, so that it cuts softer iron; this is called steel. 

This is a stone that all men generally know, and none can do without it. By nature, it is cold and dry. When it has been taken from the earth and prepared as it should be, its color is between gray and black, though it leans more toward black. It is a stone that brightens quickly and dulls quickly, though it receives dullness more easily than brightness. It possesses such virtue that when it is heated in fire and then extinguished in water or wine, and that liquid is given to drink to one suffering from chronic diarrhea <note>original: "menazon antigua"</note>, it provides great benefit and helps them heal quickly. It does the same for those with intestinal sores, an abscess in the spleen, or great weakness in the stomach caused by loosening and frequent bowel movements. Even beyond this, physicians work with the ground slag and the filings of iron, putting them into 

<column-break/>

powders, medicines, and electuaries <note>A medicinal paste made with honey or syrup.</note>, for it is useful for many illnesses. The star in the hilt of the sword of <term>Orion<gloss>The Hunter constellation</gloss></term> has power over this stone, and from it, the stone receives its virtue. When that star is in the Ascendant, the stone shows its effects most strongly.

### Of the stone they call Articam. (18 verso.)

The stone called *Articam* in Chaldean belongs to the 25th degree of the sign of Taurus; some call it *Artiqui*, and the Greeks call it *Assrá*. It is found in the land called Artica <note>Likely Attica in Greece; the stone may be a type of "Terra Sigillata" or medicinal clay.</note>. These are small stones of a yellow color, the brightest yellow being the largest. It is light in weight because it has many open pores. When it is burned, it turns red, and it is so soft that a man can break it with his fingers. By nature, it is cold and dry, and when a man places it on his tongue, it sticks to it. 

If they grind it and knead it with warm water and place it while hot upon abscesses, it cools them and helps heal them. It does the same for sores and wounds that are very inflamed; by cooling them, it makes the pain subside and, furthermore, removes the excess flesh <note>Proud flesh or granulating tissue.</note> that grows there. It has another marvelous property: if this stone is placed in a vessel with the substance called <term>Borax<gloss>A mineral salt used in soldering and medicine</gloss></term>, it breaks the Borax and turns it into powder. It receives great power for this, as we shall show later in the section where we speak of Borax on its own. The forward star of the four in the straight line on the spine of the image of Orion has power over this stone, and from it, the stone receives its virtue. When it is in mid-heaven, it shows its effects most.

### Of the stone found in the head of the hare. (19.)

The stone found in the head of the hare belongs to the 26th degree of the sign of Taurus. When the hare is killed, they quickly cut its head and open it, finding the stone inside the brain or attached to the bones. By nature, it is cold and dry. It is light in weight because it is porous. It is rough to the touch and gray in color with red spots. This is counted as one of the stones found within animals. 

Its virtues are few and harmful. It has the property that if it is brought near the flesh of any living animal, it sticks to it and pulls away all the flesh it touches, leaving a large and nasty wound according to the size of the stone. This wound heals very slowly, and if it is not treated with medicine, the animal may die from it. If this stone is touched to dead meat, it does the same. If a large quantity of the ground stone is given to a man to drink, it wounds the intestines and kills him if help is not rendered quickly. 

The star on the left shoulder of the one who holds the reins—called *Alaroz*—and the other star on the right heel of that same image, which is shared by that location and the northern horn of Taurus, have power over this stone, receiving their strength and virtue from them. When these two stars are in the Ascendant, this stone will show its effects more clearly.

### Of the stone found in man. (10.) <note>The number 10 appears in the OCR, but contextually this refers to the 27th degree.</note>

The stone of man belongs to the 27th degree of the sign of Taurus. This is also counted among the animal stones, but there is a great difference between this one and the others. The stone of man is formed inside the body, such as in the bladder or the kidneys, whereas in other animals, it forms in the head or other outer members. 

According to what the sages have distinguished, other animals (unlike man) have wide passages through which the thick humors flow and exit with the urine. But man has narrow passages, and the humors cannot flow through as easily. When they are delayed and reach the place where the heat is greatest, they congeal, as one humor is layered upon another. For this reason, when the stone is large, it is found to have layers like bark, one over the other. It is tender and easily breaks—

...color. Some of them are of a very bright red color, some are white, others yellow, and others a grayish-brown. In those that are highly "cooked" <note>This refers to the medieval belief that stones 'ripened' or were 'cooked' by the heat of the earth and the influence of the stars.</note>, a kind of light appears within them, much like in a gypsum stone. This does not happen to all men in the same way; for some it appears white, for others red, and so on for the other colors we mentioned. Even for those to whom it appears red, it sometimes changes into other colors depending on the part of the body where it "cooks," or the food they eat, or the humors they have within them, or according to the season in which it congeals. And the virtue it possesses is this: when they grind it and sift it thoroughly and place it into the eyes of those who have the blemish called <term>nuf</term> <note>Likely a pterygium or cataract; a growth or film over the eye.</note>, it dissolves it. However, it does not do this immediately, but rather by using it over some time. And the two stars—the northern one and the middle one—of the three joined at the end of the sword of <term>Orion</term> <note>original: "Urion"</note> have power over this stone, and from them it receives its strength and virtue. When these stars are in the ascendant, this stone will show its effects more clearly.

### Of the stone they call Lotarican. (Folio 19 verso.)

Associated with the twenty-eighth degree of the sign of Taurus is the stone they call <term>Lotarican</term>, which means "retainer of nature." By its nature, it is cold and dry at the end of the fourth degree of each of these two complexions <note>In medieval medicine, the 'fourth degree' was the most intense level of a quality like coldness or dryness.</note>. They are hard to break and are not uniform in size, for some are large and some are small. They are found in the land of <term>Armenia</term> in certain clay mines; when they dig, they find this stone within them. Its color is a mixture of red and yellow, and each stone is faint, resembling the color of the water that drains from meat when salt is applied to it. It is a stone that is very dull when taken from the mine, but when polished and worked, it shines somewhat, though not enough for sight to pass through it. Its virtue is this: if it is hung upon a man who has a bloody flux <note>Likely dysentery or internal bleeding.</note>, it causes it to stop immediately, so that while he wears it, he cannot pass anything; if they give him the dust produced from polishing the stone to drink, it does the same. If placed in the eyes of one whose eyes are tearing or have other moisture, it stops it as well; for the power it has to retain and dry all moist things is wonderfully great. The star at the end of the horn that looks toward the south in the figure of <term>Taurus</term>, and the other violet-colored star in the head of the figure of <term>Orion</term>, both have power over this stone, and from them it receives its strength and virtue. When they are in the ascendant, this stone will perform its works more completely.

### Of the stone called Aliaza. (Folio 19 verso.)

Associated with the twenty-ninth degree of the sign of Taurus is the stone they call

<column-break/>

<term>Aliaza</term>, and this is the second variety we mentioned that has a green color. However, this greenness is not very great, as it leans somewhat toward yellow. Generally, it is cold and dry and has loathsome properties, like the others of this nature. It is found in abundance in the land of Arabia, but the Arabs are very careful not to go near its mines. It has such a virtue that if it is hung upon a child when he is small, it makes him very drooly and tearful. Those who do not know this make vessels and bowls from it in which they eat and drink, and those who use these frequently find that its nature causes them to lose their sleep. If a man is given much of it to drink, it makes him stay awake until he dies; however, if they treat him with things intended for this purpose, they can save him from death, but he will never sleep as well as he did before. The following star of the three in the belt of <term>Orion</term> has power over this stone, and from it, the stone receives its strength and virtue. Therefore, when that star is in the ascendant, this stone will show its works more clearly.

### Of the stone they call Camiruca. (Folio 20.)

Associated with the thirtieth degree of the sign of Taurus is the stone they call <term>Camiruca</term>, which in that language means "the forgetful one." By its nature, it is cold and dry and of a red color mixed with green. Rays of light come out of it and return into itself, just as they do in a mirror; therefore, it is beautiful, and those who see it are very pleased by it if they do not already know its virtue. It is strong and hard to break and to polish, and it is also heavier than its size suggests. In the lands of <term>Arabia</term>, they find it in mines there, but the people of that land loathe it so much that they will not set it in rings, nor use it for anything, nor sell it among themselves. Instead, they send it to be sold far away in other lands where it is not known, and people buy it for a high price because of its beauty. Its virtue is such that he who carries it with him becomes forgetful of all the things he must do; he remembers none of them as long as he carries it. If they give him the powder or the polishings of it to drink, he forgets forever until he dies. It has another strange virtue often used by women who wish to act wickedly: if they take its powder and knead it with something moist and place it in their nature <note>A euphemism for the vagina.</note>, it constricts those who are not virgins so tightly that they are harder to "corrupt" than those who are virgins. The southern star of the two in the hind feet of the constellation of the Hare <note>Lepus</note> has power and dominion over this stone, and from it, the stone receives its strength and virtue. When it is in the ascendant, this stone shows its works more clearly.

# CONCERNING THE SIGN OF GEMINI.

---

### Prologue on the degrees of the sign of Gemini. (Folio 21.)

The thirty natures of the stones according to the thirty degrees of the sign of <term>Taurus</term> have been shown, and the powers they receive from the other fixed stars in the figures of other constellations that have association and connection with this sign have been told. But despite all this, it is necessary for anyone who wishes to work with this book to pay

<column-break/>

heed to the planet <term>Venus</term>, whose house is the sign of <term>Taurus</term>. He must see that she is well-received by aspect <note>A specific angular relationship between planets in astrology, such as a trine or sextile.</note>, or by conjunction in the place where the stars of that same degree are located. He should also see that the Lord of the Face <note>The ruler of the "decan," a 10-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign.</note> is in good condition at that hour and in one of its dignities; for all these things must be observed in works intended for good, and the opposite for those intended for evil.

But now we shall return to our intention of speaking about the thirty degrees of the sign of Gemini.

### Of the stone they call Zarocan. (21.)

Associated with the first degree of the sign of Gemini is the stone they call <term>Zarocan</term>. It is white in color, of a clear whiteness, such that it resembles well-scraped bone and possesses a certain clarity, though not enough for the sight to pass through it. It is light in weight and very easy to break <note>The text says both "easy to break" (*lezne de quebrantar*) and "strong and hard to break" (*fuerte et dura de quebrantár*); this may be a scribal error or imply it is brittle but requires a sharp blow.</note>. By nature, it is hot and moist. There are many mines of it throughout the world, but the best are those from the land of <term>Barbary</term> <note>The Maghreb region of North Africa.</note> and from Spain. They are found on the shores of the sea and the banks of rivers. The virtue of this stone is such that it greatly increases the milk of women who wear it. It does the same for any other animal. For this reason, the <term>Barbars</term> <note>Berbers</note> have their women wear them around their necks as they wear <term>pearls</term> <note>original: "aliofár" (from Arabic al-jauhar).</note>. It also helps for this same purpose when it is mixed into electuaries <note>A medicinal paste made with honey or syrup.</note> and given to eat. It is good against <term>melancholy</term> and helps greatly with the <term>abscesses</term> <note>original: "postemas"</note> that form in the eyes. And the star that is at the tail of the <term>Little Bear</term> <note>Ursa Minor</note>, which they call the "Little Kid of Benanais" <note>original: "cabrito de Benanais"; Benanais refers to the Arabic "Daughters of the Bier," a name for the stars of the Big and Little Dipper.</note>, has power and lordship over this stone, and from it, the stone receives the strength of its virtue. When this star is in the ascendant, this stone shows its effects most clearly.

### Of the stone of gold. (21.)

Associated with the second degree of the sign of Gemini is the stone of gold <note>In medieval science, metals were often classified alongside stones as "fossils" or mineral growths.</note>. By nature, it is hot and moist, and it is the most noble of the metals because the nobility of the Sun's virtue appears most clearly in it. It is a stone that men love and prize greatly, and it is heavier than any other found in a mine or upon the earth. Large pieces of it are not found, but rather it is always found small in the sands of the sea or the rivers. It is found in many parts of the world, but the best of all is that which they find in Spain in the western part. Its color is yellow, and when it is cleaned and polished, its yellowness increases and it becomes clearer, though not so much that the sight passes through it. If it is polished much, it brightens so much that one can see oneself in it as in a mirror. It has such virtue that when it is filed and the filings are mixed with something else given to eat or drink to one who has heart tremors or weakness, it helps them. It does the same for one who is fearful because of melancholy. Furthermore, it heals or gives great benefit to those who are scabby or have another disease where the hair is plucked out, which they call <term>alopecia</term> <note>original: "lopicia"</note>. It is also good for use in cauterizing, because it does not cause a blister and they heal from it more quickly. The nature of this metal stone is such that when it is mixed with copper, it takes on the nature of glass and breaks more easily, yet it incorporates with it. Also, if it is mixed with tin, it turns black, and if mixed with silver, it receives its whiteness; and so it does with every metal. Therefore, those who labor in <term>alchemy</term>—which they call the "Great Work"—should take care not to damage the reputation of the knowledge; for alchemy means "mastery for improving things," not for making them worse. Thus, those who take noble metals and mix them with base ones, not understanding the science or the mastery, cause the base metal to not be improved and the noble one to be ruined. In this way, they commit a great error in two ways: one, by going against the knowledge of God, and the other, by doing harm to the world. But if the gold should be corrupted with another base body, they should put sulfur into the smelting and mix it with the stone they call <term>Marcasite</term>, for this separates it from all other metals and cleanses it of all filth. This is because sulfur burns all other bodies if it stays with them long, except for gold. Also, Marcasite has the nature of sulfur in it, and for that reason, they tint copper red with it to the color of gold; they do the same to silver if they know how to mix it well, but these works are not lasting. What shall we tell you? The nobilities and virtues of gold are so many that it would be a long thing to say, but some are

<column-break/>

manifest, such as this: when men see gold, it gives great joy to their hearts, and they consider themselves richer with it than with anything else they might have. Furthermore, all things they wish to make noble and rich, they make from it more than from any other metal. It serves many purposes in the art of <term>physic</term> <note>Medicine</note> that are not appropriate to mention in this book. And it has one very marvelous property: if they make a ring of it where the "stone" is of the same gold, and they heat it and burn the wings of pigeons with it when they are put into the dovecote, they will never leave to dwell in another place, even though their wings grow back. However, some spoke against this reasoning, holding that this property was in the shape of the ring rather than in the gold; for if it were in the gold, it would work in whatever form it had. But he who composed this book said he held that the virtue came from both; because the ring could not do this if it were made of another metal and not of gold. Concerning some types of gold that have a bad color by themselves, some of the sages who labored in the Great Work said that if one took that yellow stone which is very well known to goldsmiths—of which we shall speak later in its place in this book—and ground it and threw its dust upon the poorly colored gold when it is melted, it turns it a good color. This is one of the works of right and true Alchemy, because it makes the bad good. And the star that is on the right shoulder of the figure of the <term>Charioteer</term> <note>original: "tenedor de las riendas"; likely the star Bellatrix or a star in Auriga.</note> has power and lordship over this stone and from it receives its virtue. And therefore, when this star is in the ascendant, this stone shows its works most clearly.

### Of the stone they call Barcaduniticaz. (22.)

Associated with the third degree of the sign of Gemini is the stone they call <term>Barcaduniticaz</term>, which means "oil-swallower" in <term>Chaldean</term>. This stone is very hot and moist, but not extremely so. Its mines are found in many places: and although that which they find in the land of <term>Iraq</term> <note>original: "Haracin" (likely Khorasan or Iraq/Babel area).</note> is good, better is that which is found in the <term>Promised Land</term>, for it shows its virtue more clearly. It has many open pores within it; therefore, it is rough on the outside, but despite this, it is heavy of body and strong, and hard to break; yet when they do break it, it looks like a sponge inside. They find very large ones, others of medium size, and others smaller. Its color is yellow tending toward brown. Its virtue is this: when they place it near oil of any nature, it draws it to itself and soaks up as much as its own size and weight; and according to this, it draws it from afar or near. But if they leave it near the oil for a long time and the stone is good, it draws more than its proportion; and they know this by trial, weighing first the oil separately and the stone separately; for then they clearly recognize that it has drawn its own weight and more. Whoever wishes to remove the oil from this stone after it is incorporated within it should put it in a vessel containing vinegar, and all the oil will come out immediately. And whoever grinds it and makes powder of it and mixes it with water removes every stain from cloth, of whatever nature the stain may be, if it was made with oil. And if they cook it over a gentle fire, it incorporates with it and becomes like an ointment. This is a very good medicine for wounds; for it makes them mature quickly and come to a head <note>original: "venir á venino"</note>, and it eats away the bad flesh that forms in them. It also helps greatly when it is well ground and sifted for the sores that form in the eyes. And the two stars, one southern and the other northern, which are in the head of the <term>Charioteer</term> <note>Auriga</note>—though the northern one is outside the head—both have power over this stone and from them it receives its strength and virtue. And when they are in the ascendant, this stone shows its works most clearly.

### Of the stone that pulls the flesh. (22.)

Associated with the fourth degree of the sign of Gemini is the stone that pulls the flesh. This is found in the sea they call <term>Alcuzun</term> <note>The Red Sea (Arabic: al-Qulzum).</note>, which is...

...that which the Children of Israel crossed <note>This likely refers to the Red Sea, referencing the Exodus.</note>. Its color is like bruised meat. It is smooth to the touch and light in weight. By its nature, it is hot and moist; it possesses such a virtue that when it is brought near the flesh of any living animal, it draws the flesh toward itself; but if the animal is dead, it does not do this. In this, it differs from the other stone we mentioned regarding the head of the hare; the other clings to both living and dead flesh and pulls with pain, causing blood to flow and making a bad wound, but this one does not. ### Of the stone they call Margul in Chaldean. (22 verso.)

Associated with the fifth degree of the sign of **Gemini** is the stone they call <term>Margul</term> <note>original: "Margul"; possibly related to the Arabic "marjan" for coral or a specific mineral from the East.</note> in Chaldean. By nature, it is hot and moist. Its mine is in the **Mountain of the Moon** where the **Nile** is born. It is a strong stone, hard to break, and heavy. It has a certain internal radiance, though the sight cannot pass through it. Its color is like the yolk of an egg; and when it is broken open, they find inside a substance with a kind of moisture that sticks to the hands and smells very sweet. If one anoints wounds with this, or the spots <note>Freckles, moles, or blemishes.</note> that form on the face, it clears them away and makes the skin smooth and glowing. It has yet another virtue: it is very good for bridegrooms; for if, when they are to lie with their wives, they anoint that member with which they are to produce children, it makes it grow, extending and thickening it. The moisture inside performs all these things; as for the outer part, which is like a shell, whoever grinds it into powder and puts it into <term>electuaries</term> <note>A medicinal paste made with honey or syrup.</note> designed to open the pathways of the liver, it provides great benefit; for it opens them and removes the <term>obstructions</term> <note>original: "opilaciones"</note> that form there, thus more quickly healing those who suffer from liver ailments caused by the closing of these passages. And when it is placed in fire, it does something very strange: it melts and flows like water; if it is then removed and left to cool, and placed back in the fire, it returns to its original nature. It does this as many times as it is put in the fire: the first time it melts, and the second it congeals; however, each time it is refined so that a small amount of it is lost. And the leading star of the two in the rudder that faces North in the constellation of the **Ship** <note>The constellation Argo Navis.</note> has power over this stone and from it receives its virtue. And when it is in the Ascendant, this stone manifests its works most clearly.

### Of the stone they call Lurita. (22 verso.)

Associated with the sixth degree of the sign of **Gemini** is the stone they call <term>Lurita</term>, which means "oily." This stone is hot and moist, soft to the touch, and easy to break; its color is like a white rose mixed with a certain redness. Its mine is found in the **Promised Land** <note>Palestine/Judea.</note> in very deep caves, and they are recognized in this way: when the sun strikes the mouths of those caves, the stones are seen shining deep within like burning candles. The men of that land make bowls from it; whoever habitually eats or drinks from them becomes very stout, and their face and body take on a healthy color. It increases a man’s desire to lie with a woman, and hers for a man. When this stone is burnished and cleaned, the polish that comes off it resembles oil in all its qualities; it burns and gives light just as oil does, yet it does not float upon water as oil does, but rather sinks straight to the bottom. It is very useful in the art of medicine; for if it is given ground in a drink to one who is becoming <term>consumptive</term> <note>original: "tisico"; suffering from tuberculosis.</note> or to one who has sores on the lungs, they are healed; the same is achieved by applying its dry powders. And the star in the thigh of the right arm of the figure of **Orion** <note>original: "Urion".</note> has power over this stone, and from it receives

<column-break/>

its virtue. And when it is in Midheaven, this stone manifests its works most clearly.

### Of the Serpent Stone. (23.)

Associated with the seventh degree of the sign of **Gemini** is the **Serpent Stone**. This is found on **Mount Sinai**. It is very red in color, so much so that it turns toward blackness; in some of them, a white drop is found, and this is the best and most noble kind. When it is placed in the fire, that drop grows and clarifies the stone so that it becomes very clear and radiant, which it does not show when taken from the mine; for then it is cloudy, but the fire makes it clear and bright. They come in many shapes, some large and some small. They are heavy and hard to break, but men work them and carve them into whatever shapes they desire. By nature, it is hot and moist in the second degree of both these complexions. Its virtue is such that if it is hung around the neck of one who was born possessed by a demon, they are cured. It does the same for one who has the disease called "forgetfulness" <note>likely dementia or severe memory loss.</note>, which comes from an ailment of the brain. It has yet another virtue: if it is rubbed on a viper's bite, it heals it. It performs a very strange marvel: if placed in a fire that is not well-lit, it makes it burn as well as if it were being fanned by bellows. And when a candle is extinguished, if the stone is placed there before the [heat of the] fire has departed, it causes it to reignite. And the two stars, the leading and the following ones, which are in the southern line of the quadrant in the right palm of the figure of **Orion**, have power over this stone and from them it receives its virtue. Therefore, when both are in Midheaven, this stone will manifest its works most clearly.

### Of the Dream Stone. (23.)

Associated with the eighth degree of the sign of **Gemini** is the **Dream Stone**. By nature, it is hot and moist. It is found in the **Sea of Al-Kuzum** <note>The Red Sea.</note> on the shore of the island they call **Alicuas**. It is very red in color, clear with a very great brilliance, and the sight passes through it. It is strong and hard to break, such that it cannot be broken or polished except with great labor; nor does fire have the power to do it harm or good. During the day it moves within itself, though not so as to travel from one place to another. If a man holds it before him and looks closely, it seems to him that smoke like dust comes out of it. At night it is bright like fire and illuminates a great area around itself. Those who travel that sea near the island we mentioned, when they see that light, they know immediately it is from this stone; they go there and search for it until they find it and take it. Some are large and others small. It has such a virtue that whoever keeps upon themselves the weight of one <term>drachm</term> <note>A unit of weight, roughly 3.4 grams.</note> or more will sleep for three days and three nights; if it is taken away, the person wakes up completely as they should. But if the waking happens without taking it away, the person remains for a while dazed as if drunk and returns to sleep again; it continues in this way until the stone is removed. If placed under the head of one who lies down to sleep, it does the same. Physicians and surgeons use it for those they wish to cut or lance so they do not feel the pain. It does the same for those who cannot bear the great pain of some illness they have. However, there is a difference between the sleep caused by this stone and natural sleep: this one does not fill the head with <term>vapors</term> <note>original: "bafos"; medieval medicine believed sleep was caused by digestive vapors rising to the brain.</note>, nor does the person feel tired from that sleep when they wake. And the following star of the two in the northern line of the quadrant in the right palm of the figure of **Orion** has power over this stone and from it receives its virtue. And when it is in Midheaven, this stone manifests its works most notably.

Associated with the ninth degree of the sign of **Gemini** is the stone they call <term>Bezoar</term> <note>original: "Bezahar"; a mass trapped in the gastrointestinal system, highly prized as an antidote to poison.</note>. This is a very precious and noble stone, and they find it in many colors; for some are light yellow and others...

...colors, and so each according to its color as we shall show later where it is appropriate. And the largest of these are found in the land of **China** <note>original: "Cin"</note>, and **India**, and **Khorasan** <note>original: "Horacin"; a historical region in northeastern Persia.</note>; but this one, of which we now speak here, is the most noble and better than all the others, and has a brown color that leans somewhat toward yellow. And they call it in Greek <term>Nericulequng</term> <note>original: "Nericulequng"; likely a corruption of a Greek term like "Alexipharmakon," meaning an antidote or "driver away of poison."</note>, which means as much as "remover of poison." It is a stone made of subtle parts of the elements. By nature, it is hot and moist, but not excessively so in either of these two **complexions** <note>In medieval medicine, "complexion" refers to the balance of the four qualities: hot, cold, moist, and dry.</note>. It is soft of body and easy to break. Its power is against all poison; as much against that which causes harm without killing, as against that which kills; and as much against poisons from things that grow from the earth as from those of animals. Furthermore, it works against the bite or wound of any venomous animal. The benefit it provides is in this manner: if they grind it, or file from it the weight of half a **drachm** <note>original: "dracma"; a unit of weight roughly equal to 3.5 grams.</note>, and give it to a man who has drunk any poison to drink, it makes him expel it through sweat and he heals. And if they touch the site of the wound or the venomous bite with the stone, it helps, but not as much as if they make it into powder and place it upon the sore; and if the site of the bite or wound begins to rot before they apply another medicine, and they put this powder upon it, it heals very quickly. And they even test its power in another way: if they take a scorpion, which we call an **alacran**, and touch the stinger with which it strikes with this stone, it loses the power to strike with it forever. And if they take the weight of half a drachm of its powder and throw it into the throat of a viper or a snake, it chokes immediately and dies. And although the viper and evil serpents have throats wider than their bodies—and the more they are formed this way, the worse they are than others—nonetheless, the power of this stone works so fiercely against them that it constricts their throats in such a way that it makes them die choked. And the wise men spoke much on the nature of poisons; but despite that, they put it into as few words as they could, so that the wise would understand it and others would not. And they said this: that poison does not kill so much by the complexion of cold nor of heat within it, but by the force of an evil power with which it is greatly endowed; and it goes directly to the blood of the heart and the liver, and dissolves it and makes it flow more than it should, and turns it white like the washing of meat; furthermore, it goes to the veins of the flowing blood and traps the spirit that travels through them, and pushes it so strongly that it makes it leave the man's body; and in this way it kills if they do not flee to help with those medicines meant for this. But if they delay and do not help quickly, in any case, he dies. And because the wise men who spoke on the **art of physick** <note>Medicine.</note> put this very completely in their books, he who composed this book did not wish to linger on it; but returned to speak of this aforementioned stone; and said this: that many men are deceived by it because they do not know it well, for there are other stones that resemble it, and they call one **Zafilti**, and another **Almamar**, and another **Maduz** <note>These are likely names of counterfeit or similar-looking minerals of the period.</note>. And although they resemble it in color, or in softness, or even in weight, nonetheless they do not resemble it in virtue nor in work. And each of these will be shown later in this book, what they are and how they differ, so they are known from one another. And the star that follows the other which is in the front foot of **Gemini**, and is at the joint of the leg of this Gemini, has power over this stone; and from it, the stone receives its virtue. And when that star is in the Ascendant, this stone manifests its works more clearly.

### Of the stone they call Bezoar: and it is the second kind. (24.)

Associated with the tenth degree of the sign of **Gemini** is the stone of the second **Bezoar**. And this is found in the land of **China**. Its color is yellow, and for that reason, they call it the "Yellow Bezoar," and it has no darkness in it nor anything else that obscures the color. By nature, it is hot and moist in both of these two complexions; but it is stronger than the other Bezoar and harder to break; because

<column-break/>

it is not joined by such subtle parts of the elements as the other; furthermore, it has great power that helps against some poisons, such as that of the scorpion, for by wearing it over the wound of one who is struck, he heals, and it does the same if they give it to him to drink. And it does another thing: he who carries it with him, if bitten by a rabid dog or another poisoned beast, it does not harm him nor do him evil; and for this reason, they count it among the other precious stones. And the star that is at the end of the right foot of **Canis Major** <note>original: "can mayor"</note> has power over this stone, and from it, the stone receives its strength and virtue. And therefore, when it is in the Ascendant, this stone will manifest its works more clearly.

### Of the stone they call Bezoar. (24 verso.)

Associated with the eleventh degree of the sign of **Gemini** is the stone of **Bezoar**. And this is found in the islands of **India**; and it is the third kind of which we said we would speak in this book. This one is more subtly composed of elements, but not as much as the others we spoke of before; and according to its nature, it is lowlier than them. Naturally, it is hot and moist. Its color is brown and without any radiance. And its power is shown against other poisons, except those that grow from the earth because those are cold by nature, such as **mandrakes** <note>original: "mandragoras"</note>, or **henbane** <note>original: "bellinno"</note>, or other things of that nature. And to one who is given these poisons to eat or drink, if helped with this stone by giving it to him to drink, he escapes death and is cured. And even besides this, it has another power: if they hang it upon a man who has the illness called **fainting** <note>original: "esmayamiento"</note>, which comes by reason of **melancholy**, it cures him of it. It does the same for the other illness called **numbness** <note>original: "congelamiento"</note>, which means as much as the deadening of the limbs by reason of coldness. And the star that is in the front right foot of **Gemini** has power over this stone and from it receives its virtue. And when it is in the Ascendant, this stone manifests its works more.

### Of the stone they call Coloquia. (24 verso.)

Associated with the twelfth degree of the sign of **Gemini** is the stone they call **Coloquia**. And it has this name because it is found in mines on an island called **Col**. They are yellow in color, but some are more so than others. They find large ones and others smaller. They are strong and hard to break, such that they do not break except with great labor. It is dark and without radiance; but if they polish and clean it well, it has within it some clarity; but with all this, not so much that the sight passes through it. By its nature, it is hot and moist. And the philosophers prize it highly, because it has such power that he who carries it with him, it greatly sharpens his understanding and his wit; so that no thing is difficult for them to understand or to learn. And if they grind it and mix it with something to drink, it does the same for the one who drinks it. And the ancients did this to boys before they came of age; for they saw that thus their knowledge and understanding increased, such that whatever they heard while learning once, they never forgot. And therefore, those who have the illness by which they forget things are healed by wearing this. And the star that is at the end of the front paw of **Canis Major** has power over this stone and from it receives its strength and virtue. And therefore, when it is in the Ascendant, this stone manifests its works more completely.

Its color is a citrus-yellow mixed with white. This is found in the mines of the island called **Waq-Waq** <note>original: "Vacuac"; legendary islands in medieval Arabic geography.</note>. It also does other things that are very beneficial in the art of <term>physic</term> <note>The medieval term for medicine.</note>: if a person with paralysis carries it, or one who has tremors of the head or any illness of this nature, it brings relief. ### **Of the stone they call Taroc. (25.)**

Of the fourteenth degree of the sign of Gemini is the stone they call **Taroc**, and it is one of the other varieties of <term>Bezoar</term> <note>From the Persian *pādzahar*, meaning "antidote." Bezoars were highly prized stones found in the bellies of animals, believed to cure any poison.</note>. And they find it in the land of **Balkh** <note>original: "Ballac"; a historic city in modern-day Afghanistan.</note> in mines that are well-known for it. Some are found large and others small. Its color is white, but somewhat cloudy. It is heavy, strong, and hard to break. And if they polish it with the dust of that stone called in Arabic <term>Azumberic</term> <note>original: "Azumberic"; referring to Emery, a rock used for grinding and polishing.</note>, which is what we call **Emery**, it brightens somewhat and becomes beautiful. By nature, it is hot and moist. 

Its virtue is against all the <term>toxics</term> <note>Toxins or venoms.</note> of animals that are not greatly poisonous, such as spiders, wasps, gadflies, and those small things that are born from the earth: for if they give it to drink, it heals immediately, and if they hang it over the wound or bite of these animals, it removes the pain and heals in a short time. And it does another very strange thing: if they grind it and mix it with strong vinegar made from wine, place it in an earthenware jar and bury it in the dung of large beasts, and leave it there for thirty days during the hottest time of summer, at the end of this period they will find yellow worms inside the vessel. If they burn these and take their ash and place it upon any part of a man's body they wish to cauterize, it burns like fire; so much so that there is no need to burn him with anything else, and from this burn, the man feels no pain as he would from fire. And the star in the left knee of the leading Twin has power over this stone, and from it, the stone receives its virtue. And therefore, when that star is in the <term>ascendant</term> <note>The point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon.</note>, this stone shows its works most manifest.

### **Of the stone named Quedoritoz. (25 verso.)**

Of the fifteenth degree of the sign of Gemini is the stone called **Kedoritoz**, which means "drawer of worms." This is by nature moderately hot and moist, and it has open pores; yet it is not light, but rather heavy and rough to the touch. And if they break it, they find it very rough in the break. It has a purple color like blue, and even more deeply tinted in some parts; and though it is strong, they polish it like other stones. And when it is polished, to the one who sees it, it appears smooth; but when he touches it, he finds it rough. In the mines in the land of **Aral**, they find them more than in any other place, in a mountain that is there. And the Arabs prize them highly, and wear them in rings, and their women put them in the

And whoever wears it on the belt with which he girds himself every day is safe from having worms within the body. And the star that is in the right foot of the following Twin, and the front-most of the two stars in the left knee of the **Greater Dog** <note>The constellation Canis Major.</note>—and both are of one nature—have power over this stone, and from them, it receives its virtue. And when both are in the ascendant, this stone manifests its works clearly.

### **Of the stone named Siphe. (26.)**

Of the sixteenth degree of the sign of Gemini is the stone they call **Siphe**, which means "healing." This is by nature hot and moist, and of a yellow color; but it has purple lines in it resembling trees: and in however many pieces of it they break, they always find this figure within them. It is strong and hard and of a shining color. They find some large and some small, and they tend more toward lightness than heaviness. And its virtue is such that it heals pain of the stomach and the intestines for whoever wears it hanging over them. And if one wears it before having the illness, he will be safe from getting it: and if they give it to drink to one who already has it, he is healed at that very hour: and because such great health comes from it, for that reason they gave it this name. And for this reason, it was counted as one of the most precious stones. And the star that descends toward the southern part of the three that are in the right knee of the **Greater Dog** has power and lordship over this stone, and from it, the stone receives its force and virtue. And therefore, when it is in the ascendant, this stone shows its works most manifest.

### **Of the stone that appears in the sea. (26.)**

Of the seventeenth degree of the sign of Gemini is the stone that appears in the sea when **Mercury** rises, and hides when it sets. And this is that sea which they call the <term>Shadowy Sea</term> <note>original: "mar Tenebrosa"; a medieval name for the Atlantic Ocean, thought to be dark and impassable.</note> which is in the northern part where the stones of the other planets that do this same thing are found, as this book relates. And its virtue is to appear upon the sea and hide beneath it, and to brighten and become cloudy, just as the other stones do each with its own planet; but it seems, to whoever pays close attention, that this stone obeys Mercury more than the other stones obey the planets they must obey; because when Mercury is <term>under the sun's rays</term> <note>An astrological term meaning "combust," or so close to the sun that the planet cannot be seen.</note>, the stone does not shine, even if it be above the earth; and when it is outside the rays, even if the stone be under the earth, a brightness appears in it. This stone is a mixture of many different colors, and is of great brilliance and strong, and hard to break; it is heavy, and they find it in many shapes, but all are small. By nature, it is hot and moist. And it has such virtue that whoever carries it with him, it strengthens all the members of the body, and its movements, and the senses: so that, no matter the labor he undertakes or the work he does, he does not tire. And it even has another virtue, that all beasts flee from the one who carries it, and none come near him while he has it with him. And the star that is in the thigh of the left arm of the leading Twin, and the other that is at the base of the tail of the **Little Bear** <note>The constellation Ursa Minor.</note>—and both are of one nature—have power and lordship over this stone, and from them, it receives its virtue. And when these two are in the middle of the sky, this stone shows its works most completely.
