### Of the stone that they find in the belly of the swallow. (26 verso.)

The stone of the swallow belongs to the nineteenth degree of the sign of Gemini. It is one of the most precious stones among all those that are formed within animals. Whoever wishes to find it must take the first chick that the swallow produces in the year, and let him take care that the moon is waxing when he takes it. As soon as it comes out of the egg, he must open it by the belly, and there he will find two small stones of different colors; most often they find one green and the other white, though they find them of many other colors as well. They are rough to the touch, hard to break, and small in shape. They are hot and humid in nature. Their virtue is such that if these two stones are taken and placed in deer or calf leather and tied with a red silk thread around the neck of a man who is possessed by demons <note>In the Middle Ages, "demonic possession" was often a way to describe conditions like epilepsy or severe mental illness.</note>, he is healed immediately; however, this power only works if both stones are kept together and if they come from the same swallow chick. And it has yet another virtue: if they are ground in a gold mortar with a gold pestle and the well-ground powder is placed in the eyes of one whose eyes appear clear but who cannot see because of "enclosed water" <note>This likely refers to cataracts or glaucoma.</note>, it is of very great benefit, and if used regularly, he is completely healed. And the star that is in the thigh of the left arm of the forward Twin of Gemini has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its virtue. When that star is in the ascendant, this stone shows its works most manifestly.

### Of the stone they call Koloquid. (27.)

The stone they call Koloquid belongs to the twentieth degree of the sign of Gemini. This name means "changeable" or "convertible," and it has this name because it changes between day and night into many colors; at one time it changes to white, another to yellow, another black, another green, and so through all colors. It is so radiant that it seems rays of fire come out of it. It is found in the land of the blacks <note>A common medieval reference to sub-Saharan Africa.</note> among the sands. Some are large and some are small. It is strong and hard to break. They have such a power in the place where they are created that those who try to take them have visions <note>original: "antoyaseles"</note> that people are throwing stones at them; therefore, no one dares to enter the place where they are to take them unless he is very courageous and bold, and such a man who believes that what he sees is not reality but only an illusion. This stone is hot and humid in its nature. This property mentioned only appears in the place where it is born, except at night; for if whoever carries it with him has it at night while sleeping, he will see in dreams the appearance of being stoned, so that by necessity he will have to wake up and get up from the place where he lies. But if he avoids it at night and carries it by day, he will be safe from that sickness that comes from demons. It also does another thing: if they soak the herb called *asa fetida* <note>Asafetida, a resinous gum known for its strong, pungent smell, used in medicine and cooking.</note> in water and put this stone in that water, and leave it there for a day and a night, it dissolves

<column-break/>

and turns into the nature of the water. If they then dip a comb into that water and comb their hair with it, the hair is dyed black with a tint that lasts a very long time. And the star that is between the ears of the Great Dog has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its virtue. When that star is in the ascendant, this stone shows its works more.

### Of the stone they call Tarmicon. (27 verso.)

The stone they call Tarmicon belongs to the twenty-first degree of the sign of Gemini. This name in Chaldean means the same as *Asabac* in Arabic, and in Latin "desire of woman" <note>original: "cobdicia de mugier"</note>. By its nature, it is hot and humid and of a red color—a faint redness, like the water that comes out of meat when salt is thrown on it. It is strong and hard, breaking only with great effort. It has a great dislike for silver; if the stone and silver are placed together, the stone breaks immediately, and the silver turns the color of copper. This stone is found in the Promised Land in mines located on top of a mountain they call Xereha in that land. The virtue of this stone is such that if a man puts it in his mouth, for as long as he has it there, his male member will be erect and he may lie with a woman as many times as he wishes, for it will not go down nor weaken, nor will it do him harm. And if they grind it with something humid and rub that member with it, it performs its work even more strongly. And the star that is in the chest of the Great Dog has power over this stone and from it receives its virtue. When it is in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works most manifestly.

### Of the stone they call Gemezt. (27 verso.)

The stone they call Gemezt <note>Likely a variation of Amethyst, though the properties described here are specific to this lapidary tradition.</note> belongs to the twenty-second degree of the sign of Gemini. It is hot and humid in nature in the third degree of both these temperaments. It is soft, porous, light in weight, rough to the touch, and dark without brilliance. Its color is yellow, leaning somewhat toward red. It is found in many places, such as the Promised Land, Yemen, China <note>original: "Cin"</note>, the island of Sardinia, and other lands. Its virtue is such that if a man holds it in his mouth, or on his person, and drinks a sip of wine, he immediately becomes intoxicated by it, and displays all those behaviors of one who is very drunk. If they grind this stone and throw some of it into a vessel containing wine, the wine receives the power of the stone and intoxicates just as if the stone were there; however, this drunkenness lasts only a short time and does not leave the body broken as other wine does. And the star that is under the right knee of the trailing Twin of Gemini has power over this stone and from it receives its strength and virtue. Therefore, when it is in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works most manifestly.

### Of the stone whose name is Camiulicaz. (28.)

The stone they call Camiulicaz belongs to the twenty-third degree of the sign of Gemini; its name means "horse-restrainer." This stone is found on the island of Zarandin <note>An old name for Serendib, or modern-day Sri Lanka.</note>, and it is hot and humid in nature, but not excessively so. It is strong and hard, light in weight, and of a green color mixed with a bit of redness, so that it resembles the feathers of a peacock's neck. When they take it from the mine, it has no brilliance, but it receives it afterward upon polishing. Its virtue is such that when a horse sees it, it cannot move away from it, but stands there whinnying and staring at it until it dies, unless the stone is hidden or removed from before it. It also has another virtue: if they grind it and give it to a paralytic to drink, or to one who has the sickness they call stupor <note>A state of near-unconsciousness or insensibility.</note>, he is healed immediately. And the star that is between the shoulders of the forward Twin of Gemini has power over this stone and from it receives its strength and virtue. When it is in the ascendant, this stone shows its works most manifestly.

### Of the stone that is called Mecelucan. (28.)

The stone associated with the twenty-fourth degree of the sign of Gemini is called Mecelucan, which in Chaldean <note>An ancient Semitic language often associated with occult or scientific knowledge in the Middle Ages.</note> means "resolver of nature." Its nature is hot and humid, and it is strong in both these temperaments. It is light in weight and soft of body, such that it breaks very easily. Its color is green, leaning somewhat toward yellow. When it is taken from the mine it is radiant, but once handled it loses its luster and darkens; if it is polished again afterward, it recovers its clarity, though polishing it many times in this way causes it to shrink in size. It is found in the land of Arabia in the mines located there. Its name follows its virtue; for he who possesses it, as long as he carries it with him, never suffers from a flux of the belly <note>original: "fluja del vientre"; a historical term for diarrhea.</note>. If its powder or the shavings from its polishing are put into a clyster <note>A medicinal liquid injected into the rectum; an enema.</note>, it does the same, for it purges the humors. If a drachm’s weight <note>A unit of weight; roughly 3.9 grams.</note> of it is given to drink, it draws out each of the humors individually: first the phlegm, then the melancholy, then the choler, and finally the blood from abscesses. If while drawing out these humors it causes a flux, it cannot be cured so easily except with the stone we have mentioned called Leturican; for what this one dissolves, the other retains, and what the other retains, this one dissolves. Thus, whichever is given to drink last overcomes the other; therefore, if this stone causes a flux in a sick man upon drinking it, and they afterward give him the other to drink, it heals him. If this stone is soaked in the juice that comes from the herb called asafetida <note>A pungent resin used in medieval medicine.</note>, it loses its virtue, and if it is afterward placed in human blood, it recovers it. The star in the head of the forward Twin, and the other on the left side of the rear Twin—both being of the same nature—have power and lordship over this stone, and from them it receives its strength and virtue. Therefore, when they are in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works most manifesty.

### Of the stone that draws tallow. (28 verso.)

The stone of the twenty-fifth degree of the sign of Gemini is the one that draws tallow <note>Animal fat used for making candles or soap.</note> when it is drunk, as if it were sucking it. This stone is very white in color, though some lean toward gray. It is light in weight and has open pores. By nature, it is hot and humid. It is found in mines at the edge of Spain in the western part. Its virtue is such that if it is placed with a thousand weights of tallow of its own size when the tallow is congealed, it melts it all and makes it boil as if it were placed over a fire, and the stone consumes a quantity according to its own size. If it is weighed afterward, it is found to weigh twice what it weighed before, and if the tallow is afterward extracted from it, it returns to its original weight; by this, they know that it draws the weight into itself. Furthermore, it does another thing: if it is held in the hand or placed upon the flesh or skin, that place feels as if it has been greased, because it draws through the pores the fat it finds inside the flesh, such that the man feels what he has lost from it. If tallow is mixed with wax or another substance and the stone is placed there, it dissolves the tallow, making it boil, but the wax does not dissolve. If a man is given the powder of this stone to drink, he will feel such a great heat within him that much fat will leave him, such that he will suffer a flux from which he will die unless they assist him with some purge to draw this out. The star in the right shoulder of the forward Twin has power over this stone, and from it the stone receives its strength and virtue. When it is in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works most manifesty.

### Of the stone called Batocita. (29.)

The stone of the twenty-seventh degree of the sign of Gemini is the one called Batocita, which in Chaldean means "preventer of gray hair." By nature, it is hot and humid, and it is found in the land of Ethiopia in the gold mines. It is green in color like the emerald, but there is this difference between them: the emerald is so radiant that the sight passes through it, but this one is not. However, once it is polished, rays come out of it like a mirror, which turn back into themselves. There is yet another difference: the emerald is very heavy and hard to break, while this one is very light and breaks easily. Those who wish to do evil and fraud sell it in place of emeralds to those who do not know it. Its virtue is such that he who carries it with him before he turns gray will find that it prevents gray hairs from coming except after a very long time. Furthermore, if it is ground and distilled, and a comb is soaked in the water that comes from it, and the head is combed with it, it prevents more gray hairs from growing there, and it dyes those already grown with a tint that lasts a very long time. This water has another virtue: if it is given to drink to a man who has pain in any part of the belly, he is healed immediately; in this matter, it has as much virtue as theriac <note><term>theriac</term>: A famous "universal" medicine or ointment used since antiquity to treat poisons and diseases.</note>, especially if the pain is of a cold nature. If its powder is given to drink diluted with some liquid, it does the same, though not as effectively as the water. The two stars, one in the head of the rear Twin and the other in the shoulder of the same image, have power over this stone, and from them it receives its strength and virtue. When these two are in the ascendant, this stone shows its works most manifesty.

### Of the liver stone. (29.)

It is strong and hard to break, and heavy; but when it is broken, a liquid the color of the stone itself comes out of it. By nature, it is hot and humid; it is found in mines in the lands of Egypt in certain very unpopulated places called Leruricaz, which is a land where there are many lions and other fierce beasts. Its virtue is such that if it is hung over a liver that is diseased, it heals it; if they drink the water that comes from it, it does the same and cures it. Generally, it heals all ailments of the liver and opens its passages, whether by wearing it or by drinking it. The star at the tip of the forward ear of the Great Bear has power over this stone and from it receives its strength and virtue. Therefore, when it is in the ascendant, it shows you the works of this stone most manifesty.

### **Of the stone they call Green Adehenich. (32.)**

### **Of the stone named Painted Adehenich. (32.)**

And the northern star of the two that are in the beam <note>original: "viga"; likely referring to a mast or structural part of the constellation Argo Navis.</note> which is at the curved end of the figure of the Ship <note>original: "naf"; from the Latin 'navis', referring to the constellation Argo Navis.</note>, has power and lordship over this stone, and from it, the stone receives its strength and virtue. ### **Of the stone that attracts silver. (32 verso.)**

Associated with the sixth degree of the sign of Cancer is the stone that attracts silver, and it is found in the West at the point furthest to the right where the sun sets. This stone is very soft, and when they press it between their teeth, it sounds like tin; yet there is no mixture of tin within it. And when they burn it, it turns into lime and takes into itself the heat of fire like other magnets. ### **Of the stone that attracts lead. (33.)**

And the bright star that is in the stern of the Ship has power over this stone and from it receives its strength and virtue. ### Of the stone that appears in the sea when the moon sets. (33 verso.)

Belonging to the ninth degree of the sign of Cancer is the stone that appears in the sea when the moon sets and hides itself when the moon shows. This stone is found in the dark sea <note>original: "mar tenebrosa"; a medieval term for the Atlantic Ocean.</note> where other stones are found that clearly manifest the virtue of the planets. By its nature, it is cold and humid, light in weight, and very black in color. When the moon shows itself, the stone descends and goes to the bottom; when the moon sets, it rises and floats upon the water. Once they take it from that place, it darkens when the moon is above the earth, and when the moon is below the earth, it brightens; it always acts in this way.

And it is a great wonder of its nature that, despite being as black as can be, sight passes through it just as it does through crystal. It has a very wonderful and strange virtue: he who wears it hanging between his eyes sees as well by night as by day, without a candle or any other light. The star located toward the south of the two that are at the front of the quadrangle surrounding the nebula <note>original: "nuf"; from the Arabic *al-nathra*, referring to the Praesepe or "Manger" star cluster in Cancer.</note> of the figure of Cancer, and the other star in the front body of this same figure, both have power over this stone and from them it receives its virtue. When they are in the ascendant, this stone shows its works most clearly.

### Of the stone they call Africana. (33 verso.)

Belonging to the tenth degree of the sign of Cancer is the stone they call Africana. It has this name because it is found in the land of Africa on the banks of a river that descends from a mountain and runs through all that land. Some are large and some are small, and its color is like yellow orpiment <note>original: "azarnech amariello"; a yellow arsenic sulfide pigment.</note>; however, it is not as bright, but rather darker. It is strong and hard to break. By its nature, it is cold and humid; but when they break it, they find within a body that resembles an egg yolk in color, feel, and all its qualities. If they take this and rub hemorrhoids with it, they heal very quickly. And if they put some of it in the clyster <note>A medicinal liquid injected into the rectum; an enema.</note> prepared for a man who is bleeding due to the rupturing of veins, he recovers. If they grind the outer casing—which is hard and lacks all moisture—and mix it with the inks they use for writing or painting, it brightens them and gives them good color; but it only does this for yellow, green, or red colors, for it ruins all others if mixed with them. The northern star of the two in the chest of the Great Bear has power over this stone, and from it, the stone receives its strength and virtue. Therefore, when that star is in the ascendant, this stone shows its works most clearly.

### Of the stone named Tarmicaz. (34.)

Belonging to the eleventh degree of the sign of Cancer is the stone they call Tarmicaz. It is white in color, mixed somewhat with green. They are found small, such that the largest of them weighs no more than half a drachma; yet they are quite heavy for their size. They are always found in a triangular shape and are very smooth on all sides. By nature, it is cold and humid. It is found in the sea they call Red <note>original: "Bermeya"; literally "Vermillion" or Red Sea.</note>, through which the Children of Israel passed, within certain shells that grow there. These stones form upon them like the scales found on a fish; the larger the shell, the larger the stone grown within it, though it does not exceed the usual size. Its virtue is such that if placed in psyllium water—which they call <term>azarcatona</term> in Arabic <note>from *al-zarqatuna*, the plant *Plantago psyllium*.</note>—it softens like warm wax. Once softened, if given to a woman to drink, she will never conceive anything but a daughter; the same will happen to any female animal that drinks it. The northern star of the last two in the quadrangle of the figure of Cancer—called <term>hamelin</term>—has power over this stone and from it, it receives its virtue. When it is in the ascendant, this stone shows its works more fully.

<column-break/>

### Of the stone they call Argent or silver. (34.)

Belonging to the twelfth degree of the sign of Cancer is the stone that everyone commonly calls Argent or silver, and the Moors call <term>feda</term> <note>original: "feda"; from the Arabic *fidda* (silver).</note>. This stone endures the hammer and the forge, just like other stones that are metals. It spreads under the hammer more quickly than iron or copper, but not as well as gold. Because these metallic stones are of one nature regarding their softness and hardening, they love one another and combine when mixed together. However, some of them abhor others, such as silver; when they melt lead and place silver near the smell of the smoke rising from it, the silver breaks. Quicksilver <note>original: "argent vivo"; mercury.</note> does the same. But salt is very good for this stone, for it washes it and makes it bright because of the whiteness and beauty within it.

This stone is cold and humid by nature. It is lighter than gold and heavier than iron or copper. If its filings are mixed with medicines used against phlegm—which they call <term>vitreum</term> <note>Latin for "glassy" or "clear," likely referring to a specific medicinal preparation.</note>—it is beneficial. It is also helpful for all illnesses caused by phlegm. If placed in a vessel and buried in the earth so that it does not touch the soil, it lasts a very long time without spoiling; but in the end, if it remains there too long, it turns back into earth. If buried otherwise so that there is nothing between it and the earth, it blackens immediately, loses its color, and spoils so completely that it is destroyed. The color of this stone is white; the more it is polished, the more it shines, though sight cannot pass through it. Its mines are in many places and it is well known to men because it is a noble metal, useful for many things. The southern star of the last two in the quadrangle of the figure of Cancer—called <term>hamelin</term>—has power over this stone and from it, it receives its virtue. When it is in the midheaven, this stone shows its works more fully.

### Of the stone they call lead. (34 verso.)

Belonging to the thirteenth degree of the sign of Cancer is the stone they call <term>plumbo</term> in Latin, <term>plomo</term> in Romance <note>The vernacular Spanish/Castilian language.</note>, and <term>Arrazaz</term> in Arabic <note>from *al-rasas*.</note>. It is also a metal like silver or other known metals. It is found in many places. By its nature, it is cold and humid in the second degree, and it naturally possesses a hidden oily moisture <note>original: "anguosidad humorosa"; referring to its low melting point and viscosity.</note> that it never loses unless it is placed in fire and burned; for then it becomes cold and dry. It is very close to silver; but because of the impurities of the earth and the air that sometimes mix with it unevenly, it suffers three defects: first, it gets dirty quickly; second, it smells bad; and third, it makes a sound <note>a "crunch" or "cry".</note> between the teeth. Such lead as this is called tin <note>original: "estanno".</note>. There is another lead which is the thing itself, which they call black <note>original: "negro"; referring to *plumbum nigrum*, or actual lead, as opposed to tin (*plumbum album*).</note>; this is even more natural than the other we mentioned, and this book will speak of it later in its proper place. But concerning this first kind, which is considered nobler, the wise men said that if one worked it as required with the juice of myrtle, marcasite, salt, and Spanish flies <note>original: "cantaridas"; a type of beetle used in medicine and alchemy.</note>, these four things would make it lose the three aforementioned defects. However, because this belongs to the work of alchemy, we did not wish to include it here in this book. Thus, we return to our purpose and say: burnt lead, when put into the eyes, is of great benefit, for it dries their moisture and heals the sores that form there, in animals as well as in men; it also dries the moisture in wounds, allowing them to heal more quickly. The leading star of the three in the front of the shadow of the nebula <note>original: "naf"; again referring to the *an-nathra* / Praesepe.</note> has power over this stone and from it, it receives its strength and virtue. Therefore, when it is in the midheaven, this stone shows its works most clearly.

### Of the stone that flees from honey. (35.)

Belonging to the fifteenth degree of the sign of Cancer is the stone that flees from honey. This stone is cold and humid by nature, and it is found on the island called Merataz in the Red Sea <note>original: "mar Bermeya"</note>, through which the children of Israel passed. This island is uninhabited, but ships pass near it while coming and going. Many types of stones are found there, some of which we will name in this book, each in its proper place; the one we speak of now is hard, heavy, and of a purplish-blue color, though it tends somewhat toward redness. They are found both large and small. Its property is such that it loathes honey; when placed near honey, the stone leaps and flees as far as it can. There is another test: if this stone is ground and mixed with water, it incorporates with it so that they cannot be separated, unless one takes honey and mixes it in; then the stone leaves the water and separates from it. It is a very beautiful stone to look at, so much so that if a man is not a good judge of stones, he might think it is one of those very clear sapphires that are opaque to the sight. It possesses a very harmful quality: he who carries it upon himself finds his urinary tract loosened, so that he cannot hold his urine even if he wishes, especially at night while he sleeps. The star at the end of the "crooked beam" located in the front of the <note>original: "naf"</note> has power over this stone and from it, the stone receives its strength and virtue. When that star is in mid-heaven, this stone manifests its works most clearly.

### Of the stone they call Moon-Scopetina. (35 verso.)

Belonging to the sixteenth degree of the sign of Cancer is the stone called Moon-Scopetina <note>original: "Scopetina de la Luna"</note>. It has this name because it is only found at night, specifically when the moon is full. By its nature, it is cold and humid, white in color, and very light in weight; it reflects within itself all the colors placed near it.

It is found in the Western lands more than anywhere else, in certain caves located in a wilderness; they are never found except at night when the moon is full. For this reason, the people of that land believe the moon creates them at that hour and season, and thus they give it the name we have mentioned. Others call it "Moon Foam." The people of Chaldea call it <term>ceduluquindad</term>, which means the same thing. The virtue of this stone is such that if the filings from its polishing are given in a drink to one who is possessed by a demon, they are healed immediately. He who carries it with him is likewise protected from that sickness. If it is hung from a tree, it makes the fruit grow and ripen very quickly. The two stars, the northern and the southern, which are in the head of the serpent called <note>original: "idros"; the constellation Hydra</note>, have power over this stone and from them, it receives its virtue. And when both of these

<column-break/>

are in mid-heaven, this stone will manifest its works most clearly.

### Of the stone named Zexegt. (35 verso.)

Belonging to the seventeenth degree of the sign of Cancer is the stone called Zexegt. This is found in the land of India. By its nature, it is cold and humid, and its color is between red and yellow, though it tends more toward yellow; some are found with a color tending toward brown. In color, it resembles a hazelnut, and when shaken, it rattles; if broken open, another stone is found inside, white in color tending toward yellow. When ground and mixed with water and rubbed upon a limb that has a tumor or any other sickness arising from <note>original: "malanconia"; melancholy or black bile</note>, it heals very quickly. If tied to the leg of a woman at the time of birth, she delivers well and easily. The southern star called Azobene, which is in the front horn of the figure of Cancer, has power over this stone and from it, the stone receives its strength and virtue. When it is in mid-heaven, it shows its works most clearly.

### Of the stone named Lechar. (36.)

Belonging to the eighteenth degree of the sign of Cancer is the stone Lechar <note>derived from the Spanish "leche" for milk</note>. It has this name because the moisture that comes from it resembles milk in color, substance, and taste. By its nature, it is cold and humid, white in color, soft to the touch, smooth, and heavy. When it is polished, that moisture we mentioned comes out of it. If placed upon the eyes of one whose eyes are watering, it stops it; it also heals sores that form in the eyes and those that form in the intestines. This "milk," if kept in a lead vessel, increases in its virtue. The star that is over the quadrangle of the body of the Great Bear <note>Ursa Major</note> has power over this stone and from it, the stone receives its strength and virtue. When it is in mid-heaven, it shows its works most clearly.

### Of the stone named Videga. (36.)

Belonging to the nineteenth degree of the sign of Cancer is the stone they call Vidiega. This is found in the land called <note>original: "Falaztim"; Palestine</note>. It is always found in the shape of an acorn. Its color is white with green stripes running lengthwise. By its nature, it is cold and humid, and it dissolves when thrown into water. The liquid that comes from it has no taste. Some of them are flat on one side and round on the other, shaped like a chestnut; they are about the size of a walnut. The stone is heavy in itself and has such virtue that if one takes a piece the size of a chickpea, polishes it on a black whetstone, and gives it to drink with three times its amount of sweet water to one who has a retention of urine, they are healed immediately. It breaks the stone in the bladder and also helps against stones formed in the kidneys.

The front star of the "two hidden ones" in the bright part of the <note>original: "nuf"; the nebula cluster</note> has power over this stone and from it, the stone receives its strength and virtue. When it is in mid-heaven, it shows its works most clearly.

This is found on the island of Cyprus <note>original: "Cabroz"</note> in a river that passes through there called Baciz, from which it takes its name. It is light in weight, yet strong and hard to break. By its nature, it is very cold, but not as humid. Its shape is quadrangular, but its four corners are triangular, closing at a point at the bottom like the shape of a pine cone. Its color is yellow tending toward white. It is radiant, so that sight passes through it. ### Regarding the stone that appears in the sea when the moon rises. (36 verso.)

From the twenty-first degree of the sign of Cancer is the stone that appears in the sea when the moon rises and hides itself when it sets. This is found in the "Tenebrous Sea" <note>A medieval name for the Atlantic Ocean</note> where the other stones are found that show the force of the other planets. In color, it is very white and of great radiance, and its light increases when the moon is above the earth and decreases when it is below it; it does the same when the moon is waxing or waning. In form, it is very round and large in body. By its nature, it is cold and humid. Its virtue is such that whoever carries it with them will be safe from having ailments of the spleen, nor will it do them harm if they drink much water. ### Regarding the stone named Plomenna. (37.)

From the twenty-second degree of the sign of Cancer is the stone they call Plomenna; it has this name because it resembles lead in color, but it is its opposite in weight, for lead is heavy and this stone is light. It is found in the land called <note>original: "Aquitaz"; likely referring to Aquitaine</note> in the mines located there. By its nature, it is cold and humid; when it is burned and quenched many times in oil, it changes its color, becoming reddish and light, and it receives a certain radiance. If, after it has been burned, it is sprinkled with wine, a fire comes out of it that burns whatever it reaches; this is quenched with any kind of oil and with nothing else. And if, after it is burned and quenched in oil, it is kneaded with butter and used to anoint a sickness called <term>Anaxe: likely a corruption of an Arabic term for varicose veins or leg ulcers</term>—which occurs in the vein running along the inside of the leg from the back of the knee to the heel—it heals immediately. It does the same for other diseases of the legs that cause the veins to swell, specifically that which causes one leg to swell, which they call the disease of the <term>Elcofant: elephantiasis, a condition characterized by extreme swelling of the limbs</term>. And it does even more: if three <term>drachmas: a unit of weight roughly equal to an eighth of an ounce</term> of it are given to drink, prepared with the things we mentioned, it purges raw phlegm and heals all the diseases caused by it. And the shining star of the three that are in the shadow of the ship has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its force and virtue. When it is in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works more completely.

### Regarding the stone they call Ferrenna. (37.)

From the twenty-third degree of the sign of Cancer is the stone they call Ferrenna; it has this name because it resembles iron in color. It is hard and strong. The Greeks call it *Amboneneuz*. By its nature, it is cold and humid. It is found in the land of Argent in the bottom of a river that flows there called the River Ferrenno. When it is rubbed against another stone, a moisture comes out of it that resembles rotten blood in color. If this is given to drink to one who has pain in the belly called <term>Torceyones: griping pains or colic, whether caused by bodily humors or strong medicine</term>, they heal immediately.

### Regarding the stone of the rooster. (37 verso.)

From the twenty-fourth degree of the sign of Cancer is the stone of the rooster, which is one of those found in animals. They find it in this way: they watch for the first egg a hen lays; if they find it is a male, they must raise it until it is eight months old and then kill it. Once it is dead, they will find in its belly a white stone that resembles crystal in color, and it is the size of a bean or perhaps slightly larger. By its nature, it is cold and humid. It has such virtue that if it is given ground in a drink to a man when he has great thirst, it takes it away; and if they wash it before it is ground and give that wash-water to drink, his life-spirit will be cheered, and sadness will be removed if he has any. ### Regarding the stone of Magnesia. (37 verso.)

From the twenty-fifth degree of the sign of Cancer is the stone they call <term>Almagnicia: Magnesia, often used in medieval glass-making and alchemy</term>; there are three types of it. One is brown in color, another black, and the third green. In Greek, all these types are called *Andardimuz*. In these three types, there is no difference in nature or virtue, only in color. It is found in many places. By nature, it is cold and humid. Its virtue is such that it causes glass—which is scattered like sand—to join together; this is because it has a certain amount of lead mixed within it. Men were mistaken about this stone, for they thought it was the one that "coagulated the loose and loosened the coagulated," because they saw it solidify the body of glass. Also, when ground, this stone enters into powders made for the eyes to wash away filth.

And the following star of the two that are above the shining part of the ship's shadow has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its force and virtue. When it is in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works more completely.

That which is considered a stone is what they take from the mine before they burn it. By nature, it is cold and humid and like silver, except that it has "received sickness" <note>a medieval alchemical way of saying it is an "imperfect" version of silver</note>. It also has a smell, a sound, and a tremor. By its nature, it kills lice. The earth of the stone, after it is burned, kills mice if it is mixed into some food. To a man who is reached by its smoke, it makes him paralytic, causes his limbs to tremble and his hearing to be lost, and many other diseases. From the place its smoke reaches, snakes and other reptiles flee, and those that remain die. If they burn the quicksilver and give it to drink to one with <term>Iliaco: ileus, a painful intestinal obstruction</term>, they heal. ### Regarding the stone they call Gaciegaleitiz. (38.)

### Regarding the stone named Onna. (38 verso.)

This is found in the land of <term>Argeoz</term>; it is a very humid land of great cold and many rains. When the waters are heavy in the winter time, great lagoons form in the fields there. Then, when summer comes, they dry up with the heat of the sun, and then they find these stones, some large and others small. Most of them are white, though some have a bit of yellow. They are radiant and heavy, and by nature cold and humid. If they are ground well and mixed with water, they can be fashioned into any shape; if left to dry in the sun, it becomes very hard and shining, so much so that it does not look like a counterfeit <note>likely referring to its use in making imitation marble or polished ceramics</note>. The women of that land use it on their bodies to make them soft and of a good color. Those who make paper include it in the process because it makes the paper white and more brilliant. ### Regarding the Bloodstone. (38 verso.)

The <term>twenty-ninth</term> degree of the sign of <term>Cancer</term> belongs to the stone named <term>Sanguina</term> <note>Bloodstone; though described here as green, it is distinct from modern hematite</note>. They find it in the land called <term>Daquitaz</term> on the banks of a river called <term>Sagaf</term>, from which it takes its name. Its color is green, pulling somewhat toward purple, and it greatly resembles the color of the <term>Alferuzach</term> <note>Turquoise</note> stone, except that this one is very light and porous, and easy to break—so much so that it breaks between the fingers. When broken, a moisture is found inside the crack that resembles glue. If they grind this stone and mix it with water, it makes a very strong glue. Those who bind books in the Promised Land use it, as do carpenters for joining boards. Its virtue is such that if it is given to drink to one who has an abscess in the chest or sides—being ground and mixed with water in which sea shells <note>original: "cochas marinas"</note> were boiled—it heals them in one or two doses. The southern star of the three that follow the neck of the <term>Idro</term> <note>Hydra, the Water Snake</note> has power over this stone, and from it the stone receives its strength and virtue. When it is in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works most completely.

### Regarding the stone they call Farquidiuz. (39.)

The thirtieth degree of the sign of <term>Cancer</term> belongs to the stone they call <term>Farquidiuz</term>. This is found on the island of <term>Alaiquak</term> on the seashore. It is yellow in color and has black lines inside, placed one over the other in the likeness of a tree <note>This likely describes a dendritic stone, such as moss agate or limestone with manganese dendrites</note>. It is a very heavy and strong stone, and hard to break; it can only be broken with great effort. If placed in fire, a very foul odor comes from it, smelling like rotting meat. If a person possessed by a demon smells this smoke, it seizes them immediately; but to one who is not possessed, the smell does no harm at all. By nature it is cold and humid. The dark northern star of the two in the front part of the northern side of the body of <term>Idro</term> <note>Hydra</note> has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its strength and virtue. When it is in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works most clearly.

# ON THE SIGN OF LEO.

### Regarding the stone they call Sulfur mixed in colors. (40.)

The first degree of the sign of <term>Leo</term> belongs to the stone they call <term>Sufre</term> <note>Sulphur</note> mixed with many colors; this stone is somewhat clear. They find it on the island called <term>Linar</term>. By nature it is hot and dry, like the others; but it has less color than they do. If they grind it and mix it with oil, it helps with mange, itching, the common cold, and coughs. It also heals the illness that comes from a "dripping of the head" <note>likely referring to post-nasal drip or catarrh</note> from which tuberculosis of the lung develops. The star in the handle of the Jar <note>likely referring to the constellation Crater</note> that faces south has power over this stone, and from it the stone receives its virtue. When that star is in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works most clearly.

<header>CONCERNING VIRGO. <note>original Latin: DE VIRGO</note></header>

# ON THE SIGN OF VIRGO.

### PROLOGUE. (41.)

The thirty types of stones according to the thirty degrees of the sign of Leo have been described, and it is necessary that he who wishes to use the knowledge in this book should pay attention to the state of the sun, as has been said of the other planets of the signs we have spoken of. And likewise, to the state of the <term>lord of the face</term> <note>the planetary ruler of a 10-degree subdivision of the zodiac</note> of that degree of the sign to which the stone belongs; for when it is in a good position, the virtue of these stones will be stronger for working good; and when in a bad position, the contrary. But now we shall return to follow our discourse and begin the sign of Virgo.

### Regarding the stone they call Venequen. (41.)

Of the first degree of the sign of Virgo is the stone they call Venequen. This stone is found in a river called Queveraz that runs through an island called Nelile. This river has little water: so that in the time of the heat, it dries up; and then they find this stone there, which is green in color, clear, and shining, and hard to break; and it has branches like coral: and when they break it, they find it white inside, and some are so long that they make knife handles from them. And if they grind it and mix it with wine and smear it upon a spear shaft, or any other wood, it will never warp; rather, it will straighten if it were crooked. And if they smear <term>hot apostemes</term> <note>inflammatory swellings or abscesses</note> with it, they heal: and it does this because it is of a cold and dry nature. And likewise, when they place it over the stomach, it restrains vomiting. And if they scatter the powder of it over the body of a dead man, it keeps it from rotting and dries it; but in itself it is a mortal <term>toxic</term> <note>original: "tosico"; a deadly poison</note>; for if they give it to a man to drink, it kills him; yet the body of the one who dies of this poison does not rot. And the two stars, the northern one and the southern one, which are in the cape of the figure of the Virgin <note>the constellation Virgo</note> have power over this stone and from them it receives its virtue. And when these are in the <term>ascendant</term> <note>the point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon</note> it shows its works most.

### Regarding the stone named dark Aliaza. (41.)

Of the second degree of the sign of Virgo is the stone they call dark Aliaza. And of this kind, we have already named some in this book in the degrees of the sign of Taurus, and we spoke of one green and the other black: but now we shall speak here of the one that is very dark and is of a cold and dry nature. And they find it in the land of <term>Cin</term> <note>likely China</note>. It is hard and strong of body, and in it are all the evil virtues that we said were in the other kinds of Aliaza; for he who carries it with him, men wish him ill and quarrel with him willingly. From this stone they make vessels and bowls in which they eat and drink; but it has such a virtue that for him who is accustomed to eating or drinking from them, his worries increase as do the illnesses that come from <term>melancholy</term> <note>one of the four humors, associated with black bile and sadness</note>. And the northern star that is in the mouth of the <term>jar</term> <note>original: "tinaya"; likely referring to the constellation Crater or the urn of Aquarius</note> has power over this stone and from it receives its strength and virtue. And when it is in the ascendant, this stone shows its works most fully.

<column-break/>

### Regarding the stone named variegated Aliaza. (41 verso.)

Of the third degree of the sign of Virgo is the stone they call variegated Aliaza. And it has this name because they always find it in two colors: one brown and the other red. By nature it is cold and dry; and it agrees with the other in the virtues we spoke of before; but this kind is softer to the touch than any of the others we mentioned. And the leading star of the three that are in the left hand of <term>the one who cries out</term> <note>the constellation Boötes, the Shouter</note> has power over this stone and from it receives its virtue. And when it is in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works most manifestly.

### Regarding the stone they call white Aliaza. (41 verso.)

Of the fourth degree of the sign of Virgo is the stone they call white Aliaza. And they find it in the land of <term>Liemen</term> <note>Yemen</note>. In color it is white, and of a cold and dry nature. And it is a stone that men should not carry with them; for it is in itself a mortal toxic; so that if a man drinks the weight of one <term>drachm</term> <note>a small unit of weight</note> of it, it kills; but if before three hours pass they give him as much as half an ounce of hot oil to drink, he is cured: but if three hours pass, nothing can save him from death. And the middle star of the three that are in the left hand of the figure of the one who cries out has power over this stone and from it receives its virtue. And when it is in the ascendant, this stone shows its works most fully.

### Regarding the stone named Fardicanér. (42.)

Of the fifth degree of the sign of Virgo is the stone they call Fardicanér; which means as much in <term>Chaldean</term> <note>an ancient Semitic language often associated with magic and astrology in the Middle Ages</note> as "tongue-retainer." It is a stone very black in color, and they find white spots in it. By nature it is cold and dry. And it is found in a land called Adurugen on the shore of the sea. They are small stones mixed with sand. It is light in weight and of open pores. And it is so soft that in pressing it between the fingers, it breaks. And when they burn it, it becomes hard like other stones. And if they grind any amount of it, and knead it with watered wine, and make it into whatever shape they wish, and put it in the fire, it becomes hard stone, and retains its color and its virtue. And it shows the property it has within it: that he who carries it with him will not be able to speak; and if they give him some of it to drink, he becomes even more mute: but this does not last for more than seven days. And the northern star of the two that are in the bottom of the jar and are in the body of the figure they call <term>Idro</term> <note>the constellation Hydra</note> has power over this stone, and from it receives its strength and virtue. And when it is in mid-heaven, it shows its works most manifestly.

## Regarding the stone named Azech. (42 verso.)

Of the seventh degree of the sign of Virgo is the stone they call Azech <note>Azech or Aceche refers to vitriol or metallic sulfates</note>. This is of four kinds: the first they call Zori; the second Calcatar; the third Calcadiz; and the fourth Calcant. We shall speak of each of these in its place: but first it is necessary to show the ways in which they agree with one another; and they are these: their nature is cold and dry, and they blacken the bodies upon which they are placed, and they staunch blood flowing from the nose or from wounds; however, that place remains black and it harms the nerves, though it strengthens and tightens areas that are loose. And if a man drinks a certain quantity of it, his lungs dry up with such great dryness that he dies unless they help him quickly. There are certain waters that run through the place where these stones are born; whoever is accustomed to bathing in them will suffer great and very long-lasting fevers, from which they recover very slowly. But now we wish to speak of the first of these Azeches called Zori, which is red in color. Its mine is in the land of Spain and in another called Cadiz, but the best of all is that found in the land of Egypt. This has a strong smell, and when they break it, they find it black and pitted inside: it has a certain light enclosed within itself; and its smell is so strong that it causes fainting <note>original: "faz camiar"; literally 'makes one change,' implying a loss of consciousness or state</note> upon smelling it, and especially if they drink it. It is of a harsh flavor, which they call "styptic" in Latin <note>original: "stititico"; meaning astringent</note>. Therefore, if they grind it and put it in glass, it is useful for sores on the legs: and this kind of Azech is the most stony and brightest of all the others. And the star that is in the mouth of the "Vessel" <note>original: "tinaya"; likely the constellation Crater</note> on the southern side has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its virtue. And when it is in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works most manifesty.

## Regarding the stone they call Marmunia. (42 verso.)

Of the eighth degree of the sign of Virgo is the stone they call Marmunia. It is cold and dry in nature. Its mine is in a town called Zurien, and they find it inside a cave in which there is a wide path, and at the end of that path there is a chamber in the middle of which is a sort of pool where yellow drops of water fall from above. These are hard and very strong and shine somewhat, and their light is greater when they are broken or on the outer edge of the break. This has the power to constrict greatly, so that if any man drinks of it, his throat will choke, and if he drinks much of it, it will kill him; and men prove it in this way: when they pass through where the stones are, they feel as if they are choking because of the smell; and if they put this stone in the fire, smoke comes from it that constricts greatly: so much so that it harms the throat. And if women fumigate themselves with it, provided they take care that the smoke does not enter their noses, it tightens them greatly and dries them in such a way that their husbands receive new pleasure from them. And the star that follows the last star of the shadow of the "Ship" <note>original: "naf"; referring to the constellation Argo Navis</note> has power over this stone-

<column-break/>

and from it receives its force and virtue. And when it is in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works most fully.

## Regarding the stone named Calcatar. (43.)

Of the ninth degree of the sign of Virgo is the stone of the Azech they call Calcatar, and it is the second kind of those we mentioned. It is yellow in color, and it dissolves when they cook it or throw it in water. And sometimes they find pieces of the red Azech in this one, which we mentioned before; when they remove a film that it has on top, it appears yellow inside, and by this it is understood that in time the yellow becomes red, and the red yellow; but of those that appear yellow, the best is that which has the color of brass and is easiest to break; however, there is another in which they find veins like the color of gold, and this is harder and stronger to break, and when they break it, it shines somewhat in the break, and for this reason they call it "starlike," because that brilliance it has within appears like stars; and they call it "Litarne" in Chaldean. The best of this Azech is found on the island of Cyprus <note>original: "Cabroz"</note>, yet nevertheless it is found in many other places, and likewise it shares properties with all others of this nature; and with the great power of sharpness it possesses, it constricts greatly, and it has such heat in it that it burns the flesh it is placed upon and makes a scab; but by burning this stone it loses its sharpness; therefore it is better to work with it burned than raw: for this is of a more subtle substance than the other we mentioned and easier to dissolve; and therefore it enters into the medicines they make for moisture in the eyes and for the tears that come from them. Likewise, it is useful for "hot apostemes" <note>inflammatory swellings</note> when mixed with the juice of leeks. And likewise it enters into the medicines they make for swelling of the gums, and also for scabs and sores that form on the body and for fistulas. And the leading star of the three that are in the northern right arm of the figure of Virgo has power over this stone and from it receives its force and virtue. And when it is in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works most manifestly.

## Regarding the stone named Calcant. (43 verso.)

Of the tenth degree of the sign of Virgo is the stone they call Calcant. This is one of the kinds of Azech that we have already named. It is green in color and they call it "Guielketiz" in Greek <note>likely a corruption of chalcitis</note>. This kind of Azech dissolves in water and is of more subtle parts of the elements than the other we mentioned called Calcatar. And sometimes they find this stone in layers, one over another; and this happens because it changes over very long periods of time. And such a stone as this they call "Tanner's Azech"; and some of it is made from drops that fall in its mine: and this they call Alcatar. And there is another that is made from the mine itself, and this is found in the land they call "Ezfama" in Greek, which means Spain <note>original: "Ezfama que quier decir Espanna"</note>. And likewise there is some that is of an ugly color and very weak in itself, and if they mix it with water, and cook it, and then pour it into a vessel, and place it in the air and the sun, and leave it there for a long time, it congeals and stones are made of it; and the best of these are those that tend toward the color blue. And this Azech is clear and clean of color, and heavier than the other Azeches; and it shares in all the properties they have, except that it constricts more; so that through that constriction it receives a certain bitterness; and because of this it dries the moisture of the flesh more than any other kind of the Azeches, and joins things that are separated, and is more subtle than the other Azech called Calcatar, and with less sharpness; and it is very useful for teeth that are loose: for it tightens them and makes them firm, and they even put it in the medicines they make to dye hair black. And the raw form of these Calcatars is better than the burned. And the two stars—the one that faces south, and the other middle one of the three that are in the right line, which follow the "Triangle" <note>original: "tangulo"; likely Triangulum</note>, which is in the Dragon <note>Draco</note>—have power over this stone; and from them it receives its force and virtue. And when both of these are in the ascendant, this stone shows its works most fully.

<meta>This page continues the Lapidary’s catalog for the sign of Virgo. The previous page introduced the four types of "Aceche" (vitriols or metallic sulfates), having already described the first three. This page begins with the eleventh degree and the fourth type of vitriol, Calcanth.</meta>

# OF VIRGO.

## Regarding the stone they call Calcanth. (43 verso.)

Of the eleventh degree of the sign of Virgo is the stone they call Calcanth <note>original: "Calcant"; likely blue or green vitriol (copper or iron sulfate)</note>; and it is also the fourth kind of vitriol <term>Aceche (vitriol): a category of metallic sulfate minerals used in dyes and medicine</term> that we have mentioned. It is white in color and they call it *rehera* in Arabic, which in that language means "purification." In Greek, they call it *Melintria*. This stone is more prized for certain things than *Calcadiz* <note>another form of vitriol</note>, and that one is more prized for others; thus they often change from one form into another. However, this white variety is easier to dissolve than the others because it is of a more subtle substance. There are some who find it in its mine already formed into stone; the largest are those found in the land called *Calybia* <note>likely referring to the Chalybes, an ancient people of Asia Minor known for iron-working</note>, though they are found in other places as well. The best among them are those the color of yellow sulfur, which are soft and clean; when thrown into water, they immediately turn black, for this is their natural property. In all other matters, it agrees with the other vitriols. It does even more: if given to eat or drink with water, it kills the worms that grow in the belly due to illness and causes them to be expelled. Furthermore, it is very helpful against the poison that comes from mushrooms; moreover, if one mixes it with water and drops it into the nose, it purges the "humidities" <note>excess fluids or phlegm in medieval medicine</note> that are in the head. The two stars that follow the three in the right line on the western side of the figure of the Dragon <note>the constellation Draco</note> have power over this stone, and from them it receives its virtue. When these two are in the middle of the sky, this stone will show its works most completely.

## Regarding the stone named Harminica. (44.)

Of the twelfth degree of the sign of Virgo is the stone they call Harminica. This is found in the land they call Zulunia. Its mine is at the foot of a mountain named Nacavie in a very deep cave, in which there is a square pool; in the middle of that pool is a hole from which green water flows. In the middle of that hole, these stones are found fixed, and they cannot be removed without great effort in digging them out. When they are removed, they are first yellow and later turn black. Some are found large and others small and of diverse forms, but most of them are round.

They are strong stones, hard to break, and heavy, and they shine somewhat on the surface, though the sight does not pass through them <note>they are opaque</note>. By nature, they are cold and dry. If this stone is placed upon an eye that suffers pain, it removes and heals it. If the powder from polishing it is put into an eye suffering from the illness called ophthalmia <term>obtalmia: a general term for severe eye inflammation or infection</term>, it heals it. If they grind it and mix it with water and anoint the body of a person with dropsy <term>hidrópico: a person suffering from edema or fluid swelling</term>, it brings great benefit; and if used over time, it heals them, provided the illness is of a "hot" nature. The leading star of the three at the bottom of the "Jar" <note>likely the constellation Crater</note>, which are also in the triangular figure of the Water Snake <note>the constellation Hydra</note>, has power over this stone, and from it the stone receives its strength and virtue. When it is in the middle of the sky, this stone shows its works most manifestily.

## Regarding the stone named Zulucandria. (44.)

Of the thirteenth degree of the sign of Virgo is the stone they call Zulucandria, which means "drawer of wood." By nature, it is cold and dry in the third degree. It is strong and hard to break, and rough to the touch; when broken, this same roughness is found inside. It is green in color, tending slightly toward purple, and resembles the color of blue. It has the property of attracting all kinds of wood <note>original: "fustes"</note>, just as we said other magnets <note>lodestones</note> attract the things over which they have power. However, this one does not attract wood except from nearby; yet it attracts bodies larger than itself. After it has drawn them, they stick so strongly to it that they cannot be detached except with great force by breaking them or burning them with fire. If any wood enters a man’s body—such as a splinter, or the shaft of an arrow or spear—and the stone is placed over it, it draws and pulls it out from the place where it lies embedded. If this stone is placed upon timber and pressed with the

<column-break/>

hand, it enters into it with great force, just like a nail when struck with a hammer. This stone is found on the shores of the Red Sea <note>original: "mar Bermeya"</note>, for the waves cast them out; and there they are found. It has such virtue that if they grind it and mix it with oil and anoint a fracture of the penis with it, it heals. The northern star of the three on the left side of the figure of Virgo, which they call *Alaabor* <note>this name usually refers to Sirius, but here describes a star in or near Virgo</note>, has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its strength and virtue. When it is in the ascendant, this stone shows its works most manifestily.

## Regarding the stone they call Maihutiz. (44 verso.)

Of the fourteenth degree of the sign of Virgo is the stone they call Maihutiz. In this stone, there is a leaf-like pattern like that of a vine, with branches and leaves formed by its nature. It is a soft stone of a black color, though not excessively so. It is found in the land of Egypt in the western parts, in mines that are very deep underground. By nature, it is cold and dry, though it possesses more dryness than coldness. It has such virtue that if it is ground very well and then placed upon ringworm <note>original: "tinna"; a fungal scalp infection</note>, it heals it; it also does the same for very deep wounds and for split fingernails. The second star of the four that are in a line on the side of Virgo has power over this stone, and from it the stone receives its strength and virtue. When it is in the middle of the sky, it shows its works most perfectly.

## Regarding the stone named Axufaraquid. (44 verso.)

Of the fifteenth degree of the sign of Virgo is the stone they call Axufaraquid. It is a stone hard to break, smooth, porous, and light in weight. It is found in the western lands at the bottom of a river that flows there. It has such virtue that if it is anointed with warm goat's blood, it dissolves and mixes with it. If that blood is mixed with myrrh and honey and used to anoint the tongue of one whose speech is hindered by illness, it immediately removes that impediment and the person speaks clearly. If the breasts of women are anointed with it, their milk will increase greatly. It also does another thing: it heals the illness that occurs in the veins of the eyes. By nature, it is cold and dry, yet its virtues are contrary to its nature; this is one of the great marvels found among the virtues that things possess naturally. The star on the right side of the belt of the figure of Virgo has power over this stone, and from it the stone receives its strength and virtue. When it is in the middle of the sky, this stone shows its works most manifestily.

## Regarding the stone they call Marmunietiz. (45.)

Of the sixteenth degree of the sign of Virgo is the stone they call Marmunietiz. By nature, it is cold and dry, and of a subtle substance. It is very dark in color and easy to break, so much so that it breaks when rubbed between the fingers. This stone is found on the island called Veyen, and also in the western lands; it is found in both places because it is a mineral stone. It has the property that when placed in fire, it melts and flows, but not in the manner of other metals; for this turns into water, and when removed from the fire, it never solidifies again unless cold water is poured over it. Then it becomes a hard stone, stronger than at first, and heavier; the longer it stays in water, the harder it becomes. This stone, when turned to water over the fire and used to anoint the face of a person with spots <note>likely referring to skin discolorations or vitiligo</note>, removes those marks, as well as the cracks that form in the palms and feet. If mixed with beaten egg and used to anoint a wound or a cut, it causes it to join and heal so that no scar appears; however, this must be applied while the blood is still flowing before it stops, for afterward, though it may work, it does not do so as well or as quickly. The star in the Crow's beak <note>the constellation Corvus</note>, which is associated with the Water Snake, has power over this...

### Regarding the stone named Molubedeneda. (45.)

Of the seventeenth degree of the sign of Virgo is the stone they call *Molubedeneda* <note>original: "Molubedeneda"; likely Molybdaina, a lead-related mineral such as galena or litharge</note>. Its color is gray leaning toward red; but if it is boiled in oil, it becomes white. Its mine is in the land they call Zaritez, and it also grows in another land they call Coroz; the best among them is that which does not weigh much, nor does it resemble lead dross <note>original: "escoria del plomo"</note> in color. Its nature is cold and dry, and it has within it some power to wash things. It is not hard, but rather breaks easily and is ground quickly; and when it is thus ground and mixed with oil, it dissolves entirely so that nothing remains of it except a little at the bottom like sand. When they grind that sand, they make an oil from it for wounds when they want the venom to be drawn out quickly and for the flesh to grow back in them. By this nature, it cleans wounds of the filth within them and heals them quickly. Two stars—one in the breast of the Raven <note>the constellation Corvus</note>, and the other in the front of its left wing—both have power over this stone and from them it receives its strength and virtue. And when they are in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works more clearly.

### Regarding the stone of lead. (45 verso.)

Of the eighteenth degree of the sign of Virgo is the stone they call *Poleo* <note>original: "del Poleo"; likely a variety of lead ore or galena</note>. Its nature is cold and dry in the fourth degree, and its color is gray leaning toward green, spotted with yellow and black drops. It is a dark stone and very difficult to break. It is found on the shores of the Sea of Alcuzun <note>The Red Sea</note>. These are large stones from which they make vessels and bowls; however, they are bad for eating from, for they cause one to fall ill with melancholy <term>Melancholy: one of the four humors, associated with black bile, believed to cause sadness or depression</term>. But it is beneficial for storing any fragrant thing within them, as the scent is not damaged by time nor lost; rather, it grows ever stronger within it. If this stone is placed in breast milk, it dissolves quickly; but if that milk is boiled until it is consumed, the stone refines itself and hardens. However, if that milk is later mixed with water and used to wash the head, it removes dandruff <note>original: "forfola"</note> and heals the *forciella*, which is another illness that splits the hair. The third star of the four in the left side of Virgo has power over this stone and from it receives its virtue. And if one works with this stone when that star is in the ascendant <term>Ascendant: the sign or degree rising on the eastern horizon at a specific time</term>, it will show its works more clearly.

### Regarding the stone that pulls nails. (45 verso.)

Of the nineteenth degree of the sign of Virgo is the stone that pulls the nails <note>meaning fingernails or claws</note>. Its nature is cold and dry. This is counted as one of the "pulling" stones that they call magnets <note>original: "Magnetes"</note>. Its mine is found on the island called Zarratiz near that sea, and they find it on the surface of the earth. Some are large and others small. Its color is mostly white, but the gaze does not pass through to the other side <note>it is opaque</note>. It is very smooth to the touch and strong and hard to break, so that it cannot be broken except with great labor; even diamond, which is harder than all other stones, cannot break this one without great effort. However, if it is placed in the blood of a virgin woman, it breaks and becomes like sand.

And by burning it, you calcine <term>Calcine: to reduce a mineral to powder or ash by heat</term> it; and if water is poured over it after it is made into lime, it burns like the other magnets mentioned, and even more strongly. Its virtue is such that if it is carried over nails lying on the ground, it pulls them and gathers them well, just as other magnets pull the bodies over which they have power. And if it is carried over the nails of a man, it causes them to split and twist, and blood and flesh to come from between them; if the stone is large, it pulls them out by force. If this stone is broken with iron, it does not lose its virtue, but if it is broken with diamond, it loses it. The last star of the two in the left wing of the Raven <note>Corvus</note> has power over this stone and from it receives its virtue. And therefore when

<column-break/>

it is in mid-heaven, this stone will show its works more clearly.

### Regarding the stone named Marmor. (46.)

Of the twentieth degree of the sign of Virgo is the stone they call *Marmor* <note>Marble</note>. This is the one we mentioned when we named the Bezoar <note>original: "Bezahar"; an organic stone found in the guts of animals, prized as an antidote</note>, which it resembles; but it has nothing to do with it in strength or virtue, for this one is cold and dry and the other is not. Such marble as this is called *Faraztaz* in Greek <note>original: "Faraztaz"; possibly a corruption of a Greek term for a specific marble or gypsum</note>, and much of it is found in the mines of the *Aliaza* <note>vitriol mines</note> that we mentioned previously mixed with it; it is also found in the Promised Land <note>Palestine</note> and in Damascus. The best of these marbles is that which has a white color and appears with green, yellow, and red lines. When it is burned and mixed with sal ammoniac <term>Sal ammoniac: ammonium chloride, used in medieval alchemy and medicine</term> and they are ground together, and the powder is rubbed on teeth that are yellow or black, it turns them white and tightens the gums. Furthermore, grinding this burned stone and placing its powder upon fire burns is of great benefit. If a little is given to drink to one who has a great urge to move their bowels <note>diarrhea</note>, and they use it often, it stops it by tightening the mouth of the stomach. If they grind this stone and mix it with wax and oil, it helps with pain of the fundament <note>the anus or rectum</note>. The star at the end of the Raven's foot <note>Corvus</note>, which shares a place with the Hydra <note>original: "Idro"; the water-snake constellation</note>, has power over this stone and from it receives its strength and virtue. And when it is in the ascendant, this stone shows its works more clearly.

### Regarding the stone they call Abcatritaz. (46.)

Of the twenty-first degree of the sign of Virgo is the stone they call *Abcatritaz*. It is cold and dry in nature and is found frequently in the land of Egypt, on the banks of the Nile, buried in the sand. They say that the crocodiles <note>original: "cocatrices"</note> in that river bring this stone out while cleaning the places where they lie; it has such virtue that no animal that has it nearby can sleep. It resembles the diamond in color, but these are found larger than diamonds. It is soft to the touch and easy to break. If it is placed in the milk of a female dog, it turns into its substance. If that milk is given to drink to one who has pain in the belly or intestines, they are healed immediately. If they use it to wash the head, it removes gray hairs and prevents them from growing. The middle star of the three in the leg of "He who Shouts" <note>original: "el que da voces"; the constellation Boötes</note> has power over this stone and from it receives its strength and virtue. And when it is in mid-heaven, this stone will have more power and more strength in all its actions.

### Regarding the stone they call Galetaciz. (46 verso.)

Of the twenty-second degree of the sign of Virgo is the stone they call *Galetaciz*. It is red in color, of a weak redness, so that it resembles the water that comes out of meat when salt is cast upon it. It is a strong stone and hard to break, so that nothing can mark it except diamond or red copper. It is dark, but when polished, it receives some clarity. Some are large and others small, but those most often found resemble an egg that is a little longer than usual. Its nature is cold and dry, and it is found in the Promised Land in a place called Galequid, from which the stone takes its name. It has such virtue that whoever carries it with them is safe from having an abscess <note>original: "postema"</note> in the brain. Grinding this stone with copper produces a medicine for the head and the heart. The last star of the four on the rear side of the figure of Virgo has power over this stone and from it receives its strength and virtue. And when it is in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works more clearly.

### Regarding the stone named Quetmec. (46 verso.)

### Regarding the stone that draws vinegar. (47.)

Of the twenty-fourth degree of the sign of Virgo is the stone that draws vinegar. And this is found in the land called Azeneh on a hill that is near the sour lagoon. And the water of this lagoon is contrary to all others; for it dries up in the cold time of winter and fills up in the other season when there is great heat. Its nature is cold and dry and of open pores, and rough to the touch, light in weight, and easy to break. Its taste is sour; and its color is red dotted with white spots, and some of them have lines instead of spots. Some are found large and some small. And its virtue, from which it receives its name, is such that if they throw it into a vessel in which there is vinegar, it consumes it according to its own size; and as it takes it in, it grows that much more in weight; and by this they understand how much it has received. And that which it draws in cannot be taken out of it unless it is first thrown into oil; but after it is thrown in, the vinegar it had received immediately comes out of it, and once separated from the oil, it remains much more sour than it was before it was mixed with the stone. And if it is put into wine, it becomes vinegar; and if into vinegar, it becomes marvelously strong; and if they make vessels from it and put any of these liquors we have mentioned into them, it does the same. And when they burn it, it becomes lime, and it retains fire within itself that burns just like other magnets. And if they grind it and mix it with the medicines made for the itch <note>original: "sarna"; scabies or similar skin irritations</note> it is of great benefit. And when people wash with it in the bath, it cleanses the body of all impurities and heals the disease they call Morphea <note>original: "Morfea"; a skin condition characterized by discolored patches, sometimes associated with leprosy in medieval texts</note>. And the front star of the two that are in the belt of the Shouter <note>Boötes</note> has power over this stone and from it receives its strength and virtue. And when it is in the ascendant <term>Ascendant: the sign or degree rising on the eastern horizon</term> this stone shows its works most manifestly.

### Regarding the stone named Nacarat. (47.)

Of the twenty-fifth degree of the sign of Virgo is the stone they call *Nacarat*. Its nature is cold and dry in the first degree. And its color is like that of iron, which is mixed with yellow and red; but there are some in which one color appears more, and some in which the other does. It shines within itself and resembles *Aliaza* <note>an unidentified stone or mineral mentioned in other medieval lapidaries</note> in color and qualities, and some thought it was the same: but he who pays close attention finds that it has nothing to do with it; though in some virtues it resembles it. Because this stone by its nature is detested like the other, and those who know its virtue and its property do not want to come near it, nor carry it with them. This is found in the land of Liement and its mines are found very far from inhabited areas in dangerous places for lack of water and also because of evil and poisonous animals that breed there; and therefore only poor and needy men venture to extract them, doing so out of great greed to earn something. And its malice is so great that he who carries it with him has strife with men and is hated by them. And if they make bowls or vessels of it, and eat or drink from them, it does the same; but it has other good things within it: for he who carries it with him is helped to heal from great fevers. And also, drinking of it heals the disease they call jaundice <note>original: "itericia"</note>, and the other they call sciatica, which comes from the shrinking of the nerve in the leg. And the star that is in the right hip below the belt of the figure of Virgo has power over this stone, and from it receives its strength and vir-
