### Regarding the stone named Ezbenecen. (47 verso.)

Of the twenty-sixth degree of the sign of Virgo is the stone they call *Ezbenecen*. And the best mine of this is in the land of Barca <note>in modern-day Libya</note>; but there is another mine of it in the land of Virgia; but it is not good. It is a precious stone because of the clarity it has within it, and they find large ones and other small ones; and the masters who know how to work them make of them whatever form they wish; but nevertheless it is strong and hard to break and no other body takes to it <note>marks it</note> except iron or diamond. Its color is yellow tending somewhat toward red, and its nature is cold and dry. And they call it in the land of Barca the "vinous stone," because it has the color of a very beautiful red wine. But in the land of Virgia they call it *Alharcon*. And they find no other virtue in this stone except its beauty alone. And the last star of the two that are in the belt of the Shouter <note>Boötes</note> has power over this stone and from it receives its virtue. And when it is in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works most manifestly.

### Regarding the stone they call Zumidum. (48.)

Of the twenty-seventh degree of the sign of Virgo is the stone they call *Zumidum*. Its color is black like ash. It is very heavy and hard to break; and when they break it, they find inside the appearance of hairs and twigs. Its nature is cold and dry and rough to the touch. And the mines of it are found on the shores of the sea of India and China <note>original: "Cin"</note>. It is a dark stone without light. And if they wash it as they wash the other stones used to heal wounds, this stone does so greatly and closes them. This stone has great power to retain moisture so that it does not flow, and to join divided things, and for this reason they make *Alcohol* <note>original: "Alcohol"; here referring to a fine medicinal powder or kohl for the eyes</note> from it, to heal the white spot of the eye which becomes a blemish, and also the pupil that tries to protrude because of great pain. And the northern star of the front line that is in the left leg of the figure of Virgo has power over this stone and from it receives its virtue. And when it is in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works most manifestly.

### Regarding the stone named Tifurenez. (48.)

Of the twenty-eighth degree of the sign of Virgo is the stone they call *Tifurenez*. This is found often in the land of China on the shore of the sea. It is porous and so light in weight that it seems it could hold itself in the air; but nevertheless it is strong and hard to break, and it is somewhat clear; and its color is like saffron, and for this reason some call it the "saffron stone." And this is also found in the land of Spain on the shores of the sea that faces the east. Its nature is cold and dry in the third degree. And if they grind it and give it to someone to drink, it removes moisture from the stomach, and prevents vomiting, and gives the power to retain, both in terms of digestion and flux <note>original: "menazon"; diarrhea or dysentery</note>. And it does even more; for he who carries it in his mouth prevents excessive spitting, and the drool that flows from the mouth while sleeping, and also in children when they are small. And the southern star that is in the front line of the quadrant that is in the left leg of the figure of Virgo has power over this stone, and from it receives its virtue. And when it is in the ascendant, this stone shows its works more completely.

This is found in a river they call Aztuz, which is in the land of France. And they also find it on the shore of the western sea in the land they call Baltar in the western part of Spain. And most of those they find are near the mountain palms. In color it resembles the yellow zircon <note>original: "yargonca"</note>; and there are others...

### PROLOGUE (49 verso.)

The thirty types of stones of the sign of Virgo are finished; wherefore it is necessary that he who wishes to work by this should pay heed to the state of this planet <note>Likely referring to the ruling planet or the Moon's influence as it moves through the sign</note> as we said of the others in each sign. And he who does this will reach what he desires of this knowledge.

### Regarding the stone they call Tebelcuz. (49 verso.)

Of the first degree of the sign of Libra is the stone they call Tebelcuz. This is light and of open pores, and when a man holds it in his hand, it seems to him that wind enters through it. In color it is gray, but it tends somewhat toward green. In the Eastern Sea they find it in this manner: when there is a great storm in it, the waves lift this stone because of the lightness it has in itself, and when they break on the shore, they cast it onto the sand. And if at that time they cannot cast it out, as soon as the storm calms, it returns to the bottom of the water as before. By nature it is hot and moist. And its virtue is such that whoever has ten grains of barley <note>original: "dordio"; a medieval unit of weight</note> or more of it hanging from his arm cannot be defeated in deeds of arms; but on the other hand, it is a deadly poison; for if they give it to anyone to drink, it wounds the kidneys and makes the urine run with blood and venom, so that if they do not quickly help him with something for this, there is no remedy but death. And the star that is in the belt on the right side of the Shouter <note>original: "el que da voces"; referring to the constellation Boötes</note> has power over this stone, and from it receives strength and virtue. And when it is in the ascendant, this stone shows its works most manifestly.

### Regarding the stone named Sea Foam. (49 verso.)

Of the second degree of the sign of Libra is the stone they call sea foam, and of these there are five types. The first they call Sponya; the second Algamarina; the third Ferfide; which means

And the color it has inside is black and very dark, and it is heavy. And they find it in a river they call Toriz <note>likely the Zayandeh River</note> that runs through the land of Isfahan <note>original: "Espahen"; a city in Iran</note>, and not in mines; but there are certain trees they call *populus* <note>Poplar trees</note> in Latin that have black leaves and likewise the wood: and from those trees flows a moisture <note>Resin or sap</note> that falls into that river from which this stone is made under the water; and if they grind it and knead it with any oil, it becomes soft, just like wax, and it burns in that same way. ### Regarding the stone that is made from the foam of the sea. (50.)

Of the fourth degree of the sign of Libra is the stone that is made from the foam of the sea, which is named Farfiri. This stone is entirely perforated and formed like tiny worms. Its color is red mixed with brown; and from this it took its name <note>original: "Farfiri"; likely a reference to porphyry-colored sea-growths or coral</note>; but in Greek they call it Milicion <note>original: "Milicion"; potentially related to 'militis' or a specific mineral foam</note>. It is found in the sea of the land they call Varnitaz. By nature it is hot and moist, and of a finer substance than the other we mentioned, and lighter in weight. And it has such virtue that if they give it to drink to one who cannot pass urine, he is healed: and it also aids the affliction of the stone <note>Likely kidney or bladder stones</note> and the abscess that forms in the bladder; and ringworm if they anoint it with this. But when it is burned, it has greater power in each of these things. And the following star of the two that are in the right leg of Centaurus <note>original: "Cantoriz"; the constellation Centaurus</note> has power in this stone and from it receives its force and virtue. And therefore when it is in mid-heaven it shows its works most manifesty.

### Regarding the stone named Lavenna. (50 verso.)

Of the fifth degree of the sign of Libra is the stone they call Lavenna; and this is the fourth kind of sponge we mentioned. In form it resembles dirty wool, and it smells much like it, and from this it takes its name. It is perforated like the others we mentioned, and lighter than any of them. It is strong and hard to break; and they call it Guyrunion in Chaldean <note>A Semitic language used in ancient Mesopotamia</note>. This stone is found on the shore of the sea, and especially on the island called Baritoria. By nature it is hot and moist, and the heat of this one is greater than any of the others we mentioned; but the moisture is not as great as theirs: and for this reason it has the power to penetrate bodies, and it cleanses much and peels the skin. And its virtue is such that if they grind it and mix it with water and anoint the breasts of a woman where there is an abscess, they are healed. And the star that is in the right shoulder of the figure of the one who has his knees bent <note>The constellation Hercules, often called "The Kneeler" in medieval astronomy</note> has power in this stone and from it receives its force and virtue. And when it is in mid-heaven this stone shows its works most manifestly.

### Regarding the stone they call Foguenna. (50 verso.)

Of the sixth degree of the sign of Libra is the stone they call Foguenna and this is the fifth kind of sponge we mentioned among those that are mostly sea foam. And it is hot and moist by nature. And its form is like a mushroom <note>original: "fongo"</note>; and from this it has its name. It has no smell and is smooth on the outside: but when they break it, they find it rough inside. It is not as porous as the others and therefore it is heavier. It is green in color and ashen on top: but he who breaks it finds the interior a more natural green than the exterior. And it is found on the shore of the sea on an island they call Zafunicon, and the people of that land call it Aluzáhne. It is hotter than all the others that have been mentioned; and he who puts it on his tongue feels a sharp, burning taste. And if they grind it and anoint hair with it, it burns it away; but it is good for healing the sickness they call morphoea <note>A skin condition involving localized patches of hardened skin</note>; and the other that peels the skin. And the two stars—the middle and the last of the three that are in the tail <note>original: "Alcabar"; from the Arabic 'al-dhayl', referring to the hindquarters or tail</note> of the one who is half horse and half man—have power in this stone and from it receive its virtue. And when it is in the ascendant <term>Ascendant: the sign or degree rising on the eastern horizon</term> this stone shows its works most completely.

### Regarding the stone of the fish. (51.)

Of the seventh degree of the sign of Libra is the stone they call "of the fish." This they find on the island called Zulunica on the shore of the

<column-break/>

sea in some very deep mines. Of these they find large ones and others small. It is light in weight and perforated, and rough to the touch, and strong, and hard to break; but when they break it they find it smooth inside. And the color that appears on the outside is like that of sea water, and breaking it they find it inside of a yellow color that draws somewhat toward red. By nature it is hot and moist; and they find it on the island they call Aquineniz, which means as much as "stone of the fish": and this is because it smells like fresh fish, as when it begins to spoil. And its virtue is such that if they throw it in a place where there are fish, they all gather there. And if ground they give of it to a leper <note>original: "gafo"; referring to someone afflicted with leprosy or a similar debilitating skin disease</note> the weight of three drachmas, it heals him; and if they anoint him with it in the bath it does the same. And the two stars—the one in the left shoulder, and the other under the knee of the left leg of the one who is half man and half horse—both have power in this stone and from them it receives its virtue. And when they are in the ascendant this stone shows its works most completely.

### Regarding the stone they call Elbehta. (51.)

Of the eighth degree of the sign of Libra is the stone they call Elbehta, which means "congealment" <note>original: "Elbehta"; from the Arabic 'al-bahta', a legendary stone said to cause bewilderment or paralysis</note>. This is hot and moist by nature; and its color resembles golden marcasite; but this is clearer and brighter. And they find it in the Western Sea <note>The Atlantic Ocean</note> in the places where there is great darkness when there is a great storm; for then the waves cast these stones out to the edge of the water onto the sand. Of these they find large ones and others small. And the virtue from which it receives its name is this: that when anyone sees it, he opens his mouth and eyes and remains thus dazed, staring at it, as if he were frozen by the numbness of cold, and he can never turn his eyes from it until they hang it before him <note>likely meaning move it out of sight</note> or cover it with something. And something else happens with it: in that land where they find it there are birds as large as turtledoves and they are red in color, and bright, and have long green beaks, and they call them Zulumen in Chaldean, and the men of that land eat them; and when one of these perches upon that stone, it makes it lose its virtue. And if they put this stone in human blood it dissolves and mixes with it; and if afterwards they put it to the fire the blood is consumed, and the stone remains separated from it; but it receives a great softening thereby: but if afterwards they put it in sour citron juice it becomes hard as it was at first. And they find no other virtue in this stone if not this. And even in this they cannot help themselves with it if they do not carry it covered. And the two stars—the one in the left shoulder and the other under the knee of the left leg of the one who is half man and half horse—have power in this stone and from them it receives its force and virtue. And when they are in the ascendant this stone shows its works most manifestly.

### Regarding the stone named Militaz. (51 verso.)

Of the ninth degree of the sign of Libra is the stone they call Militaz. It is a strong and hard stone that no other body can mark except diamond alone, nor does fire harm it. This is found in the land of India in mines that are there upon the surface; for not in caves, nor in any other deep place. It is a stone of great brilliance and resembles fine gold in color. Of these they find large ones and small ones, and of diverse forms. By nature it is hot and moist. And its virtue is such that flies and all evil reptiles flee before it; and the wise men even said more: that demons stay away from the one who carries it with him, and no work of necromancy nor any spells they might cast do him harm. And the star that is at the end of the hand of the beast they call Centaurus has power in this stone and from it receives its force and virtue. And when it is in the ascendant this stone shows its works most manifestly.

# OF THE SIGN [OF LIBRA]

### Regarding the split stone. (51 verso.)

Of the 10th degree of the sign of Libra is the split stone. This is found in the land they call Lebria <note>original: "Lebria"; likely referring to Libya or a specific region in North Africa</note>. Its color is that of saffron and even more deeply tinted. It is split, and for this reason, it is easy to break and very light in weight; in its characteristics, it entirely resembles ammoniac <note>original: "armoniaco"; gum ammoniac, a medicinal resin</note>; however, this stone is hot and moist in the third degree. It has such virtue that if it is ground and mixed with breast milk and placed in the eyes, it heals deep sores that form within them and closes them; it also removes the fatty growths <term>Grosura: fatty deposits or swelling</term> that form in the eye sockets. And if it is given as a drink to one who has an abscess in the liver, they are healed. The two stars that are in Centaurus <note>original: "Cantoriz"; the constellation Centaurus</note>, one in the right shoulder and the other in the horse’s spine, have the most power over this stone, and from them, it receives its strength and virtue. And when they are in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works most manifesty.

### Regarding the Tanners' stone. (52.)

Of the 11th degree of the sign of Libra is the stone of the tanners, which they call "movable" for this reason: if it is placed in still water, it stays on the surface and does not move; but if it is later placed in running water, it goes to the bottom. It is found on the island they call Argenica more than in any other place, on the seashore upon the face of the earth, for it is not found in mines; and although it has open pores within it, it is nevertheless heavy. Its color is like that of a citron; some are found large and others small. By nature, it is hot and moist. Tanners use it in the tanning of hides; furthermore, when ground and cast into the throat of one whose uvula <note>original: "huviella"; the fleshy piece hanging at the back of the throat</note> has fallen, it heals them immediately. And if it is given as a drink to one who has an abscess in the stomach, it causes them to recover quickly. The northern star of the two that are in the right knee of "the one who stays on his knee" <note>original: "el que tiene ficada la rodiella"; the constellation Hercules</note> has power over this stone, and from it, it receives its strength and virtue. And when it is in the ascendant, this stone shows its works most manifestly.

### Regarding the Serpent stone. (52.)

Of the 12th degree of the sign of Libra is the Serpent stone; in Chaldean, they call it *Bezaquid*, which means "remover of noise." These are found in gold mines where fine emeralds are also found. They are resplendent, and their color is ash-grey dappled with white spots. It is a stone much prized by the people of that land; they find both large and small specimens. Neither fire nor iron can harm it. By nature, it is hot and moist. Its virtue is such that whoever carries it with them will be safe from falling ill with the "ringing disease" <note>original: "roido que se face en la cabeza"; likely tinnitus or a buzzing in the head</note> that occurs in the head; and having it before them, they will be cured by it. If it is placed upon the wound of a viper, it heals it; and it does the same if it is ground and given as a drink. The two stars that follow the bright one of the figure called Alphecca <note>original: "Elfeca"; Alpha Coronae Borealis in the Northern Crown</note>, which are both in the Northern Crown—one of them pulling further north than the other—these both have power over this stone and from them it receives its virtue. And when they are in the ascendant, this stone shows its works most completely.

### Regarding the stone named Zfedarona. (52 verso.)

Of the 13th degree of the sign of Libra is the stone they call *Zfedarona*. This is found in the land of China <note>original: "Cin"</note> mixed with other stones containing copper <note>original: "arambre"</note>. It is hard and difficult to break, and by nature hot and moist. It is saffron-colored dappled with black spots; however, in some of them, lines are found instead of spots. These are large stones when they are taken from the mine, but later they work them and fashion them into whatever form they wish. It has such virtue that if they melt silver with an equal amount of copper, and then separate the copper to its side and the silver to its own, and—being both separated from one another—they melt the silver again by itself and mix into it this ground stone, and they fashion from

<column-break/>

that silver a hammer and an anvil, and they strike with that hammer upon it in a place where there are birds, each one will stay still in its place and not move; because of this, they can be taken by hand. No other virtue is found for this stone except this one. The leading star of the three that are in the right side of Centaurus has power over this stone and from it receives its virtue. And when it is in mid-heaven, it will show its works most manifestly.

### Regarding the stone called Lavich. (52 verso.)

Of the 14th degree of the sign of Libra is the stone they call *Lavich*. By nature, it is hot and moist, and it is found in caves and pits that are within the sea near the island they call *Cabroz*, which is to say Cyprus. It is found in the copper mines that are on that island. Its color is very red—so much so that it verges on black. It is dark and without luster, light in weight, and easy to break, for it is porous. It has such virtue that if it is ground and placed upon a wound that has "overgrown flesh" <term>Carne sobrecrecida: proud flesh or granulation tissue</term>, it removes it; and if it is ground and washed like other stones, it has greater strength in this work. The fourth star in the bright part of the Northern Crown has power over this stone and from it receives its virtue. And when it is in mid-heaven, it shows its works most completely.

### Regarding the stone of the pitch. (53.)

Of the 15th degree of the sign of Libra is the stone they call "of the pitch." It is very black and shiny, like a mirror, though sight does not pass through it. It is strong and hard to break, such that it cannot be broken except with great effort. It is found in the lands of the West more than in any other place. It is smooth to the touch, and it seems that by day a dust comes from it that resembles smoke, yet it has no manifest smell, nor does this appear at night. It has such virtue that if it is placed upon a thousand weights of pitch <note>original: "pez"; tar or resin</note>, it causes it to boil by its own property, just as if it were over a fire. And this stone, having been placed in the pitch, if it is then put into hot water, it causes the water to flee to the right and to the left; and it shows this same virtue in springs of cold water. By nature, it is hot and moist; and it does another very marvelous thing: if pearls <note>original: "aliofar"</note> that are damaged in color or are not perfectly round are placed in the pitch where this stone was, it corrects them and makes them very round; and besides all this, it is good to put into medicines intended to correct the liver. The bright star in the Northern Crown called Alphecca has power over this stone and from it receives its strength and virtue. And when it is in the ascendant, it shows its works most manifestly.

### Regarding the stone that appears in the sea when Venus sets. (53.)

Of the 16th degree of the sign of Libra is the stone that appears in the sea when Venus sets, and hides when she rises. This is found in the "Gloomy Sea" <note>original: "mar tenebrosa"; likely the Atlantic Ocean</note> where the other stones are found that show the virtue of the planets. It is found in that land on the eastern shore of the sea. Its color is a very deep yellow dappled with violet spots. It is strong and hard to break, such that no other body breaks it except gold alone. It is of a thick substance and very heavy. It is very beautiful in color, clear and bright; the power of Venus appears in it opposite to the other stone we spoke of in the 15th degree of Taurus; for this one rises and floats upon the water from the time Venus sets until she rises, and it descends to the bottom from the time she rises until she sets. It always does this and shows its virtue even more manifestly, for when they take it out onto land, it darkens when Venus rises and brightens when she sets. It has such virtue that whoever carries it with them is safe from dying by drowning in water. It is always found in the shape of a pillar, but masters carve <note>catchword: "tayan"; they carve/cut</note> from it whatever form they wish. Furthermore, whoever puts it in the juice of...

### Regarding the stone called Indiana. (53 verso.)

Of the 17th degree of the sign of Libra is the stone they call Indiana. Its nature is hot and moist in the third degree. It is found in the land of Egypt more than in any other place, and likewise, on an island they call Yequiraz. It has the color of a jujube <note>original: "uvuba"; likely the fruit of the Ziziphus jujuba</note> when it is ripe; it is heavy, without luster, and easy to break, such that it breaks when squeezed between the fingers. In Greek, they call it *Abraitoz* <note>original: "Abraitoz"; possibly a corruption of a Greek mineral name</note>. It has such virtue that if it is given ground in a drink to a man who is stung by a scorpion, he is healed immediately; it also does the same for those who have hemorrhoids. It stops every kind of blood that flows from the opening of veins. If it is soaked in boiling wine, it hardens so much that it can be worked on a lathe, or with iron, to make vessels and bowls; and in he who uses these for drinking, those virtues we have mentioned appear more manifesty. The two stars—the one in the right shoulder of the man, and the other which is one of the two under the belly of the horse in the figure of Centaurus—have power over this stone, and from them it receives its strength and virtue. When these both are in the ascendant, this stone shows its works most manifesty.

### Regarding the Bloodstone. (53 verso.)

Of the 18th degree of the sign of Libra is the stone they call the Bloodstone. It has this name because of its virtue, for it draws out <note>original: "zuma"; to suck, soak up, or draw out</note> blood: so much so that if it is placed in water, it pulls out as much as it finds there; in such a way that it cannot be removed from the stone except by placing it in the sun or in fire: for then it comes out, and it loses neither the taste of blood nor its substance, but only the color. And if this stone is put into a vessel containing blood, it draws it out according to its size, and what remains it turns into the color of water. And although this stone and the other we mentioned are similar in color, there is a great distinction between them; for the other only draws blood from a dead animal, and this one draws it from both [the living and the dead]. No virtue is found in this stone for medicine or any other thing except that which we have said. it is always found in the shape of a nut, and it is strong and hard to break, for it breaks only with great effort; yet it is so light that it nearly floats between the surface and the bottom. The dark star that is on the northern side of the two called *Azubene* <note>original: "Azubene"; referring to the stars Zubeneschamali and Zubenelgenubi in the constellation Libra</note>, which are in the southern scale of the figure of Libra, has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its strength and virtue. When it is in the ascendant, this stone shows its works most completely.

### Regarding the stone called the fish of the lagoons. (54.)

Of the 19th degree of the sign of Libra is the stone called the fish of the lagoons. It has this name for this reason: because in the middle of an island they call Canhelin, there are some lagoons very far from the rivers in which many small fish grow; so small that the largest of them is not a palm’s length; and although they are alive, they have heads of stone; and they have another stone in the spine of which we shall speak later in its place in this book. But this one from the head is hot and moist, and among the stones of animals, it is counted as one of the most marvelous of all. If it is burned and ground, and the powder is cast upon sores, it removes the excess flesh <term>Carne sobeyana: proud flesh or overgrowth of tissue in a wound</term> from them and they heal quickly. The bright star of *Azubene* that is in the southern scale of Libra has power over this stone and from it receives its virtue. And when—

<column-break/>

—it is in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works most manifesty.

### Regarding the stone called Meimeniez. (54.)

Of the 20th degree of the sign of Libra is the stone called *Meimeniez* in Chaldean <note>original: "Meimeniez"; likely a transliteration from an Arabic or Syriac source</note>, which means "drawer of foam." This is a type of the magnets we have named which have the property of drawing things by force, and in which fire is enclosed, just as in them; so much so that it burns very fiercely when sprinkled with water. But what this stone burns cannot be extinguished by anything except wine mixed with honey. By nature, it is hot and moist in the fourth degree. It is light in weight and has open pores, and is smooth to the touch, so that it slips between the fingers when taken; yet it is strong and hard to break. When it is broken, it is found to be rough inside and of a clear green color; but on the outside it appears reddish, though not with such great clarity. Its virtue is such that he who carries it upon himself dissolves his sperm and it is made to flow in such a way that if it lasts long and he is not helped by some means, he may die from it—especially if they eat or drink it with something. It does even more: if after a man has lain with a woman and departed from her, they put a little of this stone in the genitals <note>original: "en la natura"; referring to the female reproductive tract</note>, it will draw out all the sperm so that nothing of it remains; and this is done by women who desire to fulfill their will with men without becoming pregnant. The southern star, which is among the first two that are in front of the four in the branch of the Vine <note>original: "ramo de la Vit"</note> held in the hand of the figure of Centaurus—it is in Centaurus—has power over this stone and from it receives its strength and virtue. And if they work with it when it is in the ascendant, this stone shows its works most manifesty.

### Regarding the stone called Marcasite. (54 verso.)

Of the 21st degree of the sign of Libra is the stone called Marcasite in Arabic, and in Greek, *Pandes*. This is of three kinds. The first they call *Aurea* (Golden) because it has the color of gold. The second, *Argentea* (Silvery), because it has the color of silver. And the third, *Cobrenna* (Coppery), because it is red like copper. This book speaks of each of these in its proper place; but first we shall speak of the one that resembles gold in color. It is a stone very well known to men, and they find it in many places. By nature, it is hot in the third degree and dry in the first. When it is burned, it calcines, and by grinding it, a powder is made; for this reason, it loses its moisture and increases in heat, and receives into itself the natural strength of sulfur, and then the wise may put it into the Great Work <note>original: "obra mayor"; a reference to the Alchemical process of creating the Philosopher's Stone</note>. If a little of it is thrown at the hour of melting into gold that has another body mixed within it, it separates it and the gold remains refined and clean. Likewise, it is good for cleaning the venom from sores and for healing fistulas in any place they may be, and for removing the film <note>original: "tela"; likely a cataract or pterygium</note> that forms in the eyes. And if, before it is burned and made into powder, it is hung upon a small child, it removes the fear that he has by his nature. The star that is in the mouth of the serpent they call *Alhave* in Arabic <note>original: "Alhave"; from al-Hawwa, referring to Ophiuchus, the Serpent Bearer</note>, which means "hunter of serpents," has power over this stone and from it receives its strength and virtue. When it is in mid-heaven, it shows greater strength in its works.

### Regarding the stone called Silver Marcasite. (54 verso.)

Of the 22nd degree of the sign of Libra is the stone called Silver Marcasite. This resembles silver in color and appearance and is hot and moist by nature. Its virtue is such that if it is put with iron that is "sweating" <note>original: "suado"; likely referring to molten or white-hot iron</note>, the fire ignites with it more than it did before, and it purges gold as we said before. It has the strength within itself to hold [moisture] until it is burned, and when it is burned, if one works with it, it curls the hair and strengthens the...

### Regarding the stone they call Copper Marcasite. (55.)

Of the 23rd degree of the sign of Libra is the stone they call Copper Marcasite, because it resembles copper in color and redness, and therefore when it is burned, there comes out of it a certain amount of copper that it has mixed within itself. And it purifies gold, as we said of the other magnets <note>The text likely refers to marcasites used in metallurgical flux or "aimantes" as a general term for mineral attractants</note> that have the power to purify. Furthermore, when mixed with iron, it burns well just like the silver variety. ### Regarding the stone found on Mount Sinai. (55.)

Of the 24th degree of the sign of Libra is the stone found on Mount Sinai. By nature, it is hot and moist and very hard to break or dissolve, in such a way that no other body can make a mark on it except for the diamond alone. It is green like the color of an emerald, but it is more brilliant than that, and of such great splendor that those who look at it cannot keep their eyes directly upon it, because the sight is startled by its clarity. It is found at the top of Mount Sinai in a very deep cave that is there, and its entrance is very narrow, long, and fearsome because it has many turnings; but those who exert themselves and dare to enter find it wide and luminous once they are inside, and from there they take these stones. And it has such virtue that whoever carries it with him has no fear nor is startled, whether he stays still or walks alone; and all who see him prize him greatly and honor him and fear him, and he finds within himself strength and comfort, and he is pleased to have humility and to be modest. And the northern star that is outside the head of the one who holds the serpent <note>The constellation Ophiuchus</note> has power over this stone, and from it, the stone receives its virtue and strength. And therefore, when it is in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works most completely.

### Regarding the stone named Secutarica. (55 verso.)

Of the 25th degree of the sign of Libra is the stone they call Secutarica, which means "maker of pregnancy"; for its virtue is such that the woman who carries it with her becomes pregnant the first time a man joins with her. It is found in the Promised Land, and also in the lands of the East. Its color is red like a very deep-dyed rose, and it shines so much that the sight passes through it. It is light in weight, and they find large ones and other small ones; but most of them are found in the shape of an egg, and it has a hole through its width. It is hot and moist by nature, and men love and prize it much for its beauty; but they find no other virtue in this stone except this one mentioned regarding pregnancy. And the star that is in the middle of Azubene on the southern part, which is in the hanger of the weight <note>The pivot or balance point</note> of the figure of Libra, has power over this stone and from it, the stone receives its virtue. And when it is in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works most completely.

### Regarding the Vinegar Stone. (55 verso.)

Of the 26th degree of the sign of Libra is the Vinegar Stone. Its color is yellow, and it draws somewhat toward green, but it is dark. It is porous and light in weight, and easy to break, and smooth to the

<column-break/>

touch on the outside. These stones are found on the island of Sardinia on the shore of the sea, and they find them in small shapes, so that the largest of them weighs no more than four drachmas. By nature, it is hot and moist in the third degree. And its virtue is such that it seems to loathe vinegar and all sour things; so much so that when they place it near them, it leaps and flees, distancing itself as much as it can from them. And if they grind it and mix it with another substance and pour vinegar over it, it separates itself. And if they give it ground to a man to drink, it heals coughs and shortness of breath, and also the spitting of blood or poison <note>likely pus</note> that comes from an abscess that forms in the side, or in the lung, and from every other illness a man may have in the chest, or in the passages of the lung, or in the other organs of breath; and if they mix it with some oil and anoint the aforementioned places where these illnesses appear, it does the same. And the star that is in the hind leg of the bear <note>Ursa Major</note> which is near the hand of Cantoriz <note>Centaurus</note> has power over this stone and from it, the stone receives its virtue. And when it is in the ascendant, this stone shows its works more.

### Regarding the stone named Marina. (56.)

Of the 27th degree of the sign of Libra is the stone they call Marina. This is found in the parts of the West on the shore of the sea, because the waves throw it out onto the sand. Its shape is like the whorls <note>original: "torteros"; the weights used on a spindle for spinning thread</note> that they put on the spindles with which they spin, and it is pierced in the middle. Some are large and others small, and on top, they are all made like grains. Their color is yellow and as if dusty on top, and they are strong and hard to break, and dense in color. By nature, they are hot and moist. And its virtue is such that whoever drinks the weight of half a drachma of it, it breaks the stone that forms in the bladder or in the kidney, and makes him expel it like fine sand. And if they put a little of this stone in meat when they set it to cook, it softens the bones in such a way that they can be eaten just like the meat, and it does the same to the spines of fish. And the southern star of the three that follow after the turn of the neck of the serpent held by the enchanter <note>Ophiuchus</note> has power over this stone and from it, the stone receives its strength and virtue. And when it is in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works most manifest.

### Regarding the stone they call Tarnicen. (56.)

Of the 28th degree of the sign of Libra is the stone named Tarnicen, which means "leech-puller." It is strong and hard to break, and of a brown color that draws somewhat toward red. And they always find it in the shape of a flask, and there appears within it the figure of a leech; and if they break it, they find the same in every piece. This stone is found on Mount Sinai at its foot in a cave that is not very deep. By nature, it is hot and moist, and its heat is stronger than its dryness. And its virtue is such that if they put it to the mouth of any animal that has a leech in its body or in its throat, it pulls it with such great force that it makes it come out and stick to the stone. And if ground and made into powder it is placed over flesh that has healed over a wound <note>likely referring to proud flesh or scars</note>, it removes it and cures it; and it does the same to warts. And also, it has great strength to retain moisture so that it does not flow and to join things that are separated. And for this reason, they make kohl <note>original: "alcohol"</note> from it to heal the white spot of the eye where a blemish forms, and also for the pupil that wants to protrude because of great pain. And the northern star of the front line which is in the left leg of the figure of Virgo has power over this stone and from it, the stone receives its virtue. And when it is in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works more.

## PROLOGUE.

### Regarding the degrees of the sign of Scorpio. (58.)

The thirty degrees of the sign of Libra have been fully described, and likewise the thirty kinds of stones that are within it. Therefore, it is necessary that whoever wishes to work with this knowledge should pay attention to the planet Venus and to the lord of the face <note>original: "sennor de la faz"; the planetary ruler of the decan (a 10-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign)</note>, so that both are well-received and in good state with the star with which he shall work; for then he shall achieve what he desires with the pleasure of God.

### Regarding the stone they call Alazrob. (58.)

Of the first degree of the sign of Scorpio is the stone they call Alazrob, and some call it Ubar. This is a kind of lead, the most base of all others, and it smells bad, and has in its nature a portion of very congealed earth; and likewise it has a portion of air, but very little. By nature it is cold and moist, and what shows that it has a portion of air in it is that it dissolves in the fire quickly with little heat, and if they place it in a moist place it grows in its weight; and for this reason it is very heavy. And if they make from it a mortar and pestle and grind moist things with it, each of them will rise greatly in its nature. And grinding in it the medicines that are for abscesses is of great benefit; and likewise for the diseases that occur in the reproductive organs. And there is even more: if they make a thin plate from it and bind it to a man over the virile member, it removes the pollutions <note>original: "opolicion"; referring to nocturnal emissions</note> that happen at night while sleeping. And the two stars—the one in the belly and the other in the leg of the bear in the figure of Cantoriz <note>original: "Cantoriz"; the constellation Centaurus</note>—have power over this stone and from it it receives its strength and virtue. And when these both are in the ascendant, this stone shows its works most manifest.

They are strong and hard to break and light in weight, and rough to the touch, and of a white color that tends somewhat toward yellow.

By nature it is hot and moist in the third degree. And it has such virtue that if they grind it and give three drachms weight of it to drink, it breaks the stone that forms in the kidneys <note>original: "renes"</note> and heals them; and it does yet another thing: if they knead it with goat urine and place it in an earthen vessel with a narrow mouth and bury it in manure and leave it there for thirty days in the summer time, they will find at the end of this term an animal that resembles a lizard in shape, but is of a red color; and if they burn it and make powders, and give some to someone to drink, it will kill them without any sickness or sign appearing in them; and it does the same if they smell it: and against this poison <note>original: "tosico"</note> nothing that man can do is of any avail. And the star that is at the end of the hind foot that is near the hand of Cantoriz has power over this stone and from it receives its strength and virtue. And when it is in the midheaven it shows its works most completely.

### Regarding the stone they call Taccie. (58.)

Of the second degree of the sign of Scorpio is the stone they call Taccie, which means in Chaldean <note>original: "caldeo"; referring to the Aramaic or Syriac language</note> "engendered of water"; because in the land of the Greeks <note>original: "Argios"; likely referring to Argos or Greece generally</note> near the town they call Arraca <note>Raqqa in modern Syria</note> there is a spring of very sweet and savory water that descends from a mountain and falls at the bottom of it into a very wide lagoon, and in the winter it freezes, and when it dissolves in summer because of the heat, there remain some congealed pieces made like stone; and this happens every year. They are stones that are strong, and hard, and heavy, and clear, and of a white color, just like congealed water; but it is a stone that never dissolves and therefore is counted among the earthy stones. By nature it is cold and moist. And its virtue is such that if they grind it with something and anoint the palm of whomsoever they wish, he will be able to hold fire in it and will not be burned nor feel it. And likewise by anointing the forehead and the temples of one who has a fever that comes from heat, it removes it, and it does the same for one who has heat from the burning of the sun, and for this same reason it helps greatly with hot abscesses. And the star that is in the thigh of the right arm of the one who has his knee fixed has power over this stone and from it receives its virtue. And when it is in the ascendant, it shows its works most completely.

### Regarding the stone they call Murufez. (58 verso.)

Of the third degree of the sign of Scorpio is the stone they call Murufez. This is found in the eastern part of Spain in some mines that are near the town they call Celem, which means in Arabic "salvation" <note>Arabic: *salam*</note>. They are deep mines that cannot be entered except with ladders. They find some large and some small and of many shapes. It is clear so that the sight passes through it; but nevertheless it breaks very easily. It is of two colors: one part white and the other green; and each one in itself is very...

And when that star is in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works most manifest.

### Regarding the stone they call Indiana. (58 verso.)

Of the fourth degree of the sign of Scorpio is the stone they call Indiana. This stone absorbs water, and they find it in the islands of India in mines that are there near the banks of the rivers. It is always found in the shape of three corners, which is to say in English, triangular <note>original Latin: "triangular".</note>. It is porous and very light in weight and yellow in color, though not very deeply dyed. And its virtue is such that if they place it upon a dropsical person <note>One suffering from "dropsy" or edema—an accumulation of fluid in the body.</note>, it draws out the yellow-colored water and absorbs it according to its size; and they know this by the weight they find in the stone afterward from what it absorbed. And if they place it on and remove it from the dropsical person many times, it heals them by drawing out that bad water they have. It does the same thing to anything it is placed upon that contains hot water; but in cold water, it cannot do it. And it does another thing: that which it pulls out while hot, it casts out from itself as soon as it cools. By nature it is cold and moist, and when they burn it, it holds the fire within itself like the other magnets we mentioned; but its burning is weaker. And the star that is in the right side of the figure of the "one who has his knee fixed" has power over this stone, and from it, the stone receives its strength and virtue. And when it is in the ascendant, this stone shows its works most completely.

### Regarding the stone they call Crystal. (59.)

Of the fifth degree of the sign of Cancer <note>The text says "Cancro" (Cancer), but given the sequence of Scorpio degrees 4, 6, and 7, this is likely a scribe's error for Scorpio.</note> is the stone they call in Arabic *Bollár* <note>original: "Bollár"; from the Arabic *ballūr*, meaning crystal or beryl.</note> and in English, Crystal. By nature it is cold and moist, and they find it in many parts; but the best of all is that which they find in the land of Ethiopia. The matter from which it is made is frozen water that congeals and turns to stone; and the proof of this is that when they break it, they find within it small grains that were trapped in it when it became stone, and in some of them, they find things like water. It is hard and difficult to break, but not excessively so. Its color is white, like very clear water, and it has two qualities that are the opposite of all other stones: for when they heat this stone, it receives into itself whatever color they put with it; and other stones are worth more the older they are, but this one is worth less; and it is worked more easily; and likewise it melts with fire, and therefore they make from it whatever shape they wish. If the shape is perfectly round and they place it in the sun, it burns whatever is before it that can be burned; but it does this not by its own virtue but by the clarity within it and by the rays of the sun that strike it, and also by the roundness of its shape. And the two stars—the one that is the last of the two in the shoulder of the bear, and the other northern one of the two in its haunch, both being in the figure of the Centaur <note>original: "Cantoriz"; likely referring to Centaurus.</note>—have power over this stone, and from it, the stone receives its virtue. And when they are in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works most manifest.

### Regarding the brown stone found in the river they call Faret. (59.)

Of the sixth degree of the sign of Scorpio is the brown stone found in the river they call Aliarech <note>The heading says "Faret" but the text says "Aliarech"; these likely refer to the same legendary or local river.</note>. In this river, four kinds of stones are found that do not resemble one another in anything, and this book speaks of each of them where it is appropriate, showing the virtues that each has on its own and all together. First, it speaks here of this one which has a brown color; it is strong and hard to break, and they always find it in a square shape like a die. It has some light <note>original: "Lucia"; perhaps meaning translucent or reflecting light</note>, but not so much that sight can pass through it. It is of a cold and moist nature. Its virtue is such that if they place it in a vessel containing water, it always keeps it in its coldness and does not let it warm up. And if they put it in hot water, it makes it cold in a short time; and the longer it remains there, the more it makes it cool. And if they grind it and knead it with some oil and rub hot abscesses <note>original: "postemas"; inflammatory swellings.</note> with it, they are healed. And the two stars—the middle one and the southern one of the three bright ones in the forehead of the figure of Scorpio—have power over this stone, and from it, the stone receives its strength and virtue. And when it is in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works most completely.

### Regarding the second stone found in this river. (59 verso.)

Of the seventh degree of the sign of Scorpio is the white stone, which is the second kind found in this river we have already mentioned. Its whiteness is very beautiful, and it is stronger and harder than the other brown one we spoke of. They always find it in a round and flat shape, like a cake. By nature, it is cold and moist in the third degree. Its virtue is such that whoever carries it with them can live for a very long time without drinking, for they will have no thirst nor will it harm them. And if they place it in a vessel of water, whoever drinks from it will lose the desire to lie with a woman <note>original: "yacer con mugier"; to have sexual intercourse.</note> for a very long time; and if they use it often, it will make them lose the desire for their whole life. And if they give it to drink to one who has hiccups, it makes them go away. And if they rub the place where they want hair to grow with it, it makes it grow quickly and very beautifully. And the two stars—one that is in the northern part of the three bright ones in the forehead of the figure of Scorpio, and the other that looks toward the south in the foot of that same figure—both of these have power over this stone, and from it, the stone receives its virtue. And when they are in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works most manifest.

### Regarding the black stone that is in this aforementioned river. (59 verso.)

Of the eighth degree of the sign of Scorpio is the black stone of this aforementioned river, and it is the third kind of those found there. Its color is very deeply dyed and of a great blackness, and it is clear and smooth, so that it seems polished. It is always found in the shape of an acorn, and it is stronger than any of the others we mentioned that are found in that river. And when they break it, they find inside it a very thick moisture that holds fast to whatever they put it on, especially on hair, for it dyes it with a lasting tint. And if they write with it on parchment, it makes beautiful and shining letters. It is heavy and of a cold and moist nature in the second degree. It has such virtue that if a man drinks a drachm's weight of it, it purges him very strongly <note>original: "laja"; acts as a potent laxative.</note>. And whoever keeps it with them while they sleep, it makes them sleep a great deal. And the northern star that follows the other one in that same part of the three bright ones in the forehead of the figure of Scorpio has power over this stone, and from it, the stone receives its virtue. And when it is in the ascendant, this stone shows its works most manifest.

### Of the stone whose name is Belmunicen. (60 verso.)

Of the tenth degree of the sign of Scorpio is the stone they call Belmunicen. This is found on the island called Argenica on the seashore, wrapped in the sand. It is light and porous, and rough on the outside, and easy to break; and when they break it, they find it smooth inside. Its color is reddish, but not very much, and they find it in various shapes. And when it is in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works more.

### Of the stone they call Buritasen. (60 verso.)

Of the eleventh degree of the sign of Scorpio is the stone they call Buritasen. This is the color of red ochre <note>original: "almagara"; a red earthy pigment</note>. And by nature cold and moist in the second degree, and its property is that it walks <note>meaning it floats or moves</note> upon the water, and when they break it, they find it hollow inside, and all that void is full of a thin thing that resembles a spider's web. And if they grind this stone and mix it with ten times its weight of tin and melt them together, it will become silver and will endure the hammer and fire and all other things that silver can endure; but it is not fine silver, because afterwards if they melt it many times, it returns to the state it was in at first. And if they give some of it ground up to drink to any man, it makes much urine come out of him such that he cannot hold it, and if he drinks much of it, it kills him; but if he drinks it temperately, he who has great fevers is healed by making urine, and especially from those in which there is more phlegm than bile. And it even does another thing: it makes him who looks at it sweat so much that if he endures it long, he can be healed by sweating well, just like the other by making urine. And if they make a crucible of this stone to burn oil, or a wax candle, and place it there, it makes it last ten times as long in burning as it ought to last. It is found in the Promised Land, not in deep mines but upon the face of the earth in certain sandy places; and sometimes they find it in the island of Sardinia. And the forward star of the three bright ones in the body of Scorpio has power over this

### Of the stone whose name is Aslagoniz. (61.)

Of the 12th degree of the sign of Scorpio is the stone they call Aslagoniz, which means in Chaldean "damager of the sense of taste." This is found in the land of Greater Armenia; so that there are very large fields in which there are very deep wells, and in drawing water from them, these stones come out with it. It is smooth to the touch on the outside and of a color between white and yellow, like the wax from a hive of new bees. And it has such virtue that from the time the sun sets until it rises, it becomes soft like wax, so that they can do with it whatever they wish and join one piece with another, or divide it into as many parts as they see fit; and from the time it rises until it sets, it hardens and breaks in such a way that they can grind it. By nature it is cold and moist. And the name we gave it at first is very true; for he who has it in his mouth will have no taste in anything he eats or drinks. And if they put it in spices that have a bad flavor, it takes it away and likewise makes them good; but while it is with them, it protects them so that they receive no harm nor rot. And the star at the base of the left leg of the "one who has his knee fixed" <note>The constellation Hercules, often referred to in medieval astronomy as *Engonasin* or the Kneeler.</note> has power over this stone and from it receives its virtue. And when it is in mid-heaven, it shows its works more.

### Of the stone that appears in the sea when Mars sets. (61.)

Of the 13th degree of the sign of Scorpio is the stone that appears in the sea when the planet Mars sets, and hides itself when it rises. This is found in the Tenebrous Sea <note>The medieval name for the Atlantic Ocean, thought to be dark and mysterious.</note> where those other stones are found in which the virtue of the planets is clearly shown. It is white in color and very bright, and clear; so that at night it shines like a candle, and because of the great clarity it has in itself, it receives the color of whatever thing they place before it. It is strong, so that it does not break except by very great force. And its property is to loathe salt so much that it clearly appears there is a great enmity between them; for if they are placed together, the stone breaks and is ground, and the salt loses the saltiness it has. It is light in weight and the same contrariety is seen in it as is mentioned in the seventeenth degree of the sign of Aries. And when Mars rises, this stone descends to the bottom of the water; and when it sets, it swims upon it. And it even does another thing: that when it is out of the water, it becomes clear while Mars is above the earth, and when it sets, it becomes cloudy. And likewise it does even more: that when the planet is above the earth, whoever looks closely at the stone sees that it spoils <note>original: "se danna"; likely meaning it loses its luster or structural integrity</note> and can be easily broken; but when it is under the earth, it does the opposite of this. And it even has another virtue: that whoever carries it with them in the summer does not feel the heat. And if those who have great fevers drink a little of it, they are healed. And the middle star of the three bright ones that are in the body of Scorpio, which is its heart <note>Antares, the brightest star in the constellation Scorpio.</note>, has power over this stone and from it receives its virtue. And when it is in the ascendant, this stone shows its works more completely.

### Of the stone whose name is Caralxixura. (61 verso.)

Of the 14th degree of the sign of Scorpio is the stone they call Caralxixura. Its color is a very deep red spotted with white drops, and it shines somewhat; but not so much that sight passes through it. Of these they find very large stones and they carve them on a lathe and make pots, and vessels, and other things from them, and those who eat or drink from them receive great benefit; for it takes away from them the tremor of the heart, and the other illnesses that occur there; and it also heals the ailment of the liver and of the spleen. And it has another very marvelous virtue: that if they put it into some vessel where there is milk, it immediately turns it into blood in substance, color, taste, and in all its qualities. By nature it is cold and moist. And they find it in the land they call Maneruquia

### Of the stone that they call Zulufidena. (61 verso.)

Of the 15th degree of the sign of Scorpio is the stone which they call Zulufidena, which means "leaden." And this is found in the land of <note>Original: "Agriquia," possibly a corruption of Africa or a specific mining region.</note> in the mines that are there, and they are not very deep. They find large ones and other small ones, and they resemble lead in weight and color and in all their qualities; and there is no other distinction between them except that lead melts quickly when put in the fire, and the stone does not melt but instead breaks and allows itself to be ground. And when they grind this stone and mix it with rose oil, or with any other oil that is cold, it makes a very good ointment to heal dry <term>scabies<note>Original: "sarna seca," a skin affliction.</note></term> and itching, and it cures hot <term>abscesses<note>Original: "postemas calientes," inflamed swellings.</note></term> and makes flesh grow in deep wounds. By nature it is cold and moist. And the last star of the three bright ones that are in the body of Scorpio has power over this stone, and from it, the stone receives its virtue. And when it is in the <term>ascendant<note>The degree of the zodiac rising over the eastern horizon.</note></term>, this stone shows its works most completely.

### Of the stone whose name is Buluquixmen. (62.)

Of the 16th degree of the sign of Scorpio is the stone that they call Buluquixmen, which means "camphor-like"; because when they throw it in the fire, a scent comes from it that smells like very strong camphor, but in color or in anything else it does not resemble it. This stone is yellow in color, pulling a little toward red. It is porous and light and strong and hard to break, and by nature cold and moist. And they find it in the river they call Disia in the places of the fords. They are small stones and most of them are found in the shape of an egg, and it shines somewhat. And it has such virtue that he who carries it with him is safe from having an abscess in the head; and if they give it to drink to one who has such a thing, it takes it away. And if they hang it on children during the time of their upbringing, they grow well and are healthy, and therefore those who know it and its virtues prize it and love it much. And of the two stars, one which is the middle of the three in the left thigh of <term>the one who has his knee fixed<note>The constellation Hercules, historically known as "The Kneeler."</note></term>, and the other that stays with it—both of these have power over this stone and from them it receives its virtue. And when they are in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works most manifestly.

### Of the stone they call Buruquiztez. (62.)

Of the 17th degree of the sign of Scorpio is the stone they call Buruquiztez. This they find on the bank of the river they call Alfarat <note>The Euphrates River.</note>, mixed with sand. And they are all of a six-sided shape in length <note>Likely referring to hexagonal crystal pillars.</note>. And some of these sides are green in color and others are red. It is heavy, and shiny, and hard to break, and fire does it no harm no matter how long it is there; rather, the longer it stays, the more it is refined and the more it rises in its clarity and beauty. By nature it is cold and moist. And it has such a property that if they put it in honey, it darkens and breaks by itself, and it is a deadly poison; for if they give one <term>drachma<note>A unit of weight roughly equal to 3.4 grams.</note></term> of it by weight to drink, it makes the one who drinks it lose all power of retention in the stomach and the appetite for eating; and if by force he wants to eat or drink anything, he must vomit it up immediately, and in this way he stays until he dies. And it does the same to the one who

<column-break/>

carries it with him; for in carrying it, it makes one lose the sense of smell so that he smells nothing; and it does this not only to animals but even to other things upon which it is placed. And the two stars—the one which is the last of the left thigh and the other, the middle of the three that are in the left foot of the <term>Kneeler<note>Hercules.</note></term>—have power over this stone, and from them it receives its strength and virtue. And when they are in the ascendant, this stone shows its works most manifestly.

### Of the stone they call Tarnificen. (62 verso.)

Of the 18th degree of the sign of Scorpio is the stone they call Tarnificen. This is in the shape of a hollowed basin on one side, and round on the other: some are large and others small. It is green in color, pulling toward yellow, spotted with red drops. It is found in a place they call the "Cave of Paradise" which is at the beginning of the <term>Promised Land<note>Original: "tierra de Promision."</note></term> near the bank of the river they call Lardon <note>Possibly the Jordan River.</note>; and in this aforementioned cave there are many kinds of snakes and serpents: and there are some kinds of them that are a span long in the likeness of vipers, and they have such a property that when the planet Mars rises over the earth, they give such harsh cries that whoever hears them dies immediately, and therefore the men of that land who know this avoid passing by that cave at that season. And these stones that lie in that cave cannot be obtained except in this way: when the river rises by a great flood, it enters that cave and fills it; and when it recedes and the water leaves it, it brings these stones with it. And according to the strength of the water that leaves it, they find large or small stones on the riverbank; and in this way they can get them and not otherwise; for they cannot enter the cave because of the dangers mentioned. By nature it is cold, and moist, and smooth to the touch, and heavy. And when they put it in the fire, it burns quickly and turns a gray color. It is light and porous; and if they grind it after it is burned and put a little of it over iron, or over another thing at the hour of melting, and they make of it an arrow, or spear, or any other weapon, and they wound any animal with it so that blood comes out, it can never be healed and it dies. It does the same if they give it to someone to drink and it finds inside the body some skinless patch or place through which it can reach the blood; for as soon as it reaches there, it kills as was said. And the star that is in the left shoulder of the <term>Kneeler<note>Hercules.</note></term> has power over this stone and from it receives its virtue. And when it is in the ascendant, this stone shows its works most completely.

### Of the stone they call Ceminez. (63.)

Of the 19th degree of the sign of Scorpio is the stone they call Ceminez, which means in <term>Chaldean<note>A Semitic language often associated with ancient magic and scholarship in medieval texts.</note></term> "the weeper"; because he who carries it with him has a desire to weep and to be sad; and therefore those who know it abhor it. It is found on the island of Zarandin <note>Likely Sri Lanka (Serendib).</note> where they find the other very noble stones that are mentioned in this book. In color it resembles the sapphire, but in nothing else. However, it is dark, and without light, and strong, and hard to break. Of these there are very few; because men do not dare to venture to take them out because of the bad virtue that is in them, as we already said. By nature it is cold and moist. And if they grind it and mix it with the juice of <term>purslane<note>Original: "verdulagas," an edible succulent used in traditional medicine.</note></term> and wash the mouth with it, it heals the sores that form there and rot; for they are of a bad <term>complexion<note>The medieval medical theory of the balance of humors.</note></term>. And the two stars—the one which is in the first node, and the other in the second part of the body in the figure of Scorpio—have power over this stone and from it receive its virtue. And when they are in mid-heaven, this stone has more strength and greater virtue in all its works.

### Of the stone whose name is Fartinizen. (63.)

Of the 20th degree of the sign of Scorpio is the stone they call Fartinizen, which means in Chaldean "dream-frightener." And it has this name from its virtue; for he who has it with him when he sleeps—

### Of the stone that they call Martiz. (63 verso.)

Of the 21st degree of the sign of Scorpio is the stone which they call Martiz. In color it is very black and clear, so that rays of light reflect in it just as in a mirror. It is round in shape and hollow, and has within it certain lines also hollowed out like those of a <term>winepress<note>Original: "lagár."</note></term>. It is soft to the touch, light, and porous. And it has such virtue that if it is ground and mixed with something, and they rub <term>ringworm<note>Original: "tinna," a fungal skin infection.</note></term> with it, it heals it; and likewise it heals the disease they call <term>shingles<note>Original: "culubriella," likely herpes zoster or a similar creeping skin rash.</note></term>, and the <term>hangnails<note>Original: "panarizos," infections around the fingernails.</note></term> that form at the tips of the fingernails of the hands. By nature it is cold and humid in the second degree of both these temperaments. And they find it in the land called Zardel near a town called Jerez in very deep mines located atop a mountain near that place. And the two stars—the one that is in the turn of the third knot of the tail of the figure of Scorpio and is the northern one, and the other that is in this same turn toward the south—both have power over this stone, and from them it receives its strength and virtue. Therefore, when they are in the ascendant, this stone has more strength and shows all its works more manifesty.

### Of the stone named Gebraquifez. (63 verso.)

Of the 22nd degree of the sign of Scorpio is the stone they call Gebraquifez, which means <note>original: "guardador de criaturas"</note> "guardian of children" in the Chaldean language. And it has this name because its virtue is such that if a pregnant woman carries it with her, it guards the child from harm until the time of birth, and furthermore, it makes her give birth easily and without danger, and helps the child grow quickly without injury or blemish. This stone is found in Lesser Armenia near a town they call Gurfen in a dark place, and its mine is on the bank of a river that runs nearby in a sandy place. It is always found in a round shape, and at the bottom, it has raised lines. It is porous and very light and smooth to the touch. It is shiny, but only slightly; and it has a hard, refined color that leans a bit toward redness. By nature it is cold and humid and very easy to break, and if they grind it and put a little of it into copper at the time of melting, it turns the color of very beautiful gold and makes it resemble it in all its qualities; but naturally it is not gold, for melting it many times returns it to its original nature. And if they put it on wounds, it makes them heal quickly. And the star that is in the left knee of the <term>one who holds the serpent<note>The constellation Ophiuchus.</note></term> has power over this stone, and from it receives its virtue. And when it is in the ascendant, this stone shows its works more effectively.

### Of the stone named Tumen. (64.)

Of the 23rd degree of the sign of Scorpio is the stone they call Tumen. By nature it is cold and humid, and they find it on the shore of the <term>Red Sea<note>Original: "mar rubro."</note></term> in this manner: on the shore of that sea, there are certain fish they call Cumi that have no opening through which their waste exits

<column-break/>

except through the mouth, and therefore this stone forms within their bodies. And when the fish wants to cast it out, it goes to the shore and ejects it there. And it has such virtue that if, after it has been ejected, another fish reaches it, it dies immediately; and the fishermen find them in that place and prize them greatly; because when they put the stone on a hook, all the fish that come to it die immediately, and they catch them very easily. And its color is like that of green leek leaves that lean somewhat toward white. It is light in weight, rough to the touch, and easy to break. And if anyone drinks a <term>drachm’s<note>An ancient unit of weight.</note></term> weight of it, it greatly purges phlegm, and therefore it is good against all pains that occur in the joints which are of a cold nature. And the star that is in the thigh of the left arm of the figure of the <term>one with the bent knee<note>The constellation Hercules.</note></term> has power over this stone and from it receives its virtue. And when it is in the ascendant, this stone shows greater power in all its works.

### · Of the stone they call Catu. (64.)

Of the 24th degree of the sign of Scorpio is the stone they call Catu. This is counted among those of animal origin. And they find it in this way: in the land of <note>Original: "Tept," likely referring to Tibet.</note> there are mountain sheep that are small of body and have such great power for running that nothing can overtake them, and therefore they cannot be taken except with traps; and these sheep are called <term>Catu<note>Chaldean term for the animal.</note></term> in Chaldean, and from this, the stone takes its name. Each of those sheep has a stone in its forehead between the skin and the flesh, and when it forms, the skin swells; and in this way, they understand that the sheep has it. And when they take it out, they find it the color of a <term>jujube fruit<note>A dark reddish-brown color.</note></term>. And its shape is in this manner: the part that is held against the bone is flat, and the outer part against the skin is high and round; and the flat part shines like a mirror, while the other does not. It is a strong stone and hard to break; but when they break it, they find it inside like thin membranes. By nature it is cold and humid. And they make handles for knives and for swords from it, inlaying the pieces of it one with another. Its scent is like that of amber, and even stronger when they place it over fire. And if they grind it while burnt, its powders smell very good. And if they knead it with rose water and place it over a fire burn, it heals it and leaves no scar there. And the star that follows the turn which is in the fourth knot of the figure of Scorpio has power over this stone and from it receives its virtue. And therefore, when it is in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works most manifesty.

### Of the stone named Macintarican. (64 verso.)

Of the 25th degree of the sign of Scorpio is the stone they call Macintarican, which means as much as "a thing that is governed by coldness"; for this is a kind of stone that grows and maintains itself by the governance of another thing, and it is formed deep in the earth in very cold places during wintertime, and especially there where rainwater gathers during rainy years. This stone is found in the <term>seventh climate<note>In medieval geography, the world was divided into seven latitudinal bands or "climates." It is a very hard stone, so that it does not break except with great effort; it is very heavy and of two colors: one green and the other white, and each is very shiny in itself. By nature it is very cold and humid, and it has branches, some thick and others thin, and they are intertwined underground with one another like the roots of trees. And because it is more <note>The text likely means "protective"</note>, they hang it around the necks of children; and also for the virtue it possesses; for it guards them from the illness they call <term>maseda<note>A pediatric ailment, likely related to teething, excessive drooling, or convulsions.</note></term>, and from the running of drool and from crying too much. And if they grind it and give it to be drunk, it is useful for every illness of the chest and for those who spit blood and venom, and for those who suffer from urinary leakage. And when they make a poultice from it, it is of very great benefit for hot abscesses. And the two stars joined...

The northern and the southern stars that are in what is above the figure of the **hearth** <note>Original: "fogár," likely referring to the constellation Ara (the Altar).</note> have power in this stone and from them it receives its virtue.
