### Of the stone they call Zafyuri. (64 verso.)

Of the 26th degree of the sign of Scorpio is the stone they call **Zafyuri**. And this is the one we said resembles the **Bezoar** <note>A "bezoar" is a stone-like mass found in the digestive tracts of animals, highly prized in the Middle Ages as an antidote to poison.</note>, and for this reason, those who do not know it use it in its place. It is light in weight and easy to break, and of a brown color that tends somewhat toward yellow. Its nature is cold and humid, and in this, it is the opposite of the Bezoar. They find it in the land of Yemen, and also in that of China. It is somewhat shiny, but it loses its color when it is cloudy. It is of a subtle substance, for it diminishes and thins over time because the air destroys it. And if they grind it and place it upon a scorpion sting when the pain is greatest, it takes the pain away and heals it; and it does the same for the bite of a rabid dog. And if they place its powder over the marks of old wounds, it removes them. He who keeps a piece of it in his mouth while drinking wine will not be harmed by it, nor will he become drunk. The two stars—the third and the fourth of the four that are in the right foot of the **one who holds the serpent** <note>The constellation Ophiuchus.</note>—have power in this stone and from them it receives its strength and virtue. And when they are in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works most clearly.

### Of the stone they call Ancalicez. (65.)

Of the 27th degree of the sign of Scorpio is the stone they call **Ancalicez**. Its nature is cold and humid in the fourth degree of both qualities, and they find it on the shores of the Sea of Spain toward the eastern part, and also on those of Barbary <note>The coast of North Africa.</note>. This stone is very smooth to the touch, porous, and rough. When it is burned, it becomes very light, and it tightens and hardens more than it was before; then it does not dissolve in water; but if they throw it in without being burned, it dissolves like clay. And if, after burning and grinding it, they place it upon wounds on the feet caused by tripping or by the tightness of a shoe, it heals them; it also cures hangnails at the roots of the nails. Its color is yellow tending toward green, and they use it in dyeing and painting. If they put it in oil, it makes the dregs sink to the bottom so that the oil remains purified and very clear, and it protects it from rot and all other evils that occur in it. And the star that is in the right shoulder of the figure of the **Alhave** <note>From the Arabic *al-Ḥawwā’*, another name for the constellation Ophiuchus.</note>, who is the hunter of snakes, has power in this stone and from it receives its virtue. And when it is in the ascendant, this stone shows its works most effectively.

### Of the stone named Leguya. (65.)

Of the 28th degree of the sign of Scorpio is the stone called **Leguya** in Persian, **Mechinecia** in Chaldean, and **Guiraciel** in Greek; and all these names mean **"coagulator of quicksilver"** <note>Original: "cuayador de argent vivo." Quicksilver is the old name for mercury.</note>: for if they place one weight of it upon fifteen of mercury at the hour of melting, it curdles it in such a way that it can withstand melting and the hammer; however, if they press it too much by melting it many times, it returns to its original nature. This is a very white stone, light in color and weight, and easy to break. They find it in Greater Armenia near the town they call Cequid, and its mines are atop a very high mountain, and on that mountain they find many kinds of herbs and trees of which Ceherit the wise spoke in his *Chaldean Agriculture*,

<column-break/>

and he told of many wonders concerning them, both celestial and temporal; but because it does not suit the purpose of this book, they did not include it here. This stone we mentioned is dark. And it has such a property that if they put it in onion juice, it loses that virtue we mentioned of curdling quicksilver; but if they later soak it in purslane juice, it recovers it. Its nature is cold and humid in the second degree. And its virtue is such that he who carries it with him, whether by sea or by land, will not be harmed by changing air or the rotting of stagnant water. And the stars that are in the claw where the scorpion's poison is located have power in this stone and from them it receives its virtue. And when they are in the ascendant, this stone shows its works most clearly.

### Of the stone they call Nificer. (55 verso.)

Of the 29th degree of the sign of Scorpio is the stone they call **Darnificer**. Its color is yellow, speckled with very black spots. It is heavier than lead and very radiant, so much so that sight passes through it. Some are found large and others small and of many shapes. Men prize it greatly for its beauty. It is strong and hard to break, such that no other body can mark it except for the **diamond** alone, or **gypsum** <note>Original: "piedra del yeso." The text records a medieval belief that certain soft stones could paradoxically break hard ones.</note>; for even though it is common and soft, it breaks this other stone which is very noble in nature and very strong. And this name **Darnificer**, which this stone has, comes from the virtue within it; for according to the Chaldean language, this name means **"healer of the pain of half the head"**, which in Greek is called <term>Cephalea<note>Original: "Cefalea," referring to a migraine or chronic headache.</note></term>; and it heals this illness very easily when it is hung over the sufferer; furthermore, he who carries it with him is safe from having this illness. Its nature is cold and humid. They find it in the land called Mereciz by the Red Sea. And it has another very wonderful virtue: any animal that walks on four feet and eats meat dies as soon as it sees it. And the star that is in the fifth joint of the tail of the figure of Scorpio has power in this stone and from it receives its virtue. And when it is in the ascendant, this stone shows its works most clearly.

### Of the stone named Zarmiquidez. (65 verso.)

Of the 30th degree of the sign of Scorpio is the stone they call **Zarmiquidez**, which in Chaldean means **"healer of jaundice"**; because its virtue is such that he who carries it with him is safe from having this disease; and if they place it on one who already has it, they are healed immediately. And it even has another very noble and wonderful virtue: if they place it near food in which there is poison, it immediately becomes murky, mixing one with the other, and the stone itself is damaged. And if any solid body such as meat, or fish, or another closed thing like them [is poisoned], it is all ruined and lost: and this is one of the greatest wonders that the wise men found in the virtues of stones. Its color is green like an **emerald**, but darker and more brilliant and with greater radiance; it is found in many shapes, which is not easily found in the emerald except in the shape of a reed; but this stone is heavier than the emerald and stronger and harder to break, and it withstands greater fire. They find it on the island of **Alacuac** near the Red Sea in very deep mines that are in that land. And the star that is in the seventh joint near the poison claw of the figure of the scorpion has power in this stone and from it receives its strength and virtue. And when it is in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works most effectively.

# OF THE SIGN OF SAGITTARIUS.

---

### PROLOGUE. (67.)

It is necessary for anyone who wishes to work with these thirty degrees of the sign of Scorpio <note>Original: "Escorpion." Though this is the Sagittarius section, the text refers back to the preceding sign's influence or completion.</note> to pay attention to the planet Mars, ensuring it is received by the star that has power over the stone; furthermore, the Lord of the Face <note>A technical term in astrology referring to the planetary ruler of a specific ten-degree segment (decan) of a sign.</note> should be placed in a favorable position. By doing this, one will accomplish what they desire by the pleasure of God.

### Of the stone they call Zequeth. (67.)

From the first degree of the sign of Sagittarius is the stone they call **Zequeth**. This is found in the land of Lycia <note>Original: "Luquia."</note> and also near the river that runs close to the town called Mitaz. It is a stone black in color and very light in weight. When it is burned, it produces a flame and smoke that smells like pitch <note>Original: "pez."</note> when placed in the fire. By nature, it is hot and dry. If one uses its smoke to fumigate someone who is possessed by demons, it takes hold of them immediately. Likewise, fumigating a woman who has pain in her "nature" <note>A medieval euphemism for the reproductive organs or menstrual pain.</note> heals her quickly because this stone is pervasive. From the smoke of this stone when burned, reptiles flee. This stone is good when placed in medicines to heal the sickness called arthritis <note>Original: "Artetita."</note> which comes from a phlegmatic nature, because it is somewhat salty. The star in the left knee of **the one who has his knee fixed** <note>The constellation Hercules, often referred to in medieval texts as "the Kneeler" or "Engonasin."</note> has power over this stone and from it, the stone receives its virtue. When this star is in mid-heaven, the stone demonstrates its effects most clearly.

### Of the stone they call Sedinech. (67.)

From the second degree of the sign of Sagittarius is the stone they call **Sedinech**, which means **Hematite** <note>Original: "Amatites." An iron oxide stone known for its reddish streak.</note>. This is found in the cave they call Cetui, and it is also found in the land of Egypt in the mines located there. By nature, it is hot and dry and easy to break; it is red in color, and the more dyed it is, the better it is; likewise, the variety that is clean and does not crumble. It is a very well-known stone. Its property is that it possesses a retentive strength with sharpness, and for this reason, it is prized; it thins the heaviness of the eyelids <note>Original: "cuencas de los oyos," literally the sockets/rims of the eyes.</note>. If mixed with woman’s milk, it heals the sickness called ophthalmia and the sores that form in the eyes. If given to drink with wine, it cures the ailment caused by the retention of urine. Furthermore, for women who suffer illness because their "flower" <note>An archaic term for menstruation.</note> comes too abundantly, it causes them to lose that excess. If given to drink to one who spits blood, it brings great benefit and heals them quickly. He who wishes for this stone to exert its virtue more strongly should burn it, turn it into powder, and give it to drink with wine; it will have greater strength and work better than any other way. However, one must not let it burn too much, or it will be damaged; the sign of when it has burned enough is this: watch closely, and when it begins to change color, take it out immediately. When this stone is rubbed on a whetstone, it produces a red color that is very good for healing the mange <note>Original: "sarna," often referring to scabies or general skin irritation.</note> and the itching that occurs in the eyes. The two stars—the northern and the southern—of the three in the left arm of **the one who has his knee fixed** <note>The constellation Hercules.</note> have power over this stone and from them it receives its strength and virtue. And when these two are in

<column-break/>

the ascendant, this stone shows more strength and greater virtue in all its works.

### Of the stone they call Copper. (67 verso.)

From the third degree of the sign of Sagittarius is the mineral stone they call **Copper** <note>Original: "Cobre."</note>. By nature, it is hot and dry, and it is of two colors: one that tends toward red—which is the best when it is a clear red—and another that tends toward black, which is not as good. This red variety is found in the mines in the land of Cyprus <note>Original: "Cabroz." The word "copper" (cuprum) is derived from the name of this island.</note>. It has within it a deeply hidden greenness that does not appear except when it meets vinegar or another sour thing; for then it turns into green verdigris <note>Original: "acingar verde," referring to copper acetate.</note>, which is a very strong poison. If one joins this stone with the other called **Dehenich** <note>Malachite.</note> of which we already spoke in this book, and mixes both with quicksilver <note>Mercury.</note>, it makes it harden so much that it becomes brittle. If one melts the copper with a little glass and a bit of borax, and then cools it in cold water, it turns the color of fine gold; but if it is later placed in fire, it turns black. He who habitually eats or drinks from this copper develops many illnesses, such as the disease called elephantiasis <note>Original: "eleofan," characterized by the thickening of the legs.</note>, as well as cancer; it sickens the liver and the spleen, and furthermore damages all his complexions <note>In medieval medicine, the balance of the four humors.</note>. This happens especially if they put any roasted fish—of whatever nature it may be—there to be kept, because that fish absorbs a foul smell and becomes poisonous. However, on the other hand, the powders of this stone are good for thinning the thickness of the eyelids and also for healing their mange, strengthening the sight, and drying up the moisture that forms in them. If these medicines are ground on a copper plate or in a mortar, they will be better and bring relief more quickly. When copper is burned and washed, it makes good medicines for healing sores and the aforementioned illnesses. But he who wishes to work with it should take care not to use it on subtle and soft bodies unless it is burned, but use it raw on strong ones. The southern star of the two at the base of the **hearth** <note>Original: "fogár," referring to the constellation Ara (the Altar).</note> has power over this stone and from it, it receives its virtue. When it is in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works most manifest.

### Of the stone named Mazaconia. (67 verso.)

### Of the stone they call <term>Mehe</term>. (68.)

From the fifth degree of the sign of <term>Sagittarius</term> is the stone they call <term>Mehe</term>. This is found on the shores of the Red Sea in mines located there; it is also found in the land of Egypt. It is a stone that is entirely white with no other mixture within it. Some are clear, and these are the best; others are dark and brownish, which are harder to break, but all of them resemble glass. Some have said it was a type of glass, but it is not; for these do not break or work in the way that glass does. If this stone is struck hard with iron, much fire comes out of it; and there are some that look like a piece of joined salt. By nature, it is hot and dry in the third degree. If it is ground and placed upon hard swellings, such as scrofula <note>A form of tuberculosis affecting the lymph nodes of the neck.</note> and others like them, it makes them ripen and open in a short time. Even beyond this, it is of great use to those who labor in the "greater work" <note>This likely refers to alchemy or high ritual magic.</note>. And the star that is at the tip of the arrow of <term>Sagittarius</term> has power over this stone and from it receives its virtue. And when it is in the ascendant, this stone shows its effects most clearly.

### Of the stone called the "gold-binder." (68.)

From the sixth degree of the sign of <term>Sagittarius</term> is the stone they call the gold-binder <note>Original: "apegador doro." This is likely chrysocolla or a similar copper mineral used in soldering.</note>, and it has this name because it joins gold together, however small the pieces may be. It is found in the land of Armenia, and also in Cabroz. Its color is that of green leek leaves, and even a bit more tinted. It is heavy in body and easy to break. By nature, it is hot and dry and resembles <term>Acimar</term> <note>A medieval term usually referring to copper acetate or verdigris.</note> in many things. It is a stone that greatly cleanses the flesh and makes it subtle, and it has a sting like an itch; therefore, it is good for wounds, for it eats away the "proud flesh" <note>Excessive granulation tissue that prevents a wound from healing.</note> that forms in wounds, purges them, and heals them. It is also good for the eyes, for it removes the mange from them and heals the disease they call ophthalmia <note>Original: "obtalmia." A general term for severe eye inflammation.</note>; for it binds the parts of the eyes together that have been parted. Goldsmiths solder gold with it. This stone is better and has greater strength in all its works when it is taken from the mine during the time of great heat than when it is taken in winter. If it is burned like other stones, it is better; likewise, it is better for eye treatments when it has been washed. And the northern star of the three that are in the left arm of the "one who has his knee fixed" <note>Refers to the constellation Hercules, historically known as *Engonasin* or "The Kneeler."</note> has power over this stone and from it receives its virtue. And when it is in mid-heaven, this stone shows its effects most completely.

### Of the stone they call <term>Calicon</term>. (68 reverse.)

From the seventh degree of the sign of <term>Sagittarius</term> is the stone they call <term>Calicon</term>, and the Arabs call it <term>Ceni</term>. It is a kind of copper, but the ancients mixed hot spices with it, and the stone received a poison from them; most of what is made of this is copper dross soaked in cow urine. This type of copper, when brought to the fire and heated, will stretch if struck with a hammer, which no other copper does. By nature, it is hot and dry. If any weapon is made from it and an animal is struck so that the metal mixes with the blood, it causes very great pain, and if the wound is large, the animal dies from it. If fishhooks are made from it to fish, once the fish is caught on it, it cannot get away, even if the hook is small and the fish is large; this is because of the great pain the fish feels from the poison in the copper. If a man has a twisted mouth <note>Likely referring to Bell's palsy or a stroke.</note> and is placed in a dark house and looks at himself in a mirror made of this copper, he is healed. It has yet another property: if it is heated in fire and then quenched in water, no beast will go near that water. And if tweezers are made of it and used

<column-break/>

to pluck hair, the hair does not grow there anymore; but with all this, it has all the strength that other coppers have. And the two stars—one being the northern of the two in that same part of the arm of the bow of <term>Sagittarius</term>, and the other in the right hock of the horse part—have power over this stone and from them it receives its virtue. Therefore, when they are in the ascendant, this stone shows its effects most clearly.

### Of the stone of the bath. (69.)

From the eighth degree of the sign of <term>Sagittarius</term> is the stone they call "of the bath." It is porous, light in weight, and easy to break. By nature, it is hot and dry and brown in color. If it is ground and sprinkled upon the "cancer" that forms in the "natures" of women <note>A euphemism for the reproductive organs; "cancer" here refers to any malignant or spreading sore.</note>, they are healed immediately. And the star that is in the hand that grips the bow in the figure of <term>Sagittarius</term> has power over this stone and from it receives its virtue. And when it is in mid-heaven, this stone shows its effects most clearly.

### Of the stone found in the gall of the bull. (69.)

From the ninth degree of the sign of <term>Sagittarius</term> is the stone found in the gall of the bull or the ox in this manner: when they kill it during a waxing moon, they find the stone inside it, and therefore it is counted among the animal stones <note>Bezoars or gallstones.</note>. By nature, it is hot and dry in the fourth degree. It is a round and hard stone, reddish in color, leaning somewhat toward yellow. It is called <term>Varz</term> in Arabic and <term>Kiron</term> in Greek. Its property is that if it is mixed with powders for the eyes, it strengthens the nerves and sharpens the sight. If it is kneaded with the juice of beets and placed in the nostrils of one who has the disease called in Latin <term>cataract</term> <note>Original: "cataraita." In this context, it may refer to a blockage of the "spirits" of sight or a literal cataract.</note>, or one whose eyes look clear but who cannot see, he is healed quickly with use. It also removes the disease that plucks the hair from the head, which is called <term>alopecia</term> <note>Original: "lopicia."</note>, in such a way that it makes it grow back by force; and for those who are white-haired, it dyes them the color they were before. And the star toward the southern part of the arm of the bow of <term>Sagittarius</term> has power over this stone and from it receives its virtue. And when it is in mid-heaven, this stone shows its effects most completely.

### Of the Arabic stone. (69.)

From the tenth degree of the sign of <term>Sagittarius</term> is the stone they call <term>Arabic</term>. This resembles white, clean ivory in color. This has a very marvelous virtue: though it is as white as it is, when it is rubbed with some liquid, a yellow color like saffron comes out of it. It is found in the land of Arabia near the town called Carinduin in mines located there. By nature, it is hot and dry, and therefore it cleanses and removes the skin spots <note>Original: "panno." Likely refers to melasma or other facial discolorations.</note> that form on the face and other things that come from an excess of humors. If it is ground and placed on a place where blood is flowing, it makes it stop; likewise, when it is burned and ground, it makes very good powders for cleaning teeth by rubbing them. And the southern star of the two on the left side of the figure of <term>Sagittarius</term> has power over this stone and from it receives its virtue. And when it is in the ascendant, this stone shows its effects most clearly.

### Of the stone they call **Azarnech**. (70.)

From the twelfth degree of the sign of <term>Sagittarius</term> is the stone they call <term>Azarnech</term> <note>Arsenic, specifically orpiment or realgar.</note>; in Chaldean they call it <term>Zinderch</term>, and in Latin they call it <term>Orpiment</term>. This is divided into two types: one which is red and the other yellow, which is named <term>Zeurech</term>. This stone is found in many places and in many mines, but the best of all is that which they find in the land named <term>Eciconton</term>. By nature, it is hot and dry in the fourth degree and possesses a very great burning quality within it. If they burn it until it turns into something like white lime and mix it with copper and a little <term>baurac</term> <note>A mineral salt, often nitre or borax.</note>, and then melt the copper and put in a little borax and add this stone when they melt it, it tints it the color of gold inside and out, and makes it lose the foul odor it has; however, it is not natural gold. If they burn the <term>Azarnech</term> and make it into powder and rub it on the teeth, it does great good; also to the gums that are being eaten away, and this is because it becomes a finer substance upon burning. If they place it upon the hair, it scrapes it all away, and if they leave it there too long, it burns the flesh. These things are common to the <term>Azarnechs</term> we have mentioned; but as for the red one specifically, we say it is deeply tinted with redness, very clear, clean, and easy to break. If they grind it and knead it with the juice of henbane and rub the place where hair was plucked, it will never grow there again. Mixing it with resin heals the disease called <term>lopicia</term> <note>Alopecia, or patchy hair loss.</note>. Turning it with pitch removes the white spots that form on the nails. It enters into medicines used against all diseases of the nose and mouth, wounds, fistulas, and also hemorrhoids. It is good to put into medicines made for those who have phlegm gathered in their chests. If they fumigate a person who has an old cough with it, it brings great benefit; and even if they eat a little of it mixed with honey, it clears the voice greatly. The star that is the forward one of the two dark stars in the northern arch of the crown has power over this stone and from it receives its virtue. When it is in the ascendant, this stone shows its works most completely.

### Of the stone they call **Azarnech**. (70.)

### Of the stone that consumes honey. (70 verso.)

This stone is found in the land they call <term>Rabearnave</term> in a mine near a town called <term>Eniz</term>. Its color is deep purple and spotted with black drops. Its color is green tending toward white, and they always find it in the shape of a moon; but the masters who know this stone make of it whatever shape they wish. It is heavy, strong, and hard to break; it has a great luster, such that the sight passes through it. By nature, it is hot and dry. It has such virtue that if a viper or other snake sees it, its eyes instantly break and it dies. The two stars, one which is in the northern part of the arch of the crown and the other in the southern part of that same arch, have power over this stone and from it receive its virtue. When they are in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works most clearly.

### Of the stone they call Anatron. (71 verso.)

From the 17th degree of the sign of Sagittarius is the stone they call <term>Anatron</term> <note>A form of natron or soda used in ancient chemistry and cleaning.</note>. When it is in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works most manifesty.

### Of the stone of salt. (71 verso.)

From the 18th degree of the sign of Sagittarius is the stone of salt. This comes in many forms and is found in many places; some are formed in sea lagoons and are dug up like a kind of sand. There is another that exists in the form of a stone. Another is called <term>sal gema</term> <note>Gem salt or rock salt (halite).</note>, which is stony. There is yet another type called gem salt which is also hard. Besides all these, there is another gathered from inland lagoons, formed by fire or the heat of the sun; this is called "kneading salt" <note>Original: "sal de amasar," common culinary salt.</note>, and men use it more than all the others. Some of these are found in caves and marked wells; but here it is not appropriate to speak of any but these two which are counted as stones: the one they call "Indian" and the other "gem salt." The Indian salt, of which we wish to speak first, is brown in color, speckled with black spots. It is found mostly in the land of India. It is strong and very hard to break, and hot and dry in the third degree. It has a very salty taste, and thus has the power to cleanse bodies and greatly brighten gold and silver, each to its own color; it removes impurities and excessive greasiness, and for this reason, they include it in the Great Work. In most of these stones, a very salty and somewhat sulfurous substance is mixed. Because this explanation is very long and not suited to our book, we do not wish to speak further on it. But of salt, we say that if it is placed in the flesh of any animal, it dries it out by drawing out the moisture; thus it makes the body last a long time without rotting, smelling bad, or spoiling, and there is no other stone that does this but this one. However, there are

<column-break/>

other things that do so, such as aloe, myrrh, camphor, and balsam. But these only work by making the moisture within the bodies dry up where it lies, whereas salt, by gripping the moisture, forces it out and dries them. Therefore, it is good for men and helps them greatly against the phlegm that often grows within them. It is also good for abscesses caused by phlegm and for removing the "claw" <note>Original: "unna," likely referring to a pterygium or a growth on the eye.</note> that forms in the eyes when mixed with other medicines intended for this. If mixed with oil and rubbed on the body, it removes fatigue. The star in the front left heel of Sagittarius has power over this stone, and from it receives its virtue. When it is in the ascendant, this stone shows its works most manifestly.

And the largest of them is the split variety, and it appears to have more acidity <note>Original: "acesidad," referring to a sharp or caustic quality.</note> than any of the others. Of the round variety, the best is the one that tends toward yellow. And of the moist variety, the best is that which is clear and has the color of milk, is uniform in all its parts, and has the smell of fire. Because all these types are concordant in nature and virtue, we speak here of all of them together; we say they are hot and moist with astringent properties <note>Original: "restrinnimiento," a quality that constricts tissues.</note>. It cleanses the bodies of metals and makes them bright. The star located between the shoulders of the three stars in the figure of Sagittarius has power over this stone, and from it, the stone receives its strength and virtue. When this star is in the ascendant, this stone shows its effects most clearly.

### Of the stone named Red Sulfur. (73.)

Of the 22nd degree of the sign of Sagittarius is the stone they call Red Sulfur. It is one of the four types of sulfur, three of which we have already mentioned; this fourth one is a red stone and not very dark. This is found in the land of Africa toward the west, near the Ocean sea. When this stone is in its mine, it glows so much that from afar it resembles a candle; however, when it is taken out, it loses this virtue. Nevertheless, in complexion and nature, it is like the others and is in concord with them in all its qualities. It has such virtue that if a little of it is placed in the nose of one who is possessed by a demon, it helps him, and if he uses it often, he is healed. It does the same for one who has the illness they call apoplexy <note>Original: "apoplisia."</note>, and likewise for one who has the sickness called in Greek *cephalaia* <note>Original: "cefalea," referring to a severe, chronic headache or migraine.</note>. It is used much in works of gold because it tints white metal red and gives it a good color; for this reason, those who labor in the Great Work use it much in their operations. The middle star of the three located in the northern track of the headdress of Sagittarius has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its virtue. When it is in the ascendant, this stone shows its effects most clearly.

### Of the stone they call Bicedi. (73.)

Of the 23rd degree of the sign of Sagittarius is the stone they call Bicedi. This is red in color, such that it resembles the hyacinth <note>Original: "yargonza," a red or orange gemstone often associated with zircon.</note> in hue; but it does not withstand fire as the hyacinth does, but rather is ruined by it and loses its color. Its best mines are in the East, and when they are taken from the mines, they have no brilliance; but afterward, upon polishing, they become beautiful and clear. Its nature is hot and dry, though its heat is less than that of the hyacinth, and its dryness is greater. Its virtue is such that whoever carries a weight of ten barleycorns or more of it will not dream fearful dreams. If it is placed in the rays of the sun and a man later looks into it, it greatly diminishes the eyesight. If it is heated by rubbing it vigorously through the hair of the head and then placed on the ground, it draws up straws and small sticks <note>A description of static electricity.</note>. The best of all these is the reddest and clearest. There is another type called Medebich, which is not as red and does not attract straws or sticks as much as the other we mentioned; nonetheless, it possesses all the same virtues. The two final stars of the three in the northern track of the headdress of Sagittarius have power over this stone, and from them, it receives its virtue. When they are in mid-heaven, this stone shows its effects most.

<column-break/>

### Of the stone named Muruquid.
->( 73 verso. )<-

Of the 24th degree of the sign of Sagittarius is the stone they call Muruquid. This is found in the land of the blacks in a place called Zurin, near the town they call Aterbuliz. Its mine is on top of a mountain. It is strong and hard to break, light in weight, and of a brown color that tends toward red, resembling clay. Its nature is hot and dry in the third degree. It greatly cleanses the bodies of those who wash with it, especially the head; for it removes dandruff <note>Original: "forfola."</note>, kills lice, and makes the hair very beautiful. If they wash the whole body with it, it cleanses away the filth that is upon it, thins and softens the skin, gives it a good color, and dissolves abscesses and boils, especially those that form on the head. If vinegar is poured over this stone, bubbles form and it grows; if one continues this, it becomes like dough and cannot be dissolved by anything except vinegar. When it is dissolved this way, it gives off an odor like mountain rue. If it is held to the nose of one who frequently faints, it helps him. It is also good against the illness they call apoplexy. The star located between the horns of the turtle <note>Original: "galapago." The constellation Lyra was often depicted as a tortoise or turtle.</note> has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its virtue. When it is in the ascendant, this stone shows its effects most clearly.

### Of the stone they call Beinebeyri. (73 verso.)

Of the 25th degree of the sign of Sagittarius is the stone they call Beinebeyri, which means "the water-hater." Its nature is hot and dry, and it is found in the Promised Land in the East, on the shore of the lake they call Dead, which is at the end of that land. It is strong and hard to break, shining and clear so that sight passes through it. It has the color of the sky and is always found long and with three sharp edges, so that each one cuts like a knife. Most of those found are at the bottom of a cave at the edge of that lake, where there is a stone hollowed out in the shape of a grave. The virtue of this stone is according to its name; for if it is placed in any flowing liquid other than water, it sinks to the bottom; but if it is thrown into water, it leaps out as if it loathed it. If a weight of one drachm of it is given to a man to drink, it greatly purges the bile <note>Original: "colera," one of the four bodily humors.</note>. The star in the thigh of the right arm of Sagittarius has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its virtue. When it is in the ascendant, this stone shows its effects most fully.

### Of the stone they call Aryuritaz. (74.)

Of the 26th degree of the sign of Sagittarius is the stone they call Aryuritaz. This is found on a mountain called Aritar, from which it takes its name; this mountain is in the land named Cetunaz, which borders Ethiopia. The mine of this stone is on top of a mountain. It is not found deep underground, but rather on the surface. It is a heavy stone and easy to break. It is clear and bright, having the color of a violet. When it is broken, it is found to have layers <note>Original: "foyas," literally "leaves," likely referring to a lamellar or micaceous structure.</note> inside, one on top of the other, and the more of them that are removed, the more beautiful the stone remains.

Its nature is hot and dry. If it is placed upon teeth that are in pain, it removes the ache. If it is kneaded with some oil to make a plaster and placed upon the stomach of one who is in pain, it takes away the pain and heals him. If a little of it is put into a great deal of water and that water is sprinkled on timber, the wood will never rot nor warp. The hidden star that follows the three in the northern track of the headdress of the figure of Sagittarius has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its virtue. When it is in the ascendant, this stone shows its effects most clearly.

### Concerning the stone named Bulufiriz. (74.)

The stone called Bulufiriz belongs to the 27th degree of the sign of Sagittarius. This stone is found in the lake named Belfiz, from which it takes its name; this lake is located at the edge of the land called Karuquia, which borders the land of India. The water of this lake possesses a very marvelous virtue: no animal that enters it can sink to the bottom; instead, the water makes it float on the surface. This stone has the color of refined gold tending toward red, and in its substance, it resembles joined sand. It is strong and hard to break. Painters use it to help tint wood the color of gold, and in the land where it is found, they paint walls with it. Its nature is hot and dry. It has such a virtue that if it is added to gold when it is melted, the gold turns white like silver and remains so until it is melted many more times. If this stone is burned and washed like other stones and then mixed with oil, it makes a very good medicine for wounds, for it purges and cleanses them of all filth and heals them. The front star of the two located in the left shoulder of the **Flying Vulture** <note>The constellation Aquila; the star is likely Altair or a neighboring star in the constellation.</note> has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its virtue. When this star is in mid-heaven, the stone demonstrates its effects more clearly.

### Concerning the stone they call Leilericech. (74 verso.)

The stone called Leilericech belongs to the 28th degree of the sign of Sagittarius. Its name in Chaldean <note>Original: "caldeo," likely referring to Aramaic or a related Semitic language used in the source texts.</note> means "stayer of drool." It has such a virtue that whoever carries it prevents the drool that runs from a man while he sleeps; it does the same for small children. It is beautiful and clear, so much so that sight passes through it, and it has a brown color tending toward red. It is light in weight but strong and hard; nevertheless, it breaks very easily when brought near **almagra** <note>A red iron oxide or ochre used for polishing and pigment.</note>. This stone is found at the bottom of the lake called the **Lake of the Fish**, which is in the western part of the Promised Land. The water of this lake is very sweet, and its color resembles saffron. Its nature is hot and dry. If a half-drachm of the ground stone is given to drink with a little almagra, it heals the illness called colic. Furthermore, it treats pain of the stomach and intestines and greatly benefits the liver when it is weak or cold. Two stars—one in the right hind leg and the other in the front of the northern side of the quadrangle formed at the base of the tail of Sagittarius—have power over this stone and from them it receives its virtue. When these stars are in mid-heaven, the stone shows its effects most manifesty.

<column-break/>

### Concerning the stone they call Faruquid. (74 verso.)

The stone called Faruquid belongs to the 29th degree of the sign of Sagittarius. This is found in the land called Faruquia, from which the stone takes its name. The place where it is found is near the town called Atebuliz <note>Possibly Tiberias, known for its hot springs.</note>, where there are natural hot baths containing a cave of very hot sulfur water. That water rises in vapors and clings to the walls, forming stones that are strong and hard to break, and heavy. When taken from the cave, they appear dusty on top, but after they are polished, they are very black in color and shine somewhat. If one drachm's weight of the ground stone is given to drink, it wounds the intestines and kills by causing hemorrhaging. If it is burned, it becomes lime and "traps" the fire within itself; if it is later sprinkled with water, it burns all things in front of it that are flammable, and this fire cannot be extinguished with anything except melted wax. Its nature is hot and dry. If it is placed in water and left there for some time, that water benefits all those things for which the natural hot baths benefit a man who bathes in them. Two stars—one following the one on the northern side, and the other the first of the southern part, both in the quadrangle at the base of the tail of Sagittarius—have power over this stone and from them it receives its virtue. When they are in the ascendant, this stone shows its effects more clearly.

### Concerning the stone named Muludintaz. (75.)

The stone called Muludintaz belongs to the 30th degree of the sign of Sagittarius. This is found in the land of Spain more than in any other place, at the bottom of a river that runs near the town called Caide <note>Likely Cádiz.</note>. Its nature is hot and dry, and its color is black streaked with yellow lines. It is rough to the touch and light in weight. It possesses a strange property: when thrown into water, it sinks to the bottom, but if thrown into wine, it floats on top. If it is ground and mixed with resin, it heals "hot" abscesses. If it is rubbed on hair, it thins it all out; if the hair grows back later, it is weaker than the first, and if they continue to rub it this way many times, hair will no longer grow there. It is also good for medicines made for the eyes, for it removes the "whiteness" from them <note>Likely referring to cataracts or corneal scarring.</note>. The star on the southern side of the quadrangle at the base of the tail of Sagittarius has power over this stone, and from it the stone receives its virtue. When the star is in mid-heaven, this stone shows its effects most completely.

# CONCERNING THE SIGN OF CAPRICORN.
---

### PROLOGUE. (76.)

The thirty types of stones according to the thirty degrees of the sign of Sagittarius have been described. Therefore, whoever wishes to work with these must pay heed to the planet **Jupiter**, ensuring it is well-received by the star with which he performs his work; likewise, he must ensure the **Lord of the Face** <note>The ruler of the current decan (a 10-degree subdivision of the zodiac sign).</note> is in a good state for works of good, and the contrary for works of evil.

### Concerning the stone they call Tutya. (76.)

The stone called Tutya <note>Tutty, a crude zinc oxide collected from the flues of smelting furnaces, though here described as a natural mineral.</note> belongs to the first degree of the sign of Capricorn, and it is of three kinds. The first is white and is called **Indian**. The second is green and is named **Marine**. The third is yellow tending toward red, and they call it **Spanish**. We shall speak of each of these in its place, but here we will speak first of the one called Indian. This is found in the sea...

### Concerning the stone named Green Tutty. (76.)

Belonging to the second degree of the sign of Capricorn is the stone they call Green Tutty <term>Tutty: a medicinal powder made from zinc oxide, often used in medieval eye salves.</term>, which is called "The Marine One." Its mine is on the seashore of the land of China <note>Original: "Cin," referring to China.</note>. Its color is green and it is rough to the touch and porous; it is heavier than the first stone and of a coarser substance. By nature, it is cold and dry and has the virtue of drying. It is retentive and removes films from the eyes, and it is good for cancerous sores, as well as for blisters and sores of the eyes. If they grind it and knead it with water and make lozenges from it and dry them in the shade, it will then be better for all these works. The southern star of the two that are in the eye of the **Tortoise** <note>The constellation Lyra was often depicted as a tortoise in medieval astronomy following the Arabic tradition.</note> has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its virtue. When it is in mid-heaven, this stone demonstrates its effects most clearly.

### Concerning the stone named Spanish. (76 verso.)

Belonging to the third degree of the sign of Capricorn is the stone of Yellow Tutty, which they call Spanish. This is born in the land of Spain, from which it takes its name. They also find it in the land of China, and they call it *Mahudia*; however, this one from Spain is more stony than the others, heavier, and less clear. By nature, it is cold and dry; therefore, it is retentive and dries much, and there is a certain stinging quality in it. It is better than any other medicine for sores that form on the private parts. It prevents humors from passing through the membranes of the eyes and strengthens and sharpens the sight. The star that is in the nock of the **Arrow** <note>The constellation Sagitta.</note> has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its virtue. When it is in mid-heaven, this stone demonstrates its effects most clearly.

### Concerning the stone they call Jet. (76 verso.)

Belonging to the fourth degree of the sign of Capricorn is the stone they call Jet <note>Original: "Zebech," from the Arabic *az-zabaj*.</note>. It is hard and very black in color, light in weight, easy to break, and it shines like a mirror, yet the sight does not pass through it. Its mines are found in many places, but the best are those found in the islands of India. By nature, it is cold and dry in the third degree. If they grind it and mix it with medicines made to strengthen the sight of the eyes, it is very beneficial. If they make a mirror of it and use it for gazing, it greatly strengthens the sight, whether it be weak from old age or from illness. When this stone is taken from the mine, it is shaped like planks, some thick and others thin. Afterward, they work it into whatever shape they wish; however, it is not good for a man to carry it with him always, because those who carry it are overcome by sadness because of it. The leading star of the two in the left shoulder of the Eagle has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its virtue. When it is in mid-heaven, this stone demonstrates its effects most fully.

### Concerning the stone they call Clinia. (77.)

Belonging to the fifth degree of the sign of Capricorn is the stone they call

Clinia <note>Likely a form of calamine or a mineral furnace deposit.</note>. This is found in many places, for some are found in silver mines, and others are found in the furnaces where they smelt copper; some are found in rivers where the water flows very forcefully, for in digging into the sand and earth, the water uncovers them, and thus they are found tangled within it. Others are found on the island of Cyprus, which are more natural than those we have mentioned, and they are counted among the good stones; therefore, we wish to speak of them before the others. ### Concerning the stone named Carnelian. (77.)

Belonging to the sixth degree of the sign of Capricorn is the stone they call *Al-aqiq* <note>Original: "Alcaquic," the Arabic term for carnelian or agate.</note> in Greek and Carnelian in Latin. This is of a red color that leans somewhat toward yellow; it is clear and shining so that the sight passes through it, and the one that has these signs is better and more noble. There is another kind that resembles the water that comes out of meat when salt is added, and some are found with white veins that appear very discreetly. The mines for this stone are in many places, such as in the land of Arabia and in Lienten on the shores of that sea, as well as in the land of Rome and in many other parts. This stone is cold and dry by nature, and it is much loved by men for its beauty, and also highly prized for the virtue it possesses; for it has three great and good virtues. The first is that it greatly helps public speakers who lose their voice when they carry it with them, for it gives them the strength to argue without fear and helps them to do so elegantly. The second is that it is good for stopping blood that flows too much, especially for women when they bleed more than they should. And the third virtue is that it benefits the teeth when it is made into powder and rubbed upon them, for it cleanses them, makes them bright, causes the flesh to grow around them, and makes the gums very red. But the one that has the virtue of stopping blood shows its effect more than all the others—this is the one that has the color of water coming from salted meat—and this one also works better than the others on the teeth, as we have said; it even heals the cavities that form at the roots and prevents blood from leaving the gums. The star that is in the front tip of the forward horn of Capricorn has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its virtue. When it is in mid-heaven, this stone demonstrates its effects most clearly.

It is clear, but the sight does not pass through it; it is heavy, soft, and easy to break. Its nature is cold and dry, and therefore it dries much, retains, and cleanses the things upon which it is placed. However, its strength is not very great, nor is its coldness extreme; but nonetheless, it greatly benefits itching and the sores that arise from it. When it is mixed with wax, it makes a very good medicine that cools temperately, soothes pain, removes rotten flesh from wounds, and joins them together. ### **Concerning the stone they call Red Ochre.**

Belonging to the eighth degree of the sign of Capricorn is the stone they call **Red Ochre** <term>Almagra: a red earth or clay colored by iron oxide, used since prehistoric times as a pigment and for medicinal purposes.</term>. This exists in two forms. One comes from burnt bricks, which is not appropriate for us to discuss here; the other is from a mine, which is what we wish to speak of in this book. Although it is found in many places, the best of all is that found in a land named Ceimicaz. It is the color of liver, has a thick substance, is very heavy, is equal in all its qualities, and is cold and dry by nature. When it is soaked in water, it expands greatly. It is "retentive" <note>In medieval medicine, a "retentive" substance helped the body hold onto fluids or "closed" the pores and vessels.</note>, and therefore they include it in medicines made for dysentery; also, because it is drying, it effectively joins parts that have been separated. When they want it to perform its work more strongly, they mix its powder into a soft roasted egg, and then it shows its power more and greatly assists with pain of the liver. If one anoints hot abscesses with it, it is of very great benefit; likewise, it is very good for sores of the intestines and for those who spit blood, and it helps those with long-standing dysentery. If it is given to drink or administered as a clyster <note>An enema.</note>, it kills the worms that form in the intestines. The two stars—the southern and the northern—of the three located in the rear horn of the figure of **Capricorn** have power over this stone, and from them it receives its force and virtue. When they are in the ascendant, this stone demonstrates its effects most clearly.

### **Concerning the Whetstone.**

Belonging to the ninth degree of the sign of Capricorn is the **Whetstone** <term>Piedra de aguzar: literally a "sharpening stone," used for honing metal tools.</term>. This is very well known to men and is found in many places and in various colors; but the best and most noble is the green one of which this book speaks here. They call it the "oil whetstone" because its color tends toward green. It is soft, easy to break, and cold and dry by nature. If one anoints the disease called alopecia <note>Original: "lopicia," referring to hair loss.</note> with the water that comes off it when iron is sharpened, it heals the site and makes the hair grow. He who regularly drinks this water mixed with vinegar dissolves the abscess that grows in the spleen, and it helps with the illness they call "the demon" <note>Likely referring to epilepsy or severe mental distress, which were frequently attributed to demonic possession or "falling sickness" in the medieval period.</note>. If the breasts of small girls are anointed with it, it prevents them from growing, and it does the same to the private parts of young boys. If one rubs copper <note>Original: "arambre," an old term for copper or brass.</note> found on the island of Cyprus <note>Original: "Cabroz."</note> upon this stone, it greatly helps wounds that happen to men suddenly. Mixed with vinegar and natron <note>Original: "anatron," a naturally occurring soda ash.</note>, it also greatly helps with the itch, with mange, and with the sores called scrofula <note>A form of tuberculosis affecting the lymph nodes of the neck.</note>. If it is ground up and placed in the eyes, it removes the "whiteness" <note>Likely cataracts or corneal scarring.</note> that forms in them. The two stars—the first and the last—of the three in the mouth of **Capricorn** have power over this stone, and from them it receives its force and virtue. When they are in mid-heaven, this stone demonstrates its effects most completely.

<margin>(78 verso)</margin>
### **Concerning the stone they call Talc.**

Belonging to the tenth degree of the sign of Capricorn is the stone they call **Talc** <note>In medieval texts, "Talc" often refers to mica, which can be split into thin, transparent sheets, rather than the modern soft mineral talc.</note>. This is formed from the dew that descends from the air at night and settles upon the earth, forming layers one on top of the other. In Arabic, they call it *Alfath*. It also has another name in Arabic, which is *Arat Araroza*, meaning "bride's sweat" <note>Original: "suor de novia." This is a literal translation of the Arabic 'araq al-arus.</note>. Its color is like that of shells, and it is found in many places such as the land of Haruquía, Yemen, and Cyprus. When it is peeled, it shines brightly, and for this reason, in some places, they make

<column-break/>

windows for baths from it, just as if it were glass; the thinner the leaves are split, the more luminous and clear they become. It has a very wonderful virtue: if it is struck with a hammer or any other thing, it does not break except into leaves; but if it is placed in a thick woolen cloth with pebbles and shaken very vigorously, it is entirely crushed, turning into powder. With this, they "congeal" <note>In alchemy, "congeal" refers to making a liquid or spirit solid.</note> the body that has received some illness, and for this reason, they include it in the "Great Work" <note>The *Opus Magnum* or the process of creating the Philosopher's Stone.</note>. Its nature is cold and dry. If one regularly anoints any limb with it, fire will not burn it as quickly as one that was not anointed. It has the power to retain much, and therefore it stops the blood of one who spits it due to some illness; it does the same for women when they bleed more than is appropriate. Likewise, it helps with abscesses of the breasts and those that grow in the reproductive members of men, as well as those behind the ears and all manner of flesh that is corrupted by moisture. It does even more: it cleanses the sores that form on the fingertips of lepers <note>Original: "gafos," a term for those suffering from leprosy or claw-hand deformities.</note> and heals them. The southern star of the three in the mouth of the figure of **Capricorn** has power over this stone and from it receives its force and virtue. When it is in the ascendant, this stone demonstrates its effects most clearly.

<margin>(78 verso)</margin>
### **Concerning the stone Azde.**

Belonging to the eleventh degree of the sign of Capricorn is the stone they call **Azde**. Its nature is cold and dry in the second degree, and it is easy to break. it is found in many places, but the best of all is that found in the land called Milez. Its color is brown, tending a little toward yellow. It is very heavy. If it is ground and mixed with wood sawdust and then mixed with water and placed upon timbers that are cracked or that one wishes to join, it joins them so well that no sign appears of where they were split or joined. It is a stone that dries much, constricts, and removes darkness from the vision. Furthermore, mixed with water and used to anoint hot abscesses on the breasts of women, or their private parts, or the male member of men, it helps greatly, removes the pain, and heals them. The star in the right knee <note>Original: "corva," referring to the bend of the leg or knee.</note> of **Capricorn** has power over this stone and from it receives its force and virtue. When it is in mid-heaven, this stone demonstrates its effects most completely.

<margin>(79)</margin>
### **Concerning the stone named Caldamuquida.**

Belonging to the twelfth degree of the sign of Capricorn is the stone they call **Caldamuquida**. Its color is red and very clear, so that sight passes through it; but he who has sharp sight, if he looks closely at it, will see inside the figure of a deer made of yellow lines, and if it is broken into many pieces, this same figure will appear in every piece. It is strong, hard to break, and heavy. It is found in a cave called Camuy in the land named Cemhuguid, which is near the land of India. There are many other types of stones in that cave of which this book has already spoken and will speak where appropriate; but this one of which we speak is found hanging in this cave as if it were growing there, and it can be taken by hand. It is found in many shapes, some large and some small. Its nature is cold and dry, and it possesses four virtues. The first is that no one who carries it with them has ever been found drowned in water. The second is that if a man drinks the weight of one drachm of it, it purges melancholy <note>One of the four humors; an excess was thought to cause sadness or depression.</note> moderately and well. The third is that if it is hung over the abscesses that form in a man's throat, it makes them break and heal. The fourth is that he who looks at it often strengthens the sight of his eyes and heals the diseases that form in them which obstruct vision. The two stars—the northern and the southern—in the neck of the figure of **Capricorn** have power over this stone and from them it receives its force and virtue. When they are in mid-heaven, this stone demonstrates its effects most clearly.

# OF CAPRICORN.

### Concerning the stone they call Zulun. <margin>(79 verso)</margin>

Belonging to the thirteenth degree of the sign of Capricorn is the stone they call **Zulun**. This name comes from a mountain in the land called Cicopes <note>Original: "Cicopes," likely a corruption of "Cimmerians" or a reference to a mythical northern people.</note>, which means "castrated by the cold" <note>This reflects a medieval belief that extreme cold inhibited reproductive humors.</note>. This mountain is large and very high and is named Curun; the mines for this stone are found at its peak, and the stone takes its name from it. It is very heavy yet easy to break. When broken, it is found to look like coarse sand inside. Its color is black with green veins. If burned in a fire, it shrinks and becomes a very hard body, so much so that it cannot be broken except with great effort; however, it receives no other property from the fire except that it hardens. By nature, it is cold and dry in the third degree. When it is burned, they make a very good medicine from it that is highly "retentive" <note>In medieval medicine, a retentive substance helped the body hold in fluids or slowed down processes.</note> and cooling; therefore, it is good for "hot abscesses" <note>Inflammatory swellings or infections.</note> and specifically for the one called a **carbuncle** <term>Carbonclo: a severe, painful cluster of boils connected under the skin, often associated with heat in the blood.</term>; for by cooling it greatly, it prevents the abscess from forming. If it is made into powder and applied to the gums, it heals the cavities within them, as well as itching of the mouth. It is helpful against all "narrowing of the breath" <note>Likely referring to asthma or respiratory distress.</note> of whatever nature it may be. It even has another very strange virtue: if it is ground and kneaded with wine and shaped like an acorn, and placed into a woman's "nature" <note>A common medieval euphemism for the vagina or reproductive tract.</note>, it prevents her from becoming pregnant. The star located in the bent left knee of the figure of **Capricorn** has power over this stone, and from it the stone receives its strength and virtue. When it is in the ascendant, it demonstrates its effects most completely.

### Concerning the stone whose name is Capcia. <margin>(79 verso)</margin>

Belonging to the fourteenth degree of the sign of Capricorn is the stone they call **Capcia**, which means **Cappadocia**. It is a soft stone and easy to break, and it dissolves quickly in water, but not in any other substance. Its color is dark green and it has a fine substance. It is frequently found in the land of Egypt, and those who treat cloth use it, for it whitens them quickly and well. By nature, it is cold and dry. This virtue it has for whitening cloth exists of itself and against its own nature. It also stops the flow of blood in women when it occurs more than it should. It is included in medicines made to close wounds, especially those that occur in soft and moist parts of the body. This stone has no flavor at all; if it is drunk dissolved in water, it helps against pain of the bladder and stops all manner of **flux** <note>Original: "menazon," referring to dysentery or severe diarrhea.</note>. The northern star of the three located in the feathers of the right wing of the **Hen** <note>The constellation Cygnus.</note> has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its strength and virtue. When it is in mid-heaven, it shows its effects most completely.

### Concerning the stone of Sodom. <margin>(80)</margin>

Belonging to the fifteenth degree of the sign of Capricorn is the **stone of Sodom**. It is a black, dark, and porous stone, rough to the touch, yet strong and hard to break. When broken, it is found to be the same way inside. It is found in the mountains of Sodom, from which it takes its name, in mines located there; some are found large and others small, and in many shapes. By nature, it is cold and dry in the first degree. It has such virtue that if it is ground and made into a plaster and placed over the bladder, it breaks the stone that grows there; it also heals the ailment that causes urine to drip, or when a man wets the bed in his sleep. The star in the neck of the **Hen** <note>Cygnus.</note> has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its strength and virtue. When it is in mid-heaven, it shows its effects most completely.

### Concerning the stone they call Bicaruquid. <margin>(80)</margin>

Belonging to the sixteenth degree of the sign of Capricorn is the stone they call **Bicaruquid**. It is found in the land called Linar, and also in Cabroz: in both these places, it is found in wells, and when it is taken out, it is soft like wax, and afterward

<column-break/>

when the air hits it, it hardens. Its color is that of dark red ochre, and by nature it is cold in the first degree and dry in the third; therefore, the dryness in it is greater than the cold. It possesses "retentiveness" and dryness along with a certain sharpness, and its flavor is composed in that same manner; therefore, it is useful for bad and "rotten" <note>Likely meaning gangrenous or infected.</note> wounds, and especially those that form in the mouth. If the **uvula** <note>Original: "vujella."</note> is cut and this ground stone mixed with honey is applied there, it heals very quickly and protects against the dangers that usually follow the cutting of it; it also heals wounds that occur on the head or in the **rectum** <note>Original: "fondon," referring to the base or bottom of the body.</note>, and it greatly removes "excess flesh" <term>Carne sobeyana: Granulation tissue or "proud flesh" that prevents a wound from healing properly.</term>. If its powder is placed upon very thick hair, it thins it and makes it very beautiful. The star in the left shoulder of **Capricorn** has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its strength and virtue. When it is in the ascendant, it shows its effects most manifesty.

### Concerning the stone they call Bezebekaury. <margin>(80 verso)</margin>

Belonging to the seventeenth degree of the sign of Capricorn is the stone they call **Bezebekaury**. This name in Chaldean means "remover of sadness and giver of joy"; because it has such virtue that whoever carries it with them is relieved of all sadness of whatever nature it may be. It also heals all conditions that arise by reason of **melancholy** <note>In medieval medicine, melancholy was a "humor" associated with sadness, depression, and black bile.</note>. It is found in the land called Zulun near the town named Eniz where there are "men castrated by the cold." It is a stone that men love greatly for its beauty. It is always found in two colors, which are green and red, and each of them is very clear, bright, and of great splendor. By nature, it is cold and dry and strong and hard to break, yet it is light in weight. When ground, it is often included in medicines made for the heart; it also helps greatly against wounds that form in the intestines and is good for the "bloody flux" <note>Bloody diarrhea or dysentery.</note>. Two stars—the one facing north and the dark one of the three located in the front horn of the figure of **Capricorn**—have power over this stone and from it the stone receives its strength and virtue. When it is in mid-heaven, it shows its effects most completely.

### Concerning the stone whose name is Ecce. <margin>(80 verso)</margin>

Belonging to the eighteenth degree of the sign of Capricorn is the stone they call **Ecce**. This is found in Spain in a mountain above the town called Arraca; the mountain is named Cebide and is not very high. Its color is very black, speckled with yellow spots. It is shiny and light in weight, porous, and easy to break, and of a cold and dry nature. It has such virtue that whoever carries it is given great courage and has their fear removed, making them very bold in all deeds they undertake. If it is ground and kneaded with honey and used to coat glass, and then brought to the fire, it tints the glass a very beautiful gold color and strengthens it so that the glass becomes a stronger body than it was before, and it cannot be melted so easily nor does it break as lightly. If mixed with wax and resin, it makes a very good plaster for growing flesh in wounds and closing them quickly. The two front stars of the three in the bright part of the tail of the **Dolphin** <note>The constellation Delphinus.</note>—out of the four in the quadrangle on its body—have power over this stone and from it the stone receives its strength and virtue. When they are in the ascendant, it shows its effects most completely.

### Concerning the stone whose name is Guifirquizti. <margin>(81)</margin>

Belonging to the nineteenth degree of the sign of Capricorn is the stone they call **Guifirquizti**, which in Chaldean means "guardian of children," because it has such virtue that if it is placed upon children when they are born, they are protected from having **thrush** <note>Original: "maseda," an oral fungal infection common in infants.</note> or the other illnesses that usually happen to them when they are being raised. This stone resembles an acorn in shape and color. And it is found in a...

It is light in weight, yet strong and difficult to break; and when they do break it, they find inside something resembling carded wool <note>This description—a stone containing fibers like "carded wool" that resists fire—is a classic medieval description of asbestos.</note>. When it is burned, it turns to ash; if one places this ash at the root of any tree, neither frost nor any other burning heat will harm it, and it will bear its fruit in its proper time, healthy and without any defect. If given to a person to drink as a powder, it heals pain in the intestines; it likewise cures the pain of "the stone" <term>The stone: a historical term for kidney or bladder stones.</term>. ### ->Concerning the stone Tarmices. (81.)<-

Belonging to the 20th degree of the sign of Capricorn is the stone they call **Tarmices**, which in Chaldean <note>Original: "caldeo." The text frequently attributes names to ancient Chaldean, a language associated with Babylonian wisdom.</note> means "stone of the earth." This is found in a very deep well in the land named Latifi, near a place called Carcidon. The water they draw from there is turbid, very thick, and green in color; once drawn and placed in the sun, it hardens and becomes a stone of that same color. This happens in a single day, and leaving it longer does not make it harden more; after it has been polished, it acquires clarity. By nature, it is cold and dry, and very intense in these two "complexions" <note>In medieval science, a "complexion" was the specific balance of the four qualities: hot, cold, moist, and dry.</note>. It has such power that if a weight of half a drachma or more is given to drink, it dries out the whole body, shrinks the nerves, and kills. But if they knead it with wine and rub it on the body of someone with **dropsy** <term>Hidropico: a person suffering from edema or swelling caused by excess fluid in the body.</term>, it thins them in such a way that they recover well; however, if they persist too much with this, it dries them more than is appropriate, leading to death. It also has the property that whoever carries it will never sweat, nor will much moisture grow within them. The last of the three stars between the bright star of the dolphin's tail and the four of its triangle has power over this stone and gives it its virtue. When it is in the midheaven, this stone shows its works most completely.

### ->Concerning the stone that appears in the sea when Saturn rises. (81 verso.)<-

Belonging to the 21st degree of the sign of Capricorn is the stone that appears in the sea when Saturn rises and hides when it sets. This is found in the **Tenebrous Sea** <note>The Atlantic Ocean, often called the "Sea of Darkness" in medieval maps.</note> where other stones are found that clearly show the power of the other planets, as we have already said. Its color is very black and clear. It is always found in the shape of a pinecone. It is very dense, strong, and hard to break; when broken, it is found to be white inside. However, this whiteness is only visible with great difficulty, and only when the planet is above the earth; when the planet is below, the whiteness cannot be seen. By nature, it is cold and dry, and it has such power that he who carries it lives long and does not suffer the diseases or weaknesses that other old men have; instead, he remains with his "sex" <note>Likely referring to sexual potency or vitality.</note> and his strength as long as he lives. It has another very strange power: if a man or woman looks into it as if into a mirror, it greatly strengthens their sight; but if any other animal does so, it loses its sight. The forward star of the two in the belly of Capricorn has power over this stone and gives it its strength and virtue. When it is in the "ascendant" <note>The point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon.</note>, it shows its works most.

### ->Concerning the stone of the Blue. (81 verso.)<-

Belonging to the 22nd degree of the sign of Capricorn is the stone of the **Blue** <note>Original: "Azul," referring here to Lapis Lazuli.</note>. This is very well known and is found in many places. Its color is a very deep purple-blue, and the largest of all are those found in the land of Khorasan. The most prized is that in which veins or drops of gold color appear. It is easy to break, and when placed near gold or mixed with it, each appears more beautiful on its own. Its virtue is such that if its powder is placed in the

<column-break/>

eyes, it helps greatly; likewise, by placing a piece of it in a fire that is without smoke, a purple flame rises from it, and it receives great heat and sharpness, even though its nature is cold and dry. It also receives the power of "retention." If its powder is given to drink, it purges all "thick humors" and is good against any illness caused by **melancholy** <term>Malanconía: one of the four humors, associated with black bile, believed to cause sadness or sluggishness if in excess.</term>. It also has the power to cause a woman’s "flower" <note>A euphemism for the menstrual cycle.</note> to come at the proper time, both by drinking it or by applying it locally; it also helps with bladder pain. It does another thing: if mixed with water and used to wash the head, it makes the hair curly. It is a stone much used in the work of **physic** <term>Física: the medieval science of medicine and natural philosophy.</term>. The last of the two stars on the spine of Capricorn has power over this stone and gives it its virtue. When it is in the ascendant, this stone shows its works most completely.

### ->Concerning the stone they call Melizlumen in Chaldean. (82.)<-

Belonging to the 23rd degree of the sign of Capricorn is the stone they call **Melizlumen** in Chaldean, which means "the stone that breaks the other that grows in man." By nature, it is cold and dry, and when broken, a substance like glass is found inside. It is found on the shore of the Western Sea, for the waves cast it onto the bank. It is always found in the form of a **lozenge** <term>Trocisco: a small, medicinal tablet or cake shape.</term> containing tiny grains like sand. Its virtue is such that if a weight of one drachma is given to drink, it breaks the stone that forms in the kidneys or the bladder and causes it to be expelled as fine sand. It is also used frequently in powders made for the eyes. It does yet another thing: if given to drink to a beast that has "olives" <note>Original: "olivas." Likely referring to hard swellings, cysts, or stones in livestock.</note>, it heals. The southern star of the three in the wing feathers of the right wing of the Hen <note>The constellation Cygnus.</note> has power over this stone and gives it its strength and virtue. When it is in the midheaven, this stone shows its works most.

### ->Concerning the stone they call Alfeyru in Chaldean. (82.)<-

Belonging to the 24th degree of the sign of Capricorn is the stone they call **Alfeyru** in Chaldean, and others call it **Feynac** <note>This description—light, porous, and floating on water—identifies the stone as pumice.</note>. This is found in many places, but the best of all is found on a mountain in the land of Sicily called Vulcan <note>Referring to Mount Etna.</note>, and also in the land of Armenia. It is very porous and so light in weight that it floats on water just like wood. It is easy to break, and its color is white tending toward gray; its nature is cold and dry. When ground and its powder is rubbed on skins, it makes them white and beautiful. If its powder is cast upon parchment, it erases the writing upon it so that no sign remains; it also cleans the teeth and makes them white and beautiful. It also helps to remove "whiteness from the eyes" <note>Likely referring to cataracts or corneal scarring.</note> when used with other medicines made for them, but not on its own. It has another property: if placed in a vat or jar or other vessel containing wine at the time it is boiling most vigorously, it causes it to stop instantly. It makes flesh grow in wounds and removes hair from any place it is applied, as well as from the soles of the feet when carried upon them in the bath. The forward star of the two that lower toward the south and are at the root of the tail of the figure of Capricorn has power over this stone and gives it its virtue. When it is in the midheaven, this stone shows its works most completely.

There are some that tend toward red in color, and others that are a mix of red and white. It is found in many places, and there are many mines for it. By nature, it is cold and dry.
