### **Concerning the stone they call Queyebiz.** (82 verso.)

Belonging to the 26th degree of the sign of Capricorn is the stone they call **Queyebiz**, which is called in Latin *azul arambrenno* <note>original: "azul arambrenno," meaning "copper blue" or azurite.</note>; it is so named because it is the color of blue, though it is darker and harder than the other blue stone we mentioned previously, and drops of copper appear within it just as drops of gold appear in the other. When it is broken, the inside is found to be a violet color mixed with yellow; for this reason, they use it to dye wood a violet color, though it is not as fine a dye as that of the other blue stone. By nature, it is cold and dry, and therefore has great power to cool and to restrain humors. It is included in medicines made for the eyes, and it heals hot swellings <term>Hot swellings: inflammatory abscesses or "postemas."</term> as well as sores that form on the body; it also whitens the teeth and heals sores that form on the gums. It is used in the "Great Work" <note>A reference to alchemy or advanced metallurgy.</note> in this manner: when it is burned and added to gold while it is melting, it softens the metal so that it may be hammered out very easily and gives it a fine color. It likewise dyes silver the color of gold, though this does not last very long. The leading star of the two located in the belly of the Fish <note>The figure of Capricorn is often depicted as a sea-goat: half-goat, half-fish.</note> that faces toward the south has power over this stone, and from it the stone receives its strength and virtue. When this star is in the midheaven, this stone demonstrates its effects most fully.

### **Concerning the stone they call Nimiuz.** (83.)

Belonging to the 27th degree of the sign of Capricorn is the stone they call **Nimiuz**. Its color is green, and it is strong and hard to break, and rough to the touch. It is found on the island of Zarandun <note>Possibly a reference to Sarandib or Sri Lanka, famous for gems.</note>, and they use it to sharpen iron tools and polish stones. Any stone or iron polished or sharpened upon it receives its edge or polish very easily. They find very large specimens, such that they make pillars from them in that land, as well as cauldrons and pots in which they prepare food, and bowls and vessels from which they eat and drink; anything placed within it to cook boils quickly and with little fire. The foods prepared in it heal those who eat them of hemorrhoids and arthritic gout. By nature, it is cold and dry. The two stars—the first of the four located to the north at the root of the tail of Capricorn—have power over this stone, and from them it receives its strength and virtue. When these stars are in the midheaven, this stone demonstrates its effects most fully.

### **Concerning the stone named Caoz.** (83.)

Belonging to the 28th degree of the sign of Capricorn is the stone they call **Caoz**. Its color is black tending toward red. It is smooth on the outside and light in weight, yet strong and difficult to break; when it is broken, it appears inside like a very fine dust. It is always found in the shape of an almond. This name we have 

<column-break/>

mentioned is Greek <note>original: "caoz," likely from the Greek "chous," meaning soil or dust.</note>, and it means "stone of the earth," because they find it in the heart of the earth as if it had been placed there, and it is most commonly found in the land named Beimini. Some are large and others small. By nature, it is cold and dry. Its virtue is such that if the dust found inside it is mixed with glass at the moment of melting, the glass does not break when it is removed from the fire as other glass does; rather, it can be stretched by hammering and survives every blow of the hammer, and they can make from it whatever work they desire, just as with gold or silver, and it does not lose its clarity. This stone has the color of vinegar, and when placed on the tongue, it sticks to it; it dries the moistures of the nature of women, and it closes and heals wounds. It also cures sores that form in the intestines. The last star of the two located in the mouth of the "Piece of the Horse" <note>The constellation Equuleus, the Little Horse.</note> has power over this stone, and from it the stone receives its strength and virtue. When this star is in the ascendant, this stone shows its effects most manifested.

### **Concerning the stone named Sayastuz.** (83 verso.)

Belonging to the 29th degree of the sign of Capricorn is the stone they call **Sayastuz**. This stone has the color of yellow jargon <note>A variety of zircon.</note>, and it is very clear and very bright, such that sight passes through it, and it is of a beautiful yellowness, though it tends somewhat toward white. It is found in the river that flows near the town called Armuniaqui. This river rises in the south and flows toward the north, and from where it begins to flow until it enters the sea is two hundred miles <note>original: "migeros," a medieval measurement of distance.</note>, and there they are found. By nature, it is cold and dry. It has such virtue that if it is thrown into anything that is boiling, it cools it immediately. Furthermore, it causes whoever carries it to lose all desire for women. Remarkably, none of those who have carried it have been found to die by the sword. If it is ground and mixed with the juice of green coriander, it dissolves and turns into the substance of the juice; if a bite from a viper or a rabid dog is anointed with that water, it heals immediately; and if the same is done to wounds as they are closing, no scar remains. The two stars—the one declining toward the south and the other at the end of the tail of Capricorn, among the four located there—have power over this stone and from them it receives its virtue. When they are in the ascendant, this stone demonstrates its effects most clearly.

### **Concerning the stone Fanaquid.** (83 verso.)

Belonging to the 30th degree of the sign of Capricorn is the stone they call **Fanaquid**. This is found in a lagoon located between the land of those "castrated by the cold" <note>A medieval geographical reference to people living in the extreme, frozen north.</note> and the other land called Cerciuniz. The water of that lagoon has such virtue that any wood thrown into it sinks to the bottom, and this stone is found at the bottom of that water in the shape and color of a very bright and clear human eye. By nature, it is cold and dry and very hard, such that no other substance can break it except for glass. This is a very great marvel of nature: that a substance as weak as glass can break something as strong as this stone. Its virtue is such that it affects wild beasts in the same way the stone called **Beth**—mentioned elsewhere in this book—affects humans: for any beast that sees it takes such great pleasure in gazing at it that it never moves from that spot until it dies, unless it is removed from there by force. No other virtue has been found for this stone except this one. The last star of the two located in the head of the "Piece of the Horse" <note>The constellation Equuleus.</note> has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its virtue. Therefore, when this star is in the midheaven, this stone demonstrates its effects most fully.

->OF THE SIGN<-

# OF THE SIGN OF AQUARIUS.

---

### PROLOGUE (85.)

The thirty types of stones according to the thirty degrees of the sign of Capricorn have been described, and it has been shown which stars they are linked to and from where they receive their power. Therefore, it is appropriate that whoever wishes to work with these matters should pay attention to the planet Saturn, as we have said regarding the other planets.

### Concerning the stone they call Carbedic. (85.)

From the first degree of the sign of Aquarius comes the stone they call **Carbedic** <note>original: "Carbedic"</note>. This is counted among the stones of animal origin, because in the mountain called Culequin, which is in the land of Macedonia, there are very large hares; when they kill some of them before they are a year old, they find in the heart a stone of white color with a very bright red drop. It is a stone without luster and is hot and moist in nature in the second degree. Its virtue is such that he who carries it with him warms his body so strongly that the cold of winter does not harm him as much as it would another who does not carry it, and it gives great power to lie with women. If they grind this stone and mix it with wine and place it upon hard swellings—such as cancer or others that are of a melancholy nature <note>In medieval medicine, "melancholy" refers to an excess of black bile, thought to cause cold, dry tumors.</note>—they heal in a short time. The star located in the head of Aquarius has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its virtue. When this star is in the ascendant, the stone demonstrates its works most clearly.

### Concerning the stone called Maruira. (85.)

From the second degree of the sign of Aquarius comes the stone they call **Maruira**. This is found in the land of Africa on the seashore where there is a great beach. It is very green and without luster, and it is strong and hard to break; when they do break it, they find it white inside, and that whiteness is easy to scrape away. If they give between one and two drachms <note>A drachm was a classical unit of weight, roughly 3.5 grams.</note> of it to drink, it temperately purges phlegm. They find both large and small ones. If they dissolve it with water and wash the head with it, it removes dandruff and lice, and makes the hair very beautiful and smooth; likewise, it makes hair grow in places where it was pulled out by disease or other causes. It has yet another virtue: by anointing limbs that have weakened due to disease in the nerves, it heals them and restores their power and strength; those that are bad and difficult to move are softened and made to move easily. When they burn this stone, it turns black and becomes porous, and then they use it in the "greater work" <note>likely a reference to alchemy or advanced medicinal preparations.</note>. The southern star of the two located in the left flank of the one who draws water in the figure of Aquarius <note>Aquarius, the Water-Bearer.</note> has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its virtue. When it is in mid-heaven, this stone demonstrates its works most completely.

### Concerning the stone of the Esponia. (85 verso.)

From the third degree of the sign of Aquarius comes the stone of the **Esponia** <note>likely "Spongia" or a fossilized coral/sponge stone</note>. These are found in many places and in many forms, and

<column-break/>

those found in the Promised Land are small and very hard pebbles. Its color is that of a jujube <note>a dark reddish-brown fruit</note>, and its nature is hot and moist; its moisture is in the first degree and its heat in the third; therefore, it dries more than it moistens. If they give it to drink, it breaks the stone that forms in the bladder, but not those of the kidneys. It has another property: if placed in water, it moves away from it as if it hates it. But if mixed with any kind of oil, it incorporates with it and becomes one thing; if applied this way to the teeth, it heals the sores found in them; likewise, it treats mange and itching and removes their pain. If they heat it and pour it into the ear, it stops the noise made there and dries up the water and the venom <note>often used here to mean infected fluid or pus</note> enclosed within, and prevents an abscess from forming. The last star of the two located in the right foot of the Hen <note>The constellation Cygnus</note> has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its strength and virtue. When it is in the ascendant, this stone demonstrates its works most clearly.

### Concerning the stone they call Mezarigez. (85 verso.)

From the fourth degree of the sign of Aquarius comes the stone they call **Mezarigez**, which in Chaldean <note>An ancient Semitic language associated with Babylon and astrology.</note> means "cooker of meat." Its virtue is such that if they put a little of it with meat when they set it to cook in a pot or other vessel, it makes it cook quickly. If anyone eats of that meat, it strengthens their limbs and removes the fear of the spirits of life, providing comfort and giving boldness. Its nature is hot and moist, and it is strong and hard to break. It is always found in a round form. It is sandy and of a green color that leans toward purple. It is clear and bright in such a way that sight passes through it, and they find it on the island called Mata on the seashore, wrapped in the sand, and it glows at night all around itself. If they grind it and give it to drink, it is useful against all toxins, whether from animals or plants; likewise, it helps with tremors and weakness of the heart. The northern star of the two located in the left flank of the figure of Aquarius has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its strength and virtue. When it is in the ascendant, this stone demonstrates its works most completely.

### Concerning the stone they call Zarukutaz. (86.)

From the fifth degree of the sign of Aquarius comes the stone they call **Zarukutaz**, which means "golden stone"; this is because in that land of Cabeduhya near the town called Limebi there is a cave, and inside it is a mine where they find these stones, some large and others small. They resemble pieces of gold in color, luster, and in every appearance. It is strong and hard to break; but when they break it by force, they find it inside like leaves <note>suggesting a flaky or foliated structure</note>, and it cannot be ground unless it is first burned in fire; once burned, it grinds very well. If they take one part of the ground stone after it is burned and mix it with twenty parts of silver, it turns the silver a very beautiful gold color so that it cannot be distinguished from gold in any way unless it is melted many times. Its nature is hot and moist. If they steep a little of it in a lot of water and put in any cloth...

And this stone, whether burnt or raw, is used in the medicines made for the chest and opens the pathways of the lungs. ### **Concerning the stone they call Yarminez. (86.)**

From the sixth degree of the sign of Aquarius is the stone they call **Yarminez**. And the mines where it is found are in the land of Isfahan <note>original: "Espahen," a city in modern-day Iran</note> and in that of Cabroz. It is a very porous stone, light in weight, rough to the touch, and easy to break. Its color is blue, but not very dark; and if put into the fire it burns; however, despite this, it loses none of its appearance, except that it becomes more full of holes. By nature, it is hot and moist in the third degree. It has the power to retain and to drive away humors, and it is very helpful for stomach pain. And if it is dissolved in water and raisins are placed therein, it makes them fresh again as they were before. And it does the same for all kinds of fruit; for it does not let them spoil or rot, but rather keeps them always in that state they were in when they were placed in it. And if clothes containing gold—which cannot be cleaned by other means—are washed with this water, it cleans them very well so that they lose none of their beauty. And the dark star of the two located in the right shoulder of the figure of Aquarius has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its virtue. And when it is in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works most completely.

### **Concerning the stone they call Maciuquez. (86 reverse.)**

From the seventh degree of the sign of Aquarius is the stone they call **Maciuquez**. This is found on Mount Sinai. It is strong and hard to break, and of a brown color that leans somewhat toward yellow, and it contains within it the figure of a green tree; when it is broken into many pieces, this figure appears in every one of them. By nature, it is hot and moist. And if it is ground and applied to old wounds, it makes them close in a short time. And if it is mixed with wax and resin, it is even better for this purpose. And it has yet another very noble virtue: that they never found a man who carried it with him who failed in his business, and for this reason the people of the Land of Promise <note>The Holy Land/Palestine</note> always keep it guarded in their chests and among their treasures. And the bright star of the two located on the right shoulder of the figure of Aquarius has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its virtue. And when it is in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works most completely.

### **Concerning the stone that draws out Poison. (86 reverse.)**

From the eighth degree of the sign of Aquarius is the stone that draws out poison <note>original: "tosico," meaning toxic poison or venom</note>. This is of a yellow color spotted with black drops. By nature, it is hot and moist, light in weight, porous, strong, and hard to break, such that it cannot be broken except with great labor. It has some luster in itself; but if it is polished, it receives more. And when it is broken, in every piece made of it, they find yellow color with black spots inside just as on the outside. And this stone is of such a nature that when it is put in the fire, the fire is enclosed within it and it burns, though not as much nor for as long as the others we have mentioned. And its virtue is such that when it is placed in anything given to eat or drink that contains poison—whether it be animal, vegetable, or mineral—it draws out that portion of the poison just as a magnet <term>aimante|lodestone or magnet</term> draws iron, and absorbs it into itself. And if the stone is small and the poison is great, so that it cannot draw it all at once or twice, it draws it in three or more times; and to prove how much it draws each time, they act in this manner:

<column-break/>

after the stone has drawn out what it could, they place it in hot oil and as much poison as it drew out will emerge from it; then they return it to the poison again, and so on until they understand that no more comes out of it. And the ancients discovered this test so that if someone were poisoned, they might know the quantity of the poison given to them and might know more certainly and better how to cure them. And it does even more: if it is placed at the mouth of someone who has eaten or drunk poison, it makes them vomit it up immediately; and it does the same if someone is wounded by a viper or a scorpion and it is placed upon the wound. And the two stars—the one that is the latter of the two in the hip, and the northern one of the two in the left leg of the figure of Aquarius—have power over this stone and from them it receives its strength and virtue. And when they are in the ascendant, this stone shows its works most completely.

### **Concerning the stone named Yaymeni. (87.)**

From the ninth degree of the sign of Aquarius is the stone they call **Yaymeni**. This is found in a mountain in the western part of Spain called Haymeniz. This is a very high mountain that extends all the way to the sea. It is strong and hard to break, and rough to the touch; inside it is blue in color but not as clear as the part that leans toward yellow. By nature, it is hot and moist in the third degree, and it is good for rubbing over marble or other stones that one wishes to make flat and polished. Likewise, its powder is good for the teeth; for by rubbing it upon them, it whitens them and makes them very beautiful. And if a specific quantity is given to a man to drink, it purges the choler <note>Yellow bile, one of the four humors</note>. And if it is mixed with the pitch used to seal wineskins or other things, it protects the wine so it does not spoil. It is also used much in the cerates <note>waxy salves</note> made to close wounds. And the two stars—the one in the right liver <note>original: "higada," likely referring to the side or flank of the constellation figure</note> and the other southern one of the two in the left leg of the figure of Aquarius—have power over this stone and from them it receives its strength and virtue. And when they are in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works most.

### **Concerning the stone they call Cahadeniz. (87.)**

From the tenth degree of the sign of Aquarius is the stone they call **Cahadeniz**. This is found in the mountain called Zahyt, and it takes its name from there. This mountain is in the land called Cappadocia <note>original: "Cabeduquia," in modern-day Turkey</note>. It is a mineral stone, easy to break, and of a violet color, but somewhat dark. And when it is burnt, it becomes light and porous. It is hot and moist by nature. It is good for rubbing the skins used to make parchment for writing or painting. And if it is mixed with the medicines made for stomach pain, it is very helpful. And if its powder is placed in the eyes of one who has "clear eyes" but cannot see at night <note>Likely referring to night blindness or certain types of cataracts</note>, it greatly strengthens the sight and heals them. And the northern star of the two joined stars in the head of the Greater Horse <note>Pegasus</note> has power over this stone and from it the stone receives its virtue. And when it is in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works most clearly.

### **Concerning the stone named Yamez. (87 reverse.)**

From the eleventh degree of the sign of Aquarius is the stone they call **Yamez**. This is found in the mines of the land named Jurgen and in those of Canahá which are in the land of Yemen <note>original: "Liemen"</note>; these are the best and most prized, and most of them are large, and they make of them whatever shape they wish. Its color is white, leaning toward crystal, except that a very hidden redness appears in it when one looks at it very closely. By nature, it is hot and moist. And it has such virtue that whoever carries it with him feels secure and without fear, and it heals headaches and the noise that is made within the head <note>Tinnitus</note>. And if a known quantity is given to drink, it purges melancholy; and it is good against every illness that comes by reason...

### **Concerning the stone they call Menefix. (87 verso.)**

From the twelfth degree of the sign of Aquarius is the stone they call **Menefix**. This is found on the banks of a river that flows near the town named Hulven. ### **Concerning the stone named Meixineriz. (88.)**

From the thirteenth degree of the sign of Aquarius is the stone they call **Meixineriz**. By nature, it is hot and moist, and of a gray color spotted with green drops. It is light in weight, rough to the touch, and easy to break. It is found in the western part of Spain on top of a very high mountain named Carcith. ### **Concerning the stone they call Zarbenic. (88.)**

From the fourteenth degree of the sign of Aquarius is the stone they call **Zarbenic** <note>Also spelled Zarbeninenic in the text</note>, which means in Chaldean <note>original: "caldeo"; likely referring to Aramaic or Syriac</note> "healer of fright and of the paralysis of the limbs." It is found in the land called Alcarach, where there are many mines of it. When they put it in the fire, it traps the heat within itself and burns, but not as much as the other stone we mentioned. And if they grind it and throw it into deep wounds, it makes the flesh grow back in them quickly and evenly. It even has another power by which it can be known among all other stones: if they put it in blood, it mixes with it and takes on its nature. And the two stars of the three in the final right palm, and the northernmost of the three in the final turn—all being in Aquarius—have power over this stone and from them it receives its strength and virtue. ### **Concerning the stone they call Romana. (88 verso)**

### **Concerning the stone that appears in the sea. (89.)**

It brightens when Saturn sets and becomes cloudy when it rises. By nature, it is hot and moist. It has a very bad power within it: if anyone looks at it when Saturn is below the earth, they go blind, though looking at it while the star is above the earth does no harm. And when it is in the ascendant, this stone shows more strength in its works.

### **Concerning the stone they call Meciena. <gloss>(89 verso.)</gloss>**

From the twentieth degree of the sign of Aquarius is the stone they call **Meciena**, which in the Chaldean language means "stone of weeping"; for it has such a virtue that he who carries it with him is always sad and tearful. If it is placed in someone's bed and they sleep upon it, it will do the same; and if they give it to someone to drink, the same will happen to whoever drinks it; therefore, it is a stone much hated by those who know it. It is strong and hard to break and shines in such a way that sight passes through it. Its color is gray and it has yellow lines in it that seem to intertwine with one another. It is found in the islands of India on the banks of a river that flows through them called Careth. By nature, it is hot and moist. And the two stars—the northern and the southern of those that follow the flowing water of the second turn in the figure of Aquarius—have power over this stone and from them it receives its virtue. And when it is in the ascendant, this stone shows its works more completely.

### **Concerning the stone named Cidadenna. <gloss>(90.)</gloss>**

From the twenty-first degree of the sign of Aquarius is the stone they call **Cidadenna**. By nature, it is hot and moist. Its mines are near the town called Aterbuliz, which is in the land of Furunia. Its color is purple, tending somewhat toward yellow. Some are large and others small and of many shapes. This stone clears up in bright weather and becomes cloudy when it is overcast. According to the word of the sages, any stone that changes its color is of a poor substance. In this stone, there is a certain amount of gold enclosed; so much so that when it is melted, the gold is found at the bottom of the crucible in which they melt it. Its virtue is such that whoever carries it with him is feared by all who see him. If they grind it and put its powder in the eyes, it heals the "sarna" <note>A term for various skin or eye irritations, such as blepharitis or scabies</note> that forms there in a short time. And the two stars—one being the last of the two that follow the first turn of the water, and the other a solitary star far to the south after the second turn of that water, both being in Aquarius—have power over this stone and from them it receives its virtue. And when they are in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works more.

### **Concerning the stone that pulls salt. <gloss>(90.)</gloss>**

From the twenty-second degree of the sign of Aquarius is the stone that pulls salt. By nature, it is hot and moist. It has such a virtue that if it is placed near salt, it pulls it just as other magnets pull those

<column-break/>

things over which they have power. Indeed, this one has even greater strength in its pulling; for it pulls from further away than the others and twice its own weight. Its color is a pale yellow and it is spotted with white drops. It is dark in such a way that sight does not pass through it, and it is porous and light in weight. If they put it into any liquid thing in which there was salt, it draws it all out regardless of its nature, provided the thing in which it is placed is cold; if it is hot, it does not do this. And after it has drawn out the salt, if it is placed in water that is cold, it becomes as if hot; likewise, throwing it into seawater removes its saltiness and makes it good to drink. This stone is named **Alardo** and is found in the Promised Land on the shores of the sea near the place where the river called Alardo falls into it. If ground and placed in the eyes of one whose eyelashes are falling out, it prevents them from falling and makes them grow back. And the northern star of the three in the third turn of the water of the sign of Aquarius has power over this stone and from it receives its virtue. And when it is in the ascendant, this stone shows its works more.

### **Concerning the stone they call Delmenica. <gloss>(90 verso.)</gloss>**

From the twenty-third degree of the sign of Aquarius is the stone they call in Chaldean **Delmenicari**, which means as much as "healer of deafness"; for it has such a virtue that if a deaf man carries it, regardless of the nature of his deafness, he is healed. By nature, it is hot and moist in the third degree, and of the color of red ochre <note>Original: *almagra*, a deep earthy red</note>, except that it is more tinted, stronger, harder, more shining, and very heavy. If it is burned, a smoke rises from it that has a very strong and sharp smell, so much so that it can hardly be endured; but after it is burned, it becomes light and very porous. If they grind it and mix it with oil and put it in the ear, it takes away deafness and benefits all the illnesses that occur there. The mine of this stone is on the Island of Dragen far out at sea; this island is in the great sea they call the Ocean in the western part near the edge where no men dwell. And the middle star of the three in the third turn of the flowing water of the sign of Aquarius has power over this stone and from it receives its virtue. And when it is in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works more.

### **Concerning the stone they call Secutaz. <gloss>(90 verso.)</gloss>**

From the twenty-fourth degree of the sign of Aquarius is the stone they call **Secutaz**; it takes this name from a river where it is found called Secut, which is in the land of Ethiopia, and they are found at the bottom of it. Some of them are large and others small, and of long and round shape. It is hollowed out like a reed and its color is like a pomegranate grain, which is very clear and bright, and sight passes through it. It is light in weight but strong and hard to break, so that no other body breaks it except silver, by its nature; when they wish to do any work with it, they first make a saw or a chisel of silver with which they cut it; then they can make of it whatever shape they wish very easily. No other stone can affect it except the diamond alone. By nature, it is hot and moist; but there is more heat in it than moisture. It has such a virtue that he who carries it set in silver does not suffer nocturnal emissions in his dreams, and if he has them due to some illness, carrying it heals him. It does the same if they make a plaster of it and place it over the bite of a rabid dog or another poisonous beast. And the last star of the two joined stars after the second turn of the water has power over this stone and from it receives its virtue. And when it is in the ascendant, this stone shows its works more.

From the twenty-fifth degree of the sign of Aquarius is the stone that is made in the spine of the sea snail. This is counted among those of animal origin. By nature, it is hot and moist; but it has more dryness in it than moisture. Its color is gray and it is rough to the...

### Concerning the stone whose name is Seralicen. <gloss>(91.)</gloss>

Of the twenty-sixth degree of the sign of Aquarius is the stone they call **Seralicen** in Chaldean, which means in that language "dissolver of the spleen." And this resembles the shape and color of a human spleen. It has such virtue that he who wears it bound upon himself is healed of every ailment of the spleen, and it removes the thirst that comes from such disease, and he is sure not to have it as long as he carries it with him. It is light, porous, and easy to break. Its best mines are in the eastern part of Spain along the seacoasts. ### Concerning the stone that is formed in the spine of the Marine Crab. <gloss>(91 verso.)</gloss>

Of the twenty-seventh degree of the sign of Aquarius is the stone that is formed in

### Concerning the stone they call Kedunaz. <gloss>(91 verso.)</gloss>

Of the twenty-eighth degree of the sign of Aquarius is the stone they call **Kedunaz**. This is found on a mountain called Kedun, from which it takes its name. And its mines are found in the land named Milez. It is soft and dark and of a brown color spotted with green drops; it is heavy, and when they burn it, a smell comes from it that smells like when they roast fatty meat. By nature, it is hot and moist. And if they grind it after it is burned and anoint corrosive wounds with it, they heal. Furthermore, giving it to a man to drink takes away his sense and understanding, and makes him forgetful just as if he were drunk. And if he drinks much of it, he dies. And the trailing star of the two joined stars in the chest of the Horse has power over this stone and from it receives its virtue. And when it is in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works more completely.

# OF THE SIGN OF PISCES.

---

### Concerning the stone they call Bezcuiden. <gloss>(92.)</gloss>

Of the twenty-ninth degree of the sign of Pisces <note>Though listed under the header for Pisces, this entry likely concludes the sequence for the final degrees of the previous sign or initiates a transitional phase</note> is the stone they call **Rezquiden**. By nature, it is cold and moist. It is found in the land of Babylon in mines located in the great wildernesses. Its color is yellow spotted with white drops, and it is strong and hard to break, heavy, and so shiny that the sight passes through it. The virtue of this stone is the opposite of the other we mentioned in the aforementioned degree; for he who carries it with him is loved and feared by all who see him, and they speak well of him. And if they grind it and give it to be drunk, it removes the foul appetite of those who eat earth or clay <note>A condition known as pica</note> which occurs by reason of melancholy <note>An excess of "black bile," believed to cause depression and strange cravings</note>. And the trailing star of the three small ones in the head of the last fish in the figure of Pisces has power over this stone and from it receives its strength and virtue. And when it is in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works more completely.

<column-break/>

### Concerning the stone whose name is Yethbeniel. <gloss>(92.)</gloss>

Of the thirtieth degree of the sign of Pisces is the stone they call **Yethbeniel**. Its color is a very deep red, and it has very subtle purple lines within it. It is so shiny that the sight passes through it. It is frequently found in the land named Quebeliz. By nature, it is cold and moist. Its virtue is such that whoever carries it with him is greatly feared by all who see him, and he shall have no ailment in the belly nor in the intestines; for this reason, it is much loved by men, and also for its beauty. Between this stone and the Ruby <note>original: "Robin"</note>, there is great enmity, such that if they are placed together, each one damages itself and breaks. And the southern star of the two that are in the belly of the last fish in the figure of Pisces has power over this stone and from it receives its strength and virtue. And when it is in mid-heaven, this stone shows its works more completely.

# ON THE FACES OF THE SIGNS.

---

<page-num>94</page-num>
## PROLOGUE.

The thirty types of stones according to the thirty degrees of the sign of Pisces have been described, and it has been shown with which stars they have their connection, and from where they receive their strength and virtue. Therefore, it is necessary that whoever wishes to work with this book should pay heed to the planet Jupiter—that it be in a good state for works of good, and in the contrary for works of evil; for this is a general rule for all the planets and the fixed stars, and for the stones that are in accord with them. And it is the same for herbs and animals; for all have virtue and strength which they receive from God by the hand of His angels, and through the power of the heavens and the stars that are within them, and afterward from the four elements; and so it continues until every thing reaches its birth, growth, and maintenance through this power. 

Therefore, since we have shown through this book—which Abolays <note>Abolays is cited as the original author of the ancient source Alfonso X's scholars translated; he likely represents a Hellenistic or Arabic astrological tradition</note> composed from the sayings of the ancient sages who organized by true reasoning the virtue that stones receive from the thirty degrees of the twelve signs, each one according to the power of that degree which has strength over it—it is now appropriate that we speak from here forward of the virtue that stones have according to how the sun passes through the **faces** <term>faces: also known as decans, these are ten-degree subdivisions of a zodiac sign</term> of the signs and the figures of the stars that are within them. Furthermore, we shall speak of the times in which they possess that virtue most completely and when it changes from one manner to another, according to the shifting and diversity found in the constellations of the stars within the faces of those signs. These stars are beyond counting, nor could anyone name them or identify them except for God who made them, as King David showed through the Holy Spirit while praising God, saying:
> "He who counts the multitude of the stars and calls each by its name." <note>Original Latin context: Psalm 147:4</note>

And for this reason, when the sun passes through the faces of the signs, or any of the other six planets, the stone receives virtue from the rays that descend from the figures of the stars directly corresponding to the face of that sign. Just as the positions of the figures change, so too do all things change that receive virtue from them, both the living and those without souls. For as Ptolemy <note>Claudius Ptolemy, the 2nd-century astronomer whose work formed the basis of medieval science</note> and the other masters of the art of astronomy said, all the strength and virtue sent by the heavens and the stars upon the things below them depends on those things being prepared to act: some to receive, which they call **matter**, and others to act, which they call **form**. Therefore, the bodies below are low, and through their mixing with one another, they all become like one heavy and solid thing; thus they are made of "vile" <note>In the medieval sense, meaning "common" or "terrestrial" rather than "evil"</note> matter, and they always love to receive strength from the virtue of the high and noble celestial bodies. And although they always have this virtue within them—for they could not be made or maintained without it—nevertheless, they receive it more when they are prepared and in a state to receive it completely. 

The example of this is like the development of a man: when he is a child, even though his soul is complete—as much as a thing can be that has no fixed form and extends through all the forms of the bodies it enters—nevertheless, because the limbs of the child are not as complete as they should be, nor is his earthly matter fully prepared to receive the celestial form, he cannot perform as many works as when he is at the age to have all his full strength. For then, the matter finds in the form exactly what it desires: the one in receiving, and the other in giving.

<column-break/>

And therefore, a child does not have such great strength when he is small as when he is a boy; nor a boy as when he is a youth, and so on until he becomes a complete man. And this same thing happens in all other things, not only in animals, but even in plants (meaning trees and herbs), and in stones and all other metals; for they do not have such great virtue when they are being born as when they are fully formed, because their matter is not yet prepared to receive the entire form completely. Thus, they have greater virtue when they are in that state they ought to reach than when they are beginning to rise toward it or when they are already descending. 

Therefore, every man who wishes to work with these noble and ancient knowledges must pay attention to these reasons that have been stated; for through them, he will understand and see with knowledge how things are made, composed, and bound to one another, and at what time their virtue grows, and when they have the greatest power to act, and when their works appear most manifest. According to this, he will be better able to use them for what he needs and more completely. 

Furthermore, we wish to say what these "faces" are and why they have such a name. This is demonstrated by three divisions found in the figure of every sign, representing the beginning, the middle, and the end. Each of these three parts, which are called faces, has ten degrees; and in this way, there are thirty degrees in each sign, making thirty-six faces in total across the twelve signs which contain three hundred and sixty degrees. And these are called "faces" because whoever wishes to count them all together cannot do so except one by one; therefore, the one they first begin to count is as if it appeared first, and for this reason, they call it a "face." 

And just as we said of the stones that have a connection to and receive virtue from the figures in the degrees of the signs, likewise those same stones and others have strength and virtue that they receive specifically from the figures in each of the faces. For although the stones show virtue through the figures of the degrees as has been said, they must change in another way according to the movement of the other figures in the faces, because of the virtue and property within them. Therefore, it is appropriate that we first state which stone it is, and afterward, which figure it receives its strength and virtue from. And now we shall return to the first subject to speak of the stones and their virtues by the faces of the signs, and we shall speak first of the sign of Aries, which is the beginning of all the others.

### **Of the White Zircon.** (96 reverse.) <note>original: *Yargonza blanca*</note>

From the first face <term>face: a ten-degree segment of a zodiac sign, also known as a decan</term> of the sign of Leo is the stone they call White Zircon, which we have already mentioned in the nineteenth degree of the sign of Pisces. And this is most manifest when Jupiter is in this face, and in its ascendant, and in its hour, and safe from misfortunes <note>In astrology, "misfortunes" refers to the negative influence of the "malefic" planets, Saturn and Mars</note>, and in good aspect with Venus and the Moon. Finished is the second lapidary, in which is fully shown the properties that stones possess through the power they receive from the figures in the eighth heaven <note>the sphere of the fixed stars</note>, according to the division of the faces of the twelve signs through which the sun runs throughout the year, as much by night as by day; it is now fitting that the work of the third lapidary be shown, which deals with how the powers of stones often change according to the state of the planets and the figures in the eighth heaven from which they receive their power. ### Of the stone they call the Birth-Stone. (102.)

They call the third stone of Jupiter the Birth-Stone <note>original: *Paridera*; likely the *aetites* or eagle-stone, traditionally used to aid labor</note> because it makes one give birth easily. Its color is red tending toward yellow. And it rattles inside when a man shakes it. And when they polish it, that which comes off of it is white. And the virtue it has is this: he who carries it with him will be loved and well-received by men, and his reasoning will be accepted in every place he speaks. And if it is a man who wishes to observe the augury of birds, he will succeed in it very well; for they will all gather in that place where he goes with that stone. And according to Hermes, who was a very great philosopher, the virtues of the stones themselves change according to the movement that the planets have with one another and with the figures of the heavens. Wherefore this planet has much greater virtue when Jupiter is in its house, and in its ascendant, and in its hour, and in the second face of Pisces, and well-regarded by the Moon. And let the power of the figure of a fox descend upon this stone. And this stone has yet another virtue: if, when Jupiter is in its ascendant and in its hour and well-received by the Sun and the Moon, they give the water in which it was washed to be drunk by one who has a strong fever, it brings him great benefit. And this stone has another virtue as well: for when Jupiter is in its ascendant and in its hour, and in the second face of Sagittarius, and well-received by the Sun and in trine or sextile aspect <note>harmonious astrological angles of 120 and 60 degrees</note> with it, the rainwater always comes in its season without evil and without harm in the place where the stone is. And it performs this when the power of the figure of a man covered by a shroud <note>original: *sabana*</note> and riding upon a dragon descends upon it, holding a lance in his right hand.

### Of the stone they call Carnelian. (102 verso)

Carnelian <note>original: *Alaaquec*; from the Arabic *al-aqiq*</note> is the name of the second stone of Mars. But it is more so when the power of the figure of a man standing on his feet descends upon this stone, dressed in a hauberk <term>hauberk: a coat of chainmail armor</term> and having a sword hanging from his neck, and another naked sword in his right hand, and the head of a man in his left. And this stone has another virtue as well: that by wearing it over a wound or any other place from which blood flows, it makes it stop immediately. And it performs this most especially when Mars is in its exaltation, and in the ascendant, and well-received by the Moon. And let the power of the figure of a lion descend upon this stone, having before it these letters..... And even in this stone, Carnelian, there is another virtue: he who carries it with him in the hour of Mars and in its ascendant, and in the third face of Scorpio, and well-received by the Sun, and in good aspect with Jupiter, will be brave and daring in deeds though he be fearful by nature; he will not fear a king, nor will thieves or other evil men or evil beasts do him harm. But it performs this most completely when the power of the figure of a man with a crown on his head descends upon this stone, holding a naked sword in his right hand upon which are written the letters of the figure of Mars.

### Of the stone they call Aquit in Arabic. (103.)

The third stone of Mars is named *Aquit* in Arabic, and in Latin *Cornelina* <note>Cornelian</note>. This has such virtue that he who carries it with him during the hour of Mars, and in the third face of Gemini, and when the power of the figure of a scorpion descends upon this stone, blood will come out of his nostrils as long as he holds it in his hand.

### Of the stone Cayzor. (103.)

They call the fourth stone of Mars *Cayzor*. And its virtue is such that if they place it in a location where there are men, it will make them all fall ill with fever. And they also put it into the concoctions made for this purpose. And it has this virtue most completely in the hour of Mars, and by writing on it these words: "Red Bahram <note>original: *Barharan*; a Persian name for the planet Mars</note>: Mars responds."

### Of the Red Zircon. (103.)

The Sun has power over the stone named Red Zircon <note>original: *Yargonza bermeya*; also known as Hyacinth</note>. And its virtue is such that the king who carries it with him when the Sun is in its exaltation, and on its day <note>Sunday</note>, and in its hour, and well-regarded by Jupiter, will be the victor over his enemies, in such a way that they will all be obedient to him and come at his command. But it performs this most completely when the power of the figure of a king seated on a throne descends upon it, having a crown on his head and the figure of a crow before him, and beneath his feet these letters..... And this stone has yet another virtue: that when the Sun is in Leo, not aspected by Saturn or Mars, if someone takes it and carries it with him, he will not be defeated in battle, and all his affairs will be conducted easily, and he will finish well what he begins, and he will not dream a bad or frightening dream. And this is especially so when the power of the figure of a lion descends upon this stone, and likewise that of the Sun.

->**OF THE SUN AND OF VENUS. 65**<-

### Of the stone they call Diamond. (103.)

The second stone of the Sun is the Diamond <note>original: *Diamant*</note>. And its virtue is such that he who carries it with him while the Sun is in Aries and in its ascendant, and in its hour, and well-aspected <term>aspected: the geometric relationship between planets; here, "well-looked upon"</term> by the Moon, all who see him shall fear him. And it performs this most effectively when there descends upon it the power of the figure of a woman seated in a carriage pulled by four horses, holding a mirror in her right hand and a staff in the other, and with seven candles upon her head.

### Of the stone they call Sanguina. (103 verso.)

Sanguina <note>likely hematite or bloodstone</note> is the name of the third stone of the Sun. And its virtue is such that if one carves into it these figures of letters that are written here....., while the Sun is in the first decan <term>decan: a ten-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign, also called a "term" or "face"</term> of the sign of Leo and in its ascendant, and in its hour, it heals the epileptics upon whom it is placed.

### Of the stone named Cornelina. (103 verso.)

Cornelina <note>carnelian</note> is likewise the fourth stone of those of the Sun. And it has such virtue that he who carries it with him while the Sun is in Leo—and if the power of the figure of a man standing upright upon a lion descends upon this stone, with these letters figured here...... beneath the lion’s feet—he shall obtain from kings all things he may desire, provided they are just and good. And whoever carves these letters into the aforementioned stone in the first hour of Friday while the Sun is in Aries, and places it in a yellow ring of gold or brass, and seals with it Armenian bole <term>Armenian bole: a medicinal red clay used since antiquity</term> kneaded with rainwater, and gives it to a sick person with a fever to drink, or anoints their body and face with it, they shall be healed.

### Of the stone named Gold. (103 verso.)

The fifth stone of the Sun is gold. And this is counted among the other mineral stones. Thus, he who makes a ring of gold on a Sunday, and let that which is to be the stone also be made of the same metal, and let them engrave upon it in the eighth hour of the day the figure of a king seated upon his throne, wearing a crown upon his head and with a lion seated before him; and let the king hold in his right hand a lance with which he strikes the lion upon the head; and above the king’s head these figures.... and around him these others....... And if this stone is also fumigated with Indian wood <note>original: *ligno indico*</note> which they call *hot* in Arabic <note>original: *hot*; likely *'ud* or aloeswood</note>, or with a grain of musk. When the power of this aforementioned figure descends upon this stone, it has such virtue that he who carries it upon the middle finger of his right hand shall be defended and guarded from all harms that others wish to do him; and likewise, he shall be feared by all who see him, and especially by kings.

### Of the stone named Bizedi. (104.)

Bizedi is likewise the sixth stone of those of the Sun. And it has such virtue that he who carries it with him while the Sun is in the first face of Leo, and it is in the ascendant and in its first face, it takes away evil thoughts and heals pains of the liver and the stomach. But it shows this more fully when the power of the figure of a man standing on his feet, holding a spear in his right hand, descends upon this stone.

### Of the stone they call Black. (104.)

The seventh stone of the Sun is black in color, but it is so clear that sight passes through it just like crystal <note>likely obsidian or smoky quartz</note>. And its virtue is such that he who carries it with him, having carved upon it these figures of letters written here, shall be hidden from the sight of men. But this shall be more complete in the hour of the Sun and when the power of such figures as these descends upon this stone...... for then it may be, and at no other time.

<column-break/>

### Of the stone they call Alambre. (104.)

*Carabe* in Arabic, and *Alambre* <note>Amber; from the Arabic *al-'anbar*</note> in this Romance tongue, is the name of the eighth stone of the Sun. And its virtue is such that he who carries it with him when the Sun enters the first degree of the mansion <term>mansion: one of the 28 divisions of the lunar zodiac</term> called Zarfa <note>the 12th lunar mansion, associated with the tail of Leo</note>, which is in the sign of Leo, and while that same sign is in the ascendant and in the hour of Venus; if he enters before a king or any powerful man whom he fears, he shall do him no harm, but instead shall receive him well and honor him. And it is likewise good for those who travel the roads and fear thieves or enemies who might do them harm, and it is of great use to those who are bitten by snakes, or scorpions, or any other poisonous beast.

### Of the stone named Robi. (104.)

Robi <note>Ruby</note> is a stone that, although it belongs entirely to the Sun, Venus has a very great part in it. Therefore, he who carries this stone with him in the hour of Venus, she being in her exaltation and in her ascendant, and aspected by Jupiter with a good aspect, shall be loved and well-liked by men, and they shall speak well of him. But this is shown more fully when the power of the figure of a woman descends upon this stone, who holds an apple in her right hand and in her left a comb made like a tablet in which these figures are depicted..... And let the face of the woman be that of a bird and her feet those of an eagle.

### Of the stone named White Yargonza. (104 verso.)

The second stone of Venus is the White Yargonza <note>Zircon or Jargoon</note>. And its virtue is such that he who carries it with him while Venus is in her house <note>Taurus or Libra</note>, and on her day, and in her ascendant, and in her hour, and well-received by the Moon, and in the first face of Taurus, shall be joyful and well-liked by women. But this is more complete when the power of the figure of a woman who holds an apple in her right hand and a comb without figures in her left descends upon this stone.

### Of the stone they call Blue. (104 verso.)

Blue <note>likely lapis lazuli or azurite</note> is the third stone of Venus. And it has such virtue that he who carries it with him while Venus is in the ascendant and in her house, and in her hour, and well-aspected by Jupiter, shall be loved by men, and they shall gather to him and serve him willingly in whatever he commands them. But this shall be more so when the power of the figure of a naked maiden descends upon this stone, with a man before her having a chain around his neck, and behind her a small boy holding a naked sword in his hand.

### Of the stone they call Crystal. (104 verso.)

Crystal is the name of the fourth stone of Venus. And its virtue is such that he who carries it with him while Venus is in her ascendant and in her house, and in her hour, and well-received by the Moon, it protects him against every bite of a snake, or scorpion, or other poisonous beast; and it does this especially by washing the stone in water or wine and giving it to him to drink. And it shows this virtue more when the power of the figure of a snake descends upon this stone, with a scorpion upon it and a water-pitcher <note>original: *aguamanil*</note> before it.

### Of the stone named Crystal. (105.)

Venus likewise has power over the stone named Crystal. And its virtue is such that he who carries it with him while Venus is in her exaltation and in her hour and in her ascendant shall be loved by young men in such a way that after they know him, they will not wish to leave him. But this is more complete when the power of the figure of a young man, having these letters beneath his feet, descends upon this stone.

->**OF VENUS.**<-

### Of the stone they call Crystal. (105.)

The sixth stone of Venus is named Crystal. And its virtue <term>virtue: the inherent magical or medicinal power of a stone</term> is this: that he who carries it with him when Venus is in her exaltation <term>exaltation: the zodiac sign where a planet’s power is most highly elevated; for Venus, this is Pisces</term> and in her ascendant, and in her hour, and when she has no bad aspect <term>aspect: the geometric relationship between planets; a "bad aspect" refers to a square or opposition from a malevolent planet</term> with any other planet, and is well-received by the moon, and the ascendant is the first face <term>face: a ten-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign, also called a decan</term> of Taurus, he shall be successful in traveling his paths and shall receive neither evil nor harm. And this stone possesses this virtue most completely when there descends upon it the power of the figure of a woman with wings, standing upright, with long hair thrown back and spread over her shoulders, and in her bosom two small children who poke their heads out from the armholes of her garments.

### Of the stone named Crystal. (105.)

Crystal is likewise the seventh stone of Venus. And it has such virtue that he who carries it with him while Venus is in her exaltation and in her hour, and received by Jupiter and the moon, and while the ascendant is the first face of Libra, he shall be successful in all trade. However, the stone shows this more clearly when there descends upon it the power of the figure of three men joined as one, appearing as if they are speaking.

### Of the stone they call Crystal. (105.)

The eighth stone of Venus is named Crystal. And its virtue is such that he who carries it with him in the hour of this planet, when the ascendant is the first face of Pisces and it has no bad aspect from Saturn or Mars, and looks well upon Jupiter, he shall be of good temperament and joyful; and if he has the illness of melancholy <note>melancholy: a state of deep sadness or depression, thought in the Middle Ages to be caused by an excess of black bile</note>, it shall be taken from him, and it shall strengthen his heart, and he shall have the power to lie many times with a woman and shall have great pleasure from her, and likewise she from him. And if a woman who has an ailment in her nature <note>original: *mal en su natura*; likely referring to reproductive or menstrual health</note> carries it with him, she shall be healed. And the stone shows this most when there descends upon it the power of the figure of a woman standing upright with her arms open, holding an apple in her right hand and a comb in her left.

### Of the stone they call Crystal. (105 verso.)

Crystal also has virtue through the force of Venus. For he who carries it with him while Venus is in her house <term>house: the zodiac signs a planet "rules"; for Venus, these are Taurus and Libra</term>, and in her hour, and received by Jupiter, and well-aspected by the moon, and in the first face of Taurus, he shall be loved by women and shall win their love. But this is more effective when there descends upon this stone the power of the figure of a fat woman standing upright as if she is looking at an idol.

### Of the stone named Crystal. (105 verso.)

The tenth stone of Venus is Crystal. And the virtue it has is this: that whoever carries it with him while Venus is in her house and in her exaltation shall be loved by women with a very great love. And this is more effective when there descends upon this stone the power of the figure of a maiden combing her hair.

### Of the stone they call Coral. (105 verso.)

Coral is a stone that likewise receives virtue through the force of Venus, specifically to make mice and rats flee, which are harmful to men; and it does this when Venus is in her exaltation, and in her hour, and well-received by Mars, and between her and Saturn there is a bad aspect, provided that Mars is strong and Saturn is weak. And let there descend upon this stone the power of the figure of cats running after a mouse.

Coral has yet another virtue through the power of Venus. And he who carries it with him while this planet is in her hour, and in her ascendant, and in the first face of Taurus, shall be loved by every thing that sees him. But this is shown most clearly when there descends upon this stone the power of the figure of a woman with her hair loose, riding upon a deer.

### Of the stone named Coral. (106.)

Coral likewise has virtue by reason of Venus: that he who carries it with him while Venus is in her ascendant, and in her hour, and well-fortuned, young and beautiful women shall love him. But this is more effective when there descends upon this stone the power of the figure of a woman who holds a rod in her right hand and an apple in her left.

### Of the stone named Coral. (106.)

Coral has yet another virtue through the power of Venus: that he who carries it with him in the hour of Venus, and while her ascendant is good for the love of women, he shall love them much and they him. And this is more effective when there descends upon this stone the power of the figure of these letters <note>The original manuscript likely intended to show specific magical characters or sigils here</note>.

### Of the stone they call Cornelina. (106.)

Cornelina <note>carnelian</note> also has virtue to remove an illness that children often have, which they call *maseda* <note>original: *maseda*; likely referring to a childhood rash, measles, or similar skin eruption</note>. But this is more effective when Venus is in her house, and in her ascendant, and in her hour, either by placing the stone at the neck or washing it in water or another liquid they are given to drink. And there should descend upon this stone the power of the figure of a woman standing upright who has her hair thrown over one side, and in her right hand a wrapped cloth, and in her left an apple.

### Of the stone they call Coral (Carnelian?). (106.)

Carnelian <note>The text says "Coral" but the context and subsequent entries suggest the author meant "Cornelina" (Carnelian)</note> has another virtue by reason of Venus: that he who carries it with him or buries it in a place where there are flies, while Venus is in her hour, and in her exaltation, and in a good aspect with Mars, it shall remove them, and it shall do the same for other annoying things. And this shall be more effective when there descends upon this stone the power of the figure of a fly turned upside down with its head pointing down.

### Of the stone they call Cornelina. (106 verso.)

And Cornelian has yet another virtue through the power of Venus: that he who carries it with him while this planet is in her exaltation and in her hour—and if they hang it over the stomach of one who has pain there, or give them to drink the water in which it was washed—he shall be healed. But the stone does this most clearly when there descends upon it the power of the figure of the head of a zebra <note>original: *Acebra*; in medieval Spanish, this referred to the African wild ass or a similar striped equine</note> and above it the head of a fly.

### Of the stone named Cornelina. (106 verso.)

Cornelian also has virtue by reason of Venus: that he who carries it with him in the hour of Venus, when the ascendant is the first face of Libra, he shall be guarded from the harm of mosquitoes and from all kinds of flies that are poisonous or biting. And this is more effective when there descends upon this stone the power of the figure of a mosquito or some of these other flies we have mentioned.

Glass is likewise a stone of Mercury. And it has the same virtue as the one mentioned above, working with it in the manner we have described. And this shows itself most when the power descends upon this stone in the figure of a man’s hand holding a pair of scales.

### Of the stone that is called Magnesia. (108 verso.) <note>original: "Magnicia"</note>

Magnesia is likewise a stone of Mercury. And its virtue is such that he who has it with him while this planet is in his hour, and in his exaltation, and in the first face of Aries, all who see him shall fear him and honor him.

### Of the stone that has the name Hematite. (108 verso.) <note>original: "Sanguina"; literally "bloodstone," usually referring to hematite</note>

The stone Hematite also has virtue by reason of Mercury: he who carries it with him in the hour of this planet, and washes it with water and gives it to drink to someone who has melancholy <note>in medieval medicine, "melancholy" referred to an excess of black bile, causing depression or madness</note>, it shall benefit him; and if he drinks it often, he shall be healed. And this is especially so when the power descends upon this stone in the figure of Mercury.

### Of the stone that has the name Alcarabe. (109.) <note>Possibly a white variety of amber or a similar fossilized resin</note>

Alcarabe is likewise of a white color and of the nature of Mercury. And its virtue is such that he who has it with him while this planet is in his day, and in his hour, it shall unbind him if he is bound <note>likely referring to "ligadura," a magical spell intended to cause impotence</note>, and this works for a woman as well as for a man. But this virtue is most shown when the power descends upon this stone in the figure of these letters......

### Of the stone they call Coral. (109.)

Coral also has virtue by reason of Mercury; when the planet is in his day and his hour, and they wash the stone in water and give it to drink to an epileptic, or to a madman, or to one who is poisoned, using it for a long time heals them. But this is more manifest when the power descends upon this stone in the figure of these letters.........

### Of the stone they call Blue. (109.) <note>Likely Lapis Lazuli or Azurite</note>

Blue is a stone of the Moon. And its virtue is such that he who has it with him while the Moon is in her exaltation, and in her ascendant, and in her hour, and well-aspected by Jupiter, and so long as Saturn or Mars do not look upon her with bad aspect, he shall be loved by men. And if they wash this stone in water and give it to drink to two who wish each other ill, they shall come to an agreement and love each other well. And this she shows most when the power descends upon this stone in the figure of a youth standing on his feet with a crown on his head, a crook in his right hand, and a mirror in his left.

### Of the stone they call Coral. (109.) <note>Note that coral is attributed here to the Moon, whereas above it was linked to Mercury</note>

Coral is likewise of the Moon. And it has such virtue that he who has it with him while this planet is in her ascendant, and in her hour, and well-aspected by Jupiter, and in the first face of Cancer, he shall endure much in traveling his path. And even though he walks great distances <note>original: "yornadas"; a day's journey</note>, he shall not tire as quickly as another who does not carry it. But this is more so when the power descends upon this stone in the figure of a man with the head of a bird who is leaning on a staff, and in his hand something like a flowering tree.

### Of the stone that has the name Bezoar. (109.) <note>original: "Bezahar"; a stone-like mass found in the stomachs of animals, prized as an antidote</note>

Bezoar is a stone that has virtue by reason of the Moon; for he who carries it with him when she is in her ascendant, and in her hour, and that the ascendant be the first face of Cancer, and well-received by the Sun, and well-aspected by Jupiter, and provided she has no bad aspect with Saturn or Mars, his memory shall be sharpened and he shall understand well the things he hears and shall not forget them. And this is more so when the power descends upon this stone in the figure of these letters.........

### Of the stone they call Bezoar. (109.)

And furthermore, the Bezoar stone has another virtue by the power of Venus, for he who washes it in some liquid while the Moon is in her hour, and in the second face of Scorpio, and the ascendant is Leo or Taurus or Aquarius, and gives that in which it was washed to drink to one who has been stung by a scorpion, the pain shall leave him immediately and he shall be healed after drinking it a few times. But this is more completely achieved when the power descends upon this stone in the figure of a scorpion.

### Of the stone that has the name Aliaza. (109 verso.)

Aliaza is likewise a stone of the Moon. And its virtue is such that when someone has it with him while she is in the ascendant and in her exaltation and in the first face of Cancer, and he places it in a location where there are crops or trees, they shall grow well and quickly. And the same happens for all things that grow from the earth. And this is shown most manifestly when the power descends upon this stone in the figure of a man standing on his feet who has a bird upon his head and a tree before him.

<meta>This page continues the "Third Lapidary," which describes the virtues of stones as they receive influence from the figures of the heavens. The third lapidary is completed, in which the virtue of the stones is shown according to how they receive it from the figures of the sky that descend upon them, and likewise from the positions in which the planets are found. It is now appropriate to show another manner that speaks of their virtues according to the constellation in which they are created, and likewise from the form they receive during their growth. And also of the color they have by their nature, and of the other color that comes from them when they are rubbed hard against something with water. And likewise, it shows how this comes to them by the virtue of the planets that engender and create these things by the power of God, who made them, ordered them, and maintains each one in its state. And Mahomat Abenquich <note>likely Muhammad Ibn Quzman or another Arabic source</note> composed this lapidary according to the knowledge he found in the books of the wise, and he proved it by himself and ordered them by the Arabic letters A, B, C, according to how they are ordered here by the Latin ones.

### Of the first type of the stone of Axoniz.
->(110 verso.)<- <note>Axoniz: Likely a variant of Onyx.</note>

AXONIZ is the first stone of the letter A and is of seven types, each of which has its own color and its work set apart by itself for good or for evil; and the colors are these: the first, black; the second, brown; the third, red; the fourth, yellow; the fifth, white; the sixth, sky-blue; the seventh, green. And each of these belongs likewise to its planet. For the black is of Saturn; the brown of Jupiter; the red of Mars; the yellow of the Sun; the white of Venus; the sky-blue of Mercury; and the green of the Moon. Wherefore the black one, which is of the nature of Saturn, has him as its planet and its ruler on Saturday. And it has such virtue that if it is placed in a location where there are evil monsters <note>original: "bestiglos"; monstrous or mythical creatures</note>, it shall kill them. And Plato said in another place where he spoke separately of the seven types of this aforementioned stone, that when any man finds it of a black color, he should know it is of Saturn, and its taste is of an unpleasant flavor. And if, when they polish it with water, that which comes off it is white, it was made in the exaltation <term>exaltation: the zodiac sign where a planet’s power is most potent</term> of Venus. And it has such virtue that he who carries it with him is protected against any poison he might drink. And if the polish is of a red color that leans toward black and has white and green veins in it, and what comes off it is white, it was worked in the exaltation of Venus. And its virtue is that he who carries it with him shall be much honored by men in every place he goes. And if its polish is black and a woman keeps it with her, no man can sow discord between her and her husband, nor any other man she loves; nor can her husband take another woman, nor love another well, nor even have friendship with anyone else but the one she loves, and she shall be much loved by all who see her. And the man who carries it with him shall do just the same. And if the polish is yellow, it was worked in the exaltation of the Sun; and its virtue is such that he who keeps it with him shall be very honored by men in every place he goes, and they shall hold that he is very handsome and very fair in all his deeds. And if the polish is the color of the sky, it was worked in the hour of Mercury and in his exaltation. And it has such virtue that if any man of weak understanding keeps it with him, the people shall nevertheless hold him as wise, pious, and knowledgeable, and he shall fear nothing. And if the polish is green, it was made while the moon was in its exaltation; and its virtue is such that he who keeps it with him shall not be harmed by any evil beast, nor by their venom. And if the polish of the stone is black, it shall have all these aforementioned virtues. And this is because it was worked while Saturn was in the house of his exaltation. And we find in another book that when the stone is black and its polish white, it protects against all poisons for him who keeps it with him. And if it is yellow and someone keeps it with him,

<column-break/>

he shall not grow weary from any labor that comes to him, and he and all those of his house shall be safe from the illnesses that befall men. And if it is black and someone keeps it with him, he shall obtain everything he desires from men, and his wisdom shall increase, and he shall learn all things he wishes to learn. And if it is green and someone keeps it with him, he shall be much loved by his father and they shall honor him more than the other sons.

### Of the second type of the stone of Anxoniz.
->(110 verso.)<-

The second type of the seven that are in this aforementioned stone which they call Anxoniz is brown and of the nature of Jupiter, and he is its planet, and its ruler on Thursday. And its virtue is that it is beneficial for everything a man may carry. And Plato said that when this stone is brown it is of Jupiter, and its taste is sweet. And if its rubbing with water <note>original: "fregamiento"; the residue produced by rubbing the stone</note> is white, it was made in the exaltation of Venus, and in her hour. And its virtue is such that if any woman carries it with her who has company with any man, she can never be separated from him. And if any man keeps it with him, his wife can never leave him nor love another. And if its rubbing with water is black, it was made in the exaltation of Saturn. And its virtue is that whoever carries it with him shall be much honored and very prized by men in every place he goes. And if it is yellow, it was made in the exaltation of the Sun. And its virtue is such that he who carries it with him shall be honored by men and they shall love him very well. And it was worked while Jupiter was in the house of his exaltation. And its virtue is that if any man keeps it with him and does some evil, he shall not receive punishment for it. And if it is the color of the sky, it was worked in the exaltation of Mercury. And its virtue is such that whoever keeps it with him, the devils and all evil spirits shall scatter before him. And if it is red, it was made in the exaltation of Mars. And it has such virtue that if any man keeps it with him, no weapon shall harm him in battle. And if it is green, it was made in the exaltation of the Moon. And it has such virtue that he who keeps it with him and is accused by any men, they shall not be able to harm him and he shall overcome them all. And we even find in another book that when its rubbing is white and they grind it in the name of some man, mentioning his name, and then he applies it to his eyes as kohl <note>original: "alchololare"; using the powder as an eyeliner or medicinal salve</note>, they shall love him much and watch over him. And if its rubbing is black and someone applies it as kohl, all who see him shall honor him. And if it is brown and women apply it as kohl, they shall be much loved and honored by their husbands, and they shall not be contradicted in whatever they do. And if its rubbing is yellow, he who carries it with him shall be very prized and honored, and men will say that through him all his gains shall be set right. And if its rubbing is green and someone keeps it with him, he shall be honored in whatever place he sits among men. And if its rubbing is of the color of the sky and someone carries it with him, he shall be very pious even if he should not be so by his nature.

### Concerning the sixth type of the Stone of Axoniz.

And whoever carries it with them will not be left by the one they love until the day of their death. It has such virtue that he who carries it and goes among his enemies, they will not harm him nor will he have fear of them. It is also good for boys who carry it hanging upon them. And if the residue in water is black, know that it was crafted in the hour of the Moon and in the exaltation of Saturn. And he who carries it and practices <term>natural science</term>, all the medicines <note>original: "melecinas"</note> he makes will be effective. Although the liquid from its rubbing is a poison that kills, if a small amount—the weight of one grain—is given daily to drink to one who is dropsical <note>Suffering from edema or swelling.</note> or consumptive <note>original: "tisico," suffering from tuberculosis or wasting disease.</note>, they will be healed. 

And if the residue in water is yellow, know that it was crafted in the hour of the Moon and in the exaltation of the Sun. It has in itself such virtue that he who carries it will be very well received by kings and high lords. And if the residue is green, know that it is entirely lunar and the nature of no other planet was mixed with it; it helps those who have an abscess <note>original: "postema"</note> when they carry it hanging upon them. And we find in another place that when the residue of this stone is white and someone carries it and plants saplings or sows seeds, if they put the stone in a bit of cloth or cotton and bury it there where they sowed, that crop will sprout very well and will be very good. And if the residue is black, the one who carries it will always have much good. And if the residue is yellow, all the medicines they give to the sick will help them and they will be healed. And if the residue is red, everyone will honor and exalt them. And if the residue is the color of the sky, [his enemies will be] beneath him and will not be able to harm him. And if...
