...should its rubbing <note>original: "fregamiento"; referring to the residue or liquid produced by rubbing the stone against a hard surface with a liquid like water or vinegar.</note> come out brown, and if someone keeps it with them and treats a sick person, they will heal them.

**AZCRITAZ** is what they call the fourth stone of the 'A' in Greek. Its color is white and soft, and it is found in the mines of Chalcedony <note>A type of translucent quartz.</note>, and goldsmiths use it in the polishing of stones. And its virtue is such that whoever rubs it with vinegar and gives a drachm's weight <note>A unit of weight, approximately 3.5 grams.</note> of what comes off it to someone suffering from a swollen spleen, it will thin the swelling and ease the pain. It also helps against all poisons by drinking its residue.

**ATAZARIFEZ** is the name in Greek for the fifth stone of the 'A'. This one is of two colors. One is bright red <note>original: "bermeya"</note> like the Hyacinth <note>original: "Yargonza"; a yellow-red zircon or gemstone.</note>; and the other is brown, possessing such clarity at night that a man can see by it as if by the light of a fire. And the virtue of this stone helps the coldness of the kidneys by drinking its residue.

**AMETITEZ** <note>Amethyst.</note> is what they call the sixth stone of the 'A' in Greek. It is bright red in color, and when they rub it, its residue comes out red, tending toward the color of gold. And if they weigh it after it has been polished, they will find that it has not decreased in weight at all. And this stone has such a property that if a woman suffering from a flow of blood <note>Excessive menstrual bleeding or hemorrhage.</note> takes its polishings in a bit of wool and keeps it for an hour in her nature <note>A euphemism for the vagina.</note>, it will stop the flow. And whoever has a cut vein and hangs the stone upon themselves, it will seal the wound.

**AMEIDICARIZ** is what they call the seventh stone of the 'A' in Greek. It is found in Armenia and is azure <note>Blue.</note> in color. And its virtue is that its residue helps with pain of the liver.

**AMBOZIZ** is the name in Greek for the eighth stone of the 'A'. Its property is such that whoever places it in a location where there are frogs, they will all gather toward it. And the ancients used to make images from it that helped with throat pain.

**ANQUIOZ** is what they call the ninth stone of the 'A' in Greek. Its color is that of dark brazilwood <note>A deep reddish-brown.</note> and it is easy to break. It has such virtue that if it is rubbed with milk or cow’s butter and given to drink to one bitten by a rabid dog, they will be healed.

**ALDARDEMUZ** is the name in Greek for the tenth stone of the 'A'. This one has the color of iron, and when rubbed, its residue comes out bright red. With this, they clean pearls <note>original: "Aliofar"</note>, round off glass, and clarify other stones. Its virtue is that it helps with internal pains and removes "excess flesh" <note>original: "carne que sobeya"</note> such as warts from a man’s body by wearing it hanging upon oneself.

**ABRITEZ** in Greek, *Mahe* in Arabic, and *Crystal* in Latin; because it is of many types... it is the name of the eleventh stone of the 'A'. Some of them tend toward brown and help against Greek fire <note>A legendary incendiary weapon used in medieval naval battles.</note>. Its virtue is that whoever suffers from the sickness of "Greek fire" <note>Likely referring to erysipelas or a similar inflammatory skin condition.</note> and rubs this stone with oil and anoints the site of the fire, they will be healed. And whoever has pain in the groin and carries it hanging with them, it will take the pain away.

**ALMELIN** is what they call the twelfth stone of the 'A' in Greek. It is a mineral stone; it has a clarity like silver. This stone is the one they call *Atalch* <note>Talc.</note>. The sages spoke much of it, and some of them said it was Alum <note>A mineral salt.</note> that does not melt in fire; but whoever knew its solution would have its secret revealed. Others said that when they soak it in very strong vinegar made from wine, it softens until it becomes like dough, and then they can make a stone that helps against poisons and drives away evil beasts <note>original: "bestiglos"</note> from wherever they wish. And whoever knows well how to dissolve it and anoint a place with it, fire will not take hold there.

**ARHORITIZ** is the name in Greek for the thirteenth stone of the 'A'. It is black with the color of silver. It has such virtue that whoever has pain in the ears and rubs it and distills what comes from it into them, the pain will cease. It does the same by hanging it over the ears, though not as quickly.

**AITOFIQUIOZ** is what they call the fourteenth stone of the 'A' in Greek. It is black in color. Its virtue is that it helps whoever has an abscess <note>original: "postema"</note> by rubbing it with oil and giving them the residue to drink.

**ALFAZ** is what they call the fifteenth stone of the 'A' in Greek. It is found in the marshes of Egypt. Whoever drinks the water with which it was washed, or the residue from its rubbing, no poison they drink can harm them. And Yacob Al-Kindi <note>A famous 9th-century Arab philosopher and scientist.</note> said that this stone helps against any toxin a man might drink and against the mortal wounds of serpents.

**ANTOROZ** is the name in Greek for the sixteenth stone of the 'A'. Whoever drinks its residue will not be harmed by any mortal toxin.

**ARSCITIZ** is what they call the seventeenth stone of the 'A' in Greek. Its color is white like crystal; a man can see within it a bright red line like fire. It bears the figure of a woman holding her hand over her mouth. It has the virtue of removing jealousy from those who suffer from it.

**AITIOCIEZ** is the name of the eighteenth stone of the 'A' in Greek. This is a copper ore; yet it is a stone. Its virtue is that it benefits the stabbing pains a man feels in his entrails and calms the "choking" <note>Perhaps referring to respiratory distress or pressure.</note> that rises from the spleen when a man carries it hanging with him.

**AYETANIZ** is what they call the nineteenth stone of the 'A' in Greek. It is beautiful and very clear. A man’s face appears in it when he looks. This stone has the virtue that as long as a man keeps it with him, he will be safe from the wounds of poisonous beasts and from all toxins.

**BERLOZ** <note>Beryl.</note> is what they call the first stone of the 'B' in Greek. It resembles white stone. Its virtue is such that whoever has an ailment in the eyes and applies its residue as an eye-salve, it will take the ailment away.

**BATHARAXITAZ** is the name in Greek for the second stone of the 'B'. It is of many colors. It contains tiny grains that tend toward green. Its virtue is such that whoever rubs it with warm water and anoints the site of an abscess with the residue will be healed.

**BATRACIZ** is what they call the third stone of the 'B' in Greek. It has the color of gold; it contains tiny grains like a cluster of grapes. If rubbed, a green color comes out, and if the rubbing lasts long, it turns yellow. This is because it has two natures, beneficial to those who have pain in the lungs for which they find no medicine.

**BECENITIZ** is the name in Greek for the fourth stone of the 'B'. It is green in color. Gold is tested <note>original: "fregan sobre ella el oro"; likely a touchstone.</note> upon it. It is found in the tombs of the ancients in the shape of a frog. Its virtue is that it helps boys who suffer from night-terrors when they wear it hanging upon themselves.

**BABARI** <note>Amber.</note> is the name in Greek for the fifth stone of the 'B'. It is of two types. The first is of very lovely beauty and attracts straws to itself. Its virtue is such that whoever rubs it with water and gives the residue to drink to a woman in labor, she will give birth very easily. Furthermore, it makes her "flower" <note>Menstrual flow.</note> run and cleanses it when she drinks the residue with oil. Some say that when it is ground and used to anoint the *alvaraz*—which in Latin is called *morphea* <note>A skin condition involving localized patches of discolored skin.</note>—the person will be healed immediately. The second type tends toward a faint red color, and they call it "Marine Bahari." Its virtue is such that if someone who has stabbing pains carries it with them, the pain will be stilled.

**BAZD** is what they call the sixth stone of the 'B' in Greek. Alexander <note>Likely referring to Alexander the Great, to whom many medieval lapidaries were pseudo-attributed.</note> said in his book of stones that whoever hangs this stone on the neck of one possessed by a demon, it will be driven out, and the one who carries it will never remember the possession. He also said that if one with gout carries it hanging with them, it will benefit them greatly and they will not feel pain as long as they have it.

**BILOR** <note>Crystal or Beryl.</note> is the name in Greek for the seventh stone of the 'B', and in Latin, *Crystal*. Alexander said in his book that it melts like glass and takes on dyes. Benfrecythas the sage said that whoever hangs it over their head will not see anything in sleep that makes them afraid or frightens them.

### GELEFETICOZ
This is the name in Greek for the second stone of 'G'. Its upper surface is white, its underside is black, and its sides are white and bright red. It helps those who have an abscess <note>original: "postema"</note> in the heart. And if someone who has pain in their side <note>Likely referring to pleurisy or similar internal pains.</note> carries it hanging as an amulet, they will be healed. This is one of the marvelous things that the wise men used.

### GELEATIZ
This is what they call the third stone of 'G' in Greek. This one is black and white. Many of them are found in flowing rivers. Its virtue is that it helps against poisons <note>original: "tosigos"</note> and drives serpents out of places when they are fumigated with it. This stone can be identified in this way: if they put it in the fire and let it lie there until it is red-hot, and then take it out and pour water over it, it will not be extinguished until oil is poured over it; if so, then it is the true stone.

### FINAZT
This is the name in Greek for the fourth stone of 'G'. Men wear it set in rings because it is beautiful and elegant. Whoever rubs it well with water and gives what comes off it to be drunk by someone who has sharp piercing pains <note>original: "dolor de puntas"; likely stitches in the side or sharp internal pains.</note>, it will help them. It also makes a man expel worms from his belly, and the fetus <note>original: "creatura"</note> from a pregnant woman. Beostriates <note>A philosopher/author often cited in medieval lapidaries, possibly a corruption of a Greek name.</note> the philosopher said in the book he wrote about stones that whoever drinks wine from a vessel made of this stone will not become drunk, no matter how much they drink. And if they throw many small pieces of it into the wine they drink, it will do the same. He also said that whoever places this stone under their head when they wish to sleep will see good and wonderful visions, and will not see things that cause them grief. He further said that whoever sets this stone in a ring and carries it with them will never have fright nor fear as long as they have it on their finger. It has many other benefits when a man carries it as described above.

### GEZA
This is what they call the fifth stone of 'G' in Greek, and in the common tongue, Chalcedony. This is made of many colors mixed one with another. It has such virtue that whoever wraps it in the hair of a woman who wishes to give birth will make her go into labor quickly. It also makes a pregnant woman expel the fetus at whatever season she wishes. It also induces a woman’s "flower" <note>A medieval euphemism for menstruation.</note>. Linemuz Alintaqui <note>Possibly a corruption of a name like Apollonius or a similar Arabic/Greek source.</note> said in his book on stones that whoever places this stone on the side of a woman in labor will feel no pain during the birth.

### DIDRIEZ
This is the name in Greek for the first stone of 'D'. This one is of many colors and has many white, red, and black lines in it. Its virtue is such that whoever rubs it with water and applies what comes off it as eye-salve <note>original: "alcololare"; to apply like kohl or medicinal eyeliner.</note> when they have pain in their eyes, it will help them. This stone is called *Mahium Almoloh* in Arabic, which means "electuary of salts" <note>original: "lectuario de las sales"; a medicinal paste.</note>.

### DIENTOZ
This is what they call the second stone of 'D' in Greek. This is smooth like polished marble and has black lines in it. To one who sees it, it seems entirely black; but when they moisten it in water, it turns red. Its virtue is that it helps against the bites of venomous creatures <note>original: "bestiglos"</note> and drives them away from the places where they are.

### DEICARENIZ
This is the name in Greek for the third stone of 'D'. Its color is that of vinegar that is not very clear; it is strong and hard to break. Whoever rubs it and anoints with what comes off it the spots <note>Freckles or blemishes.</note> that men have on their faces will find that it removes them.

### HETUS
This is what they call the first stone of 'H' in Greek. They also call it purple Hyacinth <note>original: "Yargonza cardena"; a zircon or gemstone.</note>. It is the one that has the color of the sky, though some are white and black. When a man examines it closely, he sees in it the figure of an eagle with its wings spread, one over itself and the other under its feet. The virtue of this stone is for a man to obtain the things he desires from high-ranking lords and noble men.

### VARAHU
This is the name in Greek for the first stone of 'V'. They find it in the tombs of the ancients. Its color is green tending toward redness, and it also has the color of the sky. It has many benefits: if they rub it with cold water and give what comes off it to be drunk

### VACRIZ
This is the name in Greek for the third stone of 'V'. It is found on the island of Cyprus <note>original: "Cabroz"</note>. It has such virtue that if someone has swallowed poison <note>original: "tosico"</note> and then drinks the water that comes from its polishing, it will help them.

### ZAYETANIZ
This is what they call the first stone of 'Z' in Greek. It is the color of oil and beautiful to look at; it has great clarity, and a man can see his reflection in it. Whoever sets it in a ring and carries it with them will not be harmed by the bite of any venomous creature.

### ZAMORAT
This is the name in Arabic for the second stone of 'Z', and in Latin, Emerald <note>original: "Esmeralda"</note>. This is very well known and of very great price. There are white ones and others that are black, but all this is because of the crust they have on top; when they are cleaned, they turn green. Whoever carries it with them will achieve great honor. And whoever carves into it—while it still has its white crust—the figure of a man who bridles a lion with his hand, and carries it with them, will always be well-received by Kings and will accomplish everything they desire.

### ZOZECHE
This is the name in Arabic for the third stone of 'Z', which means Glass <note>original: "Vidrio"</note> in Latin. They use it in silver-work, especially the clearest kind, and it is close to that craft. Whoever burns it and rubs their teeth with its powder will make them very bright and very clean. This is one of the stones that neither earth nor water consumes; they last forever and are never destroyed.

### HADIT
This is what they call the first stone of 'H' in Arabic, and in the common tongue, Iron <note>original: "Fierro"</note>. All the wise men who spoke on this subject agreed and said that whoever takes the stone from which the fire draws the iron <note>Iron ore.</note> and hangs it over someone who has quartan fever <note>A form of malaria where the fever recurs every fourth day.</note>, it will remove it. If they give them the water in which iron is quenched <note>The water used by blacksmiths to cool hot iron.</note> to drink, it will help them. They also put iron filings into medicines that are useful for feverish illnesses. Mahomath Arrace <note>Referring to the famous Persian physician al-Razi, known as Rhazes (865–925 AD).</note> said in the book of the properties of things that whoever hangs iron filings over the eye of one who talks in their sleep <note>original: "devaneare durmiendo"; likely referring to sleepwalking or delirious talking.</note> will not do so while they have it.

### TACITZ
This is the name in Greek for the first stone of 'T'. It resembles crystal, but differs somewhat, for it has a darkness in the middle that looks like a black line. It is good for women, to make men fall in love with them, if they carry it with them.

### TONITOZ
This is what they call the second stone of 'T' in Greek, and in Arabic, *Taoz*. It is of many colors and was shaped <note>original: "enderazada"</note> by the work of the ancients. It is found in the places of their treasures. It helps those who have disputes, lawsuits, or legal demands against others, and they will overcome them all.

### TALICATIZ
This is the name in Greek for the third stone of 'T'. It resembles the liver of a bird they call *Zayracoz*. It helps with liver pains for whoever carries it hanging on themselves. Whoever rubs it and gives the residue from the rubbing to be drunk by someone who has this illness, it will be removed. This stone is specifically known for this virtue.

### TANIBOTUM CABOZ
This is what they call the fourth stone of 'T' in Greek. It is black, tending toward green. It helps against sadness and worries when one carries it.

TAFI is what they call the sixth stone of 'T' in Arabic. Mahomat Arriz said it has this name because it goes upon the water—it does not sink, even though it is hard and heavy. And he said he was told that whoever carries this stone with them would be very well received by the king, his wife, and all men.

### On the seventh stone of 'T'. (115 verso.)

Tortiz is the name in Greek for the seventh stone of 'T'. In Arabic, it is called Airanca. The aforementioned Mahomat said that if one rubs the skin with it, it scrapes away the hair. Likewise, wineskin makers <note>original: "odreros"</note> rub their skins with it to make them smoother. If one rubs the body with it, it will remove the hair. It has yet another virtue: if someone suffering from a fever carries it hanging upon them, it will draw the fever out without causing sweating. And if they give the water produced from rubbing the stone to someone with a fever to drink, it will take the heat away.

### On the eighth stone of 'T'. (115 verso.)

Toriz is what they call this eighth stone in Greek. In Arabic, they call it Adelun; it is white in the likeness of marble, and they make vessels for kings from it. It does not allow any ointment or oil to touch it; for whatever part of it is touched by oil immediately turns black and never becomes bright again. If they grind this stone and mix it with white "apostoligon" <note>A medicinal ointment used for cleaning wounds, named after the twelve apostles.</note>, it will dry up abscesses <note>original: "postemas"</note> and wounds that have much venom, and it will draw out the pus. If a woman drinks it, her milk will dry up; and they say it cuts off a woman's "flower" <note>A medieval euphemism for menstruation.</note>. To the woman who drinks it, it will prevent pregnancy. The dose for drinking it is the weight of one drachma <note>A unit of weight roughly equal to 3.5 grams.</note>, or more or less, according to the complexion of the woman and the hour and season in which it is given. This must be done according to the judgment and wisdom of knowing the time, the season, and the age of the woman to whom it is given.

### On the ninth stone of 'T'. (115 verso.)

Toryn is what they call the ninth stone of 'T' in Greek. It is white like crystal, though a bit darker. Men wear it in rings because it has the virtue that whoever carries it will be well received by kings. If it bears the figure of a muzzled wolf, he will be well received by all men.

### On the first stone of 'Y'. (115 verso.)

Yonuoloyz is what they call the first stone of 'Y' in Greek. They also call it Dalbelat gum, because it is found in a town in Alexandria by that name. It is of many colors and is found only in Alexandria. Its virtue is that it helps those with an abscess for which physicians can find no remedy; by rubbing it with water and anointing the place where the man has pain with what comes off it, he is healed.

### On the second stone of 'Y'. (115 verso.)

Yenetatiz is the name in Greek for the second stone of 'Y'. It resembles the heart of a bird they call Caeracoz. Whoever rubs this stone and gives the liquid to be drunk by one who has pain in the liver, it will take the pain away.

### On the third stone of 'Y'. (115 verso.)

Yalentornioz is what they call the third stone of 'Y' in Greek. It is blackish, tending toward green. It helps with anxieties and sadness when a man carries it with him; we find this same likeness of stone and its virtue under the letter 'T', except that the name varies.

### On the fourth stone of 'Y'. (115 verso.)

Yelitiz is the name in Greek for the fourth stone of 'Y'. It is a mineral by nature and its color resembles all colors, yet it tends 

<column-break/>

somewhat toward the likeness of gold; and whoever carries it with them will be safe from all evil monsters <note>original: "bestiglos malos"</note>.

### On the fifth stone of 'Y'. (115 verso.)

Yetayoloz is what they call the fifth stone of 'Y' in Greek. It helps with the pain of strong stitches <note>original: "puntas fuertes"; sharp internal pains or pleurisy.</note> when a man carries it hanging upon him.

### On the sixth stone of 'Y'. (115 verso.)

Yeticioz is the name in Greek for the sixth stone of 'Y'. It is beautiful and fair in color, and it helps with the pain of stitches in the body, and it calms the oppression <note>original: "afogamiento"; a feeling of suffocation or pressure.</note> that arises from the spleen when a man carries it with him.

### On the first stone of 'C'. (116.)

Caimicaz is the name in Greek for the first stone of 'C'. In shape it is like an egg, and it has another stone inside it that moves. All the wise men agreed and said that if a woman has it hanging from her hip when she wants to give birth, it will make her give birth quickly.

### On the second stone of 'C'. (116.)

Caaclaman is the name in Greek for the second stone of 'C'. Its color is white. The aforementioned Mahomath said that if someone sets it in a ring and places it in a vessel or a very level basin full of vinegar, and strikes the ring slightly, the stone will begin to boil and move, traveling and shifting until it reaches the bottom. Whoever carries it with them will calm anger and be well received by kings and other men.

### On the third stone of 'C'. (116.)

Caharabe is what they call the third stone of 'C' <note>Likely referring to Amber (Karabe in Arabic).</note>. It is very well known and men wear it in rings. Anficitez the wise man said in his book of stones that if a pregnant woman carries it hanging upon her, it will protect the fetus. If they grind it and knead it with water and place it upon a burn, it will help greatly. Furthermore, if they blow its powder through a tube <note>original: "cannuto"</note> directly into a candle flame, a great fire will come out of it and burn whatever it finds. Also, if its powder is given as a drink to one who has an ailment of the anus <note>original: "mal del figo"; likely hemorrhoids or rectal issues.</note>, it will help with the blood that comes from it.

### On the first stone of 'L'. (116.)

Lenelim is the name of the stone of 'L'. It resembles a woman’s breast, and it is found in the mountains of the land of Alheyez. Some are bright red and others are yellow. If a woman hangs it over a breast that has pain or an abscess, it will take it away; it also makes the milk flow in a woman who has little.

### On the first stone of 'M'. (116.)

Meli is the name of the first stone of 'M'. It is found in the lagoons of Cabraz. Whoever grinds it and drinks its powder, it will help against all poisons <note>original: "tosicos"</note> that they might eat or drink.

### On the second stone of the Mim. (116.)

The second stone of the Mim <note>Mim is the name of the letter 'M' in the Arabic alphabet.</note> is named Molio. It is found in the Nile of Egypt. It has such virtue that if someone drinks what comes from rubbing it, or carries it in a ring, no poison can harm them. This is a proven thing.

### On the third stone of the Mim. (116.)

The third stone of this letter is named Mina. It is green in color and flaky <note>original: "esconcha"; possibly meaning shell-like or scaly.</note>, and tin is found within it. Its virtue is such that whoever drinks what comes from rubbing it, it will help with very large, sharp abscesses that feel like fire when they emerge. Whoever grinds it and kneads it with water and places it upon them, it will cool them and draw out all the sharpness and the general heat. This is a proven thing.

<summary>This page describes various stones and their medicinal or magical properties, ranging from depilatories and fever reducers to amulets for safe childbirth and antidotes for poison. The text continues the alphabetical catalog, citing Greek and Arabic sources such as Rhazes.</summary>
<keywords>lapidary, stones, Rhazes, medieval medicine, amulets, Greek names, Arabic names, Alfonso X, pregnancy, poisons, abscesses</keywords>

--- Page 377 ---
<meta>This page continues the alphabetical catalog of stones and their properties, transitioning from the end of the letter 'M' (Mim) through 'N' (Non), 'Ts' (Çad), 'A' (Aim), and beginning 'F' (Fe). It continues the medical and talismanic focus seen in the previous sections.</meta>

### On the fourth stone of the letter Mim. (116.)

The fourth stone of this letter is named Magnitiz <note>original: "Magnitiz"; referring to Magnetite or Loadstone</note>. And it is that which draws iron to itself. Its virtue is such that if a person who is hydropic <note>suffering from dropsy or edema, an accumulation of bodily fluids</note> or who has sharp pains in the body because of the cold should drink the liquid resulting from rubbing this stone, it will be of great help to them. And Jacob Al-Kindi <note>A famous 9th-century Arab philosopher and scientist known as "the Philosopher of the Arabs."</note> said in his book on poisons that if one grinds two drachms <note>an ancient unit of weight</note> of this stone and gives it to be drunk with a little water to one who has swallowed iron filings, it will cause them to vomit and thus draw the iron out. And if by chance they cannot vomit, and they are given an electuary of violets <note>a medicinal paste made with honey or syrup</note> with a little scammony <note>a harsh purgative resin</note> to drink, it will cause the iron to be expelled from below in such a way that it will do them no harm at all.

### On the fifth stone of the M. (116 verso.)

The fifth stone of this letter is named Marchesica <note>original: "Marchesica"; Marcasite or Pyrite</note>. It is of two types, as is shown in the book of stones. Some are the color of gold, and others the color of silver. Goldsmiths <note>original: "Orebces"</note> put it into these two metals because it refines and prepares them well. Furthermore, it is good for mixing with all the kohls <note>original: "alcofoles"; eye powders or eyeliners used medicinally or for beauty</note> that are made for the eyes.

### On the sixth stone of the M. (116 verso.)

The sixth stone of this letter is named Marmor <note>Marble</note>. Its color is white, of a very clear whiteness. Its virtue is such that if it is ground and given as a drink to one who suffers from a flow of blood <note>hemorrhage</note>, it will help them. Moreover, if the one suffering from the aforementioned illness sits upon the stone after it has been ground, it will be of very great benefit to them.

### On the first stone of the Non. (116 verso)

The first stone of the letter Non <note>The Hebrew/Arabic letter 'N'</note> is named Necitiz. They say it resembles crystal in its color. Some are found that tend toward a brown or greyish color. The one that tends toward this color has such a virtue that if it is rubbed with oil, and the place affected by "grey fire" <note>original: "fuego grisiesco"; likely referring to shingles or erysipelas, a skin infection</note> is anointed with the polish that comes from it, it will extinguish the ailment. Furthermore, if one who has pain in the groin <note>original: "vería"</note> carries it hanging upon them, it will soothe the pain.

### On the second stone of the Non. (116 verso.)

The second stone of this letter is named Neilim in Greek, and Talc in Arabic <note>Mica or Talc</note>. This is a mined mineral; and it has a clarity within it much like silver. The wise men spoke much concerning this stone. Some said it was *Alhoxaym*; others said it was the Alum that does not dissolve in fire. To whoever knows how to dissolve it, a very great secret will be revealed. And some wise men said that if one soaks it in wine vinegar, it will become as soft as dough, and then one could make a compound from it that would protect against all poison. Furthermore, one could make stones from it that would serve to drive evil beasts <note>original: "bestiglos malos"</note> away from a place. Moreover, if one knew how to dissolve it and anointed something with it, no *Mur* <note>possibly a reference to ants or a specific pest</note> would approach it.

### On the third stone of the Non. (116 verso.)

The third stone of this letter is named Nargoritiz. In color it is like silver. Its virtue is such that if it is rubbed and the water with which it was polished is dripped into the ear of one who has pain there, it will help them. Furthermore, they make a compound from it which they call "ear."

### On the fourth stone of the Non. (116 verso.)

The fourth stone of this letter is called Nenoyoquiquod. Its color is black, and its mine is in the land of Egypt. It has such a virtue that if—after it is taken from the mine and cleaned as it should be—it is ground and given to be drunk with oil by one who has an abscess <note>original: "postema"</note>, they shall be healed.

### On the fifth stone of the Non. (116 verso.)

The fifth stone of this letter they call Neutráz. It is found on the island of Cyprus <note>original: "Cabroz"</note>. Its virtue is such that if it is ground and given to be drunk to one who has swallowed poison <note>original: "tosico"</note>, it will help them.

<column-break/>

### On the sixth stone of this letter which they call Non. (116 verso.)

The sixth stone of this letter is named Neftiz. This is found on the banks of the Nile. Its virtue is such that it protects against all poisons by washing the stone and drinking that water.

### On the first stone of Çad. (116 verso.)

The first stone of the letter Çat <note>The Hebrew/Arabic letter 'Ts' or 'Z'</note> they call Çanderitiz in Greek, which in Arabic means *Abhadidi*, and in Latin *Fierro* <note>Iron; the stone is likely Siderite</note>. Its color is that of iron. It is among the noble and certain works of the people of Greece. Many of them are found in the burials of the ancients. They are found as large as balls <note>original: "pellas"</note>, while others are small. They have the figure of a wolf carved into them. Its virtue is such that if someone who has a lawsuit before a judge <note>original: "alcande"</note> against another carries it with them, they shall be victorious.

### On the second stone of the Çat. (117.)

The second stone of the Çat is named Zerazfacoz. In this stone there are two colors and two natures: that of the Sun <note>Gold</note> and that of Venus <note>Copper</note>. Whoever finds this stone should guard it well. Its identifying mark is that it has a line through the middle and four holes in it. Its virtue is such that if one who has any growth <note>original: "nascencia"; a tumor or cyst</note> carries it hanging upon them, it will take away the pain and they shall be healed of it.

### On the third stone of the Çad. (117.)

The third stone of the Çat is called Çalninecoz in Greek, and *Doihel* in Arabic. Its color is white and of great clarity. When it is held up to the sun, many colors appear in it, such as green, red, and purple <note>original: "cardeno"</note>. When it is rubbed, the liquid that comes from it resembles milk, and there appears within it the likeness of the moon when it is new. Its virtue is such that if a man overcome by melancholy <note>a state of deep sadness or depression, then thought to be caused by "black bile"</note> hangs it upon himself at the hour when the Moon is in conjunction with the Sun, it will take the affliction away. It does the same for one who suffers from racing thoughts.

### On the first stone of the Aim. (117.)

The first stone of the Aim <note>The Hebrew/Arabic letter 'Ayin' or 'A'</note> is named Cierit in Greek. This stone is a type of lime <note>original: "calxa"</note>. It has such a virtue that if its polishings are given to be drunk with wine to one who is jealous, it will help them. It does the same if worn in a ring or in any other manner; and anointing the temples with its polish helps with headaches.

### On the second stone of the Aambruz. (117.)

The second stone of the Aim is called Aabruz in Greek, and *Aaquic* in Arabic <note>likely Agate or Carnelian</note>. This stone is of many kinds and many colors, for some are yellow and others are red. The red one has such a property that it prevents a pregnant woman <insert>that</insert> from being able to give birth at the hour of labor for as long as she carries it with her, nor will she miscarry the child before its time. Furthermore, it causes trees not to drop their fruit. There are many other benefits in it as is stated in the book of stones.

### On the third stone of the Aaim. (117.)

The third stone of the Aain is named Aaran in Greek, and *Zabach* in Arabic <note>Jet</note>. They said that this stone is "cooked from blood." It has a harmful quality in this way: if it is stirred into food, it causes the one who eats it to vomit. However, it is helpful to one who wishes to vomit to clear their stomach.

### On the first stone of the Fe. (117.)

The first stone of the Fe <note>The Hebrew/Arabic letter 'Pe' or 'F'</note> they call Fotroz in Greek. Jacob Al-Kindi described it in the book of poisons. He said it had such a virtue that whoever carries it hanging upon them, or drinks its polishings, will not be harmed by any poison they have drunk nor by the wound of any evil beast. For this virtue, it is well known in the book of stones.

<summary>This page catalogs stones categorized under the letters Mim, Non, Çad, Aim, and Fe, detailing their medicinal uses for ailments like dropsy, hemorrhage, and melancholy, as well as their magical properties for legal victory and protection against poison.</summary>
<keywords>Magnetite, Marcasite, Marble, Talc, Siderite, Agate, Jet, Al-Kindi, lapidary, medieval medicine, amulets, Greek science, Arabic science</keywords>

--- Page 378 ---
<meta>This page continues the alphabetical catalog of stones from the previous folio, moving through the letters Fe (F), Çad (Ts), Kaf (K), Re (R), Cin (S), and Zthe (Z). It maintains the focus on medicinal applications, particularly antidotes for poisons and treatments for physical and mental ailments.</meta>

### On the second stone of the letter Fe. (117.)

The second stone of the letter Fe is named Feniz <note>likely a variant of the "Phoenix stone" or a specific jasper</note>. It is found in the regions of Fatayruceten. Jacob Al-Kindi <note>The influential 9th-century Arab philosopher and scientist mentioned previously</note> spoke of it in his book on toxins. He stated that whoever carries it set in a ring will be able to handle any serpents they wish, and the creatures will not harm them. Furthermore, if the stone is ground and given as a drink to someone who has ingested poison, it will benefit them. It will do the same for those suffering from pain in the belly.

### On the third stone of the letter Fe. (117.)

The third stone of the letter Fe is called *Faararmeni* in Greek <note>original: "Faararmeni"; likely referring to *Lapis Armenus* or Armenian Stone, a blue carbonate of copper</note> and *Fayrocech* in Arabic <note>original: "Fayrocech"; the Turquoise</note>. It occurs in two colors: one is green, which is the superior variety, and the other is the color of the sky, which is not as good. The sages stated in the book of stones that the green variety has such virtue that whoever sets it in a ring and carries it with them will not suffer from the disease called dropsy <note>original: "hidropisia"; an old medical term for swelling caused by excess fluid</note>. If they already have the disease, drinking the dust from its polishing will greatly relieve them.

### On the first stone of the letter Çad. (117 verso.)

The first stone of the letter Çad <note>The Hebrew/Arabic letter Tsade</note> is named *Zdayorofe* in Greek, *Zavam* in Arabic, and *Cira* in Latin. This is a "root" stone, for the primary stones of the earth are no more than three. The first is Marble <note>original: "Marmor"</note>; the second is named Chalcedony <note>original: "Calcedonio"</note> or Flint; and the third is this very stone of which we speak. It is a stone very hard to break, appearing in various forms and many colors. We have already spoken of the benefits of these stones in other places.

### On the first stone of the letter Kaf. (117 verso.)

The first stone of the letter Kaf is called *Kafiz*. It is found in Tauracen or its surrounding regions. Whoever sets it in a ring and carries it will be able to handle any serpents they wish, and they will not be harmed. When ground and drunk, it serves as a remedy for any poison a person may have ingested.

### On the second stone of the letter Kaf. (117 verso.)

The second stone of the letter Kaf is named *Kartoiz*. Its color is black. It is deeply hollowed <note>original: "encavada"; possibly referring to natural pits or being carved</note>, and it resembles a serpent in its hollows. It is of the same type as the seal-stones <note>intaglios or signet stones</note> that the ancients used to keep. It is useful for driving dragons and serpents away from a place.

### On the third stone of the letter Kaf. (117 verso.)

The third stone of the letter Kaf is called *Karietaritiz*. This is the red Marcasite <note>original: "Marcasita bermeya"; a iron sulfide mineral similar to pyrite</note>. Using their wisdom, the sages made stones from it that helped those suffering from acute abscesses <note>original: "postema aguda"</note> and "greyish fire" <note>original: "fuego grisiesco"; likely referring to Erysipelas or "St. Anthony's Fire," an inflammatory skin infection</note>. This was done by rubbing the stone with water and anointing the place where the abscess or the fire was located.

### On the fourth stone of the letter Kaf. (117 verso.)

The fourth stone of the letter Kaf is named *Kantoz*. This stone is described very fully in this book under the first stone of the letter He. There, we named it *Hatux*. However, it is known by two names; it is one stone with the same virtues.

### On the first stone of the letter Re. (107 verso.) <note>The manuscript note says 107, but the sequence suggests 117</note>

The first stone of the letter Re is called *Renlin*. Zabor stated in the book of stones that this stone is found within fine gold. It is as small as a mustard seed. In whatever gold it is present, that gold can neither be hammered nor will a file take hold of it. It has such virtue that if a person carries it hanging upon them, and they suffer from the disease called "the demon" <note>likely epilepsy or severe mental illness, often attributed to demonic influence in the Middle Ages</note>, it will never seize them as long as they hold it, nor will they feel fear or terror.

<column-break/>

### On the second stone of the letter Re. (117 verso.)

The second stone of the letter Re is named *Roam* in Arabic, *Aymu* in Greek, and *Vuya* in the language of the Romans and in Latin <note>This refers to Marble or Alabaster</note>. This is one of the three stones that are the root of all others, as already mentioned under the first stone of the letter named *Zat*. These are *Arroham*, *Rodem*, and *Cavan*. This *Cavan* is a very hard stone that has no softness or clarity in its color. It comes in many colors. Upon this stone they rub gold, silver, tin, lead, and copper; thus its color, beauty, and quality appear <note>The author is describing a touchstone used to test the purity of metals</note>. Some of them are found in the shape of columns, all of many colors, such as black, yellow, green, red, and brown. This brownness is the color of amber. We have already discussed its benefits, its use for rubbing, and its combinations. The other, *Rohan*, is of many types; some are stone, some are composites; it possesses clarity, and from it comes Marble and many other varieties. However, *Arroham* has the property of whitening the teeth when ground and mixed with spices found in the book of medicine <note>original: "fisica"</note>. Sometimes it is ground on its own and mixed with spices, and other times it is burned before being mixed with them. It has other virtues as well: one of them is that when ground and given to a woman to drink in a known weight, according to the books of medicine, it will prevent her from becoming pregnant. It does this because it congeals in the "mouth of the mother" <note>original: "boca de la madre"; a medieval anatomical term for the cervix or uterus</note>.

### On the first stone of the letter Cin. (118.)

*Cayeriz* is the name of the first stone; it is a natural stone. It is found in the burials of the ancients. Its color is like lead. It is hard and very dense. Its virtue is that it greatly helps with leprosy <note>original: "gafedad"</note>; it draws the disease out of the sufferer when given to them to drink.

### On the second stone of the letter Cin. (118.)

The second stone of the letter Cin is called *Ceyecuz*. It has white spots and small pits. It is among the works of the ancients, found in their burials. It has such virtue that whoever carries it will not be harmed by any venomous beast <note>original: "bestiglo empozonado"</note> or any other poison.

### On the third stone of the letter Cin. (118.)

The third stone of the letter Cin is named *Caycocoz*. It is crafted through the wisdom of the ancients. It is fired <note>original: "cocho"; cooked or kiln-fired</note>, black in color, and rough; it has red and rough spots and is very hard. Its virtue is such that if one drinks the dust of this stone after it has been polished with oil, it will remove any poison that the person has ingested.

### On the first stone of the letter Zthe. (118.)

*Zthelice* is what they call the first stone of the letter Zthe. In color it is like a rose, and it has a scent like one as well. Its virtue is that if it is hung upon a man who is mad, he will be healed immediately on that very day.

### On the second stone of the letter Zthe. (118.)

The second stone of the letter Zthe is called *Ztheyceyn* in Greek and *Kaeden* in Arabic. This is one of the three principal stones we mentioned. It is white in color and is much used in building cities, towns, and castles <note>referring to limestone or structural stone</note>. Its virtue is that if it is ground and placed upon a wound, or a cut in a nerve or a vein from which blood flows, it stops the bleeding immediately.

<summary>This page catalogs stones categorized under the letters Fe through Zthe, detailing their origins, multilingual names, and medicinal uses. Significant mentions include stones used for building, stones found in ancient burials, and minerals used to treat conditions ranging from leprosy and epilepsy to poisoning and madness.</summary>
